#307. Best Open Earbuds (2026): Shokz, Bose, Soundcore, and More

📅 18 Sep 2026

Best Open Earbuds (2026): Shokz, Bose, Soundcore, and More

Tanggal: 18 Sep 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/

Sebagaimana diketahui, open earbuds are the big new thing in headphone land. Unlike in-ear variants, open earbuds are like tiny speakers that rest on the ear and let outside sound in naturally, so you can fully hear the world around you. Some use a hook style that wraps around the back of your ear, while others are clip-ons that look more like statement-piece earrings. Style aside, they are excellent for anyone who finds traditional earbuds uncomfortable or wants full environmental awareness for activities like running, biking, or even just doing chores around the house.

I’ve tested dozens of models since 2022, and while I still recommend noise-canceling earbuds, I also love open earbuds for specific use cases.

For more headphone recommendations, check out our guides to the Best Wireless Earbuds, Best Workout Headphones, and Best Wireless Headphones.

Diungkapkan bahwa updated november 2026: i am recommending the anker aeroclip 2 as the best overall, followed closely by the shokz opendots. I’ve also added the Apple AirPods 5 and CMF Clip Pro as an honorable mention.

Berdasarkan laporan, these are truly take-everywhere, do-anything headphones i would recommend to anyone looking for great open earbuds. They are exceedingly comfortable and easy to use all day, so much so that I sometimes forgot I was wearing them.

Berdasarkan laporan, they’re clip-ons that wrap around the earlobe, with the speaker end resting at the ear canal opening and the other end behind the ear. Importantly, the top of your ear is free for glasses, sunglasses, or hats. Like nearly all open earbuds, they let in sound from your surroundings, so don’t expect them to be a great companion for long-haul flights or daily gym sessions.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are other open earbuds that are nearly as good as these, and some surpass them in areas like sound quality. And, importantly, the call quality is great. The charging case is surprisingly small, smaller than most other options on this list. But it’s a combination of small details that puts the AeroClip 2 at the top. The physical button controls on each earbud are much easier to use than touch-sensitive alternatives, especially when running or exercising outdoors. These buds use the same AI-powered chip as the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro, and while they don’t sound quite as good, they are noticeably better than other open earbuds, especially in noisy environments.

The best part? They cost less than many similar competitors I tested.

Sebagaimana diketahui, my former top pick, and still a great option, especially if you value battery life. These earbuds do most of what the Soundcore AeroClip 2 does, just a little larger and a little pricier. The buds are exceedingly comfortable and stable for all-day wear, even during outdoor workouts.

Berdasarkan laporan, what sets them apart from the aeroclip 2 is battery life. They also have an IP57 dust and water-resistance rating, the same as premium, flagship earbuds like Apple AirPods Pro 3 and Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro. They are best in class—10 hours on a single charge, and 40 hours total with the charging case. I’ve worn them in the rain, on the beach, and fully submerged them in water multiple times without issue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, they are a bit pricey, though. Shokz recently launched the lower-priced Shokz OpenDots Air and Shokz OpenFit Air 2—I may update this recommendation depending on how my testing goes.

Diungkapkan bahwa the bose ultra open earbuds were a big deal when they launched in 2024—a brand-new design from bose and one of the biggest swings from a major brand in clip-on open earbuds. Two years later, the brand launched the second-generation version, and they are a solid, if expensive, option. That’s mainly because of sound quality—these earbuds sound clearer and more defined than most competitors. Another differentiator is physical button controls on each bud, which I find easier to use than touch alternatives, especially when running or biking.

Berdasarkan laporan, like the soundcore and shokz earbuds, they are very comfortable, so much so that i sometimes forgot i am wearing them. This gen-two version has a more distinct, two-tone material design that is certainly eye-catching, especially in the white colorway. They also now support wireless charging, a big omission in the first generation. But they are much pricier by comparison, and only worth it if you want the best sound quality in this clip-on form factor.

Diungkapkan bahwa it can be a little nerve-wracking to spend big bucks on a concept (open earbuds) you aren’t totally convinced by. That’s one reason I love this $50 option—the PearClip Pros aren’t super pricey and are a great way to find out if you even like open earbuds in the first place, especially the kind that clip onto the outside of your ear.

Sebagaimana diketahui, they are far less refined than shokz or soundcore. Things like the app and touch controls can be a little finicky. But that’s common at this super-low price point, and you can always upgrade to a more premium earbud if you fall in love with the clip-on form factor.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the shokz openrun pro 2 are more like headphones than earbuds—with a wraparound headband, long battery life, great sound quality (for open headphones), and no charging case. They use a combination of bone conduction (think vibrations) and air conduction (think tiny speakers pointed toward your ears) to deliver clearer sound than most smaller open earbuds, especially in noisy environments. That combination of technologies is why these are some of my favorite earbuds for outdoor fitness activities like running and biking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i do wish these headphones were a little cheaper. I’m currently testing the recently released, more affordable Shokz OpenRun Air 2, and I’m hopeful they can be a budget-friendly alternative.

Diungkapkan bahwa apple airpods 5 with wireless charging case for $149: apple airpods 5 are semi-open earbuds—they still go in your ears, but don’t have rubber eartips that block outside noise, meaning you can still hear the world around you pretty clearly. Because they go in your ear somewhat, they have better sound quality and automated noise-canceling than nearly all of my top picks. Fit, however, is a big issue. While nearly all of my top picks are excellent workout companions, the AirPods 5 are quite the opposite—they can fall out often during exercise and are tricky to control mid-run.

Berdasarkan laporan, nothing ear (open) for $99: former wired editor adrienne so loves these earbuds and uses them for almost all her outdoor activities. They fit slightly inside your ear and, like most Nothing headphones, have a distinct transparent design. They are very slim (19-mm wide) and lightweight. The case doesn’t clamp shut very firmly, so be careful, but at this price, that’s forgivable.

Berdasarkan laporan, cmf clip pro for $99: if you want something a little nicer and a little more comfortable than our budget pick (the soundpeats pearclip pro), these cmf open earbuds are a solid option. Sure, they’re a big step up in price, but for under $100, I found them more comfortable and easier to use thanks to the physical button control on each earbud (similar to my top picks).

Sebagaimana diketahui, jlab epic open sport for $100: jlab’s epic open sport stands out for its controls: the jlab emblem is a touch sensor, and each earbud also has physical buttons on top, making it a breeze to control. What holds the Epic Open Sport back is audio quality—the sound isn’t very detailed and is generally boring to listen to.

Sebagaimana diketahui, earfun clip for $70: for around $70, these are a solid pick for anyone on a budget. The problem is our budget pick, the Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, often sells for less and offers a similar overall experience. Former WIRED reviewer Waniata found the overall package punches above its price point, with a snappy, compact case, a comfortable fit, push-button controls, and reliable multi-device Bluetooth connections. Don’t dismiss these earbuds if you find them heavily discounted.

Diungkapkan bahwa shokz openfit pro for $250: the shokz openfit pro has a great premise: open earbuds with noise canceling. And while they do cancel some noise, it’s not much. Hear the world around you as you would without headphones, and turn on noise-canceling when you don’t, just like regular earbuds. The bigger issue is price: for $250, you could get open earbuds and great noise-canceling earbuds that do a better job for each task.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, suunto wing 2 for $179: these open-ear headphones are designed for endurance athletes—they have a long 12-hour battery life and come with a wireless power bank you can take on the go. Dock the headphones in the power bank for up to 36 hours of total battery life. There’s nothing inherently wrong with these headphones, but I don’t see a world where I would recommend them over the Shokz Openrun Pro 2, which retails for the same amount and offers more comfort, a sleeker design, better sound, and a more robust app.

Suunto Spark for $179: The Suunto Spark has a similar story to the Suunto Wing 2: it's built for athletes and syncs with Suunto fitness watches, but the similarly priced Shokz Openfit 2 outclasses it in the areas that matter (comfort, sound quality, battery).

What Are Open Earbuds and How Do They Sound?.

Diungkapkan bahwa at a glance, open earbuds seem a lot like typical wireless earbuds. The big difference is that, instead of going inside your ear canal, they rest somewhere on the outside of your ear, leaving it open so you can easily hear the world around you. I use them all the time for outdoor exercise like running or biking, where I want my music but also need to hear other runners, bikers, and cars to stay safe.

Berdasarkan laporan, because they leave your ears open and the sound comes from farther away (outside your ear rather than inside), audio performance isn’t as clear, intimate, or bassy as regular earbuds. They also typically lack noise-canceling features, so they are not a great fit for the office or air travel.

Berdasarkan laporan, open earbuds are perfect for outdoor activities or when you want to talk to other people without taking off your headphones. When I run or go for a bike ride, I only use open earbuds so I can hear my surroundings and stay safe. I also like using them around the house when I am cooking or doing laundry.

Berdasarkan laporan, semi-open earbuds, like apple’s airpods, sit inside the ear but don’t have eartips that create a sound seal. They can offer better audio quality than other open earbuds because the speakers and microphones are closer to your ear and mouth. Semi-open earbuds are comfortable, but they’re usually pretty loose—they can fall out easily and may be a poor option for fitness activities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i test open earbuds like i test any pair of headphones: in the real world, in my daily life. I wear each pair for at least a few weeks to test comfort, battery life, ease of use, and onboard controls. I listen to podcasts, watch TV shows, jam out to my favorite playlists, and call friends.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with open earbuds in particular, i also wear them on jogs, bike rides, and errand runs to get a better feel for how stable they are on my ears. I don’t expect them to cancel any noise, so I don’t test them on airplanes or loud commutes—they aren’t really made for that. My main audio source is Spotify Lossless, but, when possible, I test other formats and codecs as well.

Berdasarkan laporan, using the james webb space telescope (jwst), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the gemini north telescope, has been designated j1602+4228ab and nicknamed nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe. " The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Big Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen. 5 billion and 400 million times that of the sun. There is just 18,100 light-years, or roughly one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way, between the supermassive black holes, which have masses of 1. That makes Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua the most compact quasar pair found during a period of the universe's history known as Cosmic Dawn, shortly after the birth of the first stars, galaxies, and black holes.

"There is no definitive theoretical explanation for how a single one of these giant quasars exists so early in the age of our universe, much less two," research team leader Silvia Onorato of the NOIRLab said in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we observed nāpōwawāʻenakaulua at a time when the universe was only a thirteenth of its age and, astonishingly, its supermassive black holes are just as massive as those we see today. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, quasars occur when the supermassive black holes that sit at the heart of large galaxies are surrounded by a flattened cloud of swirling gas and dust called an "accretion disk," from which they feed or "accrete" matter. The immense gravity of the central black hole causes friction, heating the accretion disk and causing it to glow, often brighter than the combined light of every star in the surrounding galaxy. We see that glow as a quasar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finding such objects in the recent cosmic history of the 13. Such pairs should be common because the merger of galaxies that brings together supermassive black holes is frequent. Firstly, the "quasar phase" of a supermassive black hole is relatively short on cosmic terms. 8-billion-year-old universe isn't troubling, though finding compact pairs of them is still extremely rare. That should lead to an abundance of pairs of quasars with a separation less than the typical size of a galaxy. Secondly, even relatively close quasar pairs are very far away, making them faint and hard to detect with ground-based telescopes. There are three reasons this has proven tricky. Finally, at such great distances and with such a small separation between the two supermassive black holes, the individual members of a quasar pair are hard to individually resolve.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, yet, astronomers do find quasar pairs. Sometimes at distances and times that they would probably rather not, because it challenges everything we know about black hole growth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the trouble arises before the universe was 1 billion years. That is because, according to current models, black holes should need at least 1 billion years to feed and merge enough to reach masses millions or billions of times that of the sun.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, yet, since it began operations in 2022, the jwst has been routinely discovering supermassive black holes powering quasars as early as 400 million years after the big bang. If that wasn't confusing enough, the discovery of Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the third quasar pair seen at Cosmic Dawn, could really break current models.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nāpōwawāʻenakaulua was uncovered in data from the jwst's aether survey, which is conducting a census of objects in the early universe. Using JWST’s NIRSpec (Near-Infrared Spectrograph Integral Field Unit) instrument, the survey has uncovered 200 quasars, just under half of all currently known early universe quasars. It was while browsing the Aether dataset that the team discovered that quasar J1602+4228A is not alone, it had a companion now designated J1602+4228B.

Sebagaimana diketahui, resolving these two quasars should have been nearly impossible from the ground. But this was possible for Gemini North thanks to perfect timing and perfect weather conditions over Maunakea, the dormant volcano on the island of Hawai'i where the telescope is located.

A definite scientific feat, Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua remains a mystery for now, but it could actually help scientists better understand how galaxies were coming together during Cosmic Dawn, a vital stage in the evolution of the universe.

Diungkapkan bahwa "nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is a really unique environment," onorato said. "It's a laboratory for astronomers to study how the very first massive galaxies and their central black holes assembled together through direct galaxy interactions during these early times. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the team's results were published on tuesday (nov. 10) The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

#310. Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon

📅 09 Nov 2026

Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105224558.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa far below the ocean's surface, a constant snowfall drifts through the darkness. But unlike the frozen flakes that fall from the sky, this underwater snow consists of tiny clumps of waste, dead organisms, and other debris. Known as marine snow, these particles contain everything from mucus and animal feces to silt and the remains of microscopic plankton.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as this material sinks, it carries enormous quantities of carbon from the upper ocean toward the seafloor. Researchers estimate that marine snow removes more than 10 gigatons of carbon from surface waters each year. Yet only about two gigatons reach depths where that carbon can remain stored for hundreds or even thousands of years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, why so much carbon fails to make it into the deep ocean has long puzzled scientists. Now, researchers from UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography and the University of Lincoln have identified a surprisingly important factor: how sticky the marine snow is.

Berdasarkan laporan, their findings, published october 8 in the journal science, show that the viscosity, or thickness and gooeyness, of marine snow influences how quickly bacteria break it apart and how far it can sink. According to the researchers, the stickiest particles can transport more than six times as much carbon to the deep ocean as particles with a thinner, less viscous consistency.

Sebagaimana diketahui, marine snow plays an important role in earth's carbon cycle, the natural movement of carbon among the atmosphere, oceans, land, and living organisms. By transporting carbon into deep water, sinking particles can keep some of it isolated from the atmosphere for centuries or longer.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, not every particle survives the journey. Bacteria feed on marine snow as it descends, gradually breaking down the material and affecting how much carbon reaches the ocean's depths.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new research provides the first detailed look at how living bacteria interact with the physical structure of marine snow and, more broadly, mucus itself. These interactions are important well beyond the ocean's carbon cycle. Similar relationships between bacteria and mucus help sustain coral reefs, kelp forests, plant root systems, and the digestive systems of humans and other animals.

Until recently, scientists lacked the technology to observe these interactions at the microscopic scale needed to understand them.

A Four-Year Quest to See Inside Marine Snow.

Diungkapkan bahwa the project began in 2021, when bryce inman, then a postdoctoral researcher at scripps oceanography, set out to explore what he calls "the muscoscape. ".

"Observing individual bacteria interacting with the physical structure of mucus had never been possible," said Inman.

Diungkapkan bahwa together with colleagues including farooq azam, a microbiologist and professor emeritus at scripps, inman spent four years trying to overcome that limitation. Multiple attempts were unsuccessful before the team finally developed a working technique in 2025.

Sebagaimana diketahui, their solution combined 3d confocal microscopy with specially designed fluorescent molecules. Confocal microscopy uses light to capture detailed images at different depths within a sample, allowing researchers to reconstruct its structure in three dimensions. The fluorescent molecules helped make features of the material visible.

For the first time, the scientists could examine the "physical terrain" of individual marine snow particles while watching how living bacteria moved through and interacted with them.

The images revealed a surprisingly intricate microscopic environment, complete with structural differences that affect where bacteria can settle and how easily they can reach the material inside.

Diungkapkan bahwa much like snowflakes in the atmosphere, marine snow particles vary considerably. Each contains its own mixture of organic and inorganic materials, creating differences in composition, structure, and viscosity.

The researchers' new imaging approach, described in a companion study published in Nature Communications, revealed that bacteria preferentially colonize areas near a particle's surface where the material is less viscous.

The denser, stickier regions deeper inside are much harder for bacteria to penetrate.

Diungkapkan bahwa "bacteria can latch on to less viscous portions of each particle, but cannot reach more viscous regions until they break it down," said inman. "Think of it like a worm in an apple: the flesh is easy to penetrate, but the core is tough to chew through".

This difference has important consequences for how long marine snow remains intact.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in laboratory experiments, the scientists observed that particles with greater viscosity resisted bacterial degradation and fragmentation for longer periods. Computer simulations further suggested that these stickier particles can descend to greater depths before breaking apart.

Based on these results, the team estimates that highly viscous marine snow can deliver more than six times as much carbon to the deep ocean as less viscous particles.

The findings help explain why some sinking material transports carbon much farther into the ocean than other particles, even though both begin their journeys near the surface.

"How far marine snow can sink is a surprisingly complicated problem, and we have added another - very gooey - piece to the puzzle," said Inman.

A Discovery With Implications Beyond the Ocean.

Although the research focuses on marine snow, its implications extend to many environments where bacteria interact with mucus.

Diungkapkan bahwa mucus is often regarded as a relatively simple, slippery substance. But the new imaging technology reveals that it has a complex internal landscape, with microscopic structures that can influence how bacteria behave.

Understanding these physical features could help scientists investigate biological processes in settings ranging from human digestive health to the recovery of damaged coral reefs.

The method also opens opportunities to explore interactions that previously could not be observed directly, providing researchers with a new way to study the microscopic environments inhabited by bacteria.

Berdasarkan laporan, mucus, slime, whatever you want to call it, "has a surprising amount of structure," inman said. "There are bulges, crevasses, all this sort of structure to it that we really had no idea about at a scale smaller than bacteria. This is the first time we're really examining this physical habitat. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the discovery adds an important missing piece to scientists' understanding of how carbon travels through the ocean. It also demonstrates that something as seemingly ordinary as the thickness of underwater slime can have far-reaching consequences for the planet's natural systems.

Additional funding for the research was provided by the Simons Foundation and the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council.

Diungkapkan bahwa nvidia’s ceo and cofounder jensen huang is officially out, and longtime chief financial officer colette kress is in. The chipmaker’s board of directors announced Thursday that Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, has been named interim CEO following Huang’s resignation amid a scandal over his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman believed by US officials to be an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

Berdasarkan laporan, harvey jones, the newly appointed chair of nvidia’s board, said in a statement that kress “has helped lead nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position. ” He added that Kress will be supported by an “experienced leadership team” and that the board has “full confidence” in her.

Kress was among the most obvious candidates to fill the void after Huang’s departure, according to multiple tech executives and industry analysts who follow Nvidia closely, given her long tenure at the company, credibility on Wall Street and across the tech industry, and, perhaps most importantly, her deep familiarity with Nvidia’s business and finances.

Berdasarkan laporan, “she’s extremely strong-willed, professional, and whip-smart. She doesn’t tolerate nonsense. She can be friendly and gracious too,” says a former Nvidia executive who spoke on the condition of anonymity. “She obviously has a keen sense for how Jensen thinks. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa nvidia’s board said on sunday it was launching an independent investigation into huang’s activities following a report by the new york times that he had an affair with a woman named alice huang, who us officials suspected of being a chinese intelligence asset. WIRED reported on Monday that Huang quietly hired a crisis communications firm sometime last year to handle matters related to his personal life. By October of 2025, the firm was being looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang at Nvidia, around the same time The New York Times reported that US authorities were investigating whether a company linked to Alice Huang had helped Chinese firms evade US chip export controls through its subsidiaries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while huang has long been the public face of nvidia, kress has been responsible for managing the chipmaker’s relationship with wall street. On earnings calls, she often details Nvidia’s financial performance, customer demand, supply constraints, and other key metrics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “one of the things we don’t focus on is the stock price. We focus on our investors and how we would like to innovate,” Kress told the Israeli business newspaper Globes in 2023.

Sebagaimana diketahui, before joining nvidia, kress spent more than two decades in finance roles at microsoft, cisco, and texas instruments. Huang personally recruited her in 2013, when Nvidia was still best known for its gaming graphics cards, according to Globes. Huang laid out his vision for the company’s future on a whiteboard, explaining how Nvidia could become a major supplier of computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence.

Other potential successors to Huang included Ian Buck, an Nvidia veteran of more than 20 years who created the company’s software platform CUDA and now oversees its high-performance computing business, and Jeff Fisher, who joined Nvidia in 1994 as the head of software sales and later became senior vice president of its GeForce unit, where he led Nvidia’s strategy for bringing GPUs to market.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, nvidia’s unusual corporate structure has long meant that dozens of executives reported directly to huang. Even executive vice presidents aren’t necessarily given direct control over budgets, sources have told WIRED. The company lacks a traditional chief operating officer. As a result, few people within the organization have the same level of understanding of the company’s financials as Kress.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the former nvidia executive who spoke to wired on the condition of anonymity said that while kress is incredibly sharp and “can step into the [ceo] role immediately without needing any guidance,” she doesn’t have the same engineering and technical expertise that huang brought to the role. She has also shied away from being “at the center of public attention,” the person said.

Given the intense scrutiny surrounding Huang lately, that leadership style might be a welcome temporary change for Nvidia.

#315. A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds

📅 10 Nov 2026

A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105224555.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, a mysterious structure stretching roughly 93 billion miles across space is giving astronomers new clues about the violent events that shape young planetary systems. Known as the "Cat's Tail," this enormous cloud of dark material lies about 63 light-years from Earth, in the faint constellation Pictor (which is Latin for "painter"). For the past two years, its unusual appearance and uncertain origins have puzzled scientists.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the structure is part of a vast disk of dust and debris surrounding beta pictoris, a young star system that resembles our own solar system during its early development. Now, using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have captured previously hidden details of the Cat's Tail in visible light for the first time.

Berdasarkan laporan, the discovery is described in a study published in the astrophysical journal letters. Led by University of Arizona planetary scientist Arin Avsar, the research team combined the new Hubble images with observations spanning more than 14 years. Their findings provide a clearer picture of the structure's composition, location, and shape, along with additional evidence that a massive collision may have created it.

A Possible Collision Between Pluto-Sized Worlds.

"The Cat's Tail is thought to be the aftermath of a collision between large bodies - think something like Pluto," said Avsar, a doctoral student working with the research groups of Daniel Apai and Kevin Wagner at the University of Arizona's Lunar and Planetary Laboratory and Steward Observatory.

Berdasarkan laporan, "oddly, this feature had previously only been seen with the james webb space telescope, which detects infrared light, but remained invisible at shorter wavelengths, which has puzzled the community for a while. ".

The mystery becomes even more interesting when viewed in the context of how planetary systems form.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, today, our solar system appears relatively orderly. But 4. Planets follow established paths around the Sun, while many smaller rocky objects occupy "designated" regions such as the asteroid belt. 6 billion years ago, the situation was dramatically different.

Diungkapkan bahwa a young sun was surrounded by a swirling disk of gas and dust. Rocky objects repeatedly collided, sometimes breaking apart and sometimes combining into larger bodies. Over time, some accumulated enough material to become planets, while countless others were destroyed or scattered.

Diungkapkan bahwa astronomers study younger systems like beta pictoris because they offer an opportunity to observe processes that unfolded in our own cosmic neighborhood billions of years ago. Its debris disk, consisting of dust and fragments left behind during planetary development, is believed to be approaching the final stages of planet formation.

Why Hubble Could Finally See the Mysterious Cat's Tail.

One of the most intriguing questions about the Cat's Tail is why it was previously detectable in infrared light but so difficult to observe in visible light.

The answer may lie in the unusual material that makes up the enormous structure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we think the cat's tail has eluded our observations in visible light until now because of what it's made of," avsar explained. "It consists almost entirely of we call organic refractory material, which is heavily carbon-based. These long chains of carbon atoms absorb visible light, so they're quite black. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, organic refractory material consists of complex carbon compounds that can withstand relatively harsh conditions in space. Because these compounds absorb much of the visible light that strikes them, they can make the surrounding dust appear exceptionally dark.

The Hubble observations also support another unusual finding: the Cat's Tail appears to be composed of extremely small, surprisingly porous dust particles.

Berdasarkan laporan, individual grains measure only about a micron across, roughly one millionth of a meter. Yet instead of being compact and solid, they appear remarkably "fluffy," with substantial empty space within their structures.

Diungkapkan bahwa the scale of the entire cloud is difficult to imagine. It may stretch as far as 1,000 astronomical units, with one astronomical unit (AU) defined as the average distance between Earth and the Sun. That corresponds to approximately 93 billion miles, or the equivalent of lining up around 200 trillion house cats from tail to nose.

"How you can get dust grains that small that are as porous as we see here, no one really understands, and that's part of why we study this feature," Avsar said.

How a Violent Collision Could Create Fluffy Cosmic Dust.

If the Cat's Tail really formed when large planetary bodies smashed into each other, researchers still need to explain how that destruction produced such tiny, porous particles.

One possibility is that the collision was powerful enough to vaporize some of the material involved.

"It's possible that the velocities involved in the collisions were so high that the carbon grains vaporized, turned into gas, and then recondensed as they cooled, and that's how they became so porous," said co-author Wagner, a NASA Sagan Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Arizona's Steward Observatory.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this scenario, the intense impact would have transformed solid carbon material into gas. As the material cooled, it could have condensed back into solid particles with unusually open, lightweight structures.

However, the precise process remains uncertain, and additional observations will be needed to determine whether this explanation is correct.

A 93-Billion-Mile Structure With an Unexpected Shape.

The new research also challenges previous assumptions about where the Cat's Tail extends in space.

By combining visible light observations from Hubble with infrared measurements from the James Webb Space Telescope, the researchers used computer modeling to reconstruct the structure's possible three-dimensional arrangement.

Diungkapkan bahwa earlier observations suggested that the cat's tail extended outward from beta pictoris and far behind the star from earth's perspective. Because the surrounding debris disk is viewed nearly edge-on, it was difficult to determine how much of the structure extended away from us rather than across our field of view.

The new analysis points to a different explanation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we find that instead of extending for 1,000 astronomical units behind the star, the cat's tail may extend straight sideways relative to us, and there is no third dimension to it," avsar said. "It's essentially in the same plane of the sky as the star and possibly extends a little bit behind it. ".

This suggests the structure may be spread mainly across the sky as seen from Earth, rather than projecting deep into space behind the star.

The revised geometry gives astronomers a better understanding of where the dust is located and could help them reconstruct the event that produced it.

Hubble Discovers a Strange Warp Caused by a Giant Planet.

The Cat's Tail was not the only unusual feature revealed by the new observations.

Using Hubble in a different observational configuration, Avsar and his colleagues also identified an unexpected distortion in the broad halo of dust surrounding Beta Pictoris.

The researchers suspect this strange warp may be caused by the gravitational influence of Beta Pic b, one of three planets in the system.

Berdasarkan laporan, beta pic b is a massive gas giant estimated to be about 10 times the mass of jupiter. Its powerful gravity may be disturbing the surrounding debris, altering the paths of dust particles, comets, and other icy objects across enormous distances.

Berdasarkan laporan, "this gives us another line of evidence into how giant planets influence comets through their immense gravitational force," avsar said. "It's a testament of how much these massive planets really influence their surrounding dust and icy bodies out to hundreds of astronomical units. ".

The finding highlights how giant planets can shape their environments far beyond their immediate orbits.

A Glimpse Into Our Solar System's Violent Past.

Berdasarkan laporan, for researchers, beta pictoris offers more than an opportunity to investigate an unusual cosmic structure. It may also provide a window into the early history of our own solar system.

Consider the Kuiper Belt, the distant region beyond Neptune that contains Pluto and numerous other icy bodies.

Diungkapkan bahwa when the kuiper belt was only about 20 million years old, astronomers believe it was much more crowded than it is today. It may have contained hundreds of objects comparable in size to Pluto.

Sebagaimana diketahui, over billions of years, the gravitational influence of the solar system's outer giant planets likely changed that environment dramatically. By disturbing the orbits of smaller bodies, these planets may have pushed many objects into new regions or expelled them from the solar system entirely, effectively "clearing out" much of the original population.

The strange dust tail and newly identified warp around Beta Pictoris may offer clues to similar processes unfolding in another planetary system.

By studying these distant structures, astronomers hope to better understand how violent collisions, migrating debris, and the immense gravity of giant planets helped transform the chaos of the early solar system into the planetary arrangement we see today.

#317. Google and Samsung’s Android XR Smart Glasses Are Finally Here

📅 12 Nov 2026

Google and Samsung’s Android XR Smart Glasses Are Finally Here

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/google-samsung-intelligent-eyewear-launch-warby-parker-gentle-monster-smart-glasses/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, google and samsung's next face computers have arrived. Nearly two years after the companies first announced the Android XR platform that powers the hardware, the smart glasses are finally on sale.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the “intelligent eyewear” is a collaboration between the two tech companies, with samsung providing its hardware expertise and google handling much of the software platform. Smart glasses are just one part of Android XR—there are also mixed-reality headsets and glasses for more immersive experiences, like last year's Samsung Galaxy XR and the upcoming Xreal Aura.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eyewear brands warby parker and gentle monster are heavily involved in the new smart glasses, responsible for the design and fit, similar to how meta tapped ray-ban for its competing—and market-leading—wearables. Google and Samsung are leveraging Warby Parker and Gentle Monster's brick-and-mortar presence and retail expertise, which lets people demo the glasses before buying them. (Kering Eyewear, which owns brands like Lindberg and Maui Jim, has also signed up to make glasses for Android XR in the future. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first models are available for preorder now, with official sales starting on december 10. Warby Parker's frames start at $395 and come in three styles—Alden, Reid, and Wren—as optical or sunglasses, with various prescription, lens, and width options. Gentle Monster's glasses start at $449 and come in six designs, various colors, and tints, with prescription options for most frames.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the hardware is identical across both brands. The glasses weigh around 41 grams (10 grams less than Meta's new Gen 3 glasses), have a nine-hour battery life, and include a charging case that can recharge the glasses up to seven times. They have a 12-megapixel camera with an LED indicator that shows everyone in eyeshot that you’re recording. There’s a button to capture photos and 90-second videos at up to 3K resolution with a press. A touch-sensitive temple piece lets you tap to activate the onboard Gemini assistant, or slide two fingers back and forth to control the volume of the audio coming out of the glasses' speaker.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they are the first devices to support the “hey gemini” hotword, though you can use the well-known “hey google” hotword if you'd like. Still, the new spoken wake phrase distinguishes the glasses as Gemini's “optimal form,” according to Juston Payne, Google's senior director of product management for XR.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we felt that these are a gemini-forward device,” payne tells wired. “It's really you and Gemini going through your day together, so it was feeling a little dissonant for us. You're not talking to Google, you're talking to Gemini. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, oddly, these glasses are only compatible with certain devices—google pixel phones, samsung galaxy phones, and iphones—and only select models. You'll need a Pixel 7 or newer, Galaxy S or Z Fold running Samsung's One UI 9. 0 or higher, and the iPhone 13 Pro or newer. A Google spokesperson tells WIRED the company will share more about how it plans to expand support to other phones in 2027 after launch.

The arms of the glasses are similarly thick.

Sebagaimana diketahui, since you'll be buying the glasses from an eyewear brand, they will be the customer-facing party to handle any problems you may have with the device or prescriptions. On the backend, Payne says there are elaborate business integrations and handoffs, so the customer service workload is split between all the companies.

Diungkapkan bahwa google has already previewed intelligent eyewear glasses with displays built into the lenses—useful for showing navigation instructions or real-time captions for folks with hearing issues. As for plans to launch audio-only smart glasses, like Meta's recent Ray-Ban Audio, Warby Parker co-CEO Dave Gilboa tells WIRED, “There's a pretty robust pipeline of additional products. However, they are not ready yet; Payne says they're currently being tested by “non-Googlers” and are still on the road map, though he didn't share a specific release window. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, smart glasses have been around for a few years, but they come in many forms. Unlike display smart glasses designed to plug into a laptop to mirror or extend your screen, or more immersive glasses like Meta's VR Glasses, which layer virtual experiences over the real world, Intelligent Eyewear is more akin to what Google pitched years ago with the original Google Glass.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you can hear notifications pipe through from your connected smartphone and respond to messages by speaking to gemini. You can listen to music, take phone calls, and get audio navigation through Google Maps. Yes, you can snap photos and videos too, though Payne quickly notes that these glasses are designed more to have Gemini assist you throughout the day than to capture content.

That's likely because Meta has faced public scrutiny over how people use its smart glasses, so much so that it has spawned a new term for people wearing them: the Meta Creep (harkening back to when anyone wearing Google Glasses was called a “Glasshole”).

“We learned through Glass that you can make people uncomfortable if you're not clearly communicating,” Payne says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to that end, google is announcing a series of policies and features alongside the glasses to assuage concerns. If you try to block the indicator light while recording, the camera will stop. They include tamper detection, so the camera will know if you tried to disable the indicator light. When you ask Gemini to look at something, those visuals are not saved in your Gemini History, and Google says it will not use them to train AI models or target ads. The glasses will automatically redact the faces of people around you before Gemini processes the visual data. We've highlighted all of Google's privacy-focused announcements around its glasses in a separate story.

Gentle Monster's Intelligent Eyewear comes in six different styles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, most of the features that google is positioning around intelligent eyewear rely on gemini. See a poster for a comedy show? Just ask Gemini for more information, or add it to your calendar. You can ask Gemini to add items to your shopping list or whip up a travel itinerary with hotel recommendations and save them to a note. For example, Gemini can play music on Apple Music if you're on an iPhone. Some of these are saved in the Gemini app, but it can leverage other apps on your smartphone. And if you use Samsung Notes on a Samsung phone, it'll know that's where you likely want your notes saved.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you activate gemini, it's technically a “gemini live” experience, meaning the assistant activates and you can have a free-flowing conversation. When you want it to “look” at something in front of you, be specific in your query; otherwise, it won't use the camera. A swipe back on the glasses' arm will end the interaction. You can ask it to look at a page in a book and summarize the content, or if you have a bunch of cocktail ingredients in front of you but don't know what to make, you can ask Gemini for suggestions and step-by-step instructions to craft a drink—at your pace.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some gemini controls are on-device and don't need to travel to the cloud, like asking the assistant to play the next track. Speaking of, early next year, Google says users can use gestures on devices like the Fitbit Air or Google Pixel Watch to control music playback or activate Gemini on the glasses right from their wrist.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another big capability is translation. Gemini will automatically detect languages and translate them to your preferred tongue. You do need to stare at the individual to hear their words translated, and there's a limited range; the quality depends heavily on the environment and noise level, but it worked remarkably well in my controlled demos, with only a few errors. The translation tries to mimic the speaker's tone and voice so it feels like their own words.

Berdasarkan laporan, there's an accessibility feature called guided vision, which provides audio descriptions for people with impaired vision, like when reading fine print or locating everyday items. Google is also collaborating with Aira so you can stream the glasses' feed straight to a human interpreter for real-time visual support.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to help demystify these features—and convince consumers that smart glasses aren't just a fad for tech bros—warby parker and gentle monster are both launching pop-up experiences in new york city this week. Gentle Monster's pop-up will run for about a month, but Warby Parker's “Literatureland” will be open through 2027, letting people walk through the experience with a pair of nonprescription glasses to demo Gemini's capabilities.

Berdasarkan laporan, “these are the original wearables that have been around for hundreds of years,” warby parker's gilboa says. “A lot of people start by getting an eye exam in one of our stores, and then come in, do a demo, buy these—we just want to make it as easy and seamless as possible. ”.

#318. Comets may have destroyed life's ingredients instead of delivering them to Earth

📅 10 Nov 2026

Comets may have destroyed life's ingredients instead of delivering them to Earth

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105224553.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, for nearly a century, scientists have considered the possibility that comets helped make life on earth possible by delivering essential organic molecules from space. Now, new research suggests this long-standing explanation is extremely unlikely.

Berdasarkan laporan, comets are known to contain many of the chemical compounds associated with the origins of life. These substances, often called prebiotic molecules, can participate in the chemical reactions that eventually produce the complex ingredients needed for living organisms. For decades, researchers have proposed that comets striking the early Earth supplied a steady stream of these compounds.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, a new study led by the university of cambridge challenges that theory. Using advanced computer simulations, researchers found that comets generally approach Earth at speeds and angles that make it extremely difficult for delicate organic molecules to survive. Instead of delivering their chemical cargo intact, most would likely destroy it during their violent arrival.

Diungkapkan bahwa the findings, published in scientific reports, suggest that successful delivery of life's building blocks by comets would have been an extraordinarily rare event. Interestingly, the researchers also found that Mars may have offered somewhat better conditions for receiving these molecules, although the likelihood remains very low.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get out of jail free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said lead author dr. "It's kind of a romantic idea, but our results suggest it's highly unlikely. Richard Anslow from Cambridge's Institute of Astronomy. ".

Why Comets May Have Failed to Deliver Life's Building Blocks.

The idea that comets could transport the ingredients for life received renewed attention in 2023, when Anslow and several colleagues explored how these icy objects might behave in planetary systems where worlds orbit relatively close together.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, their earlier research suggested that comets could potentially lose speed as they passed between neighboring planets. Through a series of gravitational encounters, a comet might effectively bounce from one planet to another, eventually traveling slowly enough to deliver organic molecules without destroying them.

The team wanted to determine whether a similar process could have occurred in our own Solar System, potentially explaining how essential chemicals reached the young Earth.

"We're learning more and more all the time about how our Solar System and the Earth formed, and pulling this together with lots of different advances in modeling, which allowed us to investigate this idea that has been around for close to a century," he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa to investigate, the researchers combined several sophisticated modeling techniques. These included simulations of comet impacts, calculations of how comets interact with planetary atmospheres, and models tracing how comet populations formed and changed as the Solar System developed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the results revealed a major obstacle. Although a comet might occasionally approach Earth under conditions favorable for preserving organic compounds, such encounters would have been exceptionally uncommon. Successful delivery could not be completely ruled out, but the simulations indicated that it was highly improbable.

A Critical Ingredient for Life Faces Nearly Impossible Odds.

To better understand what happens to the molecules carried by comets, the team concentrated on hydrogen cyanide (HCN), a chemical commonly detected in comets throughout our Solar System.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite its reputation as a highly toxic substance, hydrogen cyanide is important in research on the origins of life. It contains carbon and nitrogen and can participate in reactions that produce more complex organic compounds, making it a potentially valuable ingredient in the chemistry that preceded living organisms.

Berdasarkan laporan, the simulations showed that even when hydrogen cyanide managed to survive a comet's arrival, another major problem remained. The impact would need to deposit enough of the molecule in one location to support meaningful chemical reactions. Events capable of producing those useful concentrations were extraordinarily rare.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, timing created yet another difficulty. Comet impacts were much more common during Earth's earliest history, but their frequency declined sharply over the planet's first 500 million years. According to the researchers, there may have been only a handful of opportunities during that entire early period for comets to deliver hydrogen cyanide under favorable conditions.

Diungkapkan bahwa even a successful delivery would not necessarily have helped life develop. Hydrogen cyanide deposited on Earth's surface would likely have dispersed or become diluted relatively quickly, leaving little time for the chemical reactions associated with life's origins to get underway.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for the comet theory to work, several unlikely events would therefore have needed to occur together. A comet would have had to strike at just the right speed and angle, preserve its organic cargo, deposit enough material in a suitable location, and trigger important chemical processes before those molecules dispersed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it would really have to be a one-in-a-million occurrence, because not only would you need an impact at just the right speed and just the right angle, you would also need everything to happen after that point, in terms of the concentration and the speed at which the chemical origins of life got going," said anslow. But it seems to be a really rare occurrence - at best, a one-off fluke. "We can't rule out for certain that it happened that way. ".

If Not Comets, Where Did Life's Ingredients Come From?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the findings raise a fundamental question about earth's earliest history. If comets were unlikely to supply the chemical building blocks of life, what was responsible?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one possibility involves asteroids, which collided with the early earth far more frequently than comets. The researchers suggest that asteroid impacts could have created conditions in which important prebiotic molecules formed through chemical reactions associated with those collisions.

Diungkapkan bahwa another explanation is that earth produced these compounds on its own. Natural chemical processes operating on the young planet may have generated the ingredients necessary for increasingly complex chemistry, without requiring organic molecules to arrive from space.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these possibilities do not establish exactly how life began. Instead, they highlight alternative ways that the raw materials for life could have become available on Earth.

Why Mars May Have Had a Better Chance Than Earth.

While the simulations cast serious doubt on cometary delivery to Earth, they also revealed an intriguing possibility involving Mars.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the red planet is smaller than earth and currently has a much thinner atmosphere. These characteristics make it a potentially more favorable destination for cometary molecules, since incoming objects could be more likely to reach its surface without completely destroying their chemical cargo.

According to the researchers, Mars may therefore have been better positioned to receive prebiotic compounds during the Solar System's early development, when comet encounters were considerably more frequent.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, the simulations do not demonstrate that such deliveries actually occurred. Even on Mars, the conditions required for a successful transfer of life's chemical ingredients appear difficult to achieve.

Diungkapkan bahwa "this is not to say it definitely happened on mars, of course, but suggests it would be unlikely if it happened on earth and didn't happen on mars," said anslow. "Or the other, perhaps more likely, alternative, is that it didn't happen on either planet. ".

What the Discovery Means for the Search for Alien Life.

Beyond changing how scientists think about Earth's early chemistry, the findings could help guide the search for potentially habitable planets in other star systems.

Berdasarkan laporan, future space observatories may be able to investigate distant worlds in greater detail, searching for atmospheric clues that could indicate environments suitable for life. Among the proposed missions is the Habitable Worlds Observatory, a potential successor to the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

Berdasarkan laporan, the researchers suggest that planetary systems where comets can move between closely spaced planets while gradually losing speed may deserve particular attention. In such environments, the unusual comet delivery mechanism explored in their earlier research could be more likely to operate.

Identifying these systems could help astronomers focus future observations on planets where essential organic molecules may have had a better chance of surviving their journey through space.

Berdasarkan laporan, although the new findings make comets an unlikely explanation for how life's building blocks reached earth, they do not eliminate the possibility that cometary delivery played a role elsewhere. Understanding where these chemical transfers are possible could provide valuable clues as scientists continue investigating how life emerges across the universe.

The research received partial support from the Royal Society, the Leverhulme Centre for Life in the Universe, and the Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC), which is part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI).

A long-term goal at NASA has been the ability to robotically haul back to Earth specimens from the Red Planet.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nasa is kickstarting a new initiative for its troubled mars sample return (msr) program, called the perseverance sample retrieval architecture, or psra in space shorthand. The plan is to establish a fresh NASA strategy for gathering Mars samples collected by the Perseverance rover and launching them back to Earth.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the psra initiative was noted on nov. 9 by Tiffany Morgan, director of the NASA Mars Exploration Program (MEP), during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG).

Morgan noted that there will be a PSRA strategy team kickoff in January 2027 with a final report due in winter 2027-2028.

The backdrop to the PSRA activity is that there's one busy rover already on the Red Planet snagging and bagging samples.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nasa's perseverance mars rover remains on the prowl within jezero crater following its touchdown in february 2021. That car-sized robot has been grabbing select specimens from across the area and gingerly dropping the sealed pick-me-ups on the surface of Mars, as well as stuffing them inside the rover itself.

Those collectibles may well hold signs of past life on the enigmatic, dusty and foreboding Red Planet.

NASA and the European Space Agency have for years been intently plotting out plans to send future spacecraft to Mars and haul those Perseverance-plucked bits, pieces, and sniffs of atmosphere to Earth for rigorous inspection here on Earth using state-of-the-art equipment.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, over the years, multiple reviews of a nasa mars sample return (msr) project by independent groups have reported sticker shock findings. Indeed, one last price tag came in at about $11 billion, with samples being returned to Earth in 2040. That finding was deemed by NASA itself as too costly and not doable within an acceptable time frame.

Yet another appraisal group ended up finding it feasible to return Mars samples as early as 2035 for a less costly ship and shoot cost of some $8 billion.

How the PSRA review deals with MSR cost and a multitude of other concerns is in the to-be-determined column.

In the first place, why are samples from Mars delivered by robotic means? Why not let a human expedition bring back the goods?.

Also speaking at MEPAG was Bruce Jakosky of the Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics at the University of Colorado Boulder and Department of Earth and Space Sciences at the University of Washington.

Diungkapkan bahwa jakosky called for an integrated approach to planning human missions to mars. He highlighted recommendations stemming from a workshop in which he participated, held last May and organized by Explore Mars, Inc.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that report focused on the impact of msr on reducing risk for human missions, rather than focusing on the science, jakosky told space. com.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the purpose is to understand the risk to astronauts and to hardware. "This includes perchlorates and chloromethanes that have been identified already, and detection of other species that might be present. The risk includes that from compounds that are present in the soil that are hazardous to astronauts if breathed in," said Jakosky. It also includes dust that can be breathed in by astronauts and that can affect hardware wear and tear," he said.

During the MEPAG gathering, Jakosky flagged the importance of returning samples prior to human missions to Mars, such as:.

Yet one more forcing factor for NASA in yet another relook at MSR is that China is making progress on its Tianwen-3 Mars Sample Return mission.

According to the China National Space Administration, the country's Tianwen-3 probe will have a lander, an ascender, a service capsule, an orbiter, and an Earth reentry module.

Tianwen-3 appears on track getting the trek underway around 2028 on two Long March-5 heavy-lift carrier rockets from the Wenchang Space Launch Site in China's southernmost island province of Hainan.

China's Tianwen-3 mission is dedicated to bring back to Earth roughly 500 grams of Red Planet collectibles in 2031.

Beau Jessup, the only child of British actress Lisa Maxwell and her husband Paul Jessup, died at the age of 27 while studying journalism at Columbia University in New York, according to her school.

Lisa Maxwell’s family is grieving a tragic loss.

Diungkapkan bahwa “columbia journalism school mourns the loss of beau jessup, a student in our m. “We extend our deepest condolences to her family, friends, classmates and all who knew and loved her. program,” the school shared in a Nov. S. 9 statement. ”.

#322. Here’s How Google Says It’s Making Its Smart Glasses More Private

📅 12 Nov 2026

Here’s How Google Says It’s Making Its Smart Glasses More Private

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/how-google-is-making-its-smart-glasses-more-private/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smart glasses have a public perception problem. People wearing Meta's popular Ray-Ban glasses have been labeled “Meta Creeps. ” But it didn't start with Meta—when Google Glass launched in 2013, “Glasshole” was the word used to describe people wearing them.

Berdasarkan laporan, it boils down to the fact that these smart glasses have cameras on them that let people record whatever’s in front of them with the push of a button. The cameras aren't easy to see, and while an indicator light activates when the glasses are recording, they're far less conspicuous than someone holding a smartphone up to record video or photos. It also doesn't help that people have tried to tamper with the LEDs and block them, and have recorded women without their consent.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but google is on a mission to change the perception of smart glasses as socially intrusive tech. The first Android XR Intelligent Eyewear smart glasses—made in collaboration with Samsung, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster—are now available for preorder, with sales kicking off on December 10. You can read about how they work and what they can do in this separate story.

But you might be more interested in how Google is trying to separate its glasses from Meta's optics and positioning them as the more privacy-minded option to assuage public concerns.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there's this whole feature set of ai privacy that we think is super important,” says juston payne, google's senior director of product management for xr. These are, honestly, not hard technical problems. “Ultimately, what we're trying to do here is say: Look, these are choices. They're decisions. And we would like other companies to make different decisions, sort of like a bar-raising thing. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all of the intelligent eyewear glasses have a power switch to turn them off completely, so you can wear them as regular glasses. They also have a recording light that illuminates when the glasses snap a photo or record a video, which is intentionally limited to 90 seconds for privacy purposes.

Here's a collection of the things Google says it's doing to make its smart glasses more private:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, payne hopes these policies and actions will encourage other companies to follow suit. “We hope that never again do glasses launch from some other company that doesn't have good algorithms built in,” he says. “That should not have happened; hopefully it doesn't happen again. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, privacy experts i spoke with acknowledged that google is trying not to repeat meta's mistakes, but they point out that smart glasses are still vehicles for collecting sensitive data. Even with an indicator light, it's harder to tell when someone's recording you in public than if someone is holding out their smartphone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, reem suleiman, senior campaign director at the nonprofit digital rights advocacy group fight for the future, says camera-equipped glasses shouldn't be normalized in public because they are a precursor to mass surveillance and have the capacity to identify people. (This summer, Meta silently added a face-recognition code to its smart glasses and then subsequently deleted it after a WIRED report; in 2024, two Harvard students built a face-recognition tool for Meta's glasses. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa “people find ways around it,” suleiman says. “There's no actual aspect of consent. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa janusz swierczynski, who researches human interactions with emerging tech at the university of oxford's saïd business school, tells wired these privacy measures are meaningful. However, they still largely address privacy at an individual level rather than thinking about people affected by them. That's partly because the technology is advancing faster than policy and research.

Diungkapkan bahwa “a lot of privacy is managed by social norms, by what we think is acceptable to record, and that prevents people from recording anything and everything,” swierczynski says. “Normalizing recording does have unintended consequences, which is why it's important to focus on bystander privacy. ”.

Intriguingly, Payne highlighted that tech companies like Google need to make clear, declarative statements about what the glasses are doing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “ambiguity is not your friend here,” payne says. So there is a rebuilding thing happening right now … You can hopefully have your cake and eat it too, which is cool glasses that everybody's excited about—that you're comfortable with. “I think that a lot of that concern came from some trust being broken. ”.

#323. Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread

📅 13 Nov 2026

Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03666-z

Diungkapkan bahwa thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Berdasarkan laporan, confirmed infections of bundibugyo ebola have surpassed 10,000 in the drc since may. Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.

Berdasarkan laporan, epidemiologists have used mobile-phone data and test records to map the early spread of ebola in the democratic republic of the congo (drc)1 weeks before the outbreak was declared. The authors say the study findings reveal how surveillance systems failed to detect signals of the disease early on and enabled it to spread rapidly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it is now six months since the outbreak of the bundibugyo strain of the virus was announced. The number of confirmed infections has risen to more than 10,000 and 5,198 people have died, making this the largest Bundibugyo outbreak so far. There are no licenced vaccines or approved treatments specifically for Bundibugyo, which has complicated efforts to control it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the drc declared the outbreak on 15 may after laboratory tests confirmed the first case, a person from ituri province in the country’s northeast, was infected with the bundibugyo strain. Around the same time, suspected cases were being reported in several DRC locations, including Mongbwalu, Rwampara, Bunia and Nyankunde in Ituri, and Butembo, Katwa and Goma in the neighbouring province of North Kivu. The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May, citing infections among health-care workers, the geographical spread of cases and clusters of undocumented deaths. Researchers strongly suspect that the virus had been spreading in the region months earlier.

To understand how the outbreak spread so quickly, the researchers looked at anonymized mobile-phone data to trace the movement of people between areas.

Although the first confirmed case was identified on 15 May, the study reports that the person had symptoms as early as 25 April.

Berdasarkan laporan, the team found that people travelling out of mongbwalu, bunia and rwampara between 24 april and 24 may helped to predict which health zones would report infections by 1 june. For instance, areas close to the initial centres were at greater risk of infections, the study found.

The risk of infections rose again in places 150–200 kilometres away from the initial outbreak centres because people travelled to larger towns and cities along established routes, says study co-author Pierre Akilimali, an epidemiologist at the National Institute of Public Health (INSP) in Kinshasa.

The authors say the findings show that people movement was a key driver of the rapid spread in the early phases of the outbreak.

“These are very important findings which reinforce what we initially knew at the onset of the outbreak,” says Tambe Akem, an independent public-health consultant based in Yaoundé, Cameroon.

#324. Don't miss: Meteor showers, fireballs, and a supermoon light up November's night sky

📅 06 Nov 2026

Don't miss: Meteor showers, fireballs, and a supermoon light up November's night sky

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105224547.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, november 2026 is packed with celestial events worth watching, from brilliant meteors streaking across the sky to a striking encounter between mars and jupiter. NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is also approaching an extraordinary milestone, while a dazzling supermoon will close out the month.

Berdasarkan laporan, three meteor showers offer multiple opportunities to catch shooting stars, including occasional fireballs bright enough to stand out dramatically against the night sky. Meanwhile, two of the solar system's most recognizable planets will appear unusually close together just before sunrise.

As if that weren't enough, humanity's most distant spacecraft is reaching a point where radio signals from Earth take an entire day to arrive.

Here's what NASA recommends watching for in November.

Three Meteor Showers Could Light Up November's Sky.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, november gives skywatchers several chances to see meteors flash across the darkness. The first opportunities come from the Southern and Northern Taurids, two related meteor showers that reach their highest activity levels about a week apart.

Diungkapkan bahwa the southern taurids peak around november 5, followed by the northern taurids around november 12. Both showers get their names from the constellation Taurus, where their meteors appear to originate when viewed from Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, neither shower is especially prolific. Even under excellent conditions, each typically produces only about five meteors per hour. However, the Taurids are known for occasionally producing impressive fireballs, exceptionally bright meteors that can make even a relatively quiet night of skywatching memorable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the leonids provide another opportunity later in the month. Their best viewing periods are expected during the early morning hours of November 17 and 18, particularly after the Moon has disappeared below the horizon. Under ideal conditions, observers could see approximately 15 meteors per hour, although actual counts will generally be lower.

Berdasarkan laporan, for the best chance of spotting meteors, travel somewhere away from bright city lights. Allow your eyes roughly 30 minutes to become accustomed to the darkness, then watch a broad section of the sky rather than concentrating on one small area.

Mars and Jupiter Appear Almost Side by Side.

Sebagaimana diketahui, meteor showers aren't the only reason to get outside before dawn. On November 15 and 16, Mars and Jupiter will create an eye-catching pairing in the southeastern sky.

Diungkapkan bahwa the two planets will appear separated by only about 1. 2 degrees, slightly more than the apparent width of two full Moons placed next to each other.

Diungkapkan bahwa jupiter will be the brighter of the two, making it relatively easy to identify. Nearby, Mars will stand out with its characteristic reddish appearance.

Diungkapkan bahwa no telescope or binoculars will be necessary to enjoy the sight. Both planets should be readily visible to the unaided eye under suitable viewing conditions.

Diungkapkan bahwa although they will appear remarkably close from earth's perspective, mars and jupiter remain separated by enormous distances in space. Their apparent proximity is simply a result of their positions along our line of sight.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, watching the planets over several consecutive mornings will reveal another interesting feature of their motion. They will gradually appear to move closer together before their positions shift and they begin separating again.

Voyager 1 Reaches an Extraordinary Deep Space Milestone.

While November offers plenty to observe in Earth's skies, something equally remarkable is happening far beyond the planets.

NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is reaching a historic distance of one light-day from Earth, becoming the first human-made object ever to travel that far from our planet.

Diungkapkan bahwa a light-day is the distance light travels through space in 24 hours. Because radio signals move at the speed of light, a message transmitted from Earth will require an entire day to reach Voyager 1 at that distance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if the spacecraft sends a response immediately, the return signal will take another 24 hours to arrive. That means even the fastest possible round-trip communication will require approximately 48 hours.

The milestone illustrates just how far Voyager 1 has traveled since leaving Earth and how challenging it has become to communicate with a spacecraft exploring such distant regions of space.

Diungkapkan bahwa to get a sense of the spacecraft's current direction, look toward the constellation ophiuchus, also known as the serpent bearer. Voyager 1 is traveling through space in that general direction, far beyond anything visible to the unaided eye.

NASA is marking the achievement on November 17 with its Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day activation, inviting people to celebrate this extraordinary accomplishment in space exploration.

November's Supermoon Begins a Three-Month Celestial Show.

The final major skywatching highlight arrives on November 24, when a full supermoon will rise into the evening sky.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a supermoon occurs when a full moon coincides with a period when the moon is relatively close to earth in its orbit. Because the Moon follows a slightly elliptical path rather than a perfect circle, its distance from our planet changes throughout the month.

Diungkapkan bahwa when a full moon occurs near the closer portion of that orbit, it can appear somewhat larger and brighter than an average full moon. Although the difference is real, it is often subtle enough that casual observers may not immediately notice it.

Diungkapkan bahwa november's event is particularly noteworthy because it begins a sequence of three consecutive supermoons. Another will follow in December, with a third arriving in January.

For an especially memorable view, NASA recommends looking toward the eastern horizon around sunset on November 24, when the full Moon will be rising.

Diungkapkan bahwa the moon may seem unusually enormous when it first appears near the horizon. However, much of that dramatic impression comes from a familiar visual phenomenon called the Moon illusion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this optical effect makes the moon appear larger when it is close to the horizon than when it is high overhead, even though its actual apparent size changes very little. The illusion can occur during any full Moon, not just a supermoon.

With three meteor showers, a close planetary pairing, a historic Voyager 1 milestone, and the beginning of a supermoon series, November offers plenty of reasons to look up and explore the night sky.
