Sebagaimana diketahui, fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on nov. 21.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound.

Berdasarkan laporan, fast radio bursts, or frbs, are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, despite their power, frbs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space. That changed with CHIME (the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) in British Columbia. With a very wide field of view and a supercomputer to process its data, CHIME more than quadrupled the number of known FRBs in its first year of operation alone. Catching one takes luck, as a telescope has to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right moment. Between 2018 and 2023, CHIME recorded 4,539 bursts from 3,641 sources.

Berdasarkan laporan, as pulses of radio waves, our eyes haven't evolved to see frbs, nor can we hear them as they aren't sound waves. "Artist and composer Andrew Melchior turned all of the CHIME bursts into sound for "The Logos," an installation that has played daily at Oulu Cathedral in Finland since early April and is scheduled to run through the end of the year. Well, not until now. Melchior and Kiyoshi Masui, an associate professor of physics at MIT, "sonified" the bursts, translating data into acoustics so that human ears can hear them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the structure of each real signal is mapped to varying musical pitches and played through 12 loudspeakers spread throughout the cathedral. The result is a range of tones, with distant FRBs humming, rumbling, popping, and whistling.

Berdasarkan laporan, the signals are old by any human measure. According to a description on Melchior's website, the youngest in the work are about 50 million years old, and the oldest are about 8 to 9 billion years old.

Sebagaimana diketahui, physics also plays a role in what is heard. Each burst arrives with its high frequencies first and sweeps downward, stretched by its journey through intergalactic gas, "and you can hear that dispersion as it falls from the dome," Melchior told Space. com by email.

Diungkapkan bahwa since their discovery in 2007, the bursts are also still yielding discoveries. Last month, astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope pinpointed the host galaxy of the most distant FRB yet, one that went off when the universe was only about 3 billion years old. The galaxy, a small, young, star-forming dwarf, was far smaller than expected. That makes it harder to square with the theory that FRBs come from merging neutron stars, researchers say, which would take billions of years to occur.

This fits better with a second theory, in which a young, highly magnetic neutron star called a magnetar produces the burst soon after a massive star explodes, according to NASA.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, back on earth, an upcoming event at oulu cathedral offers a more immediate encounter with the bursts. On Nov. 21, 30 singers will stand among the audience and "sing back to the sky in Finnish" while Melchior plays the bursts live from a keyboard, he told Space. com by email.

"The fast flashes will echo as snare-like beats bouncing through the cathedral," Masui said in a previous MIT statement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it should feel rich and layered, while also revealing something real about how these signals travel across billions of years of cosmic space before reaching earth. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, sharmila kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in bengaluru, india. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston.

#328. Apple’s HomeView Tries Face Authentication Without FaceID

📅 12 Nov 2026

Apple’s HomeView Tries Face Authentication Without FaceID

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/apples-homeview-tries-face-authentication-without-faceid/

Berdasarkan laporan, apple’s homeview, which debuts on friday, is a smart home device—think of it as a an iphone-apple watch hybrid sitting on your counter—that can be personalized for up to six people and connected to each of their icloud accounts. Using ambient face and voice data, it is designed to seamlessly switch between users while maintaining each of their privacy. The feature doesn’t rely on one of Apple’s battle-tested biometric locks, like FaceID or TouchID, though. You can ask HomeView about your schedule for the day and what movie your friend recommended in a text, but you’ll be stopped from asking about your roommate’s travel plans or her texts from last night. Instead, it uses new “person recognition” technology built off of an Apple architecture for securing sensor data.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is a key departure for apple. On the one hand, the company has still been very careful to think about security and privacy comprehensively. Not only does HomeView check for your face and voice before accessing your data from iCloud, it is also designed like an Apple Watch to check that your iPhone or iPad is on the same Wi-Fi network as the HomeView and has been recently unlocked (with FaceID or a PIN). On the other hand, expanding the architecture used to process biometric data and authenticate users creates more opportunities for mistakes and potential vulnerabilities. And when it comes to attempting to access users’ Apple data, both law enforcement and exploit brokers consistently go to great lengths to attempt to break the company’s on-device defenses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, faceid is built for the use case where a person is staring at their device head-on from less than an arm’s length away. The architecture is so robust that Apple also relies on the Secure Enclave as the foundation of a device’s entire encryption scheme. It provides reliable security that’s difficult to defeat because it stores your biometric data on a special, physically isolated chip known as the Secure Enclave—first introduced in 2013 for the iPhone 5s. But Apple concluded that FaceID wasn’t the best fit for the HomeView, because it needs to bounce quickly between users and relies on AI processing, which can’t all be squeezed into the Secure Enclave.

Diungkapkan bahwa as a result, homeview uses apple’s recently announced secure exclave (note the “x”) to handle the video and audio data the device uses to evaluate who is in a room at a given time. Instead of being an entirely separately chip, the Secure Exclave is a dedicated, memory-protected space in recent Apple processors. Apple says it has actually been laying the groundwork for the Secure Exclave for a long time—early versions of the architecture were already in place for the iPhone 16 and 17 and MacBook Neo. It is in Apple’s latest S11 chip for Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, as well as the A20 Pro chip for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.

Diungkapkan bahwa even though the secure exclave isn’t based on the tried and true secure enclave technology, apple argues that it is robust and expands the company’s ability to secure a range of features, including improving the security of existing mechanisms. In a blog post on Thursday, the company even goes into some detail about how it used the mathematical technique known as formal verification to vet the “microkernel” designed for the Secure Exclave.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “this work both benefits our newest features and strengthens the security of features we already ship, such as ‘hey siri’ detection,” the company writes in a blog post. “Our goal is to keep ambient sensor data secure even against highly sophisticated attacks. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, homeview also uses the secure exclave to govern the indicator light that tells users when their camera or microphone is active. The MacBook Neo uses the Exclave in this same way, though only to indicate when the camera is active, not the microphone. The goal is to isolate this process and the chain of command governing it to make it even more difficult for attackers to try to disable an indicator light when it should be on or stop it from coming on in the first place.

The HomeView’s “person recognition” technology is simply not as comprehensive as FaceID, though, and it is possible that the technology is more susceptible to reconstructed 3D depth map attacks—and potentially voiceprint attacks—than FaceID.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, of course, you don’t have to have a homeview in your house. Or if you do, you can use it on guest mode or a less involved “personalized” mode that only incorporates things like your playlists for other users to access as well and doesn’t access calendar or Messages data. But as Apple forges deeper into AI integration, HomeView’s departure from FaceID provides insight into the scale of the changes Apple is planning.

#329. NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space

📅 06 Nov 2026

NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105224545.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, nasa's neil gehrels swift observatory has returned to earth after spending nearly 22 years in space, bringing an extraordinary era of astronomical discovery to a close. The spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere on Wednesday, ending a mission that lasted more than ten times longer than originally planned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, launched in 2004, swift was a pioneering space observatory equipped with three telescopes designed to study some of the most powerful explosions in the universe. Its instruments could detect different types of light, allowing scientists to investigate energetic cosmic events that would be difficult to understand using a single telescope.

NASA's Swift Observatory Re-Enters Earth's Atmosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the u. 4 degrees north latitude and 98. The reported location was approximately 3. S. EST on Wednesday above North Sumatra, Indonesia. Space Force confirmed that Swift entered the atmosphere at 7:39 a. m. 6 degrees east longitude.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nasa anticipated that most of the spacecraft would burn up as it plunged through the atmosphere. However, officials acknowledged that some components might have survived the intense heat of re-entry.

A Two-Year NASA Mission That Lasted Nearly 22 Years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, swift was originally developed to investigate gamma-ray bursts, extraordinarily powerful flashes of high-energy radiation associated with some of the most extreme events in the cosmos. These bursts can occur when massive stars collapse or when certain compact objects, such as neutron stars, merge.

Although NASA initially planned for Swift to operate for just two years, the observatory continued making scientific contributions for more than two decades.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of its most important capabilities was its ability to respond quickly to sudden cosmic events. When Swift detected an energetic outburst, it could rapidly redirect its telescopes toward the source and notify observatories around the world. This coordinated approach allowed astronomers to study brief astronomical phenomena before they faded from view.

Swift also observed multiple wavelengths of light, giving researchers different ways to examine the same event and better understand the physical processes behind it.

Over its remarkably long lifetime, Swift's scientific contributions expanded far beyond its original focus on gamma-ray bursts.

The observatory helped astronomers investigate active galaxies powered by supermassive black holes, stars that produce powerful X-ray flares, and supernovae, the enormous explosions that mark the deaths of certain stars.

Its observations also extended much closer to home, including studies of comets and asteroids within our own solar system.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by combining rapid observations with the ability to detect different forms of radiation, swift became a valuable tool for exploring both distant cosmic explosions and nearby objects. Its re-entry marks the end of a mission that greatly exceeded its planned lifespan and helped transform scientists' understanding of some of the universe's most energetic phenomena.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, gemini 12 was the last mission of the gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin. NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks.

Berdasarkan laporan, before gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the astronauts returned to earth after four days in space. Both Aldrin and Lovell went on to join the Apollo program. Aldrin became the second person to walk on the moon during Apollo 11, and Lovell became the commander of Apollo 13.

Gemini 12 may have closed out NASA's Gemini program of two-person space missions, but it established the mission also established the fundamentals of spacewalking that Apollo astronauts would use when they walked on the moon.

Berdasarkan laporan, it's fitting that aldrin was the primary spacewalker of the mission. Diungkapkan bahwa during his spacewalks, aldrin installed handrails, used foot restraints and other tools that have since become routine on spacewalks in orbit. They also tested tools and techniques that Aldrin and other moonwalks would use on the moon.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gemini 12 also tested a computer-controlled reentry technique when it returned to earth on nov. 15, landing Lovell and Aldrin just 3 miles from their target near their recovery ship the USS Wasp in the Atlantic Ocean, about 600 miles east of Cape Canaveral.

Berdasarkan laporan, the board’s investigation was announced on november 8, slightly less than two weeks after the new york times reported that the chief executive had been the target of a chinese intelligence operation facilitated through his relationship with alice huang, who has no known relation to jensen. The pair have been spotted in public together at least twice, in June 2024 and May 2025. On November 11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also allegedly had a relationship with a direct report at Nvidia.

The alleged relationship with a subordinate, along with Huang’s business dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company where Alice Huang previously held a senior position, likely played a greater role in the board’s decision to oust Huang than the Chinese espionage allegations, a source familiar with the matter tells WIRED.

Sebagaimana diketahui, us intelligence officials reportedly briefed president donald trump on huang’s relationship with alice last year, but the president did not act on it. (The Chinese government has rejected all claims that Alice was a spy for the country. On November 6, The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Alice was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security and that she had been recruited to collect information on the Nvidia executive. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, huang sent a companywide email on sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation. The executive has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, since 1985, and both of the couple’s two children work at the company.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on monday, wired exclusively reported that last year huang began working with a crisis pr firm to manage his personal communications. In October 2025, those PR consultants started to be looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang, whether those inquiries were personal or professional in nature.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the timing lines up with a new york times report that month that the us commerce department was investigating whether alice huang’s megaspeed was helping chinese companies get around american export controls with the help of a vast web of subsidiaries. The investigation was reportedly halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter inquired about it.

Berdasarkan laporan, huang has been a vocal critic of these export controls, which he argues unnecessarily constrain the market for american chips, create discrete chinese and american tech ecosystems, and spur china to build competitive chips of its own. Huang has worked to develop a relationship with Trump in order to advocate for policies that are advantageous for Nvidia, including the idea of opening its markets to China.

Diungkapkan bahwa huang cofounded nvidia in 1993 with friends chris malachowsky and curtis priem. The trio reportedly brainstormed their vision for the company in a Denny’s diner and aspired to bring realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For the first few decades of its existence, Nvidia was primarily known in the gaming community for creating chips powerful enough to render high-quality in-game graphics.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2012, after a new kind of neural network known as alexnet won a high-profile prize in computer vision, nvidia pivoted from high-speed computer graphics to building chips that would support artificial intelligence. Huang has repeatedly said that the introduction of AlexNet, which was developed by AI engineers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, was a “Big Bang”–like event for computing.

Berdasarkan laporan, because its new gpus proved highly effective at powering ai models that require massive amounts of processing power, the value of nvidia shares soared in 2023 and 2024, in lockstep with the broader ai boom that began sweeping through the world economy. In the summer of 2025, Nvidia became the first company in history to cross $4 trillion in value.

Diungkapkan bahwa as of september 2026, the company controlled about 90 percent of the gpu market. Much of Nvidia’s epic rise over the few decades has been attributed not just to its cutting-edge chips and its software “moat,” CUDA, that keeps developers locked into those chips, but also to the fast-thinking, controlling, charismatic, and often bombastic leadership style of Huang himself. Now, that critical part of the company’s success is out.

How would the crew of the Wild Blue Yonder fare on a real exoplanet?.

Berdasarkan laporan, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Berdasarkan laporan, imagine you’ve crash-landed on an alien planet. Your ship is destroyed, your oxygen supply is dangerously low, and the landscape around you is completely unknown. Where would you begin looking for clues to your survival? Surprisingly, the best place to start could be the star overhead.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is the predicament that three crew members of the wild blue yonder face in audible’s new sci-fi thriller, "exoplanet. " This sci-fi thriller is written by acclaimed comic writer Benjamin Percy, executive produced by Andy Weir (Project Hail Mary, The Martian), and features an all-star voice cast including Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, stranded on an unfamiliar planet, they encounter volcanic wastelands, unknown skies, and environments that seem to defy reason. But behind the extraordinary events of this audio drama is a very real scientific question: what makes a planet habitable?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in “exoplanet”, the crew view skies that are not only unfamiliar but also seemingly different from one another. One character sees a sun as so dim that he can look directly at it, while another suffers under a blazing heat, surrounded by stretches of sun-scorched red rock.

For astronomers, the light emitted by a star is one of the most crucial tools for understanding planets orbiting it.

Berdasarkan laporan, using a technique called spectroscopy, astronomers split starlight into its constituent wavelengths, producing a spectrum much like a rainbow. By studying this spectrum, they can investigate the temperature, composition, and other physical properties of the star.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, stellar temperature is only part of the picture. The amount of energy a planet receives depends on both the luminosity of the star and its orbital distance.

Astronomers use these measurements to determine whether a world lies in the habitable zone of a star, where temperatures could allow liquid water to exist on the surface given a suitable atmosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a planet orbiting a cool red dwarf would need to be much closer to its star than earth is to the sun to be in this habitable zone. Unfortunately, being in this zone is no guarantee of a planetary paradise.

Diungkapkan bahwa a planet that sits comfortably in the habitable zone is ultimately still at the mercy of its star. Stars emit more than just the light we see. Ultraviolet radiation and X-rays can interact with planetary atmospheres, altering chemistry and even contributing to the loss of the atmosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, violent stellar flares can produce bursts of high-energy radiation. A planet could offer a wonderfully balmy temperature, only to be bombarded with radiation from the host star.

Diungkapkan bahwa the age of a star matters too. Young stars tend to be more active, with radiation that could erode a planet’s atmosphere over time. Meanwhile, as stars age and evolve, their changing luminosities can drastically alter the conditions a planet experiences.

For the stranded crew in “Exoplanet”, understanding the star overhead may therefore be as important as knowing the landscape beneath their feet.

Even if a planet has survived all the complications we’ve just thrown at it, there’s still a rather important question: could we actually breathe the air?.

Berdasarkan laporan, in "exoplanet", one crew member discovers that the planet’s atmosphere contains enough oxygen for him to breathe without his spacesuit. On Earth, oxygen makes up around 21% of our atmosphere. However, finding a similar percentage on another planet wouldn’t automatically mean the air is safe to breathe.

Diungkapkan bahwa atmospheric pressure matters just as much. At high altitudes on Earth, the oxygen percentage remains the same, but the lower pressure means less oxygen is available to our lungs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, oxygen isn’t the only concern, either. The fictional planet’s volcanic landscape releases gases such as sulfur dioxide and hydrogen sulfide, both of which are hazardous at high concentrations. Even an oxygen-rich atmosphere could still be lethal.

But what if you don't just need to know if a planet is habitable? What if you need to know if something already lives there?.

Berdasarkan laporan, before the wild blue yonder arrived at the planet, probes detected dimethyl sulfide, a molecule we associate with biological activity on earth. This is a beautifully timely detail, as this very molecule has been at the heart of a scientific debate about one of the most intriguing exoplanets discovered so far.

Berdasarkan laporan, astronomers have investigated possible signs of dimethyl sulfide in the atmosphere of k2-18 b, an exoplanet orbiting a red dwarf. However, both the detection itself and the biological interpretation remain heavily disputed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the challenge is that detecting a single molecule isn’t definitive evidence of life. Its presence can be influenced by factors other than biology, like atmospheric chemistry and stellar radiation.

Understanding whether such a molecule could actually indicate life means studying not just the planet’s atmosphere, but also the radiation it receives from its star.

Sebagaimana diketahui, astronomers have discovered thousands of exoplanets. Understanding whether any could support life is, however, an extraordinary challenge.

Diungkapkan bahwa the distance between the planet and the star might give us a good clue, but its atmosphere, geology, and stellar environment are all interconnected in determining whether life could survive. For the unfortunate crew of the Wild Blue Yonder, those distinctions could mean the difference between survival and utter disaster.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we might one day identify a planet with earth-like temperatures, liquid water, and abundant oxygen. But even then, there’s still a huge gap dividing a potentially habitable planet from one where we could safely remove our helmets.

Berdasarkan laporan, "exoplanet" is available now exclusively from audible. It is free for members of its subscription tiers or available to purchase separately.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one crew. Three timelines. One planet. No one survives alone. A sci-fi thriller executive produced by Andy Weir (#1 bestselling author of Project Hail Mary, The Martian), with an all-star cast led by Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose and John Leguizamo.

Exoplanet is free for Audible members, but also available for purchase separately.

Sebagaimana diketahui, alix is an astrophysicist at the university of birmingham specialising in the characterisation of stars and exoplanets. She is passionate about science communication, and how astrophysics is portrayed in movies, TV, and pop culture at large.

#335. Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years

📅 06 Nov 2026

Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105224542.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, scientists have discovered remarkably preserved traces of dinosaur blood inside 115-million-year-old bones, revealing that delicate biological molecules can survive far longer than previously believed. The breakthrough could transform how researchers study prehistoric animals and even influence the search for ancient life beyond Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an international team led by curtin university found fossilized red blood cells and chemical evidence of blood molecules in the remains of aratasaurus museunacionali, a meat-eating theropod dinosaur discovered in northeastern brazil. The findings, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, also include amino acids associated with collagen, an important structural protein found in bones and other connective tissues.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the discovery provides the first definitive chemical confirmation of molecules derived from hemoglobin inside fossilized dinosaur red blood cells. Earlier research had identified structures resembling blood cells in ancient fossils, but scientists had not conclusively demonstrated the presence of these particular molecular remains within them.

Ancient Dinosaur Blood Preserved Inside Fossilized Bones.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when researchers examined the dinosaur's limb bones, they identified numerous mineralized red blood cells inside vascular canals, the tiny passages that once contained blood vessels. Chemical analysis revealed preserved heme molecules, which are components of hemoglobin, the protein that allows red blood cells to transport oxygen.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finding these molecules provided direct chemical evidence that the fossil contained remnants of ancient blood. It also demonstrated that some biological materials once thought too fragile to survive for millions of years can remain detectable under exceptional conditions.

The study was led by John Curtin Distinguished Professor Kliti Grice, founding director of Curtin University's WA-Organic and Isotope Geochemistry Centre and an Australian Research Council Laureate Fellow.

"To detect intact heme-derived molecules in 115-million-year-old red blood cells is astonishing: this really is a landmark discovery," Professor Grice said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it not only extends the known fossil record of blood, but also offers a direct molecular window into the physiology of long-extinct animals so we may better understand them and the world they lived in. ".

How Dinosaur Blood Survived 115 Million Years.

Diungkapkan bahwa the extraordinary preservation appears to be connected to a mineral called hausmannite. This mineral helped stabilize the fossilized blood cells and preserve their molecular components (including amino acids of collagen) over an immense span of geological time.

In effect, the mineral created a natural time capsule that protected microscopic evidence of the dinosaur's biology long after its death.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, researchers believe the conditions surrounding the dinosaur's burial were also crucial. They suspect the animal was quickly covered by sediment in an environment with little oxygen and abundant microbial activity. These conditions may have helped preserve biological material that would ordinarily have broken down and disappeared.

The international research effort brought together scientists from Curtin University's School of Earth and Planetary Sciences, the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology, the Brazilian National Museum, the Regional University of Cariri, and Johns Hopkins University.

A Discovery That Challenges Fossil Preservation Limits.

The findings challenge a longstanding assumption in paleontology that molecules associated with blood, particularly those derived from hemoglobin, could not remain preserved across such enormous periods of time.

Beyond confirming the survival of ancient blood components, the discovery raises the possibility that other fossils may contain molecular information that conventional examinations have overlooked.

"These findings challenge longstanding assumptions that certain biomolecules such as hemoglobin cannot survive deep time," Professor Grice said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it opens exciting new avenues for molecular-level paleontology, allowing us to investigate the evolution of blood, metabolism and even activity levels in ancient animals. ".

Such information could eventually help researchers better understand how extinct animals functioned, including aspects of their metabolism and physiology that are difficult to reconstruct from bones alone.

Implications for Ancient Life Beyond Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the significance of the discovery may extend well beyond dinosaurs. Understanding how fragile biological structures can survive for millions of years could also help scientists identify possible traces of ancient life in other extreme environments, including those beyond Earth.

Professor Martin Van Kranendonk, head of Curtin University's School of Earth and Planetary Sciences, said the results are changing how researchers understand the preservation of molecular structures over vast timescales and under harsh conditions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these insights could be valuable to astrobiology, a field that investigates the possibility of life elsewhere in the universe. If biological molecules or their chemical signatures can persist under the right conditions for more than 100 million years, scientists may need to reconsider where and how they look for evidence of ancient organisms.

"This study exemplifies how coordinated efforts across institutions, continents and scientific disciplines can unlock extraordinary insights into ancient life," Professor Van Kranendonk said.

The research was supported by a 2021 Australian Research Council Laureate Fellowship awarded to Professor Grice.

The study, titled "Heme signatures in mineralized red blood cells within vascular canals of a 115- million-year-old dinosaur bone," was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

With comets out of the picture, attention now turns to asteroids or even Earth itself as the source of prebiotic chemistry.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the origin of life on earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet.

Diungkapkan bahwa life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth.

Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?.

New research led by planetary scientist Richard Anslow of the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Cambridge has now seemingly ruled out comets as the origin of complex organic molecules on Earth.

"Historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on Earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get-out-of-jail-free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said Anslow in a statement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, comet impacts on earth were much more frequent in the first half-billion years of the solar system’s existence, when there were still lots of debris leftover from the formation of the planets. For over a century comet impacts had been considered a prime suspect in the search for what brought the building blocks of life to Earth. However, while comets bringing the building blocks of life to Earth is "kind of a romantic idea," according to Anslow, the University of Cambridge researcher added that the team's results suggest that is highly unlikely.

Anslow and colleagues arrived at this conclusion based upon computer modeling by using the very latest simulations depicting the origin and evolution of comets and their orbits, their interactions with Earth's atmosphere as they enter it, and of the hypervelocity comet impacts themselves.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in particular, they used the fate of hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for what happens to complex organic molecules in comet impacts. Hydrogen cyanide is frequently found in comets and was even detected in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the problem is that comets are generally moving at too great a velocity. Anslow and his colleagues found that, in general, comets travel too fast and enter Earth’s atmosphere at too sharp an angle for complex organic molecules to survive. For organic molecules to survive impact, the impact velocity would have to be below 33,500 miles per hour (15 kilometers per second). Instead, they are mostly vaporized on impact. Even on the rare occasions that the complex organic molecules survived, they were usually not in great enough abundance to provide any meaningful prebiotic chemistry.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it would really have to be a one-in-a-million occurrence, because not only would you need an impact at just the right speed and just the right angle, you would also need everything to happen after that point, in terms of the concentration and the speed at which the chemical origins of life got going," said anslow. "We can’t rule out for certain that it happened that way, but it seems to be a really rare occurrence – at best, a one-off fluke. ".

It is not yet known if the origin of life on Earth was a fluke, or whether life is plentiful in the universe, so a fluke occurrence could still have been a trigger for life on our planet.

However, researchers are coming around to alternatives, either that all the pre-biotic chemistry that resulted in life took place on Earth without requiring material from space, or asteroids instead brought those important molecules to Earth.

Scientists have found asteroids to be rich in those molecules – for example, the sample of material brought back by the OSIRIS-REx mission from the near-Earth asteroid Bennu contained all the building blocks of RNA.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, other planets could have plausibly benefitted from comet impacts. "This is not to say it definitely happened on Mars, of course, but it suggests it would be unlikely if it happened on Earth and didn’t happen on Mars," said Anslow. The simulations showed that complex organic molecules in comets would stand a slightly better chance of surviving impacts on Mars, because of the Red Planet’s thinner atmosphere and lower gravity. "Or the other, perhaps more likely, alternative is that it didn’t happen on either planet. ".

More intriguing are the possibilities on exoplanets, specifically the peas-in-a-pod multi-planet systems around red dwarf stars such as TRAPPIST-1, where all the planets are bunched up close.

In 2023 Anslow wrote a research paper describing how comets could gravitationally bounce from one planet to the next, losing velocity in the process so that when they crash into one of the planets, they impact is not so severe and complex organic molecules might have a chance to survive.

The team's research was published on 28 October in Scientific Reports.

He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.

#340. A quantum breakthrough makes light behave like both a solid and a liquid

📅 09 Nov 2026

A quantum breakthrough makes light behave like both a solid and a liquid

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105224536.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa scientists have demonstrated an extraordinary form of quantum matter that combines two properties that seem incompatible. Known as a supersolid, this unusual state has the orderly structure of a crystal while also displaying the frictionless flow associated with a special kind of liquid. Even more remarkably, researchers have now observed this behavior at room temperature, eliminating the need for the extreme cooling traditionally used to investigate such phenomena.

Berdasarkan laporan, the breakthrough was achieved by an international team from the faculty of physics at the university of warsaw, the military university of technology (poland), ibm research zurich, and the french national centre for scientific research (cnrs). Rather than relying on atoms cooled to temperatures near absolute zero, the scientists created a supersolid using particles that combine properties of light and matter.

Diungkapkan bahwa published in science advances, the findings introduce a new way to investigate exotic quantum behavior under much more accessible conditions. They could also help advance future technologies ranging from optical computing to highly sensitive sensors.

How Can Matter Behave Like Both a Solid and a Liquid?.

Berdasarkan laporan, under ordinary circumstances, solids and liquids behave very differently. Crystals have an organized internal structure, with their particles arranged in repeating patterns. Liquids, by comparison, can flow and change shape.

Quantum physics, however, allows matter to behave in ways that would be impossible under the familiar rules of everyday life.

Diungkapkan bahwa one example is superfluidity, a remarkable phenomenon in which a fluid loses its viscosity, or internal resistance to flowing. Imagine placing an oar into such a liquid. You would encounter almost no resistance until the oar reached a certain speed. A superfluid can move through extremely narrow passages without experiencing the usual friction. Beyond that threshold, tiny swirling structures known as quantum vortices would suddenly form.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during the 1960s, physicists proposed an even stranger possibility. What if a superfluid could also develop the repeating internal structure normally associated with a crystal?.

Diungkapkan bahwa this hypothetical combination became known as a supersolid. In such a state, the material exhibits the spatial organization of a solid while retaining the remarkable flow properties of a superfluid.

Berdasarkan laporan, for decades, supersolidity remained a theoretical concept. Experimental confirmation finally arrived in 2017, when researchers observed the phenomenon in ultracold atomic Bose-Einstein condensates. These condensates form when particles enter a collective quantum state and begin behaving as a coordinated system rather than as separate individuals.

The catch was that producing these conditions generally required sophisticated equipment capable of cooling matter to temperatures extremely close to absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature.

Creating a Quantum Supersolid Using Light Instead of Cold Atoms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the international topolight consortium approached the challenge from a different direction. Instead of using ultracold atoms, the researchers worked with unusual hybrid particles called exciton polaritons.

Berdasarkan laporan, these quasiparticles arise when light interacts so strongly with matter that the two become coupled inside a tiny optical chamber called a microcavity. The resulting particles display characteristics of both light and matter.

Diungkapkan bahwa exciton polaritons are extremely short-lived, typically surviving for only a few picoseconds. A picosecond is one trillionth of a second. Despite their brief existence, these particles can organize into a Bose-Einstein condensate and collectively exhibit the behavior of a quantum superfluid.

Diungkapkan bahwa to create the necessary conditions, the team constructed an optical microcavity containing a specially engineered liquid crystal and covered it with an organic semiconductor. The arrangement allowed light and matter to interact strongly enough to produce the desired quantum effects without the need for extreme cooling.

"Our liquid-crystal microcavities can operate even at temperatures approaching 60°C," says Professor Wiktor Piecek from the Military University of Technology, whose group developed the liquid-crystal structures.

That temperature is approximately 140°F, far above the freezing conditions normally associated with experiments involving exotic quantum matter.

Strange Patterns of Light Reveal a Supersolid.

How can researchers determine whether a collection of particles has entered such an unusual state?.

Diungkapkan bahwa in this experiment, the evidence appeared in the light emitted by the sample. When the system transitioned into the supersolid phase, researchers observed a series of regularly spaced bright fringes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these patterns indicated that the particle condensate had spontaneously developed a repeating variation in its density. This type of spatial organization is a defining feature of crystalline structures and an important sign of supersolidity.

But the researchers noticed another intriguing effect.

Berdasarkan laporan, each time a laser pulse excited the sample, the bright fringes appeared in a different position. Rather than following a single fixed arrangement, the quantum system repeatedly selected among several equally possible configurations.

Diungkapkan bahwa "this is a textbook example of spontaneous symmetry breaking," explains professor guillaume malpuech from institut pascal (cnrs). "Theory predicted that the supersolid could choose among several equivalent states, and that is exactly what we observed. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs when a system that could exist in several equivalent arrangements settles into one particular configuration. In this case, the effect became visible through the changing positions of the light patterns.

Diungkapkan bahwa the condensate also displayed another unusual characteristic called a persistent spin helix. This refers to a repeating variation in the polarization of the emitted light. Polarization describes the orientation of light's oscillating electric field.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, together, these observations revealed two different forms of order occurring at the same time. One appeared in the intensity of the emitted light, while the other appeared in its polarization.

A Difficult Experiment With Only Hours to Succeed.

Achieving these results required overcoming an unexpected practical obstacle.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the organic semiconductor used in the device gradually reacted with the liquid crystal. As a result, the experimental samples had a limited useful lifetime, giving the scientists only a few hours to collect their measurements after assembly.

Diungkapkan bahwa this restriction made careful preparation essential. The researchers needed to determine exactly which measurements to perform and in what order before beginning each experimental run.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we had to plan the entire sequence of experiments in advance," recalls dr. "Repeating a measurement meant fabricating an entirely new sample. Marcin Muszyński, the paper's first author, now a postdoctoral researcher at The City College of New York. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the most important measurements took place at ibm research zurich. There, scientists deposited thin layers of the organic semiconductor onto specialized structures designed to manipulate light. These photonic structures had been manufactured at the Military University of Technology.

Berdasarkan laporan, the semiconductor itself was not new to the researchers. IBM scientists had investigated its quantum properties for years, including its ability to support Bose-Einstein condensation.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we have studied the organic semiconductor melppp (methyl-substituted ladder-type poly(paraphenylene) for many years and previously observed bose-einstein condensation in this material," says thilo stöferle from ibm research. "This was the first time we combined it with a liquid-crystal microcavity. ".

Bringing these materials together ultimately made it possible to observe the unusual supersolid behavior at room temperature.

Why Room Temperature Quantum Matter Matters.

The significance of the discovery extends beyond demonstrating another unusual phenomenon predicted by quantum physics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many experiments involving exotic quantum states depend on costly cryogenic systems designed to maintain temperatures close to absolute zero. These demanding conditions make research more complicated and can create substantial obstacles when scientists attempt to turn laboratory discoveries into useful technologies.

The new results show that certain exotic quantum effects can instead be investigated in photonic devices that operate at ordinary temperatures.

Diungkapkan bahwa this could create opportunities for future technologies that use light to process information. Potential applications include ultrafast photonic devices, specialized computing accelerators inspired by the way biological brains process information, and advanced optical sensors.

Diungkapkan bahwa the computing approach, known as neuromorphic computing, seeks to imitate aspects of the brain's information processing to perform certain tasks more efficiently. Light-based systems could eventually provide new ways to accelerate these operations.

The supersolid's exceptional sensitivity to light polarization may also prove useful for developing sensors capable of detecting extremely subtle optical changes.

These applications remain possibilities for future research, but the ability to generate the underlying quantum behavior without extreme cooling represents an important step toward making such technologies more practical.

Electrically Controlled Quantum Matter Opens New Possibilities.

One of the most promising features of the experiment is that the optical device can be adjusted using electricity.

Berdasarkan laporan, the liquid crystal microcavities provide the first electrically tunable platform for studying supersolid exciton-polariton condensates. This means researchers can alter the optical properties of the system by applying an external voltage.

Earlier experimental approaches did not offer this same degree of electrical control.

The ability to adjust the system dynamically gives physicists greater flexibility when investigating how quantum states emerge, interact, and respond to changing conditions.

It could also become valuable when designing practical quantum photonic devices, where precise control over the behavior of light and matter is essential.

By combining room-temperature operation with electrical tunability, the researchers have established a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena that previously required far more demanding experimental conditions.

About the University of Warsaw Faculty of Physics.

Berdasarkan laporan, the university of warsaw has a long history of research and education in physics and astronomy. Both disciplines became part of the university in 1816, when they were included in the Faculty of Philosophy. The university subsequently established its Astronomical Observatory in 1825.

Today, the Faculty of Physics includes the Institutes of Experimental Physics, Theoretical Physics, and Geophysics, along with the Department of Mathematical Methods in Physics.

Its research encompasses nearly every major area of modern physics, from the behavior of particles at quantum scales to the structure and evolution of the universe.

The faculty employs more than 250 academic teachers and serves approximately 1,350 students and more than 150 doctoral students.

According to Shanghai's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, the University of Warsaw ranks among the world's top 150 institutions for physics education.

#342. You Can Buy T-Shirts Glorifying Mass Shootings Almost Anywhere Online

📅 12 Nov 2026

You Can Buy T-Shirts Glorifying Mass Shootings Almost Anywhere Online

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/you-can-buy-t-shirts-glorifying-mass-shootings-almost-anywhere-online/

Berdasarkan laporan, on the day he carried out the columbine high school massacre, 18-year-old shooter eric harris wore a white t-shirt with the phrase “natural selection” printed on it in black lettering. His fellow assailant, 17-year-old Dylan Klebold, wore a black T-shirt with the word “Wrath” printed in red across the chest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ever since, this apparel has been closely linked with mass murder, part of an ever-growing mosaic of niche allusions to deadly attacks on schools, places of worship, government buildings, and social gathering spaces. While you might not think twice about a person wearing one of the shirts Harris and Klebold chose for their assault on their classmates, let alone recognize the reference, there’s an online community that revels in this aesthetic, using it as a means to valorize and motivate nihilistic violence.

According to a report publishing later this week from the Institute for Strategic Dialogue, a research organization that analyzes extremism and online threats, statement shirts associated with such horrific acts are widely available from at least half a dozen internet retailers.

Diungkapkan bahwa isd found sellers peddling “wrath” and “natural selection” tees modeled after the columbine shirts on tiktok shop, redbubble, temu, etsy, aliexpress, and walmart. Shirts with the slogan “Humanity Is Overrated”—like the one worn by a teen gunman who killed nine people at his high school in Finland in 2007—turned up on AliExpress, Temu, and the TikTok Shop, according to the report.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a statement, a representative for tiktok us said: “discriminatory and offensive products are prohibited from sale on tiktok shop and will be removed. ” A representative for Redbubble said that the marketplace prohibits “content that glorifies or trivializes violence” and that it had removed listings for “Wrath” and “Natural Selection” shirts flagged by WIRED.

A representative for Walmart said that a shirt flagged by WIRED was removed in accordance with its policies for third-party sellers.

None of the other retailers immediately replied to a request for comment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, katherine keneally, isd’s senior director of threat analysis and prevention, tells wired that these clothes are promoted by a cohort known as the true crime community, or tcc. Not to be confused with fans of podcasts and documentaries about unsolved or unusual crimes, the TCC “is a predominantly online fandom that is rooted in an obsession with mass killers, regardless of the mass killer’s motivation,” Keneally says.

Diungkapkan bahwa the tcc’s fascination with the lore around specific killers can lead to dissection of details as minor as what they had for breakfast on the morning of their attack, keneally says. But the statement shirts offer a convenient way to covertly endorse such massacres, with most people outside the in-group none the wiser.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “what we see from attackers is that they are often trying, in many ways, to mirror previous attackers, but putting their own sort of spin on it,” keneally says. The shirts are used to “signal interest and glorification of the violence, and also can serve as a sign of someone's plans to engage in something, engage in some sort of attack,” she adds. The ISD’s report cites the cases of a 13-year-old arrested in South Africa last month after allegedly stabbing a 6-year-old while wearing a “Wrath” shirt and an 18-year-old accused of fatally shooting two people in a California library in June, who was apprehended wearing a “Natural Selection” tee.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the isd analysis of the sale of shirts connected to past shootings is part of a planned series by the nonprofit covering various warning signs of future attacks. The idea is to give parents, teachers, and law enforcement more guidance in understanding when a young person may have intent to harm others, particularly because “within the TCC, we are seeing predominantly youth and minors being involved,” Keneally says.

Diungkapkan bahwa adolescents aren’t just engaging with this content in “the darker corners of the internet,” keneally says. “It's happening very openly across mainstream and fringe platforms. ” The prevalence of the clothing across an array of online shops is an indication of how the TCC’s extremist messaging flies under the radar.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, as isd revealed in its research, younger affiliates of this diffuse collective are trading tips on how to disguise the meaning of paraphernalia tied to mass shooter fandom. One screenshot in the report shows a TikTok user asking their followers, “How do y’all convince your parents to buy the natural selection shirt,” with commenters advising that they pretend “Natural Selection” is the name of a movie, a video game, or a brand. One person replied: “My parents don’t know what tcc is so i can buy it without any problems. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, tcc enthusiasts have also made it clear in their product reviews of the t-shirts that they admire perpetrators of deadly gun violence. ” A third person ominously noted that they would use their “Wrath” shirt “to become a bit more popular at school. In their five-star feedback on a “Wrath” shirt, a customer wrote “we love dylan klebold!” Another attached an anime-style cartoon of Eric Harris in the “Natural Selection” shirt on their review of same, noting that they were hiding it from their mom but that it was “so cute” and “good quality too. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, keneally acknowledges that there’s a “fine line” to consider with clothing that may suggest an unhealthy fixation on infamous killers, since even the best-known examples are not offensive or illegal in themselves. Context also matters: The TCC has an affinity for the German industrial band KMFDM because they were a favorite band of the Columbine shooters, but a fan wearing a KMFDM shirt could have no idea of the connection.

Diungkapkan bahwa while a teen’s purchase of the most flagrant tcc shirt doesn’t help them commit an attack or necessarily indicate the planning of real-world violence, keneally says, adults should weigh it against other factors. “If they have access to weapons or maybe another student has heard them talk about committing violence, then it can help serve as a warning sign and provide an opportunity for intervention,” she says. And wearing the shirt at all communicates a likely need for mental health support.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as for the retailers that facilitate the sale of this apparel, keneally believes that if they adequately enforced their established safety policies, much of it would be taken down. “It shouldn't be that easy to access. The clothes are something that youths seek out to be “a part of” the True Crime Community and fuel this toxic subculture, she says. ”.

The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rocket lab announced on monday (nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027.

Diungkapkan bahwa "launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," rocket lab founder and ceo peter beck said on monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "We saw a pent-up launch market on the horizon, and rather than provide early discounted launches, we set out to deliver a rocket into an environment with extreme demand at full price or higher. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa rocket lab is best known for electron, a workhorse small-satellite launcher that debuted in 2017 and now has 90 orbital missions under its belt. The 59-foot-tall (18 meters) expendable rocket and can haul 660 pounds (300 kilograms) to low Earth orbit (LEO).

Berdasarkan laporan, neutron is the company's entry into the medium-lift market. It features a reusable first stage, stands 141 feet (43 m) tall and can carry 14. 3 tons (13 metric tons) of payload to LEO.

Diungkapkan bahwa rocket lab announced neutron back in 2021 and first targeted a 2024 debut for the vehicle. But various problems have cropped up over the years, pushing things back. Last month, for example, Rocket Lab announced that it was delaying the first Neutron flight from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue (which it says is now under control).

Sebagaimana diketahui, such setbacks have not dampened demand for neutron's services, however. During Monday's call, Beck revealed that Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron launches during the third quarter of 2026, which ran from July 1 through Sept. 30.

Berdasarkan laporan, the contracts for those eight flights are worth "a total of roughly 515 million, including multiple missions on a new escalated base price of $70 million," beck said. Neutron's first 16 launches are now sold out, he added, and bookings from here on will be for flights in the 2030s.

"The demand is a function of both a tightening global launch supply and our customers' confidence that Rocket Lab is the right partner to break the world's launch bottleneck," Beck said.

Diungkapkan bahwa that bottleneck is coming in 2028 or so, when spacex plans to retire its falcon 9 rocket. For some perspective, and comparison with Neutron: SpaceX currently charges $74 million for each Falcon 9 launch. The rocket has a reusable first stage and can carry about 25 tons (22. 7 metric tons) to LEO.

Diungkapkan bahwa the medium lifter has been the world's most prolific rocket for the past few years. In 2025, for example, it flew 165 times — roughly the same number of orbital missions as all other launchers in the world combined. And all 165 of those flights were successful.

But SpaceX is phasing out the Falcon 9 — and its heavy-lift cousin, the Falcon Heavy — nonetheless, shifting all launch work over to its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which can haul more than 100 tons to LEO.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's a real worry among folks in the space community that this massive payload capacity won't be available to them for a while. SpaceX has made it pretty clear that early Starship operations will be geared toward internal priorities — specifically, the buildout of SpaceX's Starlink V3 broadband network and its Starmind AI data-center constellation.

Berdasarkan laporan, these will be very big jobs, even for the most powerful rocket ever built. For example, the Starlink V3 megaconstellation will consist of about 100,000 satellites, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk. Starship can carry about 60 of these spacecraft to LEO per launch, so just building out the constellation will require about 1,700 liftoffs.

The numbers for Starmind will be even more mind-boggling, for SpaceX wants that constellation to eventually harbor a million satellites.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the coming launch bottleneck should increase demand for electron as well as neutron, beck said during monday's call. After all, many small-satellite operators have launched with SpaceX over the years, booking spots on Falcon 9 "rideshare" flights. And those opportunities are now drying up.

"The next logical alternative is of course an Electron, so we see tremendous traction there," Beck said.

#344. Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue

📅 10 Nov 2026

Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261105085201.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, a fossil dating back more than 450 million years has revealed something scientists almost never find: delicate soft tissues from an animal that lived hundreds of millions of years before dinosaurs appeared. The extraordinarily rare discovery is giving researchers a new understanding of how some of Earth's earliest marine animals lived, fed, and evolved.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fossil belongs to an ancient crinoid, a marine animal related to modern starfish. Crinoids often resemble underwater flowers, with branching arms extending from a central body. More than 450 million years ago, these unusual creatures were among the animals thriving in Earth's earliest coral reefs, long before plants and animals had become widespread on land.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although scientists have discovered millions of crinoid fossils, nearly all preserve only hard skeletal structures. Delicate body parts usually decay long before fossilization can occur, leaving major gaps in our understanding of how these ancient creatures functioned.

Now, paleontologists at the University of Oklahoma have identified an exceptionally rare specimen that preserves soft tissue structures, providing an extraordinary opportunity to investigate life in Earth's ancient oceans.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "after an animal dies, soft tissues like skin, eyes, or internal organs are the first things to decay," said dr. Soft tissues are only preserved when the environment acts almost like a natural refrigerator or vacuum‑sealer -- conditions that are incredibly rare. Lena Cole, OU paleontologist and assistant curator of invertebrate paleontology at the Sam Noble Oklahoma Museum of Natural History. "Most fossils are only made up of hard parts like bones, teeth, or shells. ".

A 450 Million-Year-Old Fossil With Exceptionally Rare Soft Tissue.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the remarkable specimen belongs to dendrocrinus simcoensis, an extinct species of crinoid. Its preserved tube feet represent only the second known example of fossilized soft tissue in crinoids and the oldest such discovery ever documented.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tube feet are small, flexible structures found in echinoderms, a group of marine animals that includes starfish, sea urchins, and crinoids. Because these structures are soft and easily destroyed after death, finding evidence of them in fossils is extraordinarily unusual.

Diungkapkan bahwa "preservation like this is truly one in a million," cole added. "Crinoid fossils number in the millions, and this is only the second time soft tissues have ever been found. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the age of the specimen makes the discovery even more remarkable. These delicate structures have been preserved in the fossil record for nearly half a billion years, offering direct evidence of anatomy that would otherwise have disappeared.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it's incredible these soft tissues have survived more than 450 million years," said dr. "For reference, these soft tissues are more than 200 million years older than the oldest dinosaur. David Wright, another OU paleontologist and assistant curator of invertebrate paleontology at the Sam Noble Oklahoma Museum of Natural History, who co‑authored the study with Cole. ".

Ancient Feeding Structures Reveal Evolutionary Secrets.

The fossil's preserved tube feet are especially valuable because they provide clues about how crinoids obtained food and interacted with their surroundings.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unlike the teeth and jaws that many familiar animals use to eat, crinoids rely on specialized structures to capture food particles from seawater. Their tube feet play an important role in feeding and in how these animals interact with ocean currents.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the size, arrangement, and shape of these structures can differ between species, reflecting adaptations to particular habitats and feeding methods. By studying those differences, paleontologists can reconstruct aspects of an extinct animal's lifestyle, even when no living examples of that species exist.

Diungkapkan bahwa "since crinoid tube feet are used for feeding, you can think of them in a similar way to how we think about teeth in mammals," wright explained. "Differences in their structure tell us about what kinds of environments a species lived in and how it fed. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, researchers also compared the ancient fossil with crinoids living in today's oceans. Those comparisons revealed notable anatomical differences, suggesting that the feeding structures of these animals have undergone substantial evolutionary changes over hundreds of millions of years.

Diungkapkan bahwa "comparisons with living crinoids show that the anatomy of this ancient species was very different," cole added. "This gives us new insight into how crinoids evolved and how their feeding strategies changed over hundreds of millions of years. ".

A Rare Window Into Earth's Earliest Ocean Ecosystems.

Beyond revealing details about one ancient species, the discovery could help scientists piece together how marine ecosystems developed during the early Paleozoic Era.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the paleozoic was a vast chapter of earth's history that began about 541 million years ago. During its early stages, marine environments supported an expanding variety of complex animals, while life on land was still relatively limited.

Diungkapkan bahwa crinoids were among the creatures that became established in early reef communities. Their fossils provide important evidence of how marine animals occupied different ecological roles and adapted to changing environmental conditions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, studying only living species cannot reveal the full range of forms and adaptations that existed in the distant past. Some extinct animals possessed anatomical features that have no close equivalent among their modern relatives.

"Fossilized remains of long‑extinct species can show features well outside the range of variation we see in living species," Wright said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "by comparing ecological ways of life for extinct and modern species, we can understand how patterns of adaptive evolution have changed through time and what factors shaped the modern biosphere. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the biosphere includes all living organisms on earth and the environments they inhabit. Understanding how it developed requires scientists to examine not only which species existed, but also how they interacted with their surroundings and one another.

Sebagaimana diketahui, because soft tissues are so rarely preserved in ancient echinoderms, discoveries like this one provide evidence that conventional fossils cannot offer. They can help researchers identify previously unknown feeding strategies, understand ancient ecosystems, and trace evolutionary changes that eventually shaped modern marine life.

An Extraordinary Discovery Hidden in a Museum Collection.

Perhaps one of the most surprising aspects of the discovery is where the fossil was found.

Although major paleontological breakthroughs are often associated with expeditions to remote locations, valuable scientific evidence can also remain unnoticed for decades in museums.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fossil collections contain enormous numbers of specimens, many of which have never been examined by specialists with the expertise needed to recognize their most important features. As scientific knowledge and research methods improve, these collections can reveal discoveries that earlier generations overlooked.

Diungkapkan bahwa "new fossil discoveries ultimately come from fieldwork, but museum collections play a significant role in this kind of integrative research," wright said. "We don't always know the full significance of the specimens we collect. New technologies, ideas or expertise often find surprising ways to utilize existing specimens to make new discoveries. ".

The Dendrocrinus simcoensis fossil had been housed for years at Montréal's Musée de paléontologie et de l'évolution, a small museum that operates entirely with support from community donations.

Its remarkable scientific value became apparent when Cole and Wright, both specialists in crinoids, visited the museum and examined the specimen more closely.

Their investigation revealed that the fossil preserved an extraordinarily rare record of ancient soft tissue, transforming a specimen already held in a museum collection into an important source of new evolutionary evidence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this discovery highlights the importance of museum collections and the community support that keeps them alive," cole said. "Without the dedication of many people caring for these collections, this research would never have been possible. ".

More Discoveries May Be Waiting in Museum Drawers.

The finding also demonstrates why preserving and maintaining fossil collections is essential for future research.

Diungkapkan bahwa at the sam noble oklahoma museum of natural history, cole and wright oversee invertebrate paleontology collections containing more than one million specimens. Additional fossils are added every year, creating new opportunities to investigate ancient organisms and identify previously unrecognized species.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with collections of this size, no individual researcher could possibly examine every specimen in detail. A fossil that appears ordinary today might become the focus of a major discovery when studied by someone with a different specialty or new scientific tools.

Making collections available to researchers around the world increases the chances that these overlooked treasures will eventually receive the attention they deserve.

Diungkapkan bahwa "this is why we work to make our collections accessible to researchers around the world," wright said. "There are simply too many fossils to study over one person's career. There's more than a lifetime's worth of discoveries waiting to be found. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the extraordinary crinoid fossil is a reminder that some of the most revealing clues about earth's distant past may already have been collected. They are simply waiting for someone to recognize what makes them special.

#347. Alex Karp Said He’s a ‘Progressive.’ OK! Here’s Some Other Stuff He’s Said Recently

📅 12 Nov 2026

Alex Karp Said He’s a ‘Progressive.’ OK! Here’s Some Other Stuff He’s Said Recently

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/alex-karp-said-hes-a-progressive-ok-heres-some-other-stuff-hes-said-recently/

When Palantir chief executive Alex Karp sat down with Politico this week, he reportedly used the word “progressive” eight times to describe both his political philosophy and his company.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i’ve been a democrat my whole life,” karp told politico, which noted that he called the democratic party “totally irresponsible” in the distant time of october 2025. “I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir—all of our products are essentially progressive. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this isn’t the first time karp has called himself a progressive. In 2018, The New York Times reported that Karp described himself as such. In the same article, he claimed to have voted for Hillary Clinton.

Diungkapkan bahwa karp has also donated money to democratic candidates. In 2023, for instance, he donated $360,000 to a joint fundraising committee for Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. The next year, he donated $1 million to MAGA, Inc.

Berdasarkan laporan, palantir has a share of supporters from the democratic party. However, it’s not necessarily clear how the products of Palantir—a company that built the technology that underpins much of the Trump administration's brutal arrest and deportation campaign, sold tools to the US military that can use generative AI to help plan and execute drone strikes, and partnered with the Israeli military to assist in its devastating war on the Gaza strip, among other things—could reasonably be seen as progressive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s instructive, then, to look at what else karp has said in recent weeks, and how it lines up with his idea of what’s “progressive. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in his most recent quarterly letter to palantir shareholders, karp actually doubled down on his basic premise. In it, he argued that Palantir employees are “the pioneers of a genuine and viable antiwar movement. ”.

“We are all, in no uncertain terms, living through what John Lewis Gaddis, the professor of naval and military history at Yale, presciently described decades ago as the long peace,” Karp wrote, despite the fact that the US and Iran are currently engaged in direct warfare.

During Palantir’s corresponding earnings call on November 2, Karp was asked to clarify the statements in his letter.

Diungkapkan bahwa “our products are built to avoid war, meaning the adversary knows that they will have such pain inflicted upon them that in fact it's not worth going to war,” karp said. He did not, however, address the relevant possibility that the US is the party that initiates war.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i grew up as a lefty,” karp continued. I want to avoid war. ” But he said, “Sometimes they are necessary, and when they are necessary, America and its allies need the very, very, very best tools. “I don't actually like war. I don't support wars. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, karp went on to say that palantir has both a “moral imperative” and a “mission reason” for having the “somewhat crazy aspiration” of dominating its market. That mission, Karp said, is supporting the war fighter. Conveniently, it’s also very profitable.

“We are delighted that we can support the war fighter even more because we're making so much money,” Karp said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, karp’s recent comments in politico could also be seen through the lens of convenience. Democrats will have a majority in both chambers of Congress next year, and since about half of Palantir’s revenue comes from government work, it’s pragmatic to sow goodwill. Palantir has seen continued success, after all, across Democratic and Republican administrations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, karp doesn’t care about cultivating favor with everybody. ” (Karp didn’t name examples, although many critiques of Palantir have come from the American left. He pointedly excludes anyone who has criticized Palantir in what he calls “ridiculously stupid and malicious, incredibly hard to understand attacks. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, “what motivates me is helping to make sure we are fighting for you,” karp said, addressing palantir investors, “and quite frankly, making sure that the people that made fun of you and made fun of us are suffering. ”.
