#348. Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered

📅 08 Nov 2026

Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered

Tanggal: 08 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104084019.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, a tiny fish with brilliant orange markings has been discovered in the brazilian amazon, but scientists warn that the newly identified species may already be at risk of extinction. Found in a handful of forest pools threatened by human activity, the colorful fish has prompted researchers to call for urgent conservation measures.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new species, named laimosemion laranja, belongs to a group of small freshwater fish known as killifish. Males have rows of bright orange spots along the front half of their bodies, followed by bold orange chevron patterns near the tail. It measures less than three centimeters in standard length, but its appearance is anything but ordinary. These vivid markings stand out against their pale gray sides.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the discovery was made during fieldwork in the rio cajari drainage in southern amapá, a state in northern brazil. The research team included scientists from the Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte, Instituto Peixe das Nuvens, Universidade Federal do Pará, and University of West Florida.

A Striking Discovery in the Amazon Rainforest.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers were exploring how different freshwater fish in the rivulidae family have evolved their life cycles and survival strategies across brazil's diverse environments. During their surveys, they encountered a fish whose unusual coloration immediately stood out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we are developing a research project aimed at investigating the evolution of life-history strategies in freshwater fishes of the family rivulidae across different biomes in brazil," said lead researcher yuri abrantes of the universidade federal do rio grande do norte. "During our sampling in small rivers locally known as 'igarapés' in the Rio Cajari region, in Amapá State, we found this fish with a very striking coloration, which immediately caught our attention. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, although the fish looked different from known species, its appearance alone was not enough to establish that it was new to science. The team carefully examined its body proportions, counted its scales, and studied features of its skeleton. They compared these characteristics with those of closely related species and analyzed its mitochondrial DNA to determine whether it represented a distinct species.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it was an unexpected moment," abrantes recalled. "Initially, what most caught our attention was the impressive coloration of the males and females, which was unlike anything we had previously encountered in the study area. This sparked our admiration and a great deal of curiosity. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, genetic testing ultimately confirmed that the fish was a previously unrecognized species. For the researchers, the finding was particularly meaningful because it highlighted how much remains to be discovered in parts of the Amazon that are both poorly studied and increasingly threatened.

Berdasarkan laporan, once the genetic analysis confirmed the fish's distinct identity, he said, "it was something special, as we saw an opportunity to contribute to increasing our knowledge of amazonian biodiversity and to draw attention to the conservation of areas that are still poorly explored but highly threatened. ".

Why Scientists Named the New Fish Laranja.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the name laimosemion laranja reflects both the fish's remarkable appearance and the place where it was discovered. In Portuguese, laranja means orange, referring to both the color and the fruit. The name also pays tribute to Laranjal do Jari, the municipality in Amapá where the species was found.

"We wanted to choose a name that would highlight a characteristic of the fish while also fostering a sense of connection with the people of the region where it was discovered," Abrantes explained.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, beyond its colorful appearance, the discovery could help scientists better understand the evolution of amazonian killifish. Some members of this group have developed an extraordinary way to survive in habitats that periodically dry out. Their embryos can stop developing and remain dormant in damp mud, resuming development when seasonal rains refill the pools.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "laimosemion represents one of the five independent origins of the annual life cycle within the family rivulidae," said abrantes. "Laimosemion laranja is particularly interesting because it expands our knowledge of the diversity and evolution of this group in the region. ".

Newly Discovered Amazon Fish May Already Be Endangered.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite the excitement surrounding the discovery, the future of laimosemion laranja is uncertain. Scientists have found it in only three small forest pools near Laranjal do Jari, and every known location shows signs of environmental disturbance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, deforestation, mining, and urban development are putting pressure on the surrounding habitats. One of the pools is close to water that has been discolored by sediment from mining activities. Another is located within the city itself, where plastic pollution is affecting the environment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the species' entire known range is estimated to cover just 25 square kilometers. Because its habitat is so restricted and faces multiple threats, the researchers believe the fish meets the criteria for classification as Endangered under guidelines established by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

To improve its chances of survival, the team has recommended expanding the boundaries of the nearby Rio Cajari Extractive Reserve to include the areas where the fish lives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the discovery adds another species to the amazon's remarkable biological diversity while underscoring the need to protect habitats that scientists have barely begun to explore. Without stronger conservation measures, species such as Laimosemion laranja could face serious threats before researchers have the opportunity to fully understand them.

The study was published in the open access journal Zoosystematics and Evolution.

This dazzling collection of ancient stars could hold clues to the Milky Way's past.

Berdasarkan laporan, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange.

Diungkapkan bahwa but this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the exquisite image released by esa on nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus.

M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, our milky way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11. 5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13. 5 billion and 13. 8 billion years old!.

Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell.

Diungkapkan bahwa globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, astronomers have also discovered that m30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the milky way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

#352. An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin

An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104084017.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa a drug commonly used to prevent organ transplant rejection may offer an unexpected new approach to protecting people at increased risk of alzheimer's disease. Researchers at the University of Missouri have discovered that rapamycin, a medication also studied for its effects on aging, can improve blood flow in the brains of middle-aged adults who carry a gene variant linked to Alzheimer's.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the findings could help scientists develop strategies to address alzheimer's risk long before memory problems appear. The research also adds to the University of Missouri's growing contributions to understanding and potentially preventing the most common form of dementia.

Diungkapkan bahwa the study was led by ai-ling lin, a professor in the university's school of medicine and an investigator at the roy blunt nextgen precision health building. Her work focuses on identifying changes in the brain that occur before Alzheimer's symptoms develop and finding ways to intervene early.

Why Brain Blood Flow Matters for Alzheimer's Risk.

A major focus of Lin's research is the APOE4 gene variant, which is associated with a substantially increased risk of developing Alzheimer's disease later in life.

Sebagaimana diketahui, people who carry apoe4 can experience reduced blood flow in certain areas of the brain years before they begin having noticeable memory difficulties. Because these circulation changes can occur so early, researchers believe they could provide an important warning sign of increased Alzheimer's risk.

Lin's latest findings suggest that improving brain circulation with an existing medication may be one way to address these early changes.

Berdasarkan laporan, "alzheimer's tends to happen more in older people, especially for those with apoe4," lin said. "If we can slow down aging in the brain for those people most at risk, maybe we can reduce the risk of them developing Alzheimer's disease. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rapamycin is already used in medicine to prevent the immune system from rejecting transplanted organs and to treat certain rare conditions. However, researchers have also been investigating its potential to slow biological aging and protect the brain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, before joining the university of missouri, lin conducted experiments involving mice that carried apoe4. Her earlier research showed that rapamycin could slow brain aging and increase blood flow in these animals.

Those results prompted an important question: Could rapamycin produce similar benefits in people who have a genetic predisposition to Alzheimer's but have not yet developed the disease?.

To investigate, Lin studied healthy adults between the ages of 45 and 65, including people who carried APOE4 and others who did not.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all participants received a low daily dose of rapamycin for four weeks. When researchers examined the results, they found a notable difference between the two groups.

Berdasarkan laporan, brain blood flow improved among participants carrying apoe4, but the same benefit was not observed in those without the gene variant. This suggests that rapamycin may have particular potential for people whose genetics place them at greater risk of Alzheimer's.

Although the study did not establish whether the treatment could prevent Alzheimer's or preserve memory over time, the improved circulation offers a promising direction for future research.

Women With the Alzheimer's Risk Gene Saw the Greatest Benefits.

Another intriguing finding emerged when the researchers examined differences between male and female participants.

Sebagaimana diketahui, women carrying apoe4 experienced the largest improvements in brain blood flow following treatment. That result may be especially important because women account for nearly two-thirds of people living with Alzheimer's disease.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we also found that females with apoe4 saw the greatest improvement in brain blood flow, which is significant given that nearly two-thirds of people with alzheimer's are women," she said. "This research is an example of precision medicine, as we work to identify who can benefit from this drug the most. ".

The results highlight the potential of precision medicine, an approach that considers individual characteristics, including genetics, when determining which treatments may be most effective.

Rather than assuming that a medication will benefit everyone equally, researchers hope to identify the people most likely to respond.

Moving Alzheimer's Discoveries Toward Human Treatments.

Lin, who is also a professor in the university's College of Arts and Science, credits Mizzou's collaborative research environment with helping advance discoveries like these.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the roy blunt nextgen precision health building, scientists and medical professionals work together in the same facility. This collaboration is designed to help move promising laboratory findings into human clinical studies more quickly.

Berdasarkan laporan, the latest results provide an encouraging starting point for investigating whether rapamycin could eventually help delay or reduce alzheimer's risk in genetically vulnerable individuals. More research will be needed to determine whether the changes in brain blood flow lead to lasting improvements in brain health or a lower likelihood of developing the disease.

The study, "EXPRESS: Rapamycin increases cerebral blood flow and modulates metabolic, inflammatory, and microbiome profiles in healthy middle-aged APOE4 carriers: a pilot single-arm trial" was published in Journal of Cerebral Blood Flow & Metabolism.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you care about privacy, don’t feed your own personal information into a chatbot, which—among other concerns—could use it to train ai tools. Employees, though, mostly don’t have a choice.

Berdasarkan laporan, a new, multibillion-dollar industry is dedicated to selling and buying work files and emails to companies seeking fresh sources of data to improve their ai models, and it’s only getting bigger. Diungkapkan bahwa an agreement reached this week between google and a union representing an unlikely workforce—flight attendants—could reveal a more permanent answer by creating a process that might reliably separate the data that workers produce from their own personal information. But the union, the 55,000-member Association for Flight Attendants, argued that Google’s proposed safeguards would not prevent serious privacy violations for Spirit Airlines flight attendants, whose records—including 1. In August, representatives for the budget airline said in a legal brief that it would be selling decades’ worth of data to Google for $10 million; Google said it would not receive personal information as part of the sale. 99 billion emails, 664 million Microsoft Teams messages, and employee travel and training information, all dating back to 1986—would be included in the sale.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the revised deal requires spirit to hire a third-party data de-identification company, called tonic ai, to exclude information that could potentially be associated with individual consumers or employees. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many sensitive records will be excluded from the sale, including employee medical records, documents related to employee investigations and labor relations, and information about industry-wide safety management systems. In early November, a trade organization representing airlines chimed in on the sale, arguing that including that information could make employees less willing to come forward to report safety issues through voluntary programs, which are widely regarded as critical to the US aviation industry’s strong safety record.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the proposed agreement also includes an opt-out clause. Google can choose to renege on the sale if the data-cleaning process reduces the assets by more than 8 percent. Google didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Association for Flight Attendants president Sara Nelson tells WIRED she’s as surprised as anyone that flight attendants are at the forefront of AI-related workers’ rights issues, which often focus on employees who, willingly or unwillingly, train their machine replacements.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it’s very hard to replace a flight attendant—you’d need a high-functioning robot, and that seems to be further off,” she says. This is an issue for everyone. “What this shows is that this is an issue even in jobs you think are most protected from AI. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa she said the union will immediately begin to demand that other airlines include worker-data-protection clauses in their labor agreements. “If you’re not willing to meet these standards for your workers, we’re going to shame you,” she says. The Association for Flight Attendants has begun meeting with state-level politicians to craft legislation that would write worker data protections into law.

Berdasarkan laporan, ari ezra waldman, a professor at the uc irvine school of law who studies law and technology, calls the proposed settlement “a pretty good outcome” for spirit airlines employees. He points to another, and maybe easier, alternative: Banning the sale of data altogether. “From now on, unions will know to negotiate to protect the privacy rights in the event of future sales of data assets,” he wrote to WIRED in an email. “Privacy protections are necessary now more than ever,” he says.

Diungkapkan bahwa tech leaders have argued that workers understand that their information will train ai models, which will ultimately make their lives better and easier. “You have to think of the upside, the abundance that AI can result in,” one executive told WIRED this month.

Diungkapkan bahwa nelson says us workers aren’t buying the upside of ai and that they’re part of the wider electorate that seems to be growing warier of the tech by the day. She says the vision of AI abundance is “a fantasyland of people in boardrooms with beanbags who wear hoodies. ”.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03565-3

Diungkapkan bahwa thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

Berdasarkan laporan, the basal ganglia are groups of cells that sit deep in the brain and process motor, cognitive, mood and decision-making information. They are linked to neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions from Parkinson’s and Huntington’s disease to schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and addiction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, now, researchers have published the world’s most-detailed atlas of basal ganglia so far, comprising 25. The work is described in a collection of 26 papers published in Cell, Cell Reports, Cell Reports Methods, Cell Systems, Cell Genomics and Neuron. 5 million brain cells from humans, macaques and marmosets. The research includes understudied neurons1, provides insights about how some brain cells change with age2 and suggests which might be linked to diseases3.

The atlas, a collaboration between hundreds of scientists in nine countries, is part of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) — a US$500-million project launched in 2022 by the US National Institutes of Health aimed at creating reference maps of mammalian brains.

“It’s a massive dictionary that we needed in the field,” says Ana Muñoz-Manchado, a neuroscientist at the University of Cádiz in Spain, who studies the basal ganglia in neurodegenerative disorders.

Berdasarkan laporan, the basal ganglia atlas contains 21 million cells from the brains of six humans, three million cells from three rhesus and cynomolgus macaques, and 1. 5 million cells from two marmosets4. The researchers also used data from previously published maps of the whole mouse brain5,6.

By comparing the basal ganglia between the primate species, the researchers identified 61 cell types in humans, macaques and marmosets that have been conserved over 76 million years3.

Diungkapkan bahwa the team analysed brain tissue samples from different developmental stages across the lifespan of the species. The latest work combines information about these cells in unprecedented detail, from measurements of their gene expression and DNA modifications that control gene regulation to recordings of their electrical activity, as well as how DNA is folded inside their nuclei.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers also mapped where each cell is located in the brain and designed a common framework to characterize and annotate the cells. It is “essentially a scaffold on which we can now fairly readily complete the rest of the brain”, explains Michael Hawrylycz, a bioinformatician at the Allen Institute for Brain Science in Seattle, Washington, who took part in the project.

Berdasarkan laporan, one study examined 1. 1 million cells in the basal ganglia’s largest structure — known as the striatum — from 19 deceased human donors7. Unlike many other brain areas, the striatum has no neat anatomical boundaries. The researchers identified six zones in the human and macaque striatum with distinct molecular signatures, each containing distinct populations of neurons and glial cells.

“The cells in these zones all look the same under the microscope, but have very strong transcriptional differences and are strikingly consistent from person to person,” said co-author Evan Macosko, a neurobiologist at the Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in a press release from the institute.

Macosko and his colleagues also found that gene expression patterns that distinguished each zone from the other became increasingly similar with age, particularly in brain regions affected by Huntington’s and Parkinson’s disease.

Berdasarkan laporan, another study analysed nearly four million cells in the striatum and prefrontal cortex from 178 deceased adult donors between the ages of 27 and over 902. The researchers found that the cellular make-up of the two brain regions varied between people, particularly for non-neuronal cells known as glial cells. This underscores the need for brain cell atlases to account for these individual differences.

#356. A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer

📅 09 Nov 2026

A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104084013.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, for some breast cancer survivors, the effects of treatment can linger long after their cancer care ends. Memory lapses, difficulty concentrating, and persistent exhaustion can interfere with everyday life, sometimes for years. Now, researchers at the UCLA Health Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center have found promising early evidence that a supplement containing a naturally occurring molecule could help relieve these symptoms.

Berdasarkan laporan, the molecule, called oxaloacetate, is already present in the human body and plays an important role in how cells generate energy. In a small clinical trial, breast cancer survivors who took the supplement for eight weeks reported noticeable improvements in thinking, memory, concentration, and fatigue.

Berdasarkan laporan, the results, published in jco oncology advances, also showed improvements on cognitive tests measuring how quickly participants processed information and performed tasks requiring planning, attention, and mental flexibility. Although larger studies are needed to confirm the findings, the results suggest a potentially new way to address a problem that has long been difficult to treat.

Diungkapkan bahwa "cancer-related cognitive impairment can persist long after treatment ends and can have a significant impact on a person's daily life, yet we still have very few effective treatments for it," said dr. Patricia Ganz, the study's first author and a distinguished professor of medicine at UCLA's David Geffen School of Medicine and UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.

Why Brain Fog Can Persist After Cancer Treatment.

Diungkapkan bahwa cognitive difficulties are a lasting concern for many people who survive breast cancer. These symptoms are often described as "chemo brain" or "brain fog. Researchers estimate that roughly 15% to 25% experience ongoing problems with memory, concentration, or other thinking abilities after their diagnosis and treatment. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, despite the name, chemotherapy is not necessarily the only cause. Scientists increasingly recognize that cancer-related cognitive impairment can develop through several overlapping processes. The cancer itself, chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, inflammation, hormonal changes, and other biological and behavioral influences may all contribute.

Because the causes are complicated and effective treatments remain limited, researchers are investigating ways to address the underlying changes that may disrupt normal brain function.

Berdasarkan laporan, one area of interest involves the relationship between inflammation, brain chemistry, and energy production. Inflammation linked to cancer and its treatments may interfere with glutamate signaling, an important part of communication between nerve cells. It may also disturb the processes that allow brain cells to produce and use energy efficiently. Together, these disruptions could contribute to difficulties with thinking and persistent mental exhaustion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, oxaloacetate attracted the ucla team's attention because it participates in both cellular energy production and the regulation of glutamate. The researchers wanted to learn whether providing additional oxaloacetate through a supplement might reduce the cognitive symptoms and fatigue experienced by cancer survivors.

Testing Oxaloacetate for Brain Fog and Fatigue.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to investigate, the researchers carried out a phase ii clinical trial involving 18 women who had been diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer between one and five years earlier. All participants were experiencing substantial cognitive difficulties when they entered the study.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the women were approximately 50 years old on average. Most had undergone chemotherapy, and nearly 90% were still receiving endocrine therapy during the trial.

Berdasarkan laporan, each participant was instructed to take 500 milligrams of oxaloacetate twice a day for eight weeks. The researchers tracked changes in cognitive symptoms using questionnaires completed by the participants, along with standardized tests designed to evaluate memory, attention, processing speed, and executive function. Executive function includes the mental abilities needed to organize activities, maintain focus, make plans, and manage tasks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the study also examined fatigue, sleep, anxiety, depression, physical health, and mental well-being. Throughout the treatment period, the team monitored participants for possible side effects.

Brain Fog Scores Improved After Eight Weeks.

Diungkapkan bahwa of the 18 women enrolled, 16 completed the full eight weeks of supplementation. Every participant who finished the treatment reported significant improvement in her cognitive symptoms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the changes were particularly striking on the study's main measure of perceived cognitive impairment. 1. After eight weeks, that average had climbed to 55. Before treatment, the participants had an average score of 29. 5, placing the group in the range considered normal rather than impaired.

Signs of improvement were already apparent after four weeks, and the benefits reported by participants generally became more pronounced as treatment continued.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the results extended beyond memory and concentration. Participants reported significantly less fatigue, including the mental exhaustion that can make everyday activities difficult. They also described meaningful improvements in their ability to function physically.

Berdasarkan laporan, standardized cognitive testing provided additional encouraging evidence. Researchers observed improvements in processing speed and executive function, suggesting that some aspects of thinking performance may have improved alongside the participants' perceptions of their symptoms.

However, the scientists emphasized that these results remain preliminary because the trial included so few participants.

Promising Results, but More Research Is Needed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, oxaloacetate was generally well tolerated during the eight-week study. The most frequently reported side effects involved the digestive system, including indigestion, bloating, constipation, diarrhea, and nausea.

Berdasarkan laporan, two women stopped taking the supplement because of gastrointestinal symptoms. No serious adverse events were recorded.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite the encouraging improvements, the researchers cautioned against drawing firm conclusions about the supplement's effectiveness. The trial was small and did not include a placebo group or another comparison group. Without that comparison, it is not possible to determine whether oxaloacetate itself caused the improvements.

"These early findings give us a strong reason to continue studying oxaloacetate as a potential approach for managing cognitive problems after breast cancer treatment," Ganz said.

Larger Clinical Trial Will Test the Supplement's Benefits.

Diungkapkan bahwa to build on these initial findings, the ucla team has been preparing a randomized, placebo-controlled phase ii clinical trial involving breast cancer survivors with cancer-related cognitive impairment. The study was expected to begin enrolling participants in late 2026.

By comparing oxaloacetate with a placebo, the researchers hope to establish whether the supplement produces measurable benefits beyond those that might occur without active treatment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the investigators are also conducting preclinical research in mice to better understand how oxaloacetate affects the body and brain. These experiments include a placebo-controlled study examining whether the molecule produces similar improvements (improved fatigue and physical function) in animals.

The research received partial financial support from the Breast Cancer Research Foundation and the National Cancer Institute.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in addition to ganz, the study's authors were kathleen van dyk, phd, catherine m. Crespi, PhD, Laura Petersen, MS, Mina Sedrak, MD, MS, and Julienne Bower, PhD, all affiliated with UCLA.

Berdasarkan laporan, why you can trust space. com Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test and review products.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve used several smart telescopes over the last few years, but i'd recommend the zwo seestar s30 plus to almost anyone wanting to get started in astrophotography. At $499/€499, it’s a complete imaging system that can photograph galaxies, nebulae and star clusters automatically, even from a light-polluted city. Better still, it’s so small that it can live on a bookshelf.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i recently captured images of the dumbbell nebula (m27), the north america nebula (ngc 7000), the andromeda galaxy (m31) and the pleiades (m45) with the s30 plus. All were remarkably easy to capture, and none of the images accompanying this review required external processing. It’s basically point-and-shoot astrophotography — if you live under light-polluted skies, that’s a game-changer.

Berdasarkan laporan, i also think the s30 plus makes an ideal companion to a conventional optical telescope. I can set it to photograph a nebula I have no hope of seeing under light pollution while I try to find brighter objects through the eyepiece of another telescope. It will then get on with collecting photons while I enjoy observing.

For anyone who already owns a telescope but doesn’t want the expense and complexity of conventional astrophotography, that’s a compelling proposition.

Berdasarkan laporan, one problem with buying a cheap optical telescope is that deep-sky objects rarely resemble the colorful photographs you see online. The moon, planets and bright star clusters can look wonderful through an eyepiece, but faint galaxies and nebulas are much harder to appreciate, particularly from a town or city.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, like all smart telescopes, the s30 plus gets around that problem by photographing objects rather than showing them directly. Its camera takes repeated exposures, which the telescope automatically stacks to reduce noise and gradually reveal faint detail. The longer you leave it working, the better the resulting image tends to become.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, being able to photograph colorful nebulas without traveling to a remote observing site is one of the biggest attractions of the s30 plus. For beginners living in cities, it could transform their experience of astronomy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’ve always preferred spending my nights looking at the sky rather than fiddling with equipment, which is one reason i enjoy smart telescopes. Traditional astrophotography can involve a camera, tracking mount, adapters, cables, alignment, a laptop and considerable patience before the first useful exposure begins. The S30 Plus removes almost all of that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i can put it outside, connect the seestar app and choose a target from its built-in sky atlas. The telescope then moves to the correct position, identifies the star field, centers the object, focuses and begins imaging. Within minutes, a photograph starts appearing on my smartphone. That leaves me free to use an optical telescope alongside it — or stay inside and do something else.

Berdasarkan laporan, using the s30 plus’s built-in uv/ir cut filter — which blocks ultraviolet and infrared light — i captured the andromeda galaxy (m31), a popular deep-sky object. As the hours went by, the dust lanes on its outskirts appeared in ever more detail. That’s how smart telescopes work — they collect and combine dozens or hundreds of short exposures, gradually revealing fainter structure while reducing noise.

Berdasarkan laporan, so impressive is the image after only about five or six exposures that it’s tempting to stop after a few minutes — but patience makes an enormous difference. Fortunately, you don’t have to stand beside the S30 Plus. You can leave it collecting light — even overnight, thanks to its scheduling option (though it’s not waterproof, so check the weather forecast!).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, using the dual-band anti-light pollution filter, the pleiades open cluster (m45) provided another interesting test. The S30 Plus has a mosaic mode that photographs overlapping sections of sky to create a larger image than its main camera can capture in a single frame. It’s ideal for expansive targets such as the Pleiades and Andromeda, although gathering enough exposures takes time. The app shows how much of the mosaic has been completed, and if needs be, you can continue collecting data on subsequent nights.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i also photographed the double cluster in perseus (ngc 869 and ngc 884) and the great globular cluster in hercules (m13), both relatively swift targets, but as anyone who’s used a smart telescope knows, it’s the faint nebulas that are the real prize. For those, dark skies mean better data — and that’s exactly why a smart telescope needs to be portable.

Berdasarkan laporan, the s30 plus weighs just 3. 5 x 3. 15 inches (210 x 140 x 80 mm) when switched off. 25 x 5. 64 lbs (1. That’s small enough to fit into a camera bag in place of another lens or camera body, which is a major advantage because I travel to remote locations quite frequently. 65 kg) and measures 8. That fact that it sits on such a tiny tripod is also a boon.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve recently used the much larger seestar s50 pro, which weighs 6. 17 lbs (2. It’s a more capable imaging instrument with a 50mm aperture and a larger 8. 3-megapixel sensor, but its heavier, bulkier chassis is harder to get into carry-on luggage. The S30 Plus and the higher-spec S30 Pro also differ from the S50 Pro in that they come with a padded carry case. 8 kg). This has a useful carrying handle, although there’s no shoulder strap or dedicated storage for the tripod and magnetic solar filter.

It’s also worth taking along a portable battery and USB-C cable to recharge its built-in 6,000mAh battery during long sessions, though it lasts about six hours, which will suit most observing sessions.

Diungkapkan bahwa the original, now-discontinued s30 was already impressive, but the s30 plus is a substantial upgrade. It has improved four-element apochromatic optics with ED glass and two 3. 7-megapixel cameras, each producing 1,440x2,560-pixel images. That’s almost 80% more pixels than the original S30’s main camera.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the main camera’s field of view has increased slightly to about three degrees, while the wide-angle camera now covers 43. 5 degrees of sky. The latter can be used for star trails, though I suspect it’s something most people will experiment with occasionally.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there’s also an eq mode. This will align the telescope with Earth’s rotation to allow longer exposures and sharper edges, which I found worked really well. It requires an appropriately angled mount or wedge (such as the Seestar TH10 Fluid Tripod Head) and a small tripod.

Berdasarkan laporan, i tested it at 51 degrees north, which randomly appears to be the cut-off point for ease of use because of the tilt it puts on the telescope. It’s when a tripod begins to topple with the weight, meaning you need a tripod whose legs can be set at a low angle (Seestar’s TC20 tripod would be ideal, and is very compact).

Diungkapkan bahwa the app makes it all very easy to set up, and advanced imaging possibilities like this are welcome. So, too, is the option of outputting images as lossless FITS files for anyone wanting to process their images using specialist software.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that’s what makes the seestar s30 plus such a good beginner’s telescope. It’s easy to use immediately, but there’s plenty of scope to develop more sophisticated astrophotography skills without buying another instrument.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the s30 plus isn’t limited to deep-sky photography. I photographed a near-full moon against a blue daytime sky, something I particularly enjoy doing with smart telescopes because they’re so quick to set up.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it also comes with a magnetic white-light solar filter, allowing safe photographs of the sun when the filter is securely fitted. I did have to manually guide the S30 Plus to the sun and moon on a few occasions, but it’s easy enough to do, and I actually like the option to manually take control — few other smart telescopes allow it. This must always be installed before pointing the telescope towards the sun. Once you’ve found the sun or moon, the scope centers it and keeps it in view (unless you’re on a moving ship, by the way, where tracking generally fails — something for eclipse chasers to think about).

Sebagaimana diketahui, planetary photography is less impressive. The 30mm aperture and short focal length aren’t ideal for detailed views of Jupiter or Saturn, so for anyone primarily interested in observing and imaging planets, I’d recommend a conventional optical telescope instead.

Berdasarkan laporan, the s30 plus occupies an interesting position in zwo’s increasingly crowded seestar range. With dual 8. 3MP cameras and wider fields of view, the S30 Pro is a worthy upgrade from the original S30. Meanwhile, the $999 S50 Pro has a larger 50mm aperture that collects almost three times as much light, although it’s also significantly bulkier and more expensive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, alternatives exist outside zwo’s range. DwarfLab’s Dwarf Mini is exceptionally portable, but its lower resolution and more limited capabilities make it less versatile. At the other extreme, Unistellar’s Odyssey has an 85mm aperture, an electronic eyepiece and opportunities to contribute to citizen science projects, but it sits in a different price bracket.

Berdasarkan laporan, the s30 plus will hit the sweet spot for many. Crucially, it’s small enough to travel with easily. It offers almost everything a beginner needs to explore deep-sky astrophotography, with built-in filters, mosaic mode and EQ tracking giving plenty of advanced features to grow into. Yes, you can spend more and get slightly better image data, but most beginners don’t need to.

The Seestar S30 Plus is one of the most affordable smart telescopes available, but it’s also one of the best-value offerings in its class.

Diungkapkan bahwa jamie is an experienced science and travel journalist, stargazer and eclipse chaser who writes about exploring the night sky, solar and lunar eclipses, the northern lights, moon-gazing, astro-travel, astronomy and space exploration. He is the editor of WhenIsTheNextEclipse. com, author of A Stargazing Program For Beginners, co-author of The Eclipse Effect, and a senior contributor at Forbes.

#359. Rocco Classic Smart Fridge Review: A Cool Conversation Piece

📅 12 Nov 2026

Rocco Classic Smart Fridge Review: A Cool Conversation Piece

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/review/rocco-super-smart-fridge/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, updated november 2026: the rocco super smart fridge is now called the rocco classic, after rocco released two new fridges in 2026, the lower-priced essential and desktop-sized mini mini. Copy has been updated to reflect the new moniker.

Opening up someone else’s kitchen refrigerator is an intimate act.

Berdasarkan laporan, i for one would prefer my guests don’t go in there for a beer and see the raspberries that are probably moldy, revealing a dark side of my personality. I’ll just get their drink for them. Having a separate mini fridge just for drinks can help, and when I saw how fresh and innovative the Rocco seemed, I had to know more.

Diungkapkan bahwa the rocco classic feels more like a piece of furniture sitting in my living room, as opposed to a regular mini fridge, which often looks like it’s out of a college dorm, or a more industrial-looking regular wine fridge. I have the matte graphite color (it also comes in white, green, brown, and mirror-black).

Diungkapkan bahwa the whole thing is mostly made of steel, which makes it strong and heavy, and the rounded edges give it more of a soft appeal. It seems to be engineered very well, with quality materials, which I’m sure is why it costs as much as it does. This should last me a very long time in my home. Overall, it’s a beautiful statement piece that people who like to host in their home will love, but the features that make this a smart fridge are not perfect.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a typical wine fridge will generally fit full-size bottles of wine only, but the classic can fit 77 12-ounce cans (though rocco's website says 88) or 27 wine bottles in its 34. 5 x 24 x 16-inch body (H x W x D). There are six shelves, each of which is designed so you can store bottles and cans of any size and stagger them to fit like a puzzle. Each shelf is also reversible so the grooves match whichever shape bottles you choose to place on each shelf.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rocco connects to an app on your phone (currently available only for ios; rocco hopes to have an android version at some point). It really is extremely quiet. I keep mine on Quiet Mode. First of all, there are a few modes you can control from the app. The app is simple and easy to use, but there aren’t that many things to do on it, and some of the features feel forced. I rarely hear much of a rumbling noise from the compressor compared to other fridges.

Diungkapkan bahwa similarly, there’s smart mode, which makes it work more like a thermostat when the fridge is sitting in a warmer temperature. I opened it a few minutes later, and it was definitely colder in there. There’s also Party Mode, which prioritizes keeping the drinks cold more so than making less noise. After a few minutes, I did hear the compressor get a little louder. (Rocco gives the temperature range as 37 to 64 degrees Fahrenheit. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, but if i want the drinks to stay colder while i’m having a party where people are opening it often, i could just lower the temperature to where i want it myself. I really don’t see much of a need for all of these modes. Using a wireless Bluetooth thermometer, I tested the temperature changes inside the fridge for each mode to make sure they work properly. I gave each of them 10 minutes to change and tested each shelf on both ends of the fridge. I was pleased to find these were all within just a few degrees difference of what the fridge read.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the other primary feature of the app is the vision system. Every beverage then shows up on your app, organized by drawer. When you first set up the app, sensors in the fridge scan everything you’re storing in it. I’m storing some pretty obscure drinks, like OoMee algae-infused beverage and Yaté yerba mate, and it recognized most of them, so I was impressed, although some, like my Dolin vermouth, which is one of the most popular vermouth brands, were not recognized.

Berdasarkan laporan, nutrition facts also pop up for each drink, although many of them are incomplete. In theory, you could go to the grocery store and see which drinks you’re running low on just by looking at the app. I found that I didn’t do this much, although I was curious if I was running low on LaCroix once and checked the app to see that I certainly was. So it came in handy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, the system is not perfect. Right now it’s showing that I still have one LaCroix remaining, although I haven’t had one in there in a couple of weeks. I would love it if I could purchase something I’m running low on directly from the app.

Berdasarkan laporan, the dual-temperature system also allows you to make half of the fridge one temperature and the other half another, which you can adjust manually or through the app. While this is important so that I can keep seltzers and wines at different temperatures, this is the one feature that’s on many wine fridges, so it’s not unique to the Classic.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the classic has a kind of mid-century vibe but also feels contemporary. I love the fluted glass door, which looks stunning when it’s nighttime and the lights inside are peeking through it. Any time someone comes to my apartment it becomes a topic of conversation. You can turn the light on and off and adjust the brightness from the app.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the top surface of the fridge is flat and sturdy, so it doubles as a bar cart. The raised lip on the sides also helps so that bottles I’m placing on it have less of a chance of falling off. I have a bar cart that’s overflowing with bottles, so it’s nice to have this right next to it for some overflow.

Diungkapkan bahwa as someone who loves to make a nightly martini, i’ve hated having to go to my kitchen fridge for the vermouth. The Classic also comes with a pack of round playing cards that double as coasters. Now I store my vermouth right in my Rocco and I don’t have to break up my rhythm as much (other than grabbing ice and the chilled glass from the kitchen freezer). They’re a little flimsy for coasters, but it’s a cute touch.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the fridge beeps when the door doesn’t shut all the way. It’s a pretty soft beep—I didn’t hear it over the TV playing. You really have to make sure the door is all the way shut, because it’s not soft-close, nor are the drawers, which I wish were. That would have been a much better use of the app. I wish I got a push notification when the door wasn’t shut. The small bottom drawer on mine is also a little bit stubborn to pull out and close, although all the other doors slide nice and smoothly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the price does make your heart skip a beat. But that aligns with other higher-end wine fridges on the market. You also don't need to worry about installing this fridge into your cabinetry, as it’s a stand-alone piece. The precision and engineering of this fridge make the price seem reasonable when compared with others, and it actually has character, whereas just about every other wine fridge looks the same.

Berdasarkan laporan, additionally, the price includes a 10-year warranty. For an additional fee, you can get white glove delivery, where it’s placed in your home exactly where you want it and the packaging is removed for you. This is probably not worth it. Otherwise, shipping is free.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rocco makes your living room more of an active social space by keeping your guests in the same cozy area. I think people are going to buy this fridge more because of the way it looks rather than the fact that it’s a smart fridge. It’s furniture, which I wouldn’t say about most other fridges. I’m a beverage enthusiast, so I love having the Rocco to show for it.

NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.space.com/science/astrophysics/nasas-new-uvex-space-telescope-will-peer-deep-into-the-universes-most-violent-events

Sebagaimana diketahui, the uvex mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermaths of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility.

Diungkapkan bahwa the ultraviolet explorer (uvex) mission, developed by nasa in conjunction with the california institute of technology (caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, uvex's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

Berdasarkan laporan, the $590 million uvex mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, caltech physics professor fiona harrison, said in an oct. 27 statement.

"The first major ultraviolet space mission in two decades, UVEX is a bold leap forward in our exploration of the ultraviolet universe," Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana said in the same statement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, uvex will benefit from a major leap forward in uv sensitivity thanks to its caltech-built sensors, which are based on complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (cmos) imaging technology. This will help the spacecraft tap into what Harrison described as "the untapped opportunity in the UV. ".

UVEX will be uniquely poised to spot millions of nearby, small, and faint galaxies that are teeming with infant stars that emit bright UV light.

Berdasarkan laporan, "in optical light, it's very hard to distinguish these nearby galaxies from faraway ones that look similar," harrison said. "UV light will make them easier to find. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, uvex won't just be investigating the infancy of stars, however. It will also examine the deaths of ancient stars in the form of supernovas.

Sebagaimana diketahui, supernovas occur when a massive star runs out of fuel for nuclear fusion and can no longer support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the core of the star collapses, its outer layers are blasted outward in cosmic explosions we call supernovas.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is a process that scientists are keen to understand, as these explosions fling the heavy elements forged during the stars' lifetimes into surrounding galaxies. This material becomes the building blocks of the next generation of stars, planets, and possibly even life.

UVEX will also investigate what happens to the end products of some supernovas, neutron stars, when they meet and merge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, neutron stars contain between one and two times the mass of the sun crammed into a width of around 12 miles (20 kilometers). That means they are composed of matter so dense that, if a teaspoon of it were brought to Earth, it would weigh over 1 billion tons. That's equivalent to stacking around 9 million adult blue whales on a spoon.

So, when neutron stars in binary systems spiral together and merge, they create an environment so violent that it's the only place in the universe where scientists are sure that elements heavier than lead, like gold, silver, and platinum, are able to be forged.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, currently, neutron star mergers are detected via ripples in spacetime called gravitational waves. Scientists can then follow up on the aftermath of the mergers by observing them in electromagnetic light, from high-energy gamma rays to low-energy radio waves. Thus, UVEX will add another aspect to the investigation of neutron star collisions and our understanding of where heavy elements originate.

The new space telescope's maneuverability will allow it to observe these explosive events very shortly after they happen, giving it an advantage over other instruments, including NASA's long-serving Hubble Space Telescope.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "with uvex, we will now be able to follow up on gravitational-wave events in ultraviolet light," uvex team member and caltech scientist mansi kasliwal said in the same statement. Hubble is, of course, amazing and does have some ultraviolet capabilities, but it cannot rapidly pivot to observe real-time events. "I can count on two hands how many spectra we have of transient events in their infancy phase with the Hubble Space Telescope. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, uvex will also be revolutionary in the study of blue stars that have had their outer layers of hydrogen stripped away by companion stars. These stars offer researchers a unique opportunity to study the interior of stars, which is usually obscured by their outer layers.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we will be able to see what's inside the stars," kareem el-badry, an associate professor of astronomy at caltech and a member of the uvex team, said in the same statement. "We only know of a small number of stripped stars of this type now. UVEX will find hundreds. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, all of the above elements discussed are the expected discoveries and investigations that uvex will be involved with. Perhaps even more exciting, however, are the unexpected elements of the universe it will uncover.

"Every time you look at the skies in a new wavelength, you learn something new and unexpected," El-Badry said.

#361. Einstein's equations reveal how gravity could break, reconnect, and release energy

📅 08 Nov 2026

Einstein's equations reveal how gravity could break, reconnect, and release energy

Tanggal: 08 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104084011.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa more than 100 years after albert einstein developed his theory of gravity, physicists have uncovered a surprising possibility hidden within his equations. Their work suggests that gravitational fields can undergo a process in which their underlying structures break and reconnect, allowing energy to flow from gravity into matter.

Berdasarkan laporan, the phenomenon, known as "gravitational reconnection," bears an unexpected resemblance to a process responsible for some of the sun's most powerful eruptions. Researchers believe this connection could provide new insights into how gravity behaves under extreme conditions, including during collisions between black holes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the discovery comes from luca comisso, an associate research scientist in columbia university's departments of astronomy and physics and the columbia astrophysics laboratory, and felipe a. Asenjo of Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez in Chile. By examining Einstein's equations from a different mathematical perspective, they identified a remarkable similarity between gravity and the behavior of electrically charged gases known as plasmas.

Berdasarkan laporan, their approach could help scientists uncover fundamental rules governing the behavior of gravitational fields. Such insights are especially valuable in regions where gravity severely distorts space-time, making even the most powerful computer simulations difficult to interpret.

How Gravity Could Behave Like a Solar Flare.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the key to understanding this discovery lies in a well-known phenomenon called magnetic reconnection. Magnetic fields are often illustrated using curved lines, such as the patterns formed by iron filings around a magnet or the enormous magnetic loops extending above the Sun's surface.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a plasma, which consists of electrically charged particles, these magnetic field lines can be pulled, twisted, and stretched. Under certain conditions, they undergo a sudden change in their connections, releasing stored magnetic energy into the surrounding particles. This process powers solar flares and ranks among the most important mechanisms for releasing energy throughout the universe.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "magnetic reconnection is when these field lines, in some specific configuration, break and reattach in a different configuration," comisso said. "When they break and reconnect, they release energy. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the resulting energy transfer can produce extraordinarily powerful events. As Comisso explained, "It takes energy from the magnetic field and gives it to the particles in the plasma, producing explosions, energetic events. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers found that gravitational fields may undergo an analogous transformation. However, gravity operates within Einstein's four-dimensional space-time, which includes three dimensions of space and one dimension of time. This makes its underlying mathematical structure different from that of an ordinary magnetic field.

Gravitational Reconnection and the Fabric of Space-Time.

Berdasarkan laporan, "because space-time is four-dimensional rather than three-dimensional, gravity involves something like field 'sheets' rather than field lines," explained comisso. You can think of it as putting many lines together to form a 'sheet. "Adding one dimension to a line gives you a plane. '".

Berdasarkan laporan, in this mathematical description, gravity is represented by sheets rather than individual field lines. Just as magnetic field lines can change their connections and release energy, these gravitational sheets can also rearrange their connections under the appropriate conditions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, importantly, the sheets are mathematical representations, not physical surfaces that literally tear apart. Their reconnection describes a way for the gravitational field to transfer energy into matter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers arrived at this result by exploring properties of einstein's equations that are not obvious in their usual mathematical form. Their work builds on an earlier investigation that revealed previously unrecognized restrictions on how space-time can bend, stretch, and change over time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the new study, titled "reconnection of gravitational fields," was published in physical review d, a journal of the american physical society. It extends findings from an earlier study published in Physical Review Letters by Comisso, Asenjo, and Maricarmen A. Winkler.

Diungkapkan bahwa that earlier work identified mathematical constraints that determine which changes in the geometry of space-time are possible. Although these restrictions are built into Einstein's theory, they had not previously been recognized in this form.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "einstein's equations contain constraints on how space-time can evolve that are not immediately apparent," said asenjo. "By revealing these hidden new properties, we can begin to understand the fundamental rules governing how this gravitational reconnection process behaves. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, in their latest research, comisso and asenjo investigated what happens when the ideal conditions that normally preserve connections within gravitational field structures no longer hold. They found that those connections can change, producing the phenomenon they call gravitational reconnection.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "some implications are hidden in the equations, and they are not straightforward to capture just by looking at them," comisso said. "You need to rewrite them in a different way, and then you can exploit that behavior. ".

Why Plasma Physics Offers New Clues About Gravity.

Diungkapkan bahwa the breakthrough depends on a different mathematical formulation of einstein's equations developed by physicists in recent years. Although this formulation uses different variables, it is mathematically equivalent to the original equations and describes the same underlying physics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what makes it particularly useful is its resemblance to equations used to study plasmas. These electrically charged gases make up the Sun, are used in nuclear fusion experiments, and occupy much of the space between stars.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, comisso has devoted his career to understanding plasma behavior. When he and his colleagues recognized the mathematical similarities between plasma physics and gravity, they realized that methods developed to study magnetic fields could also reveal previously overlooked properties of gravitational fields.

This approach allows physicists to identify patterns and restrictions governing space-time without necessarily solving every part of Einstein's equations.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it helps us predict some patterns of the space-time," comisso said. "Even without doing the full calculation, we know that space-time needs to behave in a certain way, that it needs to satisfy those constraints. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, rather than relying entirely on complex numerical calculations, researchers can use these underlying rules to determine which behaviors are physically possible. This could provide a valuable new perspective on gravitational events that are exceptionally difficult to model.

What Gravitational Reconnection Could Mean for Black Holes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the most promising applications involves black hole collisions. When two black holes approach and merge, their immense gravitational fields produce extreme distortions in space-time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to understand these events, astrophysicists typically rely on massive supercomputer simulations. Researchers specify the initial conditions, calculate how the system changes over time, and examine the resulting behavior.

Diungkapkan bahwa these simulations help scientists predict the gravitational waves generated by merging black holes. Gravitational waves are ripples in space-time that can be detected by instruments such as the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO), which is designed to measure the extraordinarily small distortions produced by powerful cosmic events.

Berdasarkan laporan, the newly identified rules governing gravitational fields could complement these simulations by revealing patterns that might otherwise be difficult to recognize. They may also help researchers better understand how energy is transferred during some of the universe's most extreme gravitational interactions.

Berdasarkan laporan, for now, gravitational reconnection remains a theoretical finding. Scientists have not yet established how the process operates in actual astrophysical environments or whether its effects can be observed.

Berdasarkan laporan, the next step is to investigate gravitational reconnection in specific situations, particularly when black holes merge. Comisso hopes this research will eventually make it possible to estimate how much energy such events release and determine whether gravitational reconnection produces recognizable signatures in gravitational wave signals.

If those predictions can be developed and tested, the approach could offer a powerful new way to investigate the behavior of gravity under extreme conditions, revealing more of the physics concealed within Einstein's century-old equations.

The research received support from the National Science Foundation and NASA.

#363. The Polar Vortex Is About to Make Weather Weird From the UK to the US

📅 12 Nov 2026

The Polar Vortex Is About to Make Weather Weird From the UK to the US

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/the-polar-vortex-is-about-to-make-weather-weird-from-the-uk-to-the-us/

Sebagaimana diketahui, a critical blockade against some of nature’s coldest air has temporarily broken down—and much earlier in the year than normal. Disruptions in this circulation, known as the polar vortex, often push intensely cold air out of the Arctic toward lower latitudes.

Berdasarkan laporan, experts still aren’t entirely sure how the current collapse will play out in our everyday weather. But it’s another sign that we may be in for a wild ride over the weeks and months to come.

Diungkapkan bahwa the polar vortex is a band of upper-level winds wrapping around the arctic circle like a dam. This circulation is usually strong and stable, helping to keep the season’s coldest air locked near the North Pole. But the winds occasionally weaken or even reverse course, which can set off an atmospheric chain reaction, allowing bitterly cold air to spill southward.

Diungkapkan bahwa the manner in which the polar vortex breaks down determines what kind of weather conditions we might expect. Upper-level winds dipping southward in troughs are responsible for brief spells of cold temperatures. These “lobes” of the polar vortex, as they’re known, are relatively common in a typical winter.

Berdasarkan laporan, sometimes, this circulation can splinter into smaller pieces. If the vortex were a flowing river, these fragments are like leaves stuck on the riverbank, forcing extremely cold air to linger over the same areas for days or weeks at a time.

Berdasarkan laporan, one such case made this phenomenon a household name. A highly disrupted polar vortex in early 2015 sent a weeks-long burst of cold air sweeping over the eastern US. Chicago recorded its coldest February in nearly 140 years. In Lexington, Kentucky, temperatures bottomed out at –18 degrees Fahrenheit, as subfreezing air dove all the way to the Gulf of Mexico.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, seeing a breakdown of the polar vortex this early in the season is unprecedented in the historical record. Disruptions of this extent typically don’t occur until the latter half of winter. Based on the latest data, the circulation’s reversal began on Tuesday, and computer model guidance expects it to last through Thursday.

Diungkapkan bahwa weather patterns take a few weeks to respond to a polar vortex disruption, if at all. Given that reliable forecasts only extend about 10 days into the future, we can’t know where in the northern hemisphere cold air from the Arctic may spill.

While experts are still debating the exact causes driving this polar vortex breakdown, the event throws another wrench into a cool season already dominated by another unprecedented event: the strongest El Niño on record.

Historically warm sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific Ocean have already significantly affected conditions around the world, and this influence will only grow heading into the winter months.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, much of north america can expect warmer-than-normal conditions during a winter dominated by a strong el niño. But every event is different, and now with a sudden disruption in the polar vortex, those forecasts are less certain, because unexpected things can happen when unprecedented phenomena overlap.

But first, SpaceX has to successfully recover and refly both stages, something it's never done before — and that's where Flight 15 comes in. Here's when to tune in.
