#365. Scientists wipe out deadly brain tumors in every mouse tested with new cancer therapy

📅 08 Nov 2026

Scientists wipe out deadly brain tumors in every mouse tested with new cancer therapy

Tanggal: 08 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104084009.htm

Scientists at UC San Francisco have developed a new type of immune cell therapy that activates only after entering the brain, allowing it to attack cancer while remaining inactive elsewhere in the body.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in experiments involving mice, the engineered cells successfully eliminated diffuse midline glioma (dmg), an aggressive childhood brain cancer that spreads into surrounding healthy tissue. The treatment also provided lasting protection. When researchers introduced cancer cells again several weeks later, the immune cells continued fighting and prevented new tumors from developing.

Berdasarkan laporan, dmg is among the most difficult childhood cancers to treat. It grows into the brainstem, a critical region that regulates breathing, heartbeat, and swallowing. Nearly all children diagnosed with the disease die within a year, and existing treatments have had little success in stopping its progression.

Berdasarkan laporan, the experimental therapy, called b-sync car-t, could offer a new way forward. Unlike conventional CAR-T treatments, which have struggled against brain tumors, these modified immune cells are programmed to activate their cancer-fighting machinery specifically within the brain. Researchers suspect this targeted approach makes the cells more effective, although the precise reason remains unclear.

The promising results have prompted scientists to prepare for clinical trials at UCSF Health, potentially beginning as early as April 2027.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's been a struggle to make car-t cells that overcome dmg without causing unacceptable side effects," said hideho okada, md, phd, a professor of neurological surgery at ucsf and co-corresponding author of the study, published october 28 in science translational medicine. "By limiting B-SYNC's CAR expression to when and where it matters -- in the brain -- we saw consistent, total shutdown of DMG tumors in the lab. ".

Engineering Smarter CAR-T Cells to Fight Brain Cancer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, b-sync builds on years of research by okada and wendell lim, phd, a professor of cellular and molecular pharmacology at ucsf. Their goal has been to develop immune cells that can recognize and destroy brain tumors with greater precision.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, car-t therapy works by modifying the body's t cells, a type of immune cell, so they carry special receptors called cars. These receptors recognize proteins on cancer cells and trigger an immune attack. Although CAR-T treatments have shown success against certain cancers, brain tumors have remained particularly difficult to overcome.

In 2021, Okada and Lim reported encouraging laboratory findings with an earlier therapy called E-SYNC, designed to treat glioblastoma, another aggressive form of brain cancer.

Diungkapkan bahwa e-sync uses a molecular sensing system known as synnotch to identify egfrviii, a mutated protein found on some glioblastoma cells. When this protein is detected, synNotch directs the immune cell to produce a CAR that recognizes two additional tumor-associated proteins, EphA2 and IL13Rα2. This two-step process proved more effective than conventional CAR-T strategies that rely on a single activation step.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, the approach had an important limitation. Even when the protein is initially present, tumors can lose it as treatment eliminates the cancer cells carrying it. Only about 20% of patients have tumors containing EGFRvIII. This allows remaining cancer cells to escape detection.

To overcome that problem, the researchers searched for a more dependable signal that could activate the therapy in a wider range of patients.

A Molecular Switch That Activates Inside the Brain.

The scientists identified brevican, a protein naturally distributed throughout the brain, as a promising alternative.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they redesigned the synnotch system so that it would trigger car production only when it encountered brevican. Once activated, these "B-SYNC" CAR-T cells could search for cancer cells carrying EphA2 or IL13Rα2, even if those cells lacked EGFRvIII.

Berdasarkan laporan, this meant the engineered immune cells no longer depended on a tumor-specific mutation to become active. Instead, they used a protein associated with the brain itself as the signal to begin their attack.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although b-sync was initially developed for glioblastoma, the researchers recognized that it might also work against dmg. Both cancers commonly display EphA2 and IL13Rα2 on their tumor cells, making them potential targets for the same treatment.

Senthilnath Lakshmanachetty, PhD, a postdoctoral researcher in Okada's laboratory, led experiments to investigate whether B-SYNC could successfully attack this deadly childhood cancer.

New CAR-T Therapy Eliminates Brain Tumors in Mice.

The researchers first administered B-SYNC CAR-T cells intravenously (IV) to mice implanted with human DMG cells.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some of the engineered immune cells traveled through the bloodstream and entered the brain. Once there, they began producing the cancer-targeting CAR receptors and attacking tumor cells.

Sebagaimana diketahui, importantly, this activation appeared to occur only in the intended location. B-SYNC cells elsewhere in the body, including those circulating in the blood or present in the spleen, did not produce the CAR receptors.

That was "just as we designed it," Lakshmanachetty said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the team next examined whether delivering the treatment directly into the brain would produce stronger results. They administered B-SYNC using an intracerebroventricular (ICV) injection, which introduces the cells into the brain's fluid-filled ventricles.

Diungkapkan bahwa the results were striking. In two mouse models containing human DMG tumors, the treatment completely eliminated the cancer in every mouse tested. Conventional CAR-T cells, by comparison, were unable to bring the tumors under control.

The findings suggested that activating the engineered immune cells specifically within the brain could overcome some of the obstacles that have limited earlier CAR-T treatments.

Immune Cells Keep Fighting Long After Tumors Disappear.

Sebagaimana diketahui, destroying the original tumors was only part of the achievement. The researchers also wanted to determine whether the engineered immune cells could remain active and protect against cancer returning.

Nearly seven weeks after the initial treatment, they introduced another round of DMG cells into mice that had already received B-SYNC.

Every treated mouse rejected the new cancer cells, demonstrating that the therapy's protective effects continued well beyond the initial elimination of the tumors.

Further observations showed that B-SYNC cells remained functional more than 70 days after treatment.

Diungkapkan bahwa one possible explanation involves a problem known as t cell exhaustion. When immune cells remain activated for extended periods, they can gradually lose their ability to attack cancer effectively. By preventing CAR activation until the cells reach the brain, B-SYNC may help preserve their strength for when they encounter tumor cells.

The researchers believe this could be an important reason why their approach performed better than conventional CAR-T therapies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we didn't expect b-sync car-t cells to necessarily persist," lakshmanachetty said. "But they are still patrolling for cancer over 70 days out -- and they're still very functional. ".

With the laboratory results demonstrating both tumor elimination and lasting immune activity, the UCSF team is now working to move B-SYNC into human testing.

Diungkapkan bahwa okada, lim, and lakshmanachetty are collaborating with ucsf cancer specialists to prepare clinical trials. The proposed treatment will use each patient's own T cells, which will be genetically modified to become B-SYNC CAR-T cells.

The transition from laboratory research to clinical testing is moving relatively quickly, reflecting the encouraging findings from the animal experiments.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first trial will be led by ucsf physicians marie jaeger-krause, md, and sabine mueller, md, phd. Researchers plan to evaluate different combinations of intravenous delivery and direct administration into the brain.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for patients receiving icv treatment, surgeons will implant a shunt connecting the brain's ventricles to a reservoir positioned beneath the scalp. This system will allow doctors to administer repeated doses of the engineered immune cells without requiring a new surgical procedure each time.

Although the treatment has not yet been tested for effectiveness in humans, its ability to completely eliminate tumors and prevent their return in mice has generated considerable optimism.

Berdasarkan laporan, "diffuse midline glioma is a heartbreaking diagnosis for patients and their families," said mueller, director of the ucsf pediatric brain tumor center, ucsf professor of neurology, neurosurgery, and pediatrics, and co-founder of the pediatric neuro-oncology consortium (pnoc). This is exactly the kind of innovative approach they deserve. "This preclinical data is very promising. Mice with DMG are being cured, and we are incredibly excited to bring this therapy to the children and young adults we care for. ".

#369. Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined

📅 07 Nov 2026

Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined

Tanggal: 07 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012333.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, picture the wilderness of central europe 100,000 years ago, or even a million years ago. You might imagine an endless expanse of towering trees, with thick canopies blocking sunlight from reaching the ground. But according to a major new study, that familiar image of Europe's ancient forests is probably misleading.

Sebagaimana diketahui, instead, much of the continent was a vibrant landscape of scattered trees, open woodlands, grassy clearings, and colorful wildflower meadows. Birds and butterflies flourished in these sunlit habitats, while enormous grazing animals helped prevent trees and shrubs from taking over.

Diungkapkan bahwa researchers led by aarhus university have found that this mixture of habitats dominated europe's landscapes for more than 20 million years. Far from being the continent's original natural condition, the dense, dark forests common in many parts of Europe today appear to be a relatively recent development in its ecological history.

Berdasarkan laporan, published in biological conservation, the findings challenge a longstanding assumption about what europe's wilderness looked like before widespread human intervention. They also raise important questions about modern reforestation programs, which often prioritize planting dense forests to combat climate change and protect biodiversity.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the study shows that current reforestation practices are on the wrong track - both here in denmark, where subsidies are only granted for planting dense forests, and elsewhere in europe. This will not only be harmful for biodiversity; it will be in direct contradiction to the type of ecosystems that Europe's species have evolved in over millions of years," says Professor Jens-Christian Svenning from the Center for Ecological Dynamics in a Novel Biosphere (ECONOVO), Department of Biology at Aarhus University, senior author of the study.

Challenging the Myth of Europe's Ancient Forests.

Diungkapkan bahwa for decades, conservation strategies have been influenced by the "closed-forest paradigm. " This is the belief that dense forests with nearly continuous tree canopies were Europe's natural landscape before humans began clearing land for agriculture and settlements.

Under this view, restoring nature often means allowing trees to reclaim open areas or planting forests where they no longer exist.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new research suggests that this approach may overlook a crucial part of europe's ecological history. Rather than being uniformly covered by dense forests, the continent was characterized by changing combinations of grasslands, shrubs, and woodlands with different amounts of tree cover.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these landscapes supported a rich variety of species adapted to both wooded and open environments. Large plant-eating animals also played a major role in maintaining this diversity by grazing, browsing, and disturbing vegetation.

What 23 Million Years of Evidence Reveals.

To reconstruct Europe's ancient environments, the researchers examined an unusually extensive collection of evidence spanning millions of years.

Berdasarkan laporan, previous studies have generally concentrated on more recent periods. This investigation extended much further into the past, examining paleoecological records from the Miocene epoch (which began around 23 million years ago) through the pre-industrial era.

Diungkapkan bahwa paleoecology is the study of ancient ecosystems using clues preserved in fossils, sediments, and other natural records. Because no single type of evidence can provide a complete picture of the distant past, the team combined several independent methods.

Diungkapkan bahwa these included fossilized pollen and larger plant remains, charcoal left by ancient wildfires, and chemical signatures preserved in the teeth and bones of plant-eating animals. The researchers also examined fossil insects and mammals, along with ancient environmental DNA recovered from sediments.

Diungkapkan bahwa environmental dna consists of genetic material left behind by organisms in their surroundings. When preserved in ancient deposits, it can help scientists identify plants and animals that lived in an area long ago.

Together, these different sources of evidence allowed the researchers to reconstruct not only what types of vegetation existed, but also how ecosystems changed over time and how animals influenced their surroundings.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "each type of proxy offers its own perspective, but together they let us see whether the landscapes were covered by dense forests, open grasslands, or a mix of the two. By combining these datasets across time - from the Miocene to the pre-industrial era - we could trace long-term changes in vegetation and the role of large herbivores with much greater confidence than earlier studies that used only one method," explains the study's lead author, ECONOVO PhD student Szymon Czyzewski of Aarhus University.

Berdasarkan laporan, the evidence points to a consistent pattern. Across more than 20 million years, Europe's landscapes were typically a shifting mosaic of trees, open spaces, and flowering plants rather than continuous stretches of closed forest.

Sebagaimana diketahui, importantly, these mixed landscapes were not limited to one particular climate. They existed under temperate conditions comparable to those in much of Europe today, as well as during warmer and colder periods.

Elephants, Rhinos, and Bison Shaped Europe's Wilderness.

One of the most striking findings concerns the influence of large wild herbivores.

Berdasarkan laporan, ancient europe was home to animals such as elephants, rhinoceroses, aurochs, and bison. By feeding on vegetation and disturbing the ground as they moved, these animals helped keep parts of the landscape open.

Their activities created opportunities for grasses, wildflowers, and other plants that might otherwise have struggled beneath dense tree cover.

This constant interaction between animals and vegetation helped sustain a diverse mixture of habitats, providing suitable conditions for many different species.

Sebagaimana diketahui, modern europe, however, is missing much of this ecological influence. Many of the large wild herbivores that once shaped its landscapes have disappeared, and traditional grazing practices have also declined.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the ecosystems we see in europe today lack the large wild herbivores that not only shaped landscapes but also sustained its biodiversity for millions of years. The most dramatic shift has largely taken place within the last hundred years, when traditional extensive grazing disappeared from large parts of the landscape," says Czyzewski.

This loss of grazing pressure has changed how vegetation develops across much of the continent, helping explain why present-day European ecosystems differ so dramatically from those of the distant past.

Europe's Ancient Woodlands Were Full of Wildflowers.

The research also offers a different perspective on species commonly associated with farmland and other human-managed environments.

Berdasarkan laporan, birds such as larks and jackdaws, along with mammals such as the european hamster, are often regarded as characteristic of agricultural landscapes. Yet the researchers suggest that their evolutionary histories likely extend back to the open woodland environments that existed long before modern farming.

Even familiar wildflowers have connections to these ancient ecosystems.

Wild poppies, now frequently seen growing in agricultural fields, also thrived in areas where large grazing animals disturbed vegetation within ancient woodlands.

These findings challenge the sharp distinction between "forest" and "open habitats" that often guides conservation planning today.

Berdasarkan laporan, in europe's ecological past, trees, meadows, shrubs, and grazing animals were not necessarily separate parts of nature. They frequently existed together, forming interconnected habitats that supported a wide range of wildlife.

Why Planting More Trees May Not Always Help Nature.

The findings arrive as European countries continue expanding forests to capture carbon dioxide, address climate change, and restore biodiversity.

Although forests can provide important environmental benefits, the researchers argue that planting large areas of uniformly dense woodland may not be the best approach when the goal is to restore Europe's native ecosystems.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many european species evolved in landscapes containing a mixture of trees and open areas. Converting these habitats into continuous closed-canopy forests could therefore reduce the variety of environments available to wildlife.

The study suggests that restoration efforts should focus more strongly on maintaining diverse landscapes, including open grasslands, scattered woodland, and areas shaped by natural grazing.

"Instead, restoration efforts should place greater emphasis on creating and maintaining mosaics of woodland and open habitats - not least through the restoration of natural-living large herbivores," Svenning concludes.

The findings add to a growing body of research from the same scientific group suggesting that large animals played a far greater role in shaping Europe's ecosystems than previously recognized.

They also reinforce the idea that Europe's ancient landscapes were generally brighter, more open, and more varied than the dense primeval forests often depicted in popular imagination.

Rather than restoring nature by simply planting more trees, the researchers suggest that protecting biodiversity may require recreating the complex balance of woodlands, meadows, and grazing animals that shaped the continent for millions of years.

The familiar image of Europe as a vast, dark, unbroken forest may be deeply rooted in our understanding of nature, but millions of years of evidence are painting a very different picture.

#372. Scientists squeeze record-breaking X-ray power into an incredibly tiny spot

📅 08 Nov 2026

Scientists squeeze record-breaking X-ray power into an incredibly tiny spot

Tanggal: 08 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012329.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists have achieved a new world record by producing extraordinarily intense x-ray flashes that last just 300 attoseconds, an almost unimaginably brief period of time. Using the European XFEL, a powerful X-ray research facility, the team concentrated the flashes into an area roughly 100,000 times smaller than the cross-section of a typical human hair.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by squeezing so much x-ray energy into such a tiny space, the researchers created an exceptionally powerful beam that could open new possibilities for studying the behavior of electrons inside atoms and molecules. The breakthrough could eventually help scientists observe the rapid movements of electrons during chemical reactions and potentially even learn to control them.

The experiment took place in April 2026, and the findings have now been published in the scientific journal Optica.

Record-Breaking X-Ray Flashes Last Just 300 Attoseconds.

"This is a world record in intensity and fluence for a hard-X-ray attosecond pulse," says Ichiro Inoue from the University of Tokyo, first author of the publication.

Diungkapkan bahwa hard x-rays are a form of light with extremely short wavelengths. Scientists use two measurements to describe their extraordinary power. Fluence refers to the amount of energy delivered to a particular area, while intensity also considers how quickly that energy is delivered.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this experiment, each x-ray pulse lasted an estimated 300 attoseconds (an attosecond is a billionth of a billionth of a second). Such incredibly short flashes offer researchers a way to investigate events that unfold far too quickly for conventional observation.

Berdasarkan laporan, to concentrate the x-rays, the team used a specialized optical arrangement called an advanced kirkpatrick-baez, or akb, system. It consists of two exceptionally precise mirrors that focus the beam in different directions. Each pulse underwent four reflections in total, with one mirror focusing the X-rays vertically and the other horizontally.

Diungkapkan bahwa the result was an astonishingly small focal spot measuring just 180 × 330 nanometers (a nanometre is a billionth of a meter). By directing the energy into this microscopic area, the researchers were able to achieve record-breaking intensity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "a few years ago, we demonstrated terawatt-scale hard x-ray attosecond pulses at the european xfel," says desy scientist jiawei yan, one of the corresponding authors of the study. "But generating powerful pulses is only the first step. With this advance, we can now use attosecond X-rays to explore highly nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter. For experiments, what really matters is what we can deliver to the sample. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these nonlinear interactions occur when extremely intense x-rays cause matter to respond in ways that would not normally happen under weaker illumination. Studying such effects could reveal new details about how atoms and electrons behave under extreme conditions.

An Extraordinary Reaction Inside Copper Atoms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to confirm the exceptional intensity of their x-ray pulses, the researchers directed them at a thin sheet of copper. The experiment provided independent evidence that the focused flashes reached peak intensities exceeding 10²⁰ watts per square centimeter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the x-rays struck the copper, they knocked electrons out of the atoms' innermost electron shells, leaving behind empty positions known as 'holes'. Electrons from other parts of the atoms then moved into these vacancies, releasing energy in the form of X-ray light.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, under ordinary circumstances, this emitted light travels in many different directions. However, when the incoming X-rays become sufficiently intense, something remarkable happens. The emitted light can stimulate other excited copper atoms to release additional X-rays traveling in the same direction, producing an amplified beam.

Scientists call this phenomenon amplified spontaneous emission, or ASE.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it is almost magical to see this happening," says anders madsen, group leader at the mid instrument, where the study was conducted. "Normal fluorescence goes in all directions, regardless of the direction of the incoming beam. But when the ASE threshold is crossed, you see the light cone starting to condense into the forward direction. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the team also observed another important signature of extreme intensity. As they increased the energy of the X-ray pulses, the amplified signal initially became much stronger. At higher energies, however, the increase slowed and eventually leveled off, a behavior known as saturation.

Diungkapkan bahwa this pattern is expected only under exceptionally intense x-ray illumination. Its appearance provided additional confirmation of the record intensity calculated from the pulse energy, duration, and size of the focused beam.

A New Way to Explore the Hidden World of Electrons.

Beyond setting a world record, the breakthrough could significantly expand scientists' ability to investigate some of nature's fastest processes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, electrons play a central role in determining how atoms bond together, how molecules interact, and how chemical reactions unfold. Their movements happen on extraordinarily short timescales, making them difficult to observe directly.

Diungkapkan bahwa by combining ultrashort x-ray flashes with extremely high intensity, researchers hope to capture information about electrons before the incoming radiation has time to substantially alter the material being studied. This could provide a clearer picture of electron behavior inside atoms and molecules and, in the longer term, potentially lead to methods for influencing electron motion during chemical reactions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the advanced kirkpatrick-baez mirror system used for the record-setting experiment was transported from japan. European XFEL is now preparing to receive its own AKB system, with delivery expected in early 2027.

The new equipment is being funded through a collaboration with the University of Hamburg, with additional support from the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR).

Sebagaimana diketahui, once the system has been installed and commissioned, scientists from around the world using the mid instrument are expected to gain access to these exceptionally brief and intense x-ray flashes. The upgraded capabilities could allow researchers to investigate electron behavior at a level of detail that has previously been difficult to achieve, bringing them closer to understanding and potentially controlling the fundamental processes behind chemical reactions.

In any respectable audiobook project, finding the names of Andy Weir ("The Martian," "Project Hail Mary") and Benjamin Percy ("The Ninth Metal," "Wolverine") attached would elicit intense fan interest, but add the superstar vocal talents of Anthony Mackie ("Avengers: Infinity War," "Avengers: Doomsday"), Ariana DeBose ("West Side Story"), and John Leguizamo ("Ice Age"), and it catapults this sonic odyssey into the stratosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, such is the case with "exoplanet," audible original’s new 7-episode science fiction audio drama executive produced by weir and penned by percy. Its planet-hopping space disaster narrative sees the crew of the starship Wild Blue Yonder hit a quantum anomaly, forcing their ship to crash-land onto a deadly exoplanet. All is not as it seems, though, as each crew member arrives in a different era on the same world.

We hooked up with Mackie, DeBose, and Lequizamo to learn more about this renaissance of audio dramas and what attracted them to board Weir's sci-fi thriller.

Diungkapkan bahwa one crew. Three timelines. No one survives alone. One planet. A sci-fi thriller executive produced by Andy Weir (#1 bestselling author of Project Hail Mary, The Martian), with an all-star cast led by Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose and John Leguizamo.

Exoplanet is free for Audible members, but also available for purchase separately.

Diungkapkan bahwa mackie voices chief engineer jeff shaw. His attraction to the imaginative genre began at an early age thanks to some cool family friends while growing up in the Big Easy.

Berdasarkan laporan, "my brother went to college at morehouse," he tells space. He’d always bring friends home, because New Orleans is a party city, so they'd come over and get drunk. But one of his friends gave me a book by Walter Mosley and one by Octavia Butler, and I got hooked into sci-fi and the future. "I was like 8, and he was 18. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "from 'back to the future' to 'aliens,' the future was such an idea of what was going to be out there. The only thing more arrogant than wanting to be president is standing up and saying, 'Yeah, I can go to space. "It’s very important to me as a human being to have that construct as a part of my career. Now we’re living it," reveals Mackie. ' That sounds crazy to me. ".

Leguizamo's New York City childhood was influenced by absorbing classic radio dramas of the past, which primed him for this special Audible project.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it was anthony and ariana being in it that really pumped me up, and of course andy weir," he recalls regarding his portrayal of science officer logan bowers. "Then when I got the theme, that it was something relevant today and makes you think about computers and technology taking over and making us obsolete. It just hit me in that right zeitgeist, at that right little point. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "as a poor kid, there was no youtube or cell phones, and we didn’t have computers," reminisces leguizamo. I thought that was an incredible challenge. With no visuals, your voice has to create the world. It's a different art form. "I used to go to the Broadcast Museum on 53rd Street and listen to old radio plays like The Shadow and these incredible detective radio plays. ".

DeBose portrays the Wild Blue Yonder's confident First Officer Becca Bang, who’s stranded in a temporal mystery that might engulf her at any moment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i've yet to do anything like this, which is always exciting," she adds. It’s coming from brilliant minds who build worlds so impeccably. "I was a little afraid of it, which told me I should do it. I liked the idea that we could tell this story and make people listen and create a space for them to imagine themselves in it and see how they problem-solve to make the world a bit better. And it's about real stuff we’re dealing with today. These gents are so talented. It's great company. ".

Recording your character's lines is far more difficult than just stepping up to the microphone to read a script, and our ace "Exoplanet" trio delivered in every session.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i just go in and throw myself at something," debose recalls. It's great. "I don’t really have a method. But I can tell you this: it is a full-body workout. I just do what the character does and end up sweating. I love the idea of bringing back the radio play. And after three days, I have to go sit in silence. Even for myself. The art of listening is such a thing. I don’t think people listen enough. I use everything at my disposal, whether it’s a chair or a pillow or running in place. ".

Likewise, Leguizamo embraced his booth sessions with exuberance and authenticity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "you have to cancel the rest of your day, especially if you've got to talk, because your vocal chords are fried," he admits. It’s an interesting intersection where you pull it back a little and invite the audience in. If you run you have to run like a maniac and be out of breath. If I'm getting hit I start punching myself. You really have to do the physicality. "And if they're not fried you're not doing your job. Your voice has to have a little mystery, a little naughtiness. Then there’s a sexiness to doing these things. ”.

For Mackie, who’s used to athleticism needed to play MCU superheroes like The Falcon and Captain America, recording dialogue offered a different type of opportunity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i look for reasons not to talk to people, so i love doing these," he jokes. "Once I’m out of the studio, I’m not talking to anybody for two days. I’ve said enough words for the next month. I just have to come home at cut off. At a certain point for me, I find mentally I get tired of hearing myself talk. ”.

#376. Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive

📅 07 Nov 2026

Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive

Tanggal: 07 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012305.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, every human body produces carbon dioxide simply by converting food into energy. Although the amount released by one person may seem small, the combined output of billions of people adds up to an enormous quantity.

Diungkapkan bahwa a new study led by the university of bath estimates that carbon dioxide production from human metabolism increased by 74% between 1985 and 2015, reaching 2. 05 billion metric tons annually. The researchers found that the dramatic rise was primarily the result of population growth, rather than a substantial increase in how much CO2 each person produces.

Berdasarkan laporan, the findings could help scientists better understand the global carbon cycle, which describes how carbon moves between the atmosphere, living organisms, oceans, and land. By measuring humanity's contribution more accurately, researchers hope to improve predictions about how well efforts to reduce carbon emissions will work.

Why Human CO2 Emissions Are Different From Fossil Fuels.

Despite the enormous numbers, the researchers emphasize that the carbon dioxide produced by human metabolism is fundamentally different from the emissions generated by burning fossil fuels.

Berdasarkan laporan, when people breathe out co2, most of that carbon originally came from the food they consumed. Plants absorbed it from the atmosphere relatively recently, meaning it is already circulating through the natural carbon cycle.

Berdasarkan laporan, burning coal, oil, and natural gas is different. These fuels contain carbon that has remained trapped underground for millions of years. Burning them releases that long-stored carbon into the atmosphere, adding to the amount of CO2 circulating through the Earth's climate system.

The new research, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, was led by Professor Javier Gonzalez of the University of Bath's Centre for Exercise, Nutrition and Metabolism.

Diungkapkan bahwa the team calculated that global co2 production from human metabolism climbed from 1. 18 billion metric tons in 1985 to 2. 05 billion metric tons in 2015. More than 60% of that increase could be attributed to the growing number of people worldwide.

"We all produce carbon dioxide simply by turning food into energy, but until now we haven't had a good idea how much that adds up to worldwide.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "what we've found is that the increase is mainly because there are more of us. Ultimately, this information can help scientists more accurately predict how effective carbon reduction strategies may be. This gives scientists one more piece of the puzzle when working out where carbon comes from and where it goes. ".

How Scientists Measured Humanity's CO2 Production.

To estimate how much carbon dioxide people generate, the researchers analyzed thousands of measurements collected from individuals across the human lifespan, from infants to older adults.

Diungkapkan bahwa these measurements provided information about the co2 produced by the body during ordinary daily activities. The team then combined those findings with worldwide population figures and body weight data to calculate how human metabolic CO2 production had changed over time.

Berdasarkan laporan, the results showed that population growth was the dominant factor behind the 74% increase. Changes in the amount of carbon dioxide generated by individual people played a much smaller role.

Sebagaimana diketahui, accurately measuring this process is important because human metabolism contributes to the continuous movement of carbon through the environment. Its influence on local carbon measurements can be especially noticeable in densely populated cities and urban areas, where large numbers of people live and work close together.

Understanding these contributions can help researchers develop more complete carbon budgets, which track the sources, movements, and destinations of carbon within the Earth's systems.

Scientists Stress That Breathing Is Not Driving Climate Change.

Although the study reveals a surprisingly large amount of CO2 production, its findings should not be interpreted as evidence that human breathing is a major cause of global warming.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers are not recommending that people reduce their physical activity or change their diets to lower the carbon dioxide produced by their bodies. Instead, the goal is to make scientific measurements and calculations of the global carbon cycle more accurate.

Distinguishing between carbon dioxide produced through natural biological processes and carbon released by burning fossil fuels is essential for understanding the planet's changing climate.

Professor Gonzalez emphasized this distinction:.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the important thing is that the carbon dioxide we breathe out is not the same as burning fossil fuels. We're not saying that breathing is driving climate change.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "what this study does is give us a much clearer picture of how much co2 people produce around the world, and how that is changing as the population grows. This understanding can help improve the accuracy predictions of carbon reduction programs. ".

By establishing a clearer picture of humanity's metabolic CO2 production, the researchers have provided another piece of information scientists can use to track global carbon movements and evaluate strategies for reducing emissions.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Berdasarkan laporan, on nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field.

Sebagaimana diketahui, goce, its name was short for gravity field and steady-state ocean circulation explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the time, controllers weren't sure where goce would fall back to earth. Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it disintegrated about 50 miles above the falkland islands in the south atlantic ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity, mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents.

Diungkapkan bahwa the goce satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname.

Diungkapkan bahwa "goce's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,. " ESA officials said in a description.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there was more than looks behind goce's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude.

Diungkapkan bahwa goce was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space, leading to a fiery plunge to Earth.

Diungkapkan bahwa the large size of goce — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5. 3 meters) long and 3. 2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface.

#381. RSV vaccines slash infections: data show jabs’ staggering success against dangerous virus

📅 13 Nov 2026

RSV vaccines slash infections: data show jabs’ staggering success against dangerous virus

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03573-3

Diungkapkan bahwa thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Liam Drew is a freelance science journalist based near London.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, protection against the respiratory syncytial virus (rsv) must expand to lower-income countries, which are harder hit. Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “something’s wrong with the data. There are too few people in hospitals” with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), epidemiologist Caroline Klint Johannesen recalls a colleague remarking while analysing Danish health records for last winter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on 1 october 2025, denmark introduced a nationwide policy of vaccinating pregnant people against rsv — a respiratory pathogen that usually causes mild symptoms but can lead to severe disease and even death in vulnerable people, including infants and older adults. Maternal antibodies induced by the vaccine cross the placenta to protect babies for around the first six months of their lives, when they are most at risk. Newborns at high risk of severe disease, including premature infants, whose mothers had not been vaccinated, were given injections of monoclonal antibodies.

RSV wave hammers hospitals — but vaccines and treatments are coming.

RSV wave hammers hospitals — but vaccines and treatments are coming.

Diungkapkan bahwa johannesen, a vaccine researcher at nordsjællands hospital in hillerød, denmark, found1 that infant hospital admissions plummeted. The immunizations are working, she says (see ‘Newborn protection’).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the world health organization (who) estimates that every year, rsv hospitalizes roughly 3. 6 million and kills about 100,000 children under 5 years old. Of these deaths, 97% occur in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the virus is also dangerous to older adults — although those risks are widely underappreciated by both physicians and the public. But over the age of 60, hospitalizations and mortality increase with age, especially in people with other diseases such as chronic heart and lung conditions. Historically, testing has been sparse, and there are no global statistics for RSV-related adult deaths. In the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that between around 10,000 and 25,000 people have died in each of the past two winters, especially in older age groups.

Since 2022, when European regulators approved nirsevimab — a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV — a second antibody and three vaccines have been developed for use in adults, one of which is suitable for pregnant people.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s just remarkable,” says buddy creech, a paediatrician at vanderbilt university in nashville, tennessee, to have gone “from no mechanism to prevent rsv to an embarrassment of riches”. Dozens of countries across Europe, Asia and North and South America have launched various immunization programmes.

Berdasarkan laporan, doi: https://doi. org/10. 1038/d41586-026-03573-3.

#382. Scientists discover hidden brain changes linked to common sleep disorders

📅 08 Nov 2026

Scientists discover hidden brain changes linked to common sleep disorders

Tanggal: 08 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012303.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa sleep disorders may have consequences that extend far beyond fatigue. New research from Florida International University (FIU) has found that several types of sleep disorders are associated with physical changes in brain regions responsible for attention, motivation, and decision-making. These findings suggest that disrupted sleep may be connected to important differences in the brain's structure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, published in the journal scientific reports, the research offers one of the broadest examinations yet of the brain changes associated with different sleep disorders. The discoveries could eventually help scientists identify sleep problems earlier and develop treatments tailored to the specific brain systems involved.

What 57 Brain Imaging Studies Reveal About Sleep Disorders.

Diungkapkan bahwa an estimated 50 million to 70 million americans experience sleep disorders, making them a major public health concern. To investigate their effects on the brain, scientists at FIU's Center for Children and Families combined and analyzed findings from 57 studies that used brain imaging to examine adults.

Diungkapkan bahwa rather than focusing on a single condition, the researchers compared several sleep disorders to determine whether they were associated with similar changes in brain structure. This approach, which is still relatively uncommon in sleep research, also allowed the team to identify differences specific to certain disorders.

Diungkapkan bahwa the analysis focused on two broad groups. The second group, called parasomnias, includes sleepwalking, nightmare disorder, and sleep terrors. The first, known as dyssomnias, includes insomnia and sleep apnea, conditions that interfere with falling asleep, staying asleep, or getting sufficient restorative sleep. These conditions involve unusual events or behaviors that interrupt normal sleep cycles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "as more people recognize how important sleep is, there's growing urgency to understand what's happening in the brain," said matthew sutherland, a cognitive neuroscientist at fiu and senior author of the study. "By bringing together results from many studies, this research gives us a clearer picture of how sleep disorders affect brain structure and function and where we need to focus next. ".

Sleep Disorders Share Changes in a Critical Brain Region.

One of the most striking findings was that both groups of sleep disorders were associated with reductions in the thalamus, a structure deep within the brain that plays a central role in processing information, sustaining attention, and supporting complex thinking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers identified changes in a specific part of the thalamus called the pulvinar. This region helps the brain direct attention toward important information and manage cognitive control, which allows people to regulate their thoughts and actions while completing tasks.

Diungkapkan bahwa the affected areas are connected to larger brain networks that help people concentrate, make decisions, and respond to their surroundings. Differences in these systems may help explain why people with sleep disorders often experience slower reaction times, difficulty making decisions, and a greater likelihood of errors or accidents.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "most research looks at sleep disorders one at a time," said katharine crooks, a recent fiu cognitive neuroscience doctoral graduate and lead author of the study. "By looking across many studies, we found shared patterns in the brain that help explain why sleep problems can impact focus, decision-making and everyday functioning. With so many people struggling with sleep, understanding what is happening in the brain is key to finding better interventions, diagnostic tools and personalized treatments. ".

Sleepwalking and Nightmares Show Additional Brain Differences.

Although the researchers discovered common structural patterns across sleep disorders, they also found differences associated specifically with parasomnias.

Sebagaimana diketahui, people with these conditions showed changes in the posterior cingulate cortex, a brain region involved in motivation, decision-making, and the regulation of emotions. This finding may help explain why disorders such as sleepwalking, recurring nightmares, and sleep terrors can sometimes be accompanied by difficulties with mood, behavior, or emotional control.

In contrast, the analysis did not reveal a consistent pattern of structural changes found exclusively in dyssomnias, the category that includes insomnia and sleep apnea.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, together, these results suggest that different forms of disrupted sleep may be associated with both shared and distinct changes in the brain. The particular regions involved may depend on the nature of the sleep disorder.

Could Brain Imaging Lead to Better Sleep Disorder Treatments?.

The findings provide researchers with new clues about the relationship between sleep disorders and the brain systems that support everyday thinking and behavior.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by identifying which regions are associated with particular sleep problems, scientists hope to improve diagnostic methods and develop more personalized interventions. Future treatments could potentially aim not only to improve sleep quality but also to protect the brain networks involved in attention, decision-making, and emotional regulation.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, an important question remains unanswered. The research identified associations between sleep disorders and differences in brain structure, but it did not establish whether disrupted sleep causes those differences, whether existing brain differences contribute to sleep disorders, or whether both processes occur.

To investigate this relationship further, the FIU team plans to examine individual parasomnias in greater detail, including sleepwalking and REM sleep behavior disorder.

Understanding how these conditions relate to changes in the brain could help researchers develop better ways to recognize, manage, and potentially prevent some of the cognitive and emotional difficulties associated with disrupted sleep.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Berdasarkan laporan, astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the exoplanet, designated toi-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a "hot Jupiter. 25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world. The orbits of the planet weren't regular like those of other planets, with TOI-2535 b often arriving six hours early or six hours later than when astronomers expected. Then, in March this year, TESS was no longer spotting the characteristic drops in starlight that TOI-2535 b caused as it crossed, or "transited," the face of its parent star. It seemed to have vanished.

Diungkapkan bahwa this team used tess data to determine that toi-2535 b is being pulled on by an unseen neighbor and is, in turn, pulling on that planet as well. This is causing the orbits of both worlds in the TOI-2535 system to "wobble. " TOI-2535 b disappeared when that wobble tilted it out of alignment with its star.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular, but that's not true. We know of a few systems that are like this," team member Samuel Yee of the University of California, Los Angeles, said in a statement. "This is the most extreme example we've seen because the two planets are interacting so strongly. The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching. If there are multiple planets in a system, they can affect each other's orbits. ".

TOI-2535 b isn't expected to transit its parent star for at least 30 years, but the hidden neighbor tugging on it may cross the face of the star sooner than that.

In the meantime, scientists will attempt to decode what this extreme wobbling exoplanet system says about how it formed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is currently a lot of speculation about how hot jupiter planets like toi-2535 b form. That is because current routes of planet formation suggest planets like this would need to form around a great deal of ice. Obviously, ice isn't likely to be abundant as close to a star as TOI-2535 b is currently.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this means that hot jupiters likely form far from their stars and then migrate inwards. There are two ways that this could happen. The planet could be excited into an elliptical orbit by violent events like a near-collision with another planetary object, and then interactions with the star pull the planet inwards.

Alternatively, the hot Jupiter may be pulled inwards along with the other planets while sitting in a flattened cloud of gas and dust around the infant star called a protoplanetary disk.

Diungkapkan bahwa if this second, less turbulent route occurs to bring hot jupiters close to their stars, then the resultant system should be very flat. In other words, there shouldn't be extreme tilts between the orbits of the planets in that system.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, the tilt caused to toi-2535 b by its unseen companion indicates that flattened systems can be twisted by more tilted orbits later in their existence. This makes the slower migration possible despite the orbital tilt.

Berdasarkan laporan, "because toi-2535 b has a close neighbor, it probably migrated by slowly spiraling in instead of getting flung in," yee said. "We may be seeing a formation channel that doesn’t happen very often but is very interesting. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the team's research was published on monday (nov. 9) in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. ’s Open University. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U. Follow him on Twitter @sciencef1rst.

#388. SLAC scientists find conclusive proof of a mysterious third type of magnetism

📅 04 Nov 2026

SLAC scientists find conclusive proof of a mysterious third type of magnetism

Tanggal: 04 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012256.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for nearly 90 years, physicists have divided magnetic materials into two main categories: ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Now, scientists have confirmed that a third type exists, revealing a previously unrecognized form of magnetic behavior that could lead to major advances in computing and electronics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the breakthrough comes from a research team led by the u. Department of Energy's SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory. S. In a study published in Science, the researchers presented compelling experimental evidence for altermagnetism, a distinct magnetic phase that combines important characteristics of the two traditionally recognized types.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "in the past few years, scientists have observed phenomena that don't fit neatly into the ferromagnetism-antiferromagnetism dichotomy," explained lead author daniel jost, associate scientist at slac and stanford institute for materials and energy sciences. "Researchers have been compiling evidence of a third type of magnetism that bridges the qualities of these two classes. We believe our results provide robust experimental confirmation that this third phase -- altermagnetism -- is real. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the team focused on manganese telluride (mnte), a material that had long been classified as an antiferromagnet. Building on earlier research, the scientists identified direct evidence of chirality, a distinctive asymmetry in the material's magnetic structure. This property resembles the way a spiral staircase or screw twists in a particular direction and provides a crucial signature of altermagnetism.

Beyond its importance for fundamental physics, the finding could help researchers develop magnetic materials with properties suited to future technologies, including advanced memory systems, quantum devices, and more energy-efficient data centers.

Understanding the Two Traditional Types of Magnetism.

Sebagaimana diketahui, magnetism is familiar from everyday experiences, whether it is a refrigerator magnet holding up a photograph or a compass aligning with earth's magnetic field. But the physics behind these effects is far more complicated than it appears.

Berdasarkan laporan, at the atomic level, magnetism is connected to a quantum property of electrons known as spin. Scientists commonly describe the two possible spin orientations as "up" and "down. Although spin is not literally an electron rotating like a tiny ball, it behaves in certain ways as though the electron has its own angular momentum. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, when these spins become organized into particular patterns, a material can exhibit magnetic properties. However, that does not necessarily mean it will produce an externally detectable magnetic field.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in ferromagnetic materials, electron spins align in the same direction (up-up-up or down-down-down). Their combined effect produces the familiar magnetic field associated with ordinary magnets. People have used materials with this behavior for thousands of years.

Berdasarkan laporan, a second category, identified in 1933, works differently. In antiferromagnets, neighboring electron spins point in opposite directions (up-down-up-down). Because the magnetic contributions oppose one another, they cancel out, leaving no overall magnetization.

A Third Type of Magnetism Challenges the Old Rules.

Berdasarkan laporan, for almost nine decades, these two categories provided the basic framework for understanding how magnetic order arises in materials. However, experimental observations in recent years began revealing behavior that neither category could fully explain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some materials displayed alternating electron spins and no overall magnetization, just like antiferromagnets. Yet they could also support useful spin currents, a property associated with ferromagnetic behavior. Spin currents allow information to be carried through the spin properties of electrons rather than relying entirely on their electrical charge.

Berdasarkan laporan, the unusual combination suggested that scientists were dealing with something fundamentally different. In 2022, researchers introduced the term "altermagnets" for materials belonging to this proposed third magnetic class.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the key difference lies in the arrangement of atoms within the material. Altermagnets have alternating spin orientations (up-down-up-down), but the crystal structures surrounding the oppositely aligned spins are rotated relative to one another.

Diungkapkan bahwa this rotation breaks a form of symmetry that exists in conventional antiferromagnets. Although the distinction is subtle, it can dramatically change how electrons behave, allowing altermagnets to combine properties once considered incompatible.

Scientists Find the Missing Evidence for Altermagnetism.

Even as experimental support for altermagnetism accumulated, researchers still needed a decisive way to establish that it represented a genuinely distinct magnetic phase.

Berdasarkan laporan, "by 2024, there were some factors that spoke strongly in favor of altermagnetism being real," jost said, "but there was still a missing piece to the puzzle. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa that missing evidence involved chirality, a property sometimes described as "handedness. " An object is chiral when its mirror image cannot be perfectly aligned with the original. Human hands provide a simple example: Your left and right hands are mirror images, but a left hand cannot fit properly into a right-handed glove.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in an altermagnet, the unusual arrangement of atoms and electron spins can create this kind of handedness in the material's electronic and magnetic structure. Conventional antiferromagnets do not exhibit the same characteristic chiral signature.

Detecting that difference would provide a powerful way to distinguish a true altermagnet from a material that merely resembles one.

Berdasarkan laporan, the researchers selected manganese telluride as their test material. For decades, scientists considered it an ordinary antiferromagnet, but more recent studies had raised the possibility that it belonged to the newly proposed category.

Powerful X-Rays Reveal a Hidden Magnetic Signature.

Diungkapkan bahwa to investigate the material's unusual properties, the team conducted experiments at the european synchrotron radiation facility (esrf) in france. The facility's ID32 beamline produces precisely controlled polarized X-rays, allowing scientists to examine subtle magnetic structures that are otherwise extremely difficult to detect.

Berdasarkan laporan, the researchers used circularly polarized x-rays, which have electric fields that rotate in either a left-handed or right-handed direction as the light travels. By measuring how the material scattered these two forms of light, they could search for evidence of chirality.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "chiral materials scatter left-handed polarized x-ray beams differently than they do right-handed beams," explained jost. "Non-chiral materials would scatter each beam of light the same way. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the experiment revealed a clear difference in the way manganese telluride interacted with the two x-ray polarizations. This distinctive chiral response was precisely the kind of signal expected from altermagnetism and would not be present in a conventional antiferromagnet.

"This chiral signature gave us the solid experimental ground to say altermagnetism stands in a class of its own," Jost said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers first performed the experiment in 2024. They returned in early 2025 and repeated the measurements, successfully reproducing the results and strengthening the evidence for the new magnetic phase.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this technique helped us confirm that manganese telluride was really exhibiting altermagnetic properties," said rachel nickel, postdoctoral scientist with esrf, a co-author who helped design and conduct the experiment on the id32 beamline. "Altermagnetism was only proposed a few years ago, and the rapid progress in confirming these models is incredible. ".

Why Altermagnetism Could Transform Future Computers.

The discovery could have important consequences for spintronics, a growing field that seeks to use electron spin to develop more capable electronic devices.

Berdasarkan laporan, conventional electronics store and process information primarily by controlling the electrical charge of electrons. Spintronics adds another way to work with information by taking advantage of electron spin as well.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this extra capability could enable devices that operate faster, withstand interference more effectively, and consume substantially less electricity. Such improvements would be especially valuable in computer memory, large data centers, and other technologies that require enormous amounts of information processing.

However, the two traditional types of magnetism present different obstacles that have limited the development of spintronic systems.

Berdasarkan laporan, "ferromagnets are too easily influenced by magnetic fields," jost explained. "If you have a permanent magnet in your pocket and walk by a spintronic device built with ferromagnets, you could start flipping the bits, scrambling the information stored there. Antiferromagnets fix that problem, but they are practically invisible -- so you can't easily read the data stored in them or use them to drive efficient spin currents. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa altermagnets offer a potentially valuable alternative. Like antiferromagnets, their opposing spins produce no overall magnetization, helping protect them against unwanted magnetic interference. At the same time, their unusual electronic structure allows them to generate spin-polarized currents that can be used to retrieve information.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "altermagnets combine the best of both," jost said. That gives you an additional degree of freedom to work with. "They have zero net magnetization, so they're stable, but they still have the capability to generate spin-polarized currents needed to easily extract information. ".

A New Frontier for Quantum Technology and Electronics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, confirming altermagnetism gives scientists a new class of materials to investigate and potentially engineer for technological applications. By combining magnetic stability with the ability to manipulate spin-based information, these materials could help overcome challenges that have held back conventional spintronic devices.

Berdasarkan laporan, the next step will be learning how to control altermagnetic states using external influences such as light and electricity. Researchers hope that mastering this control will make it possible to design practical devices that take advantage of the unusual magnetic properties.

Although significant development is still needed before these materials can be widely used, the findings establish a stronger experimental foundation for future work on quantum technologies, computer memory, and more efficient data centers.

The research received partial funding from the DOE Office of Science.

#393. NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope

📅 04 Nov 2026

NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope

Tanggal: 04 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012254.htm

NASA is investigating whether private space companies could help extend the life of the Hubble Space Telescope, which has spent more than 35 years transforming our understanding of the universe.

Berdasarkan laporan, on october 29, the agency issued a request for information seeking details about commercial technologies that could be used to service hubble while it remains in orbit. The goal is to determine whether new spacecraft capabilities could keep the iconic observatory operating longer, improve its performance, or help bring its mission to a safe conclusion.

Diungkapkan bahwa "hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible," said nasa administrator jared isaacman. "If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already on orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble's life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe. ".

NASA Considers Raising Hubble Into a Higher Orbit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one possibility under consideration is sending a spacecraft to push hubble into a higher orbit. This could counteract the gradual loss of altitude that threatens the telescope's future and potentially allow it to continue making scientific discoveries for additional years.

Berdasarkan laporan, nasa is also interested in missions that could service the telescope and improve its capabilities. Another option would focus on safely retiring Hubble when its scientific work is complete, either by guiding it through a controlled descent into Earth's atmosphere or arranging for its disposal in orbit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these possibilities are being explored rather than formally approved. By reaching out to commercial companies, NASA hopes to better understand what technologies are available and whether they could provide practical, affordable solutions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "hubble is a national icon that has fundamentally changed how humanity views our universe for more than 35 years," said nicky fox, associate administrator, science mission directorate, nasa headquarters in washington. Given the time we have until Hubble's anticipated re-entry, we are eager to explore the breadth of possibilities to boost Hubble to a higher orbit while we develop the flagship mission to follow. "Commercial industry has rapidly evolved in recent years to offer new capabilities for in-space satellite capture and servicing. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, companies interested in participating can review nasa's request for information online. m. The agency is accepting responses until 3 p. EST on Monday, November 30.

Why Hubble Could Fall Back to Earth by 2034.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, although hubble continues to operate in space, its orbit is gradually shrinking. The telescope travels through low Earth orbit, where traces of Earth's atmosphere create drag that slowly reduces the altitude of orbiting spacecraft.

Diungkapkan bahwa even hundreds of miles above the planet, the atmosphere is not completely absent. The tiny amount of remaining gas produces resistance as spacecraft move through it. Over long periods, this effect can cause satellites to lose altitude and eventually descend into denser layers of the atmosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unlike spacecraft equipped with engines that can periodically raise their orbits, hubble has no propulsion system capable of maintaining its altitude. Without outside assistance, it cannot reverse this gradual orbital decline.

Berdasarkan laporan, nasa's current analysis suggests that hubble will likely reenter earth's atmosphere sometime between 2033 and 2034. To prevent that outcome through an orbital boost, the agency expects that a mission would need to occur by 2032.

That timeline leaves a limited window to evaluate potential solutions, develop a mission, and carry it out before the telescope descends too far.

Extending Hubble's Legacy of Cosmic Discoveries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since beginning operations more than three decades ago, hubble has become one of the most influential scientific observatories ever launched. Its observations have helped reshape astronomers' understanding of the cosmos, and the telescope continues to produce discoveries that advance research across many areas of astronomy.

Hubble is also the product of a longstanding international partnership between NASA and ESA (European Space Agency).

NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, oversees the telescope and its mission operations, with additional operational support from Denver-based Lockheed Martin Space.

Scientific operations are handled by the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, which is operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy on NASA's behalf.

Diungkapkan bahwa with commercial spaceflight technology advancing, nasa is now evaluating whether hubble could benefit from capabilities that were not available when it was originally designed. A successful mission to raise its orbit or enhance its systems could allow the historic telescope to continue exploring the universe well beyond its currently projected orbital lifetime.

The ice giants' skewed magnetic fields are a window into the high-pressure, high-temperature environment deep inside Uranus and Neptune.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the posided magnetic fields of uranus and neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, only one spacecraft has ever visited uranus and neptune, the voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past uranus in january 1986 and neptune in august 1989. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. If we compare these planets to Earth, which has a stable magnetic field tilted by just 11 degrees to our planet’s rotation, we can see how extreme the magnetic fields of the ice giants are.

Berdasarkan laporan, various explanations for the strange magnetic fields of the ice giants have been put forward over the years. Uranus as a whole is tilted by 97 degrees and effectively rolls around the sun, and speculation is that billions of years ago it was knocked on its side by a collision with a long-lost Earth-sized planet. Could this collision have also skewed its magnetic field?.

Diungkapkan bahwa this might be a plausible explanation were neptune’s magnetic field also not similarly skewed without having experienced a collision. Now, a new study by scientists in the U. Clearly, whatever the cause, it must be intrinsic to the nature of the two ice giant planets. S. and the UK, based on computer simulations and Voyager 2’s measurements of the two planets’ magnetic fields, may have found a solution.

Berdasarkan laporan, the solution to the weird magnetic fields of the solar system's ice giants may come down to how planets generate their magnetic field through the dynamo effect. This arises from the swirling, convective motion of an electrically conducting liquid within a rotating body, which is able to generate and maintain a powerful magnetic field.

Inside Earth, the electrically conducting fluid is the molten iron in the outer part of our planet’s core, and the magnetic field that it generates has clear north and south poles – what we call a dipole, a phenomenon that we can also see in the two magnetic poles of a simple bar magnet.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, the conditions inside uranus and neptune are somewhat different. 5 and 17 times the mass of our planet, respectively. Furthermore, Uranus and Neptune are substantially larger than Earth, with 14. As ice giants, they contain a lot of volatiles – ammonia, hydrogen, helium, methane, and water surrounding a probable rocky core. This increased mass creates crushing conditions within the interior of the ice giants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "deep inside uranus and neptune, pressures and temperatures become extremely high," research team leader chi yan of the university of texas at austin, who led the new findings, said in a statement. "Under those conditions, which can cause water molecules to break apart into ions, the material may become increasingly electrically conductive with depth. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, given the increasing electrical conductivity and the compositions of the two planets, the computer simulations were able to replicate the bizarre magnetic fields of uranus and neptune. This showed how the magnetic-field structure co-evolves alongside changes in the fluid motion driven by convection and the temperature inside the planets.

Diungkapkan bahwa it also seems that this co-evolution might not yet be over. The simulations indicate that the magnetic fields of both planets can change quite significantly in the space of just a few decades.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "earth’s magnetic tilt drifts by only a degree or so over 50 years," said yan. In some stretches, the tilt swings by tens of degrees within decades. In others, it shifts only slightly over the same span. "Our models show the ice giants can behave very differently. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa nasa have prioritized a new mission to return to uranus in the early 2040s, while the china national space administration’s tianwen-4 mission launching to jupiter in 2029 will deploy a small probe to carry onwards to uranus via a gravitational slingshot. Until then, scientists are coming up with creative ways to not have to rely only on the 40-year-old Voyager 2 measurements of the magnetic fields.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for example, tom stallard of northumbria university in the uk, who is a co-author with yan on the new research paper, has been leading james webb space telescope (jwst) observations of the faint infrared auroral lights on both uranus and neptune. Aurorae are generated when charged particles on the solar wind interact with a planet’s magnetic field, driving some of those charged particles into the atmosphere above the magnetic poles. (Neptune actually has a quadrupolar component, muddling its defined north and south magnetic poles. ) As such, the location of aurorae is a good indicator of what’s going on with a planet’s magnetic field.

"We are busy working on what’s contained within these observations, but the shape and structure of the aurora, as well as other weird patterns in the ionosphere [upper atmosphere], promise to provide us with a way of understanding how the magnetic fields have changed, [which is] an important stepping stone," said Stallard.

The hope is that by combining JWST’s observations of the aurora with Voyager 2’s magnetic-field measurements and the results of the computer simulations, it will be possible to estimate the configuration of the magnetic fields on Uranus and Neptune today and see how they compare to the 1980s.

This would provide an experimental test to help show whether the new model describing the magnetic fields is on the right track, although we won’t know for sure until a new mission arrives in the ice giants’ backyard.

The findings were described on 3 November in the journal Communications Physics.

Rubin Observatory in Chile has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way, offering an early glimpse of what could become a much larger wave of discoveries. Berdasarkan laporan, located on cerro pachón in the chilean andes, the recently completed nsf-doe vera c. Rubin Observatory is designed to explore the sky in extraordinary detail.
