Two Hidden Companions of the Milky Way Discovered.

Using observations collected before the observatory's official launch, researchers identified two exceptionally faint satellites that had never been seen before.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first, aquarius iv, is a tiny galaxy located in the distant outskirts of the milky way, approximately 355,000 light-years from earth. The second, Rubin-GC1, is a star cluster on the opposite side of our galaxy, hidden within a region where thick clouds of cosmic dust make observations especially challenging.

Both discoveries are remarkable because astronomers made them using only a small amount of the data Rubin is expected to collect over its lifetime.

"What I find especially exciting is that these discoveries are just the beginning for Rubin," said William Cerny, an astronomy student in Yale's Graduate School of Arts and Sciences.

Cerny is the lead author of the Aquarius IV study, published in Research Notes of the AAS, and the second author of the Rubin-GC1 study, which has been accepted by The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Berdasarkan laporan, "if the observatory can find systems this faint and difficult with only its preview data, its full 10-year survey will undoubtedly provide us with many more milky way satellite discoveries," cerny said. "These new satellites will give us new opportunities to test models of galaxy formation, trace the assembly history of the Milky Way, and investigate the nature of dark matter. ".

A Powerful New Telescope Is Just Getting Started.

Diungkapkan bahwa rubin began its ambitious 10-year legacy survey of space and time (lsst) in june. The project aims to produce an exceptionally detailed record of the changing night sky while searching for objects that previous telescopes have been unable to detect.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of its major scientific goals is to map the milky way's "halo," a vast, roughly spherical region that surrounds the galaxy's main disk. This halo contains scattered stars, gas, and dark matter, along with faint satellite galaxies, star clusters, and other structures that preserve clues about the Milky Way's past.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to carry out this enormous survey, rubin uses the 8. 2 gigapixels of resolution. 4-meter Simonyi Survey Telescope and the largest digital camera ever constructed, capable of capturing images with 3. By repeatedly photographing large areas of the Southern Hemisphere sky, the observatory will build an extraordinarily wide-ranging time-lapse record of the universe.

Berdasarkan laporan, the facility is jointly funded by the national science foundation and the u. S. Department of Energy's Office of Science.

Just 7% of the Night Sky Revealed Two New Satellites.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for the new studies, astronomers examined preview observations gathered between april 2025 and january 2026. These images covered only about 7% of the entire night sky, yet they were sufficient to reveal two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way.

The discoveries offer an encouraging indication of what could emerge as Rubin continues collecting data across a much larger portion of the sky.

Berdasarkan laporan, "finding new milky way satellites in rubin observatory data has been an exciting future prospect for most of my career," said marla geha, a professor of astronomy and physics in yale's faculty of arts and sciences, and co-author on both studies. "It is remarkable this is now a reality. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the research involved a broad international collaboration. In addition to Yale, participating institutions included the University of Chicago, the University of Virginia, the University of Washington, Dartmouth College, the University of Tampa, NSF NOIRLab, Duke University, the University of Toronto, the Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía in Spain, the University of Colorado-Boulder, and Lund University in Sweden.

Aashay Pai of the University of Chicago served as the first author of the study describing Rubin-GC1.

Hidden Galaxies Could Reveal New Clues About Dark Matter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finding additional satellites could do much more than expand the known population of galaxies surrounding the milky way. These faint objects may also help astronomers investigate one of the universe's greatest mysteries: dark matter.

Berdasarkan laporan, dark matter is an invisible form of matter that does not emit or reflect light, making it impossible to observe directly with conventional telescopes. Scientists infer its existence from the gravitational effects it produces on stars, galaxies, and other cosmic structures. It accounts for most of the matter in the universe and provides much of the gravitational framework that holds galaxies together.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ultra-faint galaxies such as aquarius iv are particularly valuable for studying dark matter. They contain only a small fraction of the stars found in larger galaxies, yet dark matter dominates their total mass. By examining their properties and movements, researchers can test ideas about how dark matter behaves and influences the formation of galaxies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these discoveries could also help scientists reconstruct the milky way's long history. The positions, motions, and properties of small satellite galaxies can reveal how larger galaxies assembled over billions of years, including how they accumulated matter and interacted with smaller systems.

Rubin's early findings may also provide important clues about how the universe's smallest and faintest galaxies form, evolve, and survive.

Berdasarkan laporan, "these discoveries are incredibly promising," geha said. "Continued discoveries will allow us to complete the census of satellite galaxies around the Milky Way, which is a key to understanding how the faintest galaxies form. ".

#400. A dead star's mysterious rings reveal what could happen when our Sun dies

📅 06 Nov 2026

A dead star's mysterious rings reveal what could happen when our Sun dies

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012250.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, astronomers have discovered an extraordinary ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star, offering a possible preview of what could happen to our own solar system billions of years from now. Even more surprising, the debris is divided into two distinct rings, with a clear gap between them that may be maintained by planetary bodies that somehow survived their star's death.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the discovery was made using the european southern observatory's very large telescope (eso's vlt). Unlike previously observed debris systems around dead stars, this one appears to contain two separate discs of material left behind by destroyed planets. Researchers believe two surviving objects may be shaping the unusual structure, including one potentially as large as Pluto or even the Moon.

"We have known for some time that planets may survive beyond the transformation of their central star, but this is the first example of a complex system with a double debris disc and potentially two surviving planetesimals," says Nicola Gentile Fusillo, an astronomer at the Università degli Studi di Trieste in Italy and lead author of the study published in Nature Astronomy.

A Dead Star Surrounded by Planetary Wreckage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the center of the system is j1328−1450, a white dwarf. These extremely dense stellar remnants form when stars similar to our Sun exhaust their fuel and reach the final stages of their evolution. After expanding dramatically and shedding their outer layers, they leave behind their exposed cores.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this transformation can be catastrophic for nearby planets. More distant rocky objects can survive the initial upheaval, although gravitational disturbances may eventually tear some of them apart. As a star swells, it may engulf and destroy worlds orbiting too close to it. Their remains can form rotating discs of debris around the dead star.

Sebagaimana diketahui, astronomers have observed such debris discs around other white dwarfs, but j1328−1450 is different. Instead of a single ring of vaporized planetary material, it has two concentric rings, meaning one lies farther from the star than the other. The rings remain clearly separated, creating an unusual structure that scientists are now trying to explain.

"The structure we see in this system is particularly intriguing because the two gaseous rings are remarkably stable and remain separated by a gap," says co-author Felipe Lagos-Vilches, an astronomer at the University of Warwick, UK, and at the Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María in Chile.

"The system is a rare glimpse of the violent, chaotic process by which a planetary system meets its end, and it hints that dead stars can have disc structures far more complex than previously realized," adds Gentile Fusillo, who is also affiliated with the INAF-Astronomical Observatory of Trieste.

Two Surviving Worlds May Be Shaping the Rings.

The researchers suspect that two surviving planetary bodies, each traveling along a separate orbit, are responsible for maintaining the double ring structure.

Berdasarkan laporan, one of these objects, associated with the inner ring, is thought to be comparable in size to a typical asteroid, measuring only a few kilometers across. The other, farther from the star, could be much larger, potentially reaching the size of Pluto or even our Moon.

Sebagaimana diketahui, such objects are known as planetesimals, a term used for smaller solid bodies associated with the formation and evolution of planetary systems. Although the two suspected survivors have not been directly observed, their gravitational influence could help explain why the debris remains organized into two distinct rings rather than forming one continuous disc.

Berdasarkan laporan, the evidence comes from observations collected with the x-shooter instrument on eso's vlt in chile's atacama desert. The instrument analyzes light across a broad range of wavelengths, allowing astronomers to examine the chemical makeup and motion of material surrounding distant objects.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, previously discovered debris discs around white dwarfs have shared a recognizable observational signature consistent with a single, flat, rotating disc. J1328−1450 breaks that pattern. Its observations instead reveal the unique fingerprint of a double disc, providing evidence of a far more complicated arrangement of planetary remains.

Chemical Clues Reveal the Remains of Destroyed Planets.

The debris also contains important clues about the worlds that once orbited the star.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, astronomers detected calcium, oxygen, magnesium, and iron, elements commonly found in rocky planetary material throughout our solar system. Their presence indicates that the rings contain remnants of solid bodies rather than simply gas left over from the star itself.

Berdasarkan laporan, more intriguingly, the two rings have noticeably different chemical compositions. The inner ring contains substantial amounts of magnesium gas, while the outer ring is largely depleted of magnesium.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this difference suggests that the material in the two rings may have originated from separate planets with different compositions. If so, the system could preserve evidence of multiple destroyed worlds.

Berdasarkan laporan, another possibility is that both rings contain material from different layers of the same planetary body. For example, one ring could contain debris from a planet's outer crust, while the other contains material from deeper inside, such as its core.

Either explanation would offer valuable insight into the destruction of rocky worlds and the complex processes that can continue long after a star has exhausted its fuel.

A Possible Preview of Our Solar System's Future.

The discovery also raises a compelling question about the ultimate fate of our own planetary neighborhood.

Berdasarkan laporan, billions of years from now, the sun will undergo a similar transformation. It will expand into a red giant, shed its outer layers, and eventually become a white dwarf. During this process, the inner Solar System will experience enormous changes, and Earth itself may be destroyed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet the observations of j1328−1450 suggest that the death of a star does not necessarily mean the complete disappearance of its planetary system. Some objects may survive, while others could be shattered into debris that continues orbiting the stellar remnant in complex arrangements.

By studying this distant dead star and its unusual double rings, astronomers are gaining a rare opportunity to investigate what remains after a planetary system experiences such a violent transformation.

"The system therefore offers a remarkable glimpse of what the future of planetary systems, including systems like our own, might look like," concludes Lagos-Vilches.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the final weeks of 1960, two young radio enthusiasts were monitoring transmissions from a home-built listening station on a rooftop in turin, italy, when the brothers detected something extraordinary: a faint signal that bore the hallmarks of one originating from space. That wasn't the only surprising thing about the alleged signal:, the transmission carried a very familiar message: it was Morse code for the international distress signal SOS.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as the youths listened, the signal seemed to grow weaker. This raised a troubling possibility: could it be that the signal's source was moving farther away from Earth? And if so, was it possible that this concerning signal was of Soviet origin — perhaps a spacecraft drifting helplessly into space, carrying a cosmonaut on board whose doomed mission had never been publicly acknowledged?.

Diungkapkan bahwa these strange events from november 1960 became the first in a series of alleged radio signal interceptions that would form the basis of an enduring cold war-era mystery involving so-called "lost cosmonauts" — early soviet space travelers rumored to have died during secret spaceflight missions before yuri gagarin's historic flight the following spring, in april 1961. Today, more than six decades later, the story remains one of the most haunting legends of the Space Age. Were there truly early Soviet space missions — with tragically ill-fated cosmonaut crews — that remain undisclosed to this day?.

The peculiar story began in October 1957, as the Italian brothers Achille and Gian Battista Judica-Cordiglia learned, along with the rest of the world, about the Soviet Union's successful launch of Sputnik 1, Earth's first artificial satellite.

Diungkapkan bahwa immediately, the two became fascinated with the idea of trying to listen in on signals from such spacecraft and began working to assemble their very own radio tracking station, which they put together mostly from secondhand military surplus equipment. What they couldn't easily find and purchase, the brothers would often assemble themselves. They built an improvised tracking station in an abandoned World War Two bunker, which the brothers dubbed Torre Bert, that eventually became a fully functional radio facility with an antenna they built from salvaged materials like chicken wire and scraps of metal.

Diungkapkan bahwa whatever it lacked in aesthetics, the station made up for in functionality, and soon the brothers' amateur efforts reportedly allowed them to successfully intercept transmissions associated with sputnik 2, the first soviet spacecraft to carry a living creature into orbit: a dog named laika, who became a one-way passenger on the mission. Later, the boys also said they were able to track transmissions from America's Explorer 1 satellite.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some of what the judica-cordiglia brothers were able to achieve could be chalked up to being in the right place at the right time. Specifically, their location in northern Italy was advantageous, since it allowed them to monitor signals from Soviet spacecraft passing overhead.

By late November 1960, the Judica-Cordiglia brothers learned of reports from a West German observatory suggesting there may have been an unidentified satellite in orbit, raising an intriguing possibility: could there have been a spacecraft launch that had not been disclosed to the public?.

Berdasarkan laporan, intrigued, the brothers began spending their evenings at torre bert scanning the skies for radio frequencies in search of the alleged mystery object. Eventually, they claimed to have detected a signal that differed significantly from those they had tracked in the past. Unlike the familiar electronic beeps they had intercepted from other satellites, this transmission seemed unmistakable: it was Morse code for SOS.

According to their account, as the pair listened to the alarming transmission, the signal gradually began to fade, raising a disconcerting possibility: what if the spacecraft they were monitoring hadn't merely been traveling through orbit, but had been drifting away from Earth?.

If correct, the implications were staggering: the Soviet Union may have launched a secret space mission, but this time with a human cosmonaut on board — and something had gone terribly wrong, ending with a spacecraft and its occupant becoming lost in space.

Significantly, the brothers appear to have reached this conclusion independently, and no verified evidence has ever surfaced establishing that the transmission they claimed to have intercepted originated from a crewed spacecraft, let alone one associated with an unacknowledged Soviet mission that somehow escaped Earth's gravitational influence, with tragic results.

Nonetheless, the brothers' claims would soon help give rise to a disturbing possibility: that there had been unknown "lost" cosmonauts who perished during missions that remained hidden from public knowledge.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the alleged distress signal was only the beginning of a series of unsubstantiated claims the judica-cordiglia brothers made, and by the first days of february 1961, the amateur radio sleuths would claim to have intercepted another odd signal. This time, the pair claimed to have heard labored breathing coming across the airwaves, and even what resembled the strained moans of a person aboard an orbiting spacecraft.

Diungkapkan bahwa in an equally eerie recording the brothers produced, what sounded like a rapidly beating human heart could be heard. The brothers shared the recording with Italian cardiologist Achille Dogliotti, whose examination reportedly led him to conclude that the sounds were consistent with strained breathing and an elevated human heartbeat.

With time, more recordings would begin to appear, featuring transmissions the boys believed to be evidence of unsuccessful Soviet missions that preceded the successful spaceflight of Yuri Gagarin, whose 108-minute journey around Earth in 1961 made him the first human to travel into space.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, what may be the brothers' most controversial claim involved a recording they believed captured the final moments of a female cosmonaut whose ill-fated journey allegedly occurred prior to the historic 1963 spaceflight of valentina tereshkova, the first woman to travel into space. However, experts have pointed out that these transmissions do not follow typical military communications protocols, further casting doubt on their legitimacy.

As the Judica-Cordiglia brothers' notoriety increased, journalists and curiosity-seekers weren't the only ones whose attention they reportedly began to attract; their activities also allegedly garnered interest from intelligence officials.

Diungkapkan bahwa in one instance, the brothers claimed a man identifying himself as a russian reporter had visited them. Shortly thereafter, another individual — this time claiming to be an Italian counterintelligence agent — warned them that the "journalist" who had come to see them was a KGB agent.

The Judica-Cordiglias and their unconventional hobby, it seemed, had now placed them in the crosshairs of Soviet intelligence officials.

Berdasarkan laporan, an unusual twist in this part of the italian brothers' story would eventually emerge decades later, when london-based journalist kris hollington began reinvestigating their claims for a feature story that appeared in the paranormal-focused magazine fortean times. According to Hollington, a former Soviet KGB operative who later served as a Russian ambassador to a European country had reportedly confirmed (on condition of anonymity) that Moscow was indeed interested in the Judica-Cordiglias and their claims.

"Our cosmonauts were warned to be careful what they said while in space after this and we had the brothers followed," the former KGB agent reportedly told Hollington.

Sebagaimana diketahui, things could have ended tragically for the brothers if it were not for the fame they achieved at the time for their alleged radio interceptions. As the former KGB agent told Hollington, it was believed for a time that the brothers "had to be dealt with — an accident perhaps," although after they appeared on a television program that brought them significant attention, any Soviet plans that would have endangered the brothers became impractical.

Berdasarkan laporan, "that saved their lives," the former kgb agent reportedly told hollington, who expressed gratitude for the circumstances that may well have saved the italian brothers, with the former agent confiding to hollington that he thought "they were good kids. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, the claims of alleged soviet surveillance are difficult to verify given the anonymity requested by hollington's source. The same must be said of many of the claims made by the Judica-Cordiglias — even if the brothers were successful in intercepting Soviet transmissions at the time, that alone does not prove that they uncovered evidence of unacknowledged missions during which cosmonauts may have perished.

Some, like spaceflight researcher Sven Grahn, have acknowledged the genuine tracking capabilities the brothers possessed while remaining skeptical of the more sensational "lost cosmonaut" claims, suggesting the brothers might have misinterpreted some of the transmissions they recorded.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i think that the judica-cordiglia brothers did run a tracking station and picked up signals from various spacecraft," grahn said in an assessment of the brothers and their claims. "Once they over-interpreted some receptions and made fantastic claims they were 'trapped' and had to continue to produce sensations. "However, for some reason they thought that they needed sensational stories [to] maintain their image of a 'hot-shot' operation," he adds. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is also the possibility that the recordings were hoaxes, of course. Whatever the case, there are no independently verified launch records, authenticated communications, or other evidence from the period that provides additional support for what the brothers claimed to have intercepted.

Berdasarkan laporan, something that can be verified, however, is the soviet union's well-documented secrecy, adding a further layer of complication to matters. As space historian James Oberg has observed, there are verified instances in which Soviet officials altered photographs and records from the early years of human spaceflight, a fact that has perhaps helped fuel rumors about alleged missing cosmonauts. 24, 1960 that killed a high-ranking Soviet military officer and at least 100 others. It is also known that the Soviet space program covered up several deadly disasters, such as a launch pad explosion on Oct. At the time, Soviet state news outlets reported it as a plane crash.

Diungkapkan bahwa no verified evidence has emerged to support claims of failed, unacknowledged soviet crewed spaceflights of the kind described in the lost-cosmonaut legends. Yet the Judica-Cordiglia brothers' accounts have drawn attention for decades and remain among the strangest stories in the lore of the early Space Age — a fact that illustrates humanity's enduring fascination with Cold War mysteries and phenomena that exist beyond Earth.

#405. MIT scientists break a 20-year rule and unlock never-before-seen crystal structures

📅 04 Nov 2026

MIT scientists break a 20-year rule and unlock never-before-seen crystal structures

Tanggal: 04 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104012248.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scientists have spent decades trying to control how tiny particles connect to form advanced materials. Now, researchers at MIT and their collaborators have discovered that doing the exact opposite of what was previously believed necessary can produce remarkable results.

Sebagaimana diketahui, instead of relying on rigid molecular connections to hold nanoparticles in carefully planned arrangements, the team developed extremely flexible connectors that bend and adjust as particles come together. This unexpected strategy gives scientists a new way to control how nanoparticles organize themselves, allowing them to create crystal structures that have never been observed before.

Diungkapkan bahwa the discovery could help overcome a major obstacle in materials science and open new possibilities for creating substances with precisely engineered properties. Potential applications include electronics, medicine, energy technologies, agriculture, and chemical manufacturing.

The findings, described in a paper that will appear in Nature Materials, demonstrate how the flexibility and electrical charges of molecular connectors can determine the structures that nanoparticles form.

MIT Researchers Challenge 20 Years of Materials Science.

Berdasarkan laporan, "people are interested in nanoparticle superlattices because of the promise of building designer materials where you have more say in what types of structures they can actually build into," says rob macfarlane, the richard p. It's exciting to have a new tool that is so counterintuitive. It's the exact opposite of what the dogma has been for 20 years: that you need to make connector ligands rigid, and any deviation causes assembly to fail. "This is a new approach in nanoparticle assembly that hasn't been investigated before. Simmons (1953) Professor in Metallurgy in MIT's Department of Materials Science and Engineering. We showed if you just crank it all the way to the opposite extreme, it works just as well. ".

The research team also included MIT PhD candidate Nicholas Sbalbi, University of Delaware doctoral student Stephen Kronenberger, MIT undergraduate Hana Shinzawa, Matthew Ye PhD '26, and Arthi Jayaraman, a former professor at the University of Delaware.

At the heart of the discovery is a basic principle of materials science: The way a material's smallest components are arranged determines how that material behaves.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "that means if you know what your building blocks are and how they're arranged, you can explain what properties materials have," macfarlane says. "Controlling that is how you make materials that have new properties. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, this principle is especially important when working with nanoparticles, which are extremely small pieces of matter whose shapes, sizes, and properties can be adjusted for different purposes. Scientists already use individual nanoparticles in technologies involving drug delivery, energy storage, computing, and sensors.

But turning these tiny building blocks into larger, organized materials presents a difficult challenge.

Why Nanoparticles Are So Difficult to Control.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the biggest obstacles is controlling how nanoparticles attach to one another. Scientists need to determine not only how many neighboring particles each nanoparticle connects with, but also the directions in which those connections form.

Diungkapkan bahwa without that control, nanoparticles tend to assemble into tightly packed arrangements that restrict the variety of structures researchers can produce. This limits their ability to create materials with unusual or specialized properties.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, researchers have traditionally approached the problem in two ways. One strategy involves changing the shapes of nanoparticles to influence how they fit together. Another involves modifying specific areas of their surfaces so that only certain regions attract neighboring particles.

In effect, scientists attempt to control where the particles stick to one another, much like designing puzzle pieces that can connect only in particular positions.

Although these methods can produce useful structures, they are often complicated, highly specialized, and difficult to adapt for large-scale production.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the challenge with both of those approaches is they're difficult to do synthetically as we make the particles," macfarlane explains. It's good for studying, but you can't do much with it. "The methods for defining stickiness that have been developed are always bespoke: They work for one material, at one size scale, in one condition. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, both strategies also depend on molecular connectors called ligands. These molecules attach to the surfaces of nanoparticles and help link neighboring particles together.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, traditionally, researchers have tried to make these ligands rigid so the connections remain at carefully controlled angles. This helps maintain a desired arrangement, but it also restricts the types of structures that can form and the functions they can perform.

The MIT team decided to explore a radically different possibility.

A Surprising Discovery About Flexible Molecular Bonds.

Rather than forcing molecular connectors to remain in fixed positions, the researchers wondered whether giving them almost complete freedom to bend could offer an entirely new form of control.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we thought, 'let's do the exact opposite: make the bonds so flexible it doesn't matter what direction they're initially pointing. ' The ligands can then reorganize as the particles come together, and that reorganization itself limits how many neighbors each particle can bind," Macfarlane says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the idea reverses the usual approach to nanoparticle assembly. Instead of controlling the orientation of every connection in advance, the scientists allow the connectors to adjust naturally as the particles interact.

Sebagaimana diketahui, macfarlane's laboratory has spent years developing ways to construct different types of nanoparticles using attached polymer chains. Polymers are large molecules made of repeating smaller units, and their flexibility makes them useful for creating adjustable molecular connections.

Diungkapkan bahwa for the new system, the team equipped nanoparticles with highly flexible ligands that carry electrical charges at their ends. Some have positive charges, while others have negative charges.

Berdasarkan laporan, because opposite electrical charges attract, the connector molecules naturally bend toward partners with the opposite charge. This attraction helps the nanoparticles join together, while the flexibility of the connectors influences how many connections each particle can make.

"The idea is, instead of defining a specific direction the bonds are going to occur in with complicated synthesis methods, we just said, 'The bonds are going to be as flexible as they want to be, and they'll spontaneously go to whatever valency is going to maximize bond stability,'" Macfarlane says.

Diungkapkan bahwa in this context, valency refers to the number of connections a nanoparticle forms with its neighbors. By allowing the connectors to move freely, the researchers found that the system could naturally settle into stable arrangements without requiring every connection to be designed beforehand.

Scientists Create Crystal Structures Never Seen Before.

Experiments led by Sbalbi demonstrated that the researchers could adjust the connections between nanoparticles by changing two relatively straightforward characteristics: the sizes of the particles and the lengths of their flexible molecular chains.

These adjustments altered how the particles assembled, giving the team control over the number of neighboring particles each one could connect with.

Most importantly, the researchers used this method to produce previously unseen crystal structures.

Berdasarkan laporan, crystals are materials whose building blocks form organized, repeating patterns. In this case, the repeating arrangements are made from nanoparticles rather than individual atoms or small molecules. Such ordered nanoparticle networks are often called superlattices.

By reducing the number of connections between neighboring particles, the team was able to create more open arrangements instead of the densely packed structures that commonly form during nanoparticle assembly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "without having to predesign where the particles connect or what their shapes are, we can control the number of bonds each particle has," macfarlane explains. It allows us to lower the number of bonds each particle has and make lattices we have never seen before. "The amount of flexibility of the polymer dictates how many bonds it has. ".

The results suggest that molecular flexibility, once viewed as an obstacle to precise nanoparticle assembly, can instead become a powerful tool for engineering new material structures.

A New Path Toward Customizable Designer Materials.

The researchers believe their method could bring scientists closer to a long-sought goal in materials science: choosing the properties of individual nanoparticles independently of the larger structures into which they assemble.

Ideally, scientists could select nanoparticles for their electrical, optical, chemical, or other useful characteristics and then organize those particles into whatever arrangement best serves a particular application.

In practice, however, existing assembly methods have made that level of flexibility difficult to achieve.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we in the nanoparticle assembly community talk about having completely independent control over what your particle is and what assembly it goes into," macfarlane says. In reality, it absolutely has not been. "In theory, that should be the case. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the new approach could help close that gap. Because the researchers can influence nanoparticle arrangements through the flexibility of their connectors and the attraction between electrical charges, they may be able to create a wider variety of structures without the complicated manufacturing techniques required by traditional methods.

The team also sees the discovery as a promising route toward producing customizable materials at larger scales, potentially helping move nanoparticle technologies beyond laboratory experiments and into practical use.

Potential Applications in Electronics, Medicine, and Energy.

The ability to build more open and varied nanoparticle structures could prove particularly valuable for developing advanced materials.

Berdasarkan laporan, in photonics, which involves controlling and manipulating light, precisely organized nanoparticles could help researchers engineer materials with specialized optical properties. In chemical catalysis, where substances accelerate chemical reactions, new particle arrangements could create opportunities to improve the way catalysts operate.

The approach may also support future developments in medicine, agriculture, electronics, and energy technologies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a major advantage is that nanoparticles can already possess a wide range of desirable properties. By controlling how those particles come together, scientists may be able to combine their individual capabilities in new ways.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "nanoparticle superlattices offer a way to create designer materials where your building blocks have all sort sorts of unique properties," macfarlane says. "But just densely packing these nanoparticles together limits your applications. This offers a way to get less dense formations of nanoparticles, and that's where a lot of the interesting applications are. ".

Although further development will be needed to translate the method into commercial technologies, the discovery establishes molecular flexibility as a new strategy for creating materials with tailored structures.

Instead of treating bending molecular connections as a problem to eliminate, scientists may now be able to use that flexibility to unlock arrangements that rigid designs could not easily achieve.

A robot just played Tinkertoys in space, assembling the first satellite structure ever made without a human touching the controls.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the darpa-funded project saw a robotic "truss builder" create a reflective antenna using kapton film, composite fiber tubes and aluminum joints. The implications are huge for future missions, potentially opening up new possibilities to build — or fix — satellites in the final frontier.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space," sergio pellegrino, an aerospace and civil engineering professor at the california institute of technology (caltech), said in a statement on nov. 5.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the need for such spacecraft will likely rise substantially in the future, as companies assemble giant megaconstellations for cell-phone communications, ai compute and other purposes. Indeed, the ball is already rolling on such ambitious projects, generating enough hype for space startups around the globe to raise a record $20. 8 billion in the third quarter of 2026 alone.

Diungkapkan bahwa anything that launches aboard a rocket is limited by the size of that vehicle's fairing — the nose cone that protects payloads during their ride to space. In space, however, the ability to stretch out is practically infinite — after taking into account, of course, engineering and financing constraints.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, assembling structures robotically off earth could therefore be revolutionary, advocates say. And the recent milestone was a step in that direction.

"This work could be useful not only for astronomy and astrophysics, but also for communications and other areas, such as building very large solar arrays for space solar power," said Pellegrino, who's team leader of the truss-building project, a Caltech demonstration mission called Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA).

Berdasarkan laporan, astra built a 1. 5-foot) structure in orbit. 4-meter-wide (4. That's an impressive achievement, but it just scratches the surface of what DARPA wants to accomplish via a program it calls Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design, or NOM4D for short.

Diungkapkan bahwa "nom4d's objective is to enable efficient, scalable construction of very large structures in space," nom4d program manager andrew detor said in a nov. 5 DARPA statement.

Berdasarkan laporan, "by 'very large,' i mean hundreds of meters or kilometers in scale. Nothing approaching that scale can be achieved today," Detor added.

Diungkapkan bahwa astra was a demonstration, allowing researchers to check boxes and identify obstacles before shooting for a bigger goal. And the team did run into issues — specifically, time limitations, which prevented them from building additional sections of the antenna. Still, the researchers were able to prove out the third phase of a larger DARPA project.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, pellegrino's team completed the two previous phases — defining the mission and testing the hardware in a lab — before shipping the astra payload to the spaceflight company momentus, inc. for integration into its Vigoride 7 space tug. Vigoride 7 launched on March 30, along with many other payloads, aboard SpaceX's Transporter-16 rideshare mission.

Berdasarkan laporan, astra flew with two prebuilt sections of a truss, a robotic "manipulator" and parts to make the rest of the truss in space. In brief communication windows totaling 15 minutes a day, engineers sent up commands and checked in on the robot's progress as it picked up things, readied them in the right spot, and performed construction on an assembly plate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the team overcame many "little surprises" on the way but were not able to finish the entire truss in time. Still, Pellegrino framed the effort as a success.

"Developing a payload of this complexity on such a short timeline was an enormous undertaking for our small team," he said.

Looking into the future, he is hopeful that robots will be able to build larger telescope mirrors for observatories to peer deeper into space, as well as more advanced structures for radio telescopes to listen for distant signals.

NOM4D is also supporting a project from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, but that one will take place at the International Space Station, focusing on how to harden carbon tubes in orbit.

#410. AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage

📅 04 Nov 2026

AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage

Tanggal: 04 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261104004909.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, scientists at stanford medicine have identified a naturally occurring molecule that could lead to a new generation of weight loss medications. Early animal experiments suggest that it can suppress appetite and promote fat loss much like semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic, while potentially avoiding some of the drug's troublesome side effects.

Diungkapkan bahwa the molecule, known as brp, works differently from existing treatments. Rather than affecting several organs throughout the body, it appears to act more selectively on a part of the brain responsible for controlling hunger and metabolism. This more focused approach could eventually help people lose weight without experiencing problems such as nausea, constipation, or substantial muscle loss.

Berdasarkan laporan, researchers discovered brp with the help of artificial intelligence, which allowed them to search through thousands of possible biological compounds. The findings were promising enough that the scientists began preparing for the next major step: determining whether the molecule is safe and effective in humans.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the receptors targeted by semaglutide are found in the brain but also in the gut, pancreas and other tissues," said assistant professor of pathology katrin svensson, phd. "That's why Ozempic has widespread effects including slowing the movement of food through the digestive tract and lowering blood sugar levels. In contrast, BRP appears to act specifically in the hypothalamus, which controls appetite and metabolism. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the hypothalamus is a small but essential region deep within the brain. Among its many responsibilities, it helps regulate hunger, energy use, body temperature, and other functions needed to maintain the body's internal balance. Because it plays such a central role in appetite, it is an important target for researchers developing obesity treatments.

Diungkapkan bahwa semaglutide works by imitating a hormone called glucagon-like peptide 1, or glp-1. This hormone helps regulate blood sugar and signals that influence hunger and feelings of fullness. However, GLP-1 receptors are distributed throughout several parts of the body, which helps explain why medications that activate them can produce effects beyond appetite suppression.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, brp appears to take another route. Although it influences some of the same broad metabolic functions as semaglutide, it activates different populations of brain cells. Scientists believe this distinction could make it possible to control hunger more precisely while reducing unwanted effects elsewhere in the body.

Diungkapkan bahwa svensson, who served as senior author of the study, published in nature, has also cofounded a company to advance brp toward human clinical trials. The research was led by senior research scientist Laetitia Coassolo, PhD.

How Artificial Intelligence Uncovered a Hidden Molecule.

Berdasarkan laporan, finding brp required solving a problem that has long complicated the search for new hormones. The human body produces enormous numbers of small protein fragments, but only a fraction have important biological functions. Identifying the ones that influence appetite or metabolism can be extremely difficult.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many hormones begin as larger, inactive proteins known as prohormones. Specialized enzymes cut these proteins into smaller pieces called peptides. Some of those peptides become chemical messengers that help coordinate processes such as energy metabolism, appetite, and organ function.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a single prohormone can be cut in several different places, potentially producing numerous peptides with distinct effects. The challenge is determining which fragments are biologically useful and which are simply leftovers from normal protein processing. The important peptide hormones (which are relatively rare) can be difficult to distinguish from the much larger collection of ordinary protein fragments.

Berdasarkan laporan, traditional approaches often involve extracting proteins from biological tissues and analyzing them with techniques such as mass spectrometry. This method identifies molecules by measuring characteristics related to their mass, but the sheer number of possible peptides makes searching for new hormones a demanding process.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the stanford team decided to approach the problem differently. They concentrated on an enzyme called prohormone convertase 1/3, which cuts prohormones at particular amino acid sequences and has previously been linked to human obesity. Amino acids are the molecular building blocks of proteins, and their arrangement helps determine where enzymes can cut them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the hormones produced through this process is glp-1, the same hormone whose effects semaglutide mimics. The researchers reasoned that other peptides generated through similar processing might also help regulate appetite and energy use.

AI Searches 20,000 Human Genes for New Hormones.

Berdasarkan laporan, to accelerate the search, the scientists created a computer algorithm called peptide predictor. Instead of physically isolating and examining hundreds of thousands of peptides, the program analyzed the roughly 20,000 genes that encode human proteins, looking for sequences where the enzyme was likely to make cuts.

Diungkapkan bahwa the team then refined the results by concentrating on genes associated with proteins released outside cells, a common characteristic of hormones. They also required each candidate protein to contain at least four potential cutting sites.

These filters reduced an enormous collection of possibilities to 373 prohormones, making experimental testing much more practical.

"The algorithm was absolutely key to our findings," Svensson said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, peptide predictor estimated that the enzyme could produce 2,683 distinct peptides from those 373 proteins. From this collection, Svensson and Coassolo selected candidates that appeared particularly likely to influence brain activity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers eventually tested 100 peptides, including glp-1, using nerve cells grown in the laboratory. Their goal was to find substances capable of stimulating neuronal activity, an early indication that a peptide might influence important brain processes.

A Tiny Peptide Produces a Surprising Result.

GLP-1 performed strongly in the laboratory tests, increasing neuronal activity to three times the level observed in untreated control cells.

Berdasarkan laporan, one previously unrecognized peptide, however, produced an even more striking response. Consisting of just 12 amino acids, it increased neuronal activity tenfold compared with the controls.

The researchers named the molecule BRP after the larger protein from which it originates, BPM/retinoic acid inducible neural specific 2, or BRINP2 (BRINP2-related-peptide).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that unusually powerful response made brp a promising candidate for further investigation. The next question was whether stimulating laboratory-grown brain cells would translate into meaningful changes in appetite and body weight in living animals.

Food Intake Drops by Up to 50% in Animal Experiments.

Diungkapkan bahwa the team tested brp in lean mice and minipigs (which more closely mirror human metabolism and eating patterns than mice do). Before the animals were fed, researchers administered BRP through an injection into the muscle.

Diungkapkan bahwa the results were striking. During the following hour, the treated animals consumed up to 50% less food than expected, suggesting that BRP could strongly influence hunger.

Berdasarkan laporan, the scientists then examined whether repeated treatment could produce sustained changes in body weight. Obese mice received daily BRP injections for 14 days. By the end of the experiment, the treated mice had lost an average of 3 grams, while untreated control mice had gained approximately 3 grams.

Berdasarkan laporan, importantly, nearly all the weight lost by the brp-treated mice came from body fat rather than muscle. Preserving muscle is an important goal in obesity treatment because muscle tissue supports strength, mobility, and metabolic health.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the treated animals also showed improvements in glucose and insulin tolerance. These measurements reflect how effectively the body handles sugar and responds to insulin, the hormone that helps move glucose from the bloodstream into cells.

Together, the findings suggest that BRP may influence both appetite and metabolic health, although it remains unknown whether people would experience comparable benefits.

Could BRP Avoid Common Ozempic Side Effects?.

One of the most intriguing aspects of the discovery is the possibility that BRP could provide weight loss benefits while avoiding some unwanted effects associated with semaglutide and similar medications.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to investigate potential side effects, the researchers monitored the behavior and physical responses of the treated mice and pigs. They found no significant differences in movement, water consumption, anxiety-related behavior, or fecal output compared with control animals.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the absence of changes in fecal production was particularly interesting because constipation is a known side effect of medications such as ozempic. The experiments also showed that BRP promoted fat loss without the substantial muscle loss that can accompany some weight reduction treatments.

Berdasarkan laporan, nausea is another common concern with existing glp-1 medications, although animal experiments cannot fully establish whether brp would prevent that symptom in people. Human testing will be essential to determine the molecule's actual side effect profile.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, additional investigations into brain activity and other physiological responses reinforced the idea that brp works differently from semaglutide. The peptide activated distinct neuronal and metabolic pathways rather than simply copying the effects of GLP-1.

This difference may explain why the researchers observed strong appetite suppression without several of the behavioral and digestive changes they were monitoring.

What Comes Next for the Potential Ozempic Alternative?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, despite the encouraging findings, brp is still at an early stage of development. Researchers need to understand more about exactly how the molecule communicates with cells and how its effects might be sustained over longer periods.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one priority is identifying the cell surface receptors that recognize brp. Receptors are specialized proteins that respond to particular chemical signals, allowing cells to detect messages and trigger appropriate biological responses. Determining which receptors BRP activates could help explain its effects on hunger and metabolism.

Diungkapkan bahwa the team also wants to investigate ways of extending the molecule's activity inside the body. Peptides can be broken down relatively quickly, potentially requiring frequent injections. A longer-lasting version of BRP could make treatment more convenient if it eventually proves effective in people.

Diungkapkan bahwa the ultimate challenge will be establishing whether its apparent advantages in animals translate into meaningful benefits for patients. Clinical trials will need to evaluate its safety, effectiveness, appropriate dosage, and potential side effects before it could become a practical obesity treatment.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the lack of effective drugs to treat obesity in humans has been a problem for decades," svensson said. "Nothing we've tested before has compared to semaglutide's ability to decrease appetite and body weight. We are very eager to learn if it is safe and effective in humans. ".

Scientists from the University of California, Berkeley; the University of Minnesota; and the University of British Columbia also participated in the research.

Financial support came from the National Institutes of Health (grants R01DK125260, P30DK116074, K99AR081618 and GM113854), the SPARK Translational Research Program at Stanford, Stanford Bio-X, the Stanford Maternal and Child Health Research Institute, the American Heart Association, a Stanford Medicine Dean's Fellowship Award, the Carlsberg Foundation, and the Wu Tsai Human Performance Alliance.

Berdasarkan laporan, svensson and coassolo are named inventors on patents involving the use of brp peptides to treat metabolic disorders. Svensson is also a cofounder of Merrifield Therapeutics.

A pioneering therapy that edits genes inside a recipient’s body continues to be effective four years after treatment, according to data released by its developer, Intellia Therapeutics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the therapy, named lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z), was designed to treat one form of a genetic disorder that causes episodes of painful and potentially dangerous swelling in the throat and other parts of the body. Lonvo-z deploys the CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing system to disable the gene that produces prekallikrein, a protein made in the liver that promotes blood-vessel leakage.

Bigger than CRISPR? A guide to the latest genome editors.

Bigger than CRISPR? A guide to the latest genome editors.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, intellia, headquartered in cambridge, massachusetts, has applied for approval of lonvo-z to the us food and drug administration (fda), which is expected to issue a decision by 10 march. If approved, the therapy will become the world’s first CRISPR medicine to be delivered directly inside the body, or in vivo, John Leonard, Intellia’s chief executive, told investors on 12 November. Currently, the only CRISPR therapy approved by the FDA is performed on cells that have first been removed from the body and are subsequently re-infused.

Berdasarkan laporan, for people with the condition, hereditary angioedema, the gene-editing approach could offer relief from a lifetime of juggling medications to prevent and treat swelling attacks, says jonathan bernstein, a hereditary angioedema specialist at the university of cincinnati in ohio and an investigator on a lonvo-z trial. “It’s very reassuring,” he says of the four-year data. “That’s what you’re supposed to see. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the only approved crispr therapy is casgevy, a treatment for two genetic blood disorders, sickle cell anemia and ß-thalassemia. To create a dose of Casgevy, physicians first remove blood stem cells from the recipient, then send them off for gene editing. The edited cells are infused back into the recipient.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the therapy must be made anew for each person, adding time, cost, and complexity. The recipient also has to undergo harsh chemotherapy treatment to make room for the edited cells.

CRISPR makes enhanced cancer-fighting immune cells inside mice.

CRISPR makes enhanced cancer-fighting immune cells inside mice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in vivo gene-editing approaches aim to sidestep these concerns by editing genes directly in the body. The particles are infused into the blood and taken up by the liver, where prekallikrein is produced. Lonvo-z, for example, consists of fatty particles that encase mRNA encoding CRISPR-Cas9 components. The procedure takes one day.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in vivo gene editing can introduce other safety concerns, however. The therapy affords no opportunity to screen out cells with unwanted edits at other locations in the genome, or in other organs. Recipients might also have harmful immune responses to the treatment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last year, the fda placed a clinical hold on two other in vivo studies sponsored by intellia after a participant — an older man with other health conditions — developed liver damage and died after receiving a crispr treatment. The FDA lifted the hold this year after requiring added safety measures.

NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet.

The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it.

Diungkapkan bahwa curiosity snapped the close-up image on oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mahli is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image.

Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow.

Diungkapkan bahwa the relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of nazca — which shares its name with an ancient south american civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

#415. Scientists discover that a clogged filter could revolutionize oil refining

📅 05 Nov 2026

Scientists discover that a clogged filter could revolutionize oil refining

Tanggal: 05 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261103003207.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, researchers have developed a surprisingly simple way to separate crude oil without heating it, potentially transforming one of the world's most energy-intensive industrial processes. The breakthrough uses an inexpensive membrane that could significantly reduce the energy required for oil refining while lowering operating costs and carbon emissions.

Diungkapkan bahwa the international research effort was led by professor dong-yeun koh at the korea advanced institute of science and technology, known as kaist, in collaboration with professor ryan lively's research group at georgia tech. KAIST(President Kwang Hyung Lee) announced that the team had successfully demonstrated a membrane capable of separating crude oil at room temperature. The findings were published in Nature, one of the world's leading scientific journals.

Sebagaimana diketahui, crude oil is essential for far more than gasoline and other transportation fuels. It also supplies the raw materials used to manufacture plastics, packaging, clothing, and numerous everyday products. Because refining costs affect the prices of these materials, making the process more efficient could have widespread economic and environmental benefits.

Why Traditional Crude Oil Refining Requires So Much Energy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for more than a century, oil refineries have relied heavily on distillation to separate crude oil into useful components. The process involves heating oil to temperatures above 350 °C, turning portions of it into vapor, and then cooling those vapors to collect different fractions.

Diungkapkan bahwa this approach requires an enormous amount of energy. Worldwide, crude oil distillation consumes approximately 1,100 terawatt-hours (TWh) annually. That is comparable to the combined yearly electricity production of roughly 130 continuously operating nuclear power plants, each with a capacity of about one gigawatt.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the massive energy demand makes distillation a major contributor to both fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions within the refining industry. Meanwhile, growing economic pressures across global petrochemical markets have increased interest in technologies that can separate oil more efficiently.

Berdasarkan laporan, membranes have emerged as a promising alternative because they can separate substances without requiring the extreme temperatures used in conventional distillation. However, previous designs have faced significant obstacles.

Berdasarkan laporan, traditionally, researchers have assumed that effective molecular separation requires a membrane covered with an extremely thin, specialized coating. Although these coatings can provide the necessary precision, they are expensive to produce and can develop defects when manufactured on a large scale. These limitations have made widespread industrial adoption difficult.

A Surprising Discovery Turns Clogged Filters Into an Advantage.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the kaist and georgia tech researchers approached the problem differently. Rather than adding a complicated coating, they used a bare membrane made from porous polyacrylonitrile (PAN), an inexpensive, chemically stable polymer already commonly used as a supporting material in industrial filtration systems.

What happened when crude oil passed through the membrane was unexpected.

Berdasarkan laporan, as the oil flowed through its pores, heavier hydrocarbon molecules accumulated along the inner walls. This buildup gradually reduced the size of the openings, producing extremely narrow channels measuring less than 2 nanometers across.

In effect, the crude oil helped create the microscopic pathways needed to separate its own components.

These naturally formed channels allowed lighter oil fractions, including naphtha, gasoline, and kerosene, to pass through quickly while preventing heavier substances from traveling through the membrane as easily.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the discovery was especially surprising because the buildup of material inside membrane pores, known as fouling, is normally considered a serious problem. Fouling typically reduces filtration performance and requires cleaning or replacement. In this case, however, the same phenomenon made the membrane highly effective at separating different molecules.

Diungkapkan bahwa the results were impressive. The uncoated PAN membrane achieved crude oil permeation rates approximately 23 times higher than those reported for previous leading crude oil separation membranes. It also continued operating with stable performance for 28 consecutive days.

Sebagaimana diketahui, professor ryan lively (georgia tech) commented: "one of the key challenges facing membrane systems for crude oil separation was the low productivities of the membrane units -- the pan membranes with their surprising separation mechanism -- dramatically increase the productivity of the membrane unit, to the point where industry should seriously consider adopting the technology. ".

New Membrane Could Cut Oil Refining Energy Use by Nearly a Third.

One of the technology's biggest advantages is that refineries would not necessarily need to replace their existing equipment to use it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the membrane could instead be installed as a modular filtration system that processes crude oil before it enters conventional distillation equipment. This would reduce the amount of work required during the heating and separation stages while allowing facilities to continue using much of their current infrastructure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, computer simulations suggest that incorporating the membrane into the refining process could deliver substantial improvements. 6%, while carbon dioxide emissions could decrease by 37. 6%. Energy consumption could fall by 31. The same calculations projected a 20. 7% reduction in cooling water consumption and a 36% decrease in operating costs.

The potential environmental benefits could be considerable if the technology were adopted widely.

Sebagaimana diketahui, researchers estimate that implementing the system throughout korea's refining and petrochemical industries could prevent approximately 10 million tonnes of greenhouse gas emissions each year. That is roughly equivalent to the annual emissions produced by four million vehicles powered by internal combustion engines.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these savings are projections based on process simulations rather than reductions already demonstrated across operating refineries. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that membrane filtration could become a practical way to improve the efficiency of existing facilities.

Although crude oil separation was the main focus of the research, the same technology could eventually be useful in several other industries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one potential application involves treating pyrolysis oil produced when waste plastics are broken down for recycling. The membranes could also help recover solvents used in battery manufacturing, purify pharmaceutical compounds, and improve biofuel production.

Berdasarkan laporan, the broader opportunity lies in using complex liquid mixtures to help form the tiny filtration channels needed to separate their components. This approach could provide a more affordable and versatile alternative to conventional membranes that require precisely manufactured surface coatings.

Berdasarkan laporan, professor dong-yeun koh of kaist said, "this study reveals a new scientific principle in which a membrane interacts with a complex mixture and spontaneously forms its own separation channels. Working with real crude oil supplied by HD Hyundai Oilbank allowed us to validate the technology under conditions relevant to industrial operation. ".

The use of actual crude oil was an important part of the research because it allowed the team to examine how the membrane performed with the complicated mixture of hydrocarbons found in industrial feedstocks.

Before the technology can be deployed more widely, the researchers plan to improve membrane production at larger scales and establish its reliability during extended operation.

Diungkapkan bahwa professor jae w. #419. Scientists accidentally solve a chemistry mystery that lasted 60 years

📅 06 Nov 2026

Scientists accidentally solve a chemistry mystery that lasted 60 years

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261103003205.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, a chemistry challenge that had frustrated researchers for more than 60 years has finally been overcome. Scientists at the University of Würzburg in Germany have discovered a way to produce and isolate oxoboranes, a group of unusual molecules that were long considered too unstable to study under ordinary laboratory conditions.

Diungkapkan bahwa the breakthrough, published in nature chemistry, was led by professor holger braunschweig and his team, with computational support from researchers led by professor ashwini k. Phukan at Tezpur University in India. Their findings reveal a surprisingly straightforward way to create these elusive compounds, potentially opening new possibilities for molecular chemistry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, boron is an element that rarely forms triple bonds, a type of chemical connection in which two atoms share three pairs of electrons. For more than 15 years, Braunschweig has focused on overcoming this limitation and creating molecules containing unusual bonds involving boron.

Diungkapkan bahwa his laboratory has already achieved several important milestones. In 2012, the team reported the first molecule containing a triple bond between two boron atoms. Another breakthrough followed in 2025, when the researchers produced the first neutral molecule featuring a triple bond between boron and carbon.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one major challenge remained among the elements in the first row of the periodic table's p-block. Researchers had yet to isolate stable organic oxoboranes, molecules characterized by a triple bond between boron and oxygen.

Diungkapkan bahwa chemists around the world had been pursuing these compounds since at least the early 1960s. Other experiments provided indirect evidence of their existence, and researchers succeeded in creating several related derivatives. Over the decades, scientists working in both organic and inorganic chemistry had managed to detect and trap oxoboranes under extreme conditions. However, obtaining stable examples that could be isolated and examined remained an unsolved problem.

An Unexpected Reaction Produces Elusive Molecules.

The long-awaited breakthrough emerged from experiments that initially appeared to be heading in a different direction.

Two doctoral students at the University of Würzburg, Lukas Lubczyk and Christian Markl, were independently investigating reactions between a compound known as a diboracumulene and various ketones, which are commonly used chemicals in organic synthesis.

Sebagaimana diketahui, both researchers noticed something unusual. Instead of producing only the outcomes they might have expected, the reactions generated distinctive orange or yellow solids.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the discovery was a pleasant surprise. I never thought the diboracumulene would react the way it did, let alone with multiple different, simple substrates. And when Christian came to me with his compound, I knew we were onto something," says Lukas Lubczyk.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what made the results particularly remarkable was that oxoboranes emerged as the main products of these reactions, even though several other chemical outcomes had appeared more likely. After decades of unsuccessful efforts to isolate such molecules, the researchers had found that they could form unexpectedly from reactions involving relatively simple starting materials.

Braunschweig described just how surprising the discovery was to scientists familiar with the long-standing challenge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "nearly everybody in the field had given up on oxoboranes, as they were thought to be just too unstable to be isolated. So we were stunned to see them spontaneously form in these reactions and stick around long enough that we could study them," says Holger Braunschweig.

Diungkapkan bahwa using their newly discovered method, the scientists successfully prepared three different oxoboranes. The fact that the approach worked with multiple compounds suggests that it could provide access to a much wider range of these previously difficult to isolate molecules.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the team is now investigating how broadly the technique can be applied. Beyond producing additional oxoboranes, the researchers hope to determine whether similar strategies could help them create other elusive compounds involving elements throughout the periodic table.

The discovery not only resolves a problem that challenged chemists for more than six decades but also demonstrates how unexpected chemical reactions can reveal possibilities that researchers once considered beyond reach.

International Research Collaboration and Funding.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the findings were published through a collaboration between the würzburg research team and the group led by professor ashwini k. Phukan at Tezpur University (India), whose computational research helped support the work.

Funding was provided by the German Research Foundation (DFG), the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), and the Department of Science & Technology (DST) of India.

Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island.

Berdasarkan laporan, both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences. The 2027 event combines over six minutes of totality with some of the very best weather prospects possible, while 2028 offers over five minutes of totality above some of the world's most famous wildernesses and cityscapes.

Diungkapkan bahwa eclipse chasing requires careful planning and dedication, but also significant funds. If you can only choose one, which should it be?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for europeans, southern spain is the obvious easy option. Tarifa, at the country's southern tip, will see about 4 minutes, 39 seconds of totality, while the U. Overseas Territory of Gibraltar gets about 4 minutes, 25 seconds. K. Weather prospects generally improve, too, as the path crosses the deserts of North Africa.

Diungkapkan bahwa egypt is the headline destination. The climatic odds are excellent, with clouds extremely rare in early August. Luxor will see about 6 minutes, 20 seconds of totality near midday, with Karnak Temple, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the world's greatest ancient monuments nearby. That combination of a very long totality, ancient landscapes and a very high probability of a clear sky makes 2027's path of totality highly unusual.

Diungkapkan bahwa but there are downsides. m. when the sun (and moon) will be high overhead — making photography very difficult. Temperatures around Luxor can exceed 105°F (41°C) in August, a dust storm is not impossible, and totality occurs shortly after 1 p. Demand is already intense, making organized trips expensive. Spain will be considerably easier and probably cheaper for European eclipse chasers, but at the expense of roughly two minutes of totality — and slightly less favorable weather prospects.

Diungkapkan bahwa if 2027 is about extreme duration, 2028 is about choice. That's about 6. 3 million people, according to Time and Date. On July 22, 2028, a path of totality will cross the Cocos Islands, Christmas Island, Australia, from northwest to southeast — passing directly over Sydney — before continuing across the Tasman Sea to New Zealand's South Island. This will be an exclusive eclipse experienced by relatively few people, certainly when compared to the eclipses in 2024, 2026 and 2027.

Diungkapkan bahwa maximum totality will last 5 minutes and 10 seconds in the remote kimberley region of western australia. Diungkapkan bahwa then there's sydney. Sydney Opera House and Harbor Bridge beneath a totally eclipsed sun could produce some of the decade's defining astronomical images, while millions of people experiencing totality together should create an extraordinary atmosphere. But in 2028, anyone prioritizing their chances of a clear totality will be tempted by a (albeit pricier) trip to the Outback. For Europeans, reaching Australia also comes with considerable cost and time. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's another reason to think beyond those few minutes of darkness. With the right planning, an eclipse trip can also become an extraordinary astronomy vacation (tip: come a week before the eclipse for the darkest evening skies). Here, 2028 offers visitors from Europe and North America something very different — the Southern Hemisphere night sky.

Berdasarkan laporan, july is a superb time to see the bright central regions of the milky way from dark locations in australia. The Southern Cross, or Crux, is one of the southern sky's defining sights, with Alpha and Beta Centauri nearby. Omega Centauri, the largest and brightest globular cluster visible from Earth, is another showpiece, while the Eta Carinae region offers one of the richest sections of the Milky Way for binoculars and small telescopes.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are other reasons to extend the trip. A partial lunar eclipse occurs on July 6-7, 2028, while the Southern Delta Aquariid meteor shower peaks around July 28 — a week after the eclipse, during a first-quarter moon — and is particularly well seen from the Southern Hemisphere. Diungkapkan bahwa the 2027 eclipse has fewer night-sky extras. The Delta Aquariid meteor shower peaks a few days before the eclipse — in dark, moonless skies — while Jupiter will dominate the western sky shortly after sunset. However, anyone traveling from the Northern Hemisphere will largely see a familiar celestial hemisphere. Australia offers a genuinely different sky experience.

Perhaps the most useful way to choose between these eclipses is not to compare their durations, but to imagine where you would most like to be when the moon's shadow arrives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2027, the decision largely comes down to how far along the eclipse track you want to travel. Stay in southern Spain for convenience and around four minutes of totality, head into Tunisia for longer totality and excellent weather prospects, or go all-in on Egypt for more than six minutes beneath almost cloudless desert skies — and bragging rights among eclipse chasers.
