Head thousands of miles away into the Australian interior and the same event becomes a lonely "me eclipse" in the wilderness, with up to five minutes of totality above an immense Outback landscape. Continue to New Zealand, and there's yet another possibility — a shorter totality with the sun much lower in the afternoon sky.

Berdasarkan laporan, if your priority is purely totality duration, 2027 marginally wins. More than six minutes of totality combined with extraordinarily reliable weather is a rare combination. There's a good reason Aug. 2, 2027 is being marketed as the "eclipse of the century. " But if you've always wanted to visit Australia or New Zealand, the 2028 eclipse is an extraordinary excuse to finally go, in addition to experiencing a long totality.

Sebagaimana diketahui, choose the trip you most want to take, then find the best possible place for you within the path of totality. After all, no total solar eclipse lasts long enough, and most eclipse chasers struggle to recall exactly how long totality lasted. They're just left with the same question as always — when is the next one?.

#424. Five-inch-long beetle larvae are quietly destroying blueberry roots

Five-inch-long beetle larvae are quietly destroying blueberry roots

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261103003200.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, north carolina's blueberry growers are facing an emerging threat from a destructive beetle whose larvae feed underground, damaging plant roots and potentially killing blueberry bushes. Scientists have now identified the insect responsible, providing an important first step toward protecting crops from the pest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a research team at north carolina state university has confirmed that the culprit is prionus imbricornus, a species of longhorn beetle distinguished by its long antennae. These wood-boring insects are becoming a growing concern for blueberry producers in the state.

Sebagaimana diketahui, female beetles generally deposit their eggs in soil near the roots of hardwood trees. After hatching, the larvae feed on the roots, sometimes destroying enough tissue to kill the tree. The larvae can reach an impressive five inches in length, while the adult beetles do not feed.

A Decade-Old Mystery Beneath Blueberry Fields.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, north carolina is the first state to document p. imbricornus feeding on blueberry bushes. However, signs of a similar problem have existed for years. Reports of unidentified Prionus larvae damaging blueberry roots date back to 2010, but researchers had struggled to determine which species was responsible.

Diungkapkan bahwa part of the challenge was the insects' underground habitat. Because the larvae remain near plant roots, they are difficult to locate and study. Making matters more complicated, larvae from different longhorn beetle species often look remarkably similar, making visual identification unreliable.

According to Kenneth Geisert, a graduate student in NC State's College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and lead author of the study, this uncertainty has made it difficult to develop appropriate pest control strategies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "before now, researchers often just assumed the species of prionus on their commodities based on adult identification," geisert said. "If that guess was incorrect, it could mean using a treatment strategy that did not line up with the problem and incorrectly associating species and their hosts. Without knowing which species of beetle you're dealing with and their ecology, incorrect management can cause adverse effects on non-target insects. imbricornus attacks roots, another type of longhorn beetle might attack the trunk of a tree, or dead branches. For instance, while P. ".

To identify the insects, the research team conducted fieldwork at six blueberry farms in North Carolina's Pender, Sampson, Bladen, and New Hanover counties.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the scientists installed black panel traps containing sex pheromones, chemical signals that attract adult beetles. After collecting the insects, they used a DNA identification technique known as genetic barcoding to determine the identity of larvae found in the fields.

Diungkapkan bahwa this method examines short, standardized sections of dna and compares them with reference sequences from known species. By matching genetic material from the unidentified larvae with DNA from adult Prionus beetles, the researchers could determine which species was present.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the analysis produced a 98 to 99 percent match with p. imbricornus, confirming the identity of the beetle responsible for the root damage.

A Growing Threat With No Approved Insecticides.

Although identifying the pest represents an important breakthrough, it also highlights a serious challenge for blueberry growers.

Lorena Lopez, an assistant extension professor in NC State's Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology and a co-author of the study, explained that the discovery brings both encouraging and troubling news.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "on one hand, it's very important that we know which species we're dealing with," she said. "On the other, North Carolina was the first state to ever report Prionus infestation in blueberries, and there are no insecticides currently labeled against this pest in blueberries. ".

To help address this problem, Lopez has begun testing insecticides to determine which treatments might effectively control the beetles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a major focus is finding the best time to apply treatments. By coordinating insecticide applications with the beetles' reproductive cycles, researchers hope to disrupt larval development before the insects can inflict extensive damage on blueberry roots.

If successful, this approach could give farmers a much-needed way to protect their crops against an emerging pest that has remained difficult to identify and manage for more than a decade.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the findings appear in the journal of integrated pest management in a paper titled "prionus imbricornis (coleoptera: cerambycidae), an emerging pest in north carolina blueberries. " Gareth Powell, an assistant professor at NC State and director of the NCSU Insect Museum, also contributed to the research.

Twin NASA spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long escapade, ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the escape and plasma acceleration and dynamics explorers (escapade) spacecraft launched in november 2025 on the second-ever flight of blue origin's new glenn rocket. But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory. Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars.

Diungkapkan bahwa "no nasa mission has ever done this before," said rob lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the university of california, berkeley and principal investigator of the escapade mission. "For most missions, it just isn't necessary. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa that's because traditionally nasa's mars missions have been carefully choreographed within cosmic launch constraints, leaving earth during a brief window of planetary alignment that only occurs every 26 months. ESCAPADE was meant to launch in October 2024, when Earth and Mars were favorably aligned, but delays with the New Glenn rocket forced the mission to sit out the precious launch window.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rather than wait to launch this fall, nasa decided to try something new. ESCAPADE mission planners designed a "loitering" orbit, shaped like a kidney bean. It called for the twin probes to loop through that trajectory to be back at Earth in early November 2026, ready to continue on to Mars.

Diungkapkan bahwa once they arrived, however, the twin probes faced a major hurdle: each had to perfectly execute an engine burn within earth's gravity well. The maneuver is similar to the slingshot flybys that spacecraft regularly conduct to adjust their trajectories — but here, the probes had to fire their engines to amp up the effect of the burn rather than acting alone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first spacecraft tackled the feat on nov. 7; the second did so on Monday (Nov. And according to NASA, the burns went perfectly. 9). "This is the first time NASA has used a powered Earth flyby to propel a spacecraft toward Mars, and we've now executed this maneuver twice, flawlessly, in just two days," Asal Naseri, acting associate flight director for NASA's Heliophysics Division said in a statement.

After just a few minor course corrections, ESCAPADE will be sailing toward a September 2027 Mars arrival.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the twin escapade spacecraft have made the most of their extended tour. Each spacecraft is about the size of two refrigerators and equipped with three scientific instruments and a couple cameras. All are tailored for studying the strange magnetic field of Mars, which is created both globally by charged particles from the sun interacting with the atmosphere and locally by areas of highly magnetic crust.

Sebagaimana diketahui, earth's magnetic field is much stronger and generated by the planet's core. But it too is affected by the solar wind, as scientists call the constant stream of charged particles flowing off the sun and across space. On the side of Earth opposite the sun, the solar wind stretches the magnetic field to form an elongated tail structure, like a terrestrial windsock.

Diungkapkan bahwa a range of missions have studied this magnetotail at various points up to nearly 800,000 miles (1. Conveniently, the two ESCAPADE spacecraft traveled through the structure over the course of about 10 days early last year at a much greater distance from Earth — some 1. 19 million miles (1. 27 million kilometers) away from Earth, but beyond that, it has been a mystery. 91 million km) away.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we were able to capture the magnetic field structure of that distant tail, how it flaps, how it moves, how the plasma flows within it," lillis said, gathering data that he called "unprecedented. " "And not only that but for the first time, we were able to do that with two spacecraft simultaneously. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa a second shot at the magnetotail came over the summer, when the spacecraft were much closer to earth but the moon was also passing through the magnetic structure. The two ESCAPADE spacecraft were able to partner with twin ARTEMIS-THEMIS spacecraft at the moon to observe the structure from four different perspectives simultaneously.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's a huge boon when trying to study the magnetotail and its intricate and ever-changing magnetic field lines and plasma, lillis said. "These are generally not things you can measure remotely," he said. "You kind of have to be there. ".

#428. Permanent daylight saving time has a dark side, scientists warn

📅 04 Nov 2026

Permanent daylight saving time has a dark side, scientists warn

Tanggal: 04 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261103003157.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, keeping daylight saving time in effect all year could bring brighter evenings, but new research suggests the change would come with a troubling consequence for american children. A nationwide switch could result in at least 2 billion additional trips to school in darkness, potentially increasing safety risks while reducing children's exposure to important morning sunlight.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the debate over permanent daylight saving time has gained momentum in washington, d. This past summer, the U. S. C. House of Representatives approved legislation that would eliminate the annual return to standard time in the fall. Nineteen states, including Washington, have already approved measures supporting the change, which would take effect in those states if the federal bill becomes law.

Berdasarkan laporan, the legislation remains stalled in the senate, with school start times emerging as a major concern. Permanent daylight saving time (DST) would push sunrise an hour later during the winter months, leaving mornings darker from November through March. Although this would affect everyone traveling early in the day, researchers at the University of Washington wanted to understand what it would mean specifically for children heading to school.

Permanent Daylight Saving Time Could Add Billions of Dark School Commutes.

Berdasarkan laporan, to measure the potential impact, the research team examined 14 of the 19 states that have already approved permanent daylight saving time measures. They combined school enrollment figures, individual school start times, and geographic coordinates to determine how frequently students would need to travel to school before sunrise. The researchers then calculated the total number of these trips under the proposed system and compared it with the current practice of changing clocks twice a year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the results revealed substantial increases. In Washington state alone, permanent daylight saving time would produce nearly 35 million additional school commutes in darkness. Similar patterns emerged across the other 13 states, with Georgia showing the largest increase at approximately 71 million additional dark trips.

When the researchers extended their findings to estimate the nationwide impact, they calculated that permanent daylight saving time would create at least 2 billion more trips to school before sunrise compared with the current system.

Berdasarkan laporan, the potential consequences go beyond inconvenient mornings. An analysis of U. traffic collision records found that fatal crashes involving school-aged pedestrians were roughly twice as likely to occur during dark mornings as after sunrise. S. The findings were published October 29 in the journal Current Biology.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it's called the 'sunshine protection act' because you get an extra hour of light at the end of the day. But you will take that hour from the morning. Nobody wants their kids to go to school in the dark. It's a very tangible metric that anybody from any state or socioeconomic background can relate to. You could call it the Sunshine Destruction Act," said senior author Horacio de la Iglesia, a professor of biology at the University of Washington. "These dark mornings will inequitably affect children who have to go to school at a certain time. ".

Why Morning Sunlight Matters for Children's Health.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, beyond concerns about traffic safety, losing access to morning sunlight could interfere with the body's natural daily rhythms. Bright light early in the day helps synchronize the circadian clock, the internal timing system that influences sleep, mood, appetite, and other important functions. When people receive too little morning light, maintaining these biological rhythms can become more difficult.

For children, who must typically follow fixed school schedules, darker mornings could mean missing a valuable opportunity to receive daylight at a time when their bodies need it.

Berdasarkan laporan, "when we send kids to school in the dark, we are depriving them from an opportunity to get that morning daylight," said lead author guadalupe rodríguez ferrante, a postdoctoral researcher in biology at the university of washington. "We were asking what's the cost for these children. We wanted actual numbers, a real number of kids based on the geographic location of each school. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the researchers also identified which communities would experience the greatest changes. Schools located near the western boundaries of time zones, including those in Forks, Washington, would be particularly affected because sunrise already occurs relatively late in those locations. Districts that begin classes early in the morning would face similarly large increases in dark commutes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mississippi and alabama offer striking examples. m. Under the current clock system, each state has approximately 2 million school trips in darkness. Schools in both states begin, on average, before 8 a. With permanent daylight saving time, that figure would rise to more than 20 million trips per state.

Diungkapkan bahwa "some districts probably never experience a dark commute under the current system, and, if this passes, suddenly they will wake up to this new reality that their kids are going to school in the dark," rodríguez ferrante said. "Keep in mind that we used the actual start time listed for each school, and a lot of schools offer breakfast or other things before school, so the kids could be getting there even earlier. ".

Why the 2 Billion Estimate May Be Too Low.

Berdasarkan laporan, although the researchers used detailed school information to calculate changes in 14 states, their nationwide estimate required broader assumptions. To project what would happen if the entire United States adopted permanent daylight saving time, they assumed students would generally be leaving for school at around 8 a. m.

Because many children begin traveling earlier, the team believes the projected increase of approximately 2 billion dark commutes may substantially underestimate the actual impact.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "for the estimation, we assumed students would be leaving home around 8 a. "That's pretty late, so our calculation is likely an underestimation of the real number. m. ," Rodríguez Ferrante said. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the findings also raise questions about efforts to improve teenagers' sleep by delaying high school start times. Adolescents typically have biological clocks that shift later than those of younger children and adults, making later school schedules beneficial. The researchers argue that permanently moving clocks forward could undermine some of those gains by making morning sunlight less accessible.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one possible solution would be to start school later to compensate for the darker mornings. However, de la Iglesia argues that such a change could have ripple effects throughout daily life, potentially requiring families and workplaces to adjust their schedules as well.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i've heard the argument, 'if we're in permanent dst, we can just delay the school start time to address these issues,'" de la iglesia said. And everything is going to get delayed. "Well, if we do that, you will end up going to work later. That, by definition, is Standard Time. And essentially, we're just going to be realigning everybody to solar time. You will get out of work an hour later, and you will miss the opportunity to enjoy your evening light. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the researchers' findings highlight a central tradeoff in the debate over permanent daylight saving time. While eliminating seasonal clock changes would provide more evening sunlight during winter, the additional daylight would come at the expense of morning light, potentially affecting children's safety, sleep, and daily routines.

Sebagaimana diketahui, additional study authors include high school student daniel zhang and university of washington biology undergraduates nirekh dasika, alicia nam, jessie lu, navneet tumber, elena kully-rivera, viridian klei, and micaela e. Romero.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the saturn v moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.

The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the space agency had bet the moon on its new saturn v booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nasa also needed a new launch site for its apollo missions. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. Yet, everything went according to plan.

“It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun, director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time.

The launch came as NASA was on its heels.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, just months earlier, on jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test.

“The maiden voyage of the Saturn V dramatically increased the confidence of people across the nation in the management of the largest research and development undertaking in which the western world has ever engaged,” George Mueller, NASA's then-Associate Administrator for Manned Space Flight, said at the time.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ever since nasa's james webb space telescope (jwst) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old.

Berdasarkan laporan, new research suggests that little red dots may actually be connected primordial black holes, tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the big bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole.

Berdasarkan laporan, "a black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement.

Berdasarkan laporan, "they come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added.

Diungkapkan bahwa though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by stephen hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "little red dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," de luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?".

Sebagaimana diketahui, de luca and colleagues turned their attention to qs01, located around 13. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. 1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots.

Berdasarkan laporan, the team modeled how a little red dot like qs01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "there are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member loris del grosso, also of jhu's department of physics and astronomy. "There can only be so many primordial black holes in the universe, for example, and there cannot be too many of them in a given cluster. ".

Considering three possible scenarios, the team found that the most likely situation is a smaller primordial black hole consuming surrounding gas and energy until it grew to be the size of QSO1.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the door was open on this theory — that little red dots could be primordial black holes," del grosso said. "We've now cracked it open a little farther by showing some scenarios are more likely than others. ".

Del Grosso and crew now intend to look at the other 100 or so Little Red Dots seen by the JWST to determine how many of them could have started life as primordial black holes.

Then scientists may finally have the evidence to say these long-theorized ancient black holes actually existed.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we don't have a clear understanding of what happens in the early universe right after the big bang," de luca concluded. "If primordial black holes do exist, then something had to happen to make them in the first place, which would be a groundbreaking discovery in physics. ".

The team's findings were published in June in the journal Physical Review Letters.

Diungkapkan bahwa it does seem like an eternity since news first broke that portland-based new york times bestselling author daniel h. Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay.

Diungkapkan bahwa that was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue ai named archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in america’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but now we have been blessed with the news, first broken by the hollywood reporter, that ron howard ("apollo 13," "the da vinci code") and akiva goldsman ("a beautiful mind," "star trek: strange new worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new tv series. And what timing, just as AI fever has gripped the planet with paranoia centered around our eventual robot overlords.

As a PhD graduate of Carnegie Mellon University’s Robotics Institute and a future king of the techno-thriller, Wilson was the ideal writer to bring this frightening story to life, and a 2014 sequel titled "Robogenesis" was equally gripping.

The prolific, award-winning writer has since set up a multitude of other Hollywood projects spawned from his catalog of works, including "Amped," "The Clockwork Dynasty," the authorized sequel to Michael Crichton's "The Andromeda Strain," "The Andromeda Evolution," and his 2025 alien invasion novel "Hole in the Sky," still alive at Netflix.

Howard's Imagine Entertainment will partner with Akiva Goldsman's Weed Road Pictures on this episodic adaptation, with Howard attached to direct the pilot episode and Goldsman serving as series showrunner.

Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier.

Diungkapkan bahwa the seattle startup announced on tuesday (nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable.

The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase.

Diungkapkan bahwa otter 24c launched oct. 1 on SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher, Google's planned AI constellation).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the starfish satellite was flying a mission for nasa called small spacecraft propulsion and inspection capability, or sspicy for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site.

"This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added.

Berdasarkan laporan, starfish space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing, using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers.

Diungkapkan bahwa sspicy marked otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U. S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections.

But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "while working through commissioning steps, starfish eventually stopped receiving data from otter 24c," the company said in a nov. 3 X post.

Berdasarkan laporan, "an investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [california company] astro digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain.

"The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, otter pup 2 is now operating as close as 25 meters away from @gilmourspace's elarasat, fully autonomously. We’ve demonstrated our ability to safely and precisely operate at very close range, executing intricate maneuvers, gathering detailed imagery, and testing the capabilities we’ll need for docking. That leaves just one phase left: attempting docking, and a chance to make history. This vid contains imagery captured when we were separated by just 33. 6 meters. With this progress, Otter Pup 2 has officially completed Characterize, the penultimate phase of its mission. October 27, 2026.

The Seattle company has other work to do in LEO at the moment as well: Its Otter Pup 2 prototype craft is currently gearing up to conduct a historic docking of its own in LEO.

Sebagaimana diketahui, otter pup 2, which launched in june 2025, has been getting closer and closer to another private spacecraft, gilmour space's elarasat. Last week, the company announced that Otter Pup 2 got within a mere 82 feet (25 meters) of its target.

Berdasarkan laporan, "with this progress, otter pup 2 has officially completed characterize, the penultimate phase of its mission. That leaves just one phase left: attempting docking, and a chance to make history," Starfish Space said in an Oct. 27 X post.

Diungkapkan bahwa two private satellites have docked before, but only much higher above earth, in geostationary orbit. Such a meetup has not yet happened in LEO.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cape canaveral, fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners.

Diungkapkan bahwa to build and sustain a base on the moon, nasa will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8).

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at nasa's kennedy space center visitor center amidst the agency's max power air show event. Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd.

Diungkapkan bahwa the audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group.

But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we need ways to generate power through the long lunar night. We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this challenge is open to high school and post-secondary students based in the u. For participating students, they will form teams that will work on an idea from one of six different technical topics related to creating and running a moon base. S. These six topics include power systems, habitats, communications, mobility, life support and astronaut safety.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this will be what isaacman described as a "multi-phase competition that mirrors how ideas are developed actually in the aerospace industry. ".

"Teams will first submit concepts, then they're going to refine them, and finalists will have the opportunity to present their solutions directly to NASA leaders and stakeholders," he further explained.

"The prize money is great for sure, but the the real opportunity is to work on problems NASA is actively trying to solve right now, so students don't need to wait to graduation to contribute to that effort," Isaacman added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, right now, nasa has a long road ahead of them before a moon base is actually built. In mid-2027, the agency is planning to launch its Artemis III mission which will see a crew of four astronauts practice rendezvous maneuvers with two different lunar landers. If all goes to plan, this will be followed by Artemis IV landing humans on the moon's surface for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the agency is making these big steps forward to not just a crewed return to the moon, but a sustained, long-term return to the moon. However, knowing that a fully-fledged moon base is still firmly in the future, they are banking on the ingenuity, creativity and passion of.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you're a student or know a student interested in participating in this challenge, you can find more information on nasa's website here. Interested students can register until Jan. 25, 2027.

#447. Hands-on: The Apple HomeView is gorgeous, costs $299, and has no App Store

📅 12 Nov 2026

Hands-on: The Apple HomeView is gorgeous, costs $299, and has no App Store

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/tech/apple-homeview-smart-display-hands-on-first-impressions

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the apple homeview finally arrives on doorsteps (and in apple stores) on friday, and i think this gorgeous little smart display is about to become a common sight in homes around the world. I've been testing the HomeView ahead of its release, and I would definitely recommend it to homeowners, parents, and anyone looking for Christmas gift ideas.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, from the moment i saw the homeview up close, i've had a premonition: apple is going to sell a million of these things. And after adding it to my own home, I'm even more confident in that prediction.

Diungkapkan bahwa as a product reviewer, you get a sixth sense for this. The last time I felt this way about a product? Back in March, when Apple debuted the MacBook Neo, which proved to be extremely popular.

Berdasarkan laporan, for someone like me, who lives in a one-bedroom new york city apartment and tries not to think about whether or not i'll ever be able to afford a down payment, the apple homeview is an awesomely unnecessary sidekick. Personally, I'd buy an iPad stand before a HomeView, but YMMV. However, for my parents, my big sister, and my better-off friends who do own their own homes, I would definitely recommend this device.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for upper-income homeowners, the homeview is a beautiful digital butler for the modern smart abode. (Side note: Apple products have always been high-end, but after the latest price increases, it feels more and more like a luxury brand to me. ) If you plan on investing in Apple's other new smart home gadgets — the new Apple TV 4K, HomePod Mini 2, new home security cameras, and video doorbells — I'd even say the HomeView is a necessity.

Diungkapkan bahwa thanks to the apple home app, you can use the homeview to adjust smart thermostats, view live security camera footage, dim the lights, and turn connected devices on or off. An intercom function lets you use connected speakers to send messages around the house. For this type of user, the wall-mounted model is ideal, though the mount is sold separately and brings the total to $378. 99. For those of you who can afford all those smart home gadgets, why not get a HomeView for your entryway and your kitchen? I suspect many wealthy homeowners will do exactly that.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the homeview doesn't just act as a smart home hub. You can also listen to Apple Music, watch Apple TV, FaceTime with family, browse for recipes in Safari, and check your Apple calendar. (The HomeView runs on its own custom OS that Apple calls HomeView software. The App Store is conspicuously missing, so Safari is your only option for services like YouTube, Gmail, TikTok, and Disney+. ) That lack of apps is the biggest problem with the HomeView so far.

But if you're already a happy little pea in the iOS pod, you can get a lot done with Apple's own apps and widgets, and I think the HomeView justifies its $299 price for the right user.

Berdasarkan laporan, after apple announced the homeview, i said on mashable's instagram that this was a 10/10 product design. 5/10, as it does have larger bezels than most modern displays. I might revise that down to 9. But I'm still enamored with the design.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the homeview actually comes in two models: one with a domed speaker base and an adjustable hinge for the display, and a wall-mounted version. Whether you set it on your kitchen counter or mount it in your entryway, it looks beautiful. For this review in progress, I'm going to focus on the speaker version I tested, which I also think will have a wider appeal.

Berdasarkan laporan, the homeview has a premium design, with a recycled aluminum body and a stainless steel adjustable hinge for the display. The 7-inch Liquid Retina display looks clear and bright whether you're catching up on the latest Silo cliffhanger on Apple TV or admiring the lava lamp-inspired home screen. It has perforations on the bottom of the display and speaker base for audio, and a camera and sensor in the upper bezel. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the homeview defaults to a swirling abstract clock face that responds to light and movement. Like the opening/closing animation on the iPhone Duo, it's the kind of subtle design flex that reminds you Apple does consumer tech design better than anyone. The shapes on the display will darken in low light and track your movements. You can also cycle through a variety of widgets and clock faces at your leisure.

Berdasarkan laporan, apple's new smart display may lack third-party apps, but apple taught it some pretty cool tricks. The HomeView recognizes up to six people in your household by face and voice (if they have a connected iPad or iPhone running iOS 27. 2). So, when you step up to the HomeView, it instantly pulls up your messages, your calendar, and your preferences. But if your husband or wife walks up to it, they'll see their own information, or personal context, as Apple calls it.

What about visitors? Settings for unrecognized visitors let you toggle off explicit content, device control, and sensitive data, protecting the family's privacy.

Diungkapkan bahwa the homeview also has a custom recipe experience, which recognizes a recipe on safari and breaks it down into simple lists of ingredients and steps. (I'm not sure how recipe writers will feel about this feature, but it's undeniably useful. ) And if you don't have a smart thermostat, the HomeView has its own temperature and humidity sensors.

Diungkapkan bahwa the homeview also makes good use of the new siri ai beta. ," the new Siri logo drops from the top bezel with a nifty teardrop animation. But if you've tried the new Siri AI, then you know it's still not done cooking. When you say, "Hey, Siri. Siri sometimes makes stupid mistakes, though in general, the combination of broad world knowledge and personal context results in useful answers to my questions.

Siri AI has been improving with each OS update, and hopefully that continues to be true.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like most new apple products, the homeview has a 12mp center stage camera for video calls. It works well enough for FaceTime calls, which is good, because that's its main job.

Berdasarkan laporan, i did find the speakers a little disappointing. The new MacBook Pro PROLED has much better speakers, for instance. Because the HomeView is more speaker-shaped than a MacBook, I expected more from it. I found the bass disappointing, not in terms of volume, but in depth and mix.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the speaker system isn't bad exactly. It's just not quite as good as I expected. But for jamming out to music while you work or cook, it's just like the Center Stage camera: good enough.

Berdasarkan laporan, look, there's no way around this fact: if you're a privacy-sensitive person, adding another camera and microphone to your home isn't a good idea. Not because Apple is using your data or accessing the camera in inappropriate ways, but purely on principle. The HomeView would benefit from a physical switch that blocks the camera and shuts off the microphone, however.

Berdasarkan laporan, unfortunately for our privacy, most of us already have plenty of devices with cameras and microphones planted all over our homes. So, it comes down to personal preference.

Colors: Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink, and Space Gray.

Display Panel: 7-inch Liquid Retina display.

Sebagaimana diketahui, display brightness: up to 500 nits (0. 3 nits minimum brightness).

Power: Wired USB-C 30W power adapter (wall-mounted model comes with 20W power adapter).

Sebagaimana diketahui, connectivity: wifi 6e, bluetooth 6. 0, Thread.

Diungkapkan bahwa the teaser trailer certainly teases the possibility of a trip to the world's most paradoxically famous secret military base, showcasing a bike and radio resting outside of a fence with a sign that clearly says it's a restricted area (in any tv show or film, that's actually an invitation to see what's on the other side). Sebagaimana diketahui, was it really a site to test highly advanced weapons and aircraft, or was e. T. 's cousin held hostage there until he revealed Colonel Sanders' 11 herbs and spices? SpaceX will make spaceflight history this week, if all goes according to plan.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the company announced over the weekend that it's targeting friday (nov. 13) for the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket, which will attempt something that's never been done before.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both starship and super heavy to the launch site for catch," spacex wrote in a description of flight 15. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, super heavy is starship's giant booster, and starship (or ship for short) is its upper-stage spacecraft. As SpaceX's description noted, both elements are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable.

"Catch" refers to SpaceX's recovery mechanism for both stages: Each will return to the launch mount at SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas and be plucked out of the sky by the tower's "chopstick" arms.

Berdasarkan laporan, spacex has caught super heavy on three starship flights to date, but it has never tried the maneuver with ship. It's a taller order; Ship flies higher and farther than Super Heavy, so its return to Earth is more complex and energetic.

Berdasarkan laporan, spacex founder and ceo elon musk already told us that flight 15 would likely feature a double-catch attempt. But the newly released mission description gives us a launch date, as well as details about the flight.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, flight 15 is scheduled to launch from starbase on friday during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p. m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p. m. local Texas time).

Sebagaimana diketahui, super heavy will come back to starbase for its tower catch about 6. 5 minutes after liftoff, if all goes to plan. But Ship will stay up quite a bit longer.

Diungkapkan bahwa the upper stage will go orbital, something starship did for the first time on flight 14 on sept. 28. And, as on Flight 14, Ship will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, the vanguard of a new megaconstellation that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft, according to Musk.

But Ship should stay aloft for much longer on Flight 15 than it did on Flight 14, which ended with a splashdown in the northern Pacific Ocean about three hours after liftoff.

"Starship’s initial return to launch site mission is expected to orbit the Earth at an altitude of ~275 km [171 miles] and complete approximately 14 orbits around the planet over the course of a more than 22-hour flight," SpaceX wrote in its description of Flight 15.

"Similar to Starship’s first orbital mission, the flight profile has been designed with the opportunity to insert into a passively safe suborbital trajectory or safely deorbit at multiple pre-determined areas over the ocean after raising to an orbital altitude," the company added.

Diungkapkan bahwa so there's no guarantee that ship will indeed come back to starbase for a catch on flight 15; spacex will call off the try if anything is amiss. Whatever happens, however, you should definitely tune in. It's not every day, after all, that you can watch a rocket the size of a 40-story building take flight.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Thanks to a combination of radar, infrasound, dash-cam and security camera footage, astronomers have tracked the bright daytime meteor that fell over Cape Cod Bay in May 2026 back to its origin as a small asteroid perturbed by Jupiter and sent on a comet-like orbit towards Earth.

Sebagaimana diketahui, meteor fireballs visible in the daytime are referred to as 'bolides'. m. At 1:06 p. local time (18:06 UTC) on May 30, 2026 one such bolide was widely witnessed falling out of the sky over coastal Massachusetts, with members of the public also reporting an associated sonic boom that rumbled across the north-eastern coast of the United States.

Now, a team of scientists from Europe and the United States, led by space physicist Juha Vierinen of the Arctic University of Norway in Tromsø, have patched together measurements from a meteor-observing radar network, regular weather radar, infrasound stations and camera footage to fully characterize the fall of this meteoroid and trace its orbit around the sun.

Sebagaimana diketahui, key to these observations were measurements by the spread spectrum interferometric meteor observing network (simone) based at the massachusetts institute of technology's (mit's) haystack observatory. SIMONe is a project jointly developed by MIT, the Arctic University of Norway and the Leibniz Institute of Atmospheric Physics in Kühlungsborn, Germany.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we were fortunate that the event occurred within the coverage of simone," vierinen told space. com.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this is echoed by ryan volz, a radio scientist at haystack observatory who is a member of the team who studied the may 30 bolide. "We got pretty lucky to observe this one," Volz told Space. com. "A bolide like this would have to enter the atmosphere within about 62 miles (100 kilometers) of a SIMONe-like meteor radar system for the head echoes we saw to be detectable, and there are only a handful of places in the world that currently meet that criteria. ".

A head echo is what radar sees when a meteoroid – what we call the lump of rock that becomes a meteor while it is still in space – enters Earth's atmosphere, generating a cloud of plasma around it as it superheats the atmosphere and its outer surface.

"The head echoes give the best constraints on the meteoroid's trajectory," said Volz.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the existence of the head echo is usually very brief, taking place at 56 miles (90 kilometers () altitude down to about 44 miles (71 kilometers) when the plasma around the meteoroid is dense enough to return a radar echo. The head echo transitions into a 'trail echo', which is produced by a streak of turbulent plasma that is left in the wake of the meteoroid after it has passed through a given part of the atmosphere.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the case of the 30 may bolide, the trail echo was detected down to an unusually low altitude of 20 miles (32 kilometers), at which point the falling rock fragmented with an explosive force equivalent to 500 tons of tnt, whereas the total impact energy of the bolide was in the region on 1. 1 kilotons of TNT. Only three recorded bolides around the world had a greater impact energy in the year before (2025), giving an indication of how rare such events are.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at this point, four of the next generation weather radars (nexrad) jointly operated by the national weather service, the federal aviation administration and the u. S. Air Force took over, recording the debris from the fragmentation as solid chunks of rock fell as meteorites into Cape Cod Bay.

Diungkapkan bahwa the radar detections were supported by infrasound readings of the atmospheric pressure waves resulting from the hypervelocity fall and break-up of the object. These pressure waves can travel hundreds or thousands of kilometers and were picked up by the Elginfield Infrasound Array (ELFO) in Ontario, Canada, as well as by citizen scientists operating their own Raspberry Shake/Boom pressure sensors, which are build-your-own micro-barometers produced by the Raspberry Pi Foundation.

Diungkapkan bahwa "six citizen-operated sensors jointly constrained the arrival direction," said vierinen. We are grateful to the citizen scientists whose measurements expanded the coverage and helped locate the event. "Five other single-station detections and ELFO supplied the signal periods used to estimate the energy release. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, from the data gathered, the team were able to deduce certain properties about the object that fell to earth over massachusetts. The meteoroid that entered the atmosphere was about a meter (approximately three feet) across, and based on how deep it penetrated into the atmosphere before fragmenting it must have been a pretty solid body, possibly rich in iron.

"We cannot determine its exact history, but we found no association with any known meteor shower," said Vierinen.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, extrapolating its trajectory back into space, the team found that the meteoroid had a comet-like elongated orbit around the sun that took it almost as far out as jupiter. Comets on such orbits are referred to as Jupiter-family comets, since their orbits are governed by perturbations from Jupiter's powerful gravitational influence.

However, the meteoroid was definitely not a comet, and previous research has found that Jupiter can draw out small asteroids from the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter and place them on such orbits.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "meteoroids can be perturbed by other bodies including jupiter," team-member marc fries told space. "The meteoroid's aphelion – the point where it is farthest from the sun – is close to Jupiter's orbit, which suggests a close pass by the gas giant may have indeed flung it into its recent Earth-crossing path. com. This same process has slowly depopulated the asteroid belt throughout the solar system's history. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meteoroids on meter-sized scales are in something of a black spot – they are not very easy to detect in space from earth unlike larger asteroids, and they are not common enough to be falling to earth all the time unlike the pebble-sized meteoroids and smaller that burn up as shooting stars. As such, we know relatively little about this population of bodies and every bolide that we see helps us to learn more.

Berdasarkan laporan, "every new piece of data we glean about earth impactors adds to the statistics," said fries. "It is especially helpful to have measurements of total power, location, originating orbit and similar data points for the more massive meteorites, because those are the meteoroids and asteroids we encounter less frequently. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, that the meteoroid fell over such a highly populated area was a stroke of luck. Although the atmosphere is carefully monitored on a global basis by both ground stations and satellites high above us, meaning that even if a meteor streaks above an uninhabited area there is usually enough data to narrow down its trajectory somewhat, radar observations are able to do so more accurately.

"We would love to have global coverage with meteor radar networks and we and others are making progress with SIMONe and similar systems, but the current coverage is still sparse," said Volz.

Nevertheless, the Cape Cod bolide resoundingly shows that by combining radar echoes from head and trail plasma with weather radar observations and ultrasound pulses from the break-up of falling rocks, scientists can ascertain the orbits of impacting meteoroids very accurately.

While the Cape Cod meteoroid was much smaller than the asteroid that exploded over Chelyabinsk in 2013, which was about 18 meters across and exploded with an energy equivalent to between 400 and 500 kilotons of TNT, being able to trace meteoroids back to their orbits may in future reveal new populations of potentially hazardous impactors.

The research into the Cape Cod bolide is available as a preprint on the arXiv server.

#457. Iconic first image of black hole holds up to scrutiny

📅 13 Nov 2026

Iconic first image of black hole holds up to scrutiny

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03642-7

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, physicists used an algorithm to combine telescope measurements of a black hole in a different way from the original analysis. Wong and F. I. Thyagarajan, O. Lai, N. Credit: S. Diakogiannis/CSIRO.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the event horizon telescope (eht) collaboration wowed the world in 2019 with the first picture ever taken of a black hole’s shadow. Some researchers were unconvinced, arguing that the circular shape seen in that shot was an artefact of the team’s image-reconstruction techniques. Now, an independent group has reanalysed the EHT data, and its results, published on 11 November in Nature — including new images of the black hole — largely corroborate the original findings1.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to image black holes, the international eht collaboration stitches together data it collects simultaneously from an array of ground-based radio telescopes that stretches across several continents. The reconstruction is extremely challenging, but in principle, the result is an image with the same level of detail, or resolution, that would be achieved with a single radio dish as wide as Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, although blurry, the eht shot of a supermassive black hole at the centre of the m87 galaxy was consistent with astrophysical models based on albert einstein’s general theory of relativity, which first predicted the existence of black holes. The image had a bright ring of roughly the correct radius, given what was known about the size of the black hole, with a darker disk at the centre.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, starting in 2022, junichiro makino, an astrophysicist at kobe university in japan, and his collaborators began questioning those conclusions2. By applying one of the data-analysis techniques the EHT collaboration had used, but with slightly different assumptions, Makino’s team obtained a different result. Their image shows a glob of radio emissions rather than a ring.

Diungkapkan bahwa cape canaveral, fla. — NASA is pushing ahead with its plan to build a moon base for astronauts by 2032, with the agency unveiling up to $10 billion in contracts to launch and deliver cargo to the moon and other efforts on Saturday (Nov. 7).

Berdasarkan laporan, the nasa announcement, revealed here during the space agency's "max power" air show event at kennedy space center, included plans for a new $10 billion commercial lunar payload services (clps) framework, dubbed clps 2, about$1. 3 billion in funding for the agency's Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) program, and the nuclear-powered "PROMISE" rover on the moon.

The announcements mark another step in NASA's effort to establish infrastructure on the moon before Artemis astronauts return to its surface, including a rover and other cargo and research elements.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "under the current clps contract, it's all all or nothing, which might be fine if you're only doing one or two of those [missions] per year," nasa administrator jared isaacman told space. "But when you're trying to scale up to what we're talking about today, you want to have the flexibility to move pieces around. com during a press conference on Saturday. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nasa selected eight companies to compete for the new clps 2 missions under the framework: blue origin, firefly aerospace, intuitive machines, ispace-u. S. , Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, SpaceX and Voyager Technologies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the contracts for the 10-year clps 2 architecture carry a combined maximum value of $10 billion, rather than $10 billion in immediately awarded missions. 6 billion to $4. NASA also increased the ceiling of its existing CLPS contract from $2. 2 billion to support the agency's "Phase One" Moon Base objectives.

Diungkapkan bahwa nasa is also following through on a promise isaacman made in june, when he proposed repurposing an engineering model of the perseverance and curiosity mars rovers (essentially an earth-based twin) as a mission-ready rover to send to the moon. That rover, called PROMISE (short for "Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration"), is a nuclear-powered robot intended to explore the lunar south pole beginning in late 2028.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the autonomous rover will carry a drill and scientific instruments to search for volatiles and water ice on the lunar surface. NASA awarded Blue Origin a $94 million base contract, with an additional $140 million option period based on performance, to deliver PROMISE to the lunar surface aboard its Blue Moon Mark 1 lander.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in addition to that contract for blue origin, nasa awarded six launch and orbital transportation task orders worth a total of approximately $1. 3 billion to Arrow Science and Technology, Blue Origin and Impulse Space under its Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) program.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the missions will demonstrate commercial launch and orbital transportation capabilities, including cargo transfers between earth and lunar orbits, navigation tests with the capstone 2 spacecraft and lunar scouting with "moonfall" drones. Blue Origin, SpaceX and Relativity Space will provide launch support with their New Glenn, Falcon 9 and Terran R rockets, respectively.

Under a separate lunar logistics contract, NASA selected SpaceX to launch communications satellites aboard its Starship megarocket in 2028, helping to establish a future lunar communications network with spacecraft similar to the company's Starlink spacecraft.

NASA also awarded contracts to Honeybee Robotics, Redwire and Yank Technologies to develop components for a lunar power and communications tower, known as miniCAST.

Diungkapkan bahwa the announcements support nasa's phase one moon base strategy, which is scheduled to extend through 2029 and focuses on robotic exploration, infrastructure demonstrations and commercial deliveries. Phase Two, which runs from 2029 to 2032, will continue to build out infrastructure for the base, which will get up and running during Phase 3.

Berdasarkan laporan, while the kindle may have the kobo beat on processing and battery life, i still think the libra colour is a worthy upgrade, as it offers the best design of an e-reader with the perk of color. Diungkapkan bahwa don't get us wrong, though; we still love the kindle paperwhite. If you want to save $50, the next best e-reader you can buy is the basic Kindle Paperwhite. It's still a quick, well-rounded e-reader but doesn't come in fun colors and has lockscreen ads.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you want a cheap, waterproof e-reader: the cheapest waterproof e-reader is the kobo clara. The black and white version is $159. 99, while the color model is $179. 99. Diungkapkan bahwa having tried my hand at more than a dozen e-readers in all shapes, sizes, and brands, i wasn't expecting to be so deeply impressed by the kobo clara colour, but it is a wonderful e-reader. Sebagaimana diketahui, its processing system is otherwise really smart and fixes one of my biggest e-reader pet peeves. When you adjust the font size on a Kindle, the device doesn't recalculate how many pages are in the book, making it inaccurate, so you don't know exactly how many pages you have left in a chapter. Though, one thing to note: Kobo counts the number of digital pages, whereas Kindle page numbers typically match up with physical book copies.

Diungkapkan bahwa for a lower price than the kindle paperwhite, the kobo clara offers color displays, something you can't get in the kindle lineup unless you're willing to spend $290. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, no, not all e-readers are waterproof. All of the e-readers in this guide are waterproof, with an IPX8 rating. That means the device can be fully submerged in two meters of water without harm to the device.

But if you're looking at e-readers like the basic Kindle or e-readers from Boox, be cautious before using them near water, as none of these e-readers have waterproof ratings.

Diungkapkan bahwa yes, with their ipx8 rating, these e-readers can be fully submerged in water. However, there's a limit to the water exposure. The devices can only be submerged up to two meters for up to 60 minutes.

So if your e-reader falls into the bath, pick it up as soon as possible, dry it off, and shake off as much water as possible.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all of these e-readers are tested using the same criteria as every e-reader we test. In addition to analyzing the devices' performance and value, we prioritized waterproof rating and special features.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this guide, we only included e-readers with waterproof ratings, knowing that if you're reading in the bath, it will definitely be exposed to water. The devices had to have an IPX8 rating, which makes them safe to be submerged in water.

Diungkapkan bahwa we prioritized e-readers with page-turn buttons, a rare feature on e-readers. This allows you to turn the page without touching the screen with wet fingers. Since so few devices have page-turn buttons, we also chose e-readers that could be used with page-turn covers or remotes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tech is expensive these days, so we also considered value. If a device was over $200, it had to have special features that made us prioritize it over a more affordable device. #474. A free way to make your earbuds sound better? Give them a deep clean.

📅 12 Nov 2026

A free way to make your earbuds sound better? Give them a deep clean.

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/tech/how-to-deep-clean-earbuds

I say this without judgment: you're likely overdue for an earbud clean.

Sebagaimana diketahui, earwax, sweat from workouts, dirt, and dust — daily use exposes earbuds to a myriad of ways to get nice and dirty. And when was the last time you spot-cleaned them? Exactly.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's where the deep clean comes in. In addition to the sanitation of it all, cleaning your earbuds periodically can help prevent damage that might impact their use, whether it be causing issues with the charging case, wear detection features, or even how the buds themselves sound. In other words, the less dirt getting into the internals of your buds, the better. Even the best earbuds can start to suffer without proper maintenance. For optimal performance, Bose recommends cleaning your earbuds every two months.

Berdasarkan laporan, if the idea of cleaning your earbuds makes you worried you'll cause more harm than good, don't fret. It's easier than you think, and you likely have most, if not all, of the supplies already.

Micellar water (or distilled water, though regular water can also be used in a pinch).

Step 1: Remove the ear tips.

How to do this can vary slightly from model to model, but generally a light pinch and pull will get the job done.

Step 2: Wipe down the earbuds and exterior of the case with a dry microfiber cloth.

Step 3: Check specific earbuds guide for any areas you may need to avoid during cleaning.

For example, Apple's AirPods Pro instructions make clear where to avoid cleaning.

Sebagaimana diketahui, step 4: apply a very small amount of micellar water to a microfiber cloth, cotton swab, or soft bristled toothbrush. Lightly clean earbuds' mesh for 15 to 30 seconds.

You can repeat this step as many times as needed, but be sure to dry the mesh immediately after with a dry microfiber cloth.

Step 5: Use a microfiber cloth to wipe the interior of the case.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you can use a small amount of micellar water here, but make sure your cloth is damp, not wet. If possible, avoid getting charging pins wet.

Step 6: Wipe ear tips down with microfiber cloth.

Diungkapkan bahwa in most cases, it's completely fine to also use a damp cloth here. However, if you're unsure, check specific instructions for brands. Sony recommends not getting the XM6 ear tips wet, while Bose and Apple say you can submerge the ear tips in water.

Step 7: Set aside ear tips to dry if necessary.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tapping the ear tips on a towel to remove any excess moisture can work well here. You'll want to leave them sitting out in a secure, clean space while the rest of your earbuds dry.

Step 8: Dry case and earbuds for at least two hours.

This may seem like overkill (and honestly, in some cases, this probably is excessive), but letting the case dry open and the earbuds sit out on a clean surface guarantees that not a drop of moisture will threaten the performance of your earbuds.

Step 9: Replace the ear tips, and enjoy your newly cleaned buds!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, do: double-check the specific manufacturer instructions for your earbuds. That might mean actually cracking open the user guide. Oftentimes, guides or specific cleaning instructions will tell you the specific areas to avoid on your earbuds. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Find cleaning instructions for Apple AirPods Pro models, Apple AirPods 4 and 5, Bose earbuds, Sony WF-1000XM6 earbuds, Beats Powerbeats Pro 2, Bowers & Wilkins Pi8 earbuds, and Soundcore earbuds.

Berdasarkan laporan, don't: put earbuds back into their charging case until both the earbuds and the case are completely dry. You didn't get your earbuds extra clean just to introduce moisture problems.

Berdasarkan laporan, do: be aware of small openings and ports. Minimizing moisture is key, so even when using a lightly damp cloth, it's important to avoid getting liquid into tiny openings, as it could affect the efficacy of the hardware. After using any damp materials for cleaning, dry your earbuds with another microfiber cloth immediately. Do NOT use any heat, such as hair dryers, as they're liable to cause damage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, don't: turn to harsh alcohols for disinfecting. While some brands — Beats and Soundcore included — mention using rubbing alcohol as a cleaning tool, several other brands warn against it. The harshness of the alcohol can degrade earbuds and ultimately affect performance, so relying on water, micellar water, or a dry cloth is ultimately the safest route.

Sebagaimana diketahui, do: be careful with cotton swabs and charging cases. Though cotton swabs are a great shape for getting into nooks and crannies, their fibers can easily get caught and lodged into those same nooks and crannies. The best solution is to use a microfiber cloth instead — if you're having trouble maneuvering it, you can always wrap the cloth around the cotton swab to give yourself more dexterity.

That knowledge comes in handy when she's covering shopping holidays like Prime Day and Black Friday, which she's now done for three years at Mashable.
