Sebagaimana diketahui, cameras aside, we also gave high marks to this phone for its capable everyday performance, multi-day battery life, brighter display, and attractive color options. Its HiLight feature is kind of a flop, but the rest of it makes up for that.

Berdasarkan laporan, multitaskers on the move: the new iphone duo is thinner and lighter than apple's ipads, and it has a huge, gorgeous inner display with a glare-reducing "nano-texture" finish. Its design makes it great for on-the-go multitasking and entertainment (think reading, watching movies, or playing games); it can replace an e-reader or tablet in a pinch.

Sebagaimana diketahui, stylus users: the duo is the only foldable we've tested that supports stylus input on its inner and outer displays. It works with the Apple Pencil (USB-C), which is sold separately for $79.

Diungkapkan bahwa early adopters: foldable phones aren't in their infancy anymore, but they're still pretty niche devices. And as Apple's very first foldable, the Duo has some quirks — namely, many apps aren't optimized for it yet. Its ideal buyer is a tech enthusiast who wants to check out the latest and greatest in smartphone design and is willing to put up with some bugs for a bit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, people with cash to burn: the duo starts at an eye-watering $1,999, making it apple's most expensive phone ever — not to mention, the priciest phone on this list. (It maxes out at $3,199 with 2TB of storage. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, patient people: the duo was backordered for months at the time of writing. If you order it through the Apple Store right now, you probably won't get it until the opening weeks of 2027.

Read Mashable's full review of the Apple iPhone Duo.

Berdasarkan laporan, the iphone duo is the first and only foldable that apple's made so far, but it's quite impressive for a first-generation device. ) It certainly helps that the Duo's matte inner screen is "the nicest phone display I’ve ever seen," said Senior Editor Stan Schroeder, who described it as "crisp, sharp, [and] beautiful to look at; it’s downright addictive. It's basically an iPhone that doubles as an iPad when unfolded — you can look at apps side by side, enjoy e-books and games in greater immersion, or use it as a MacBook's secondary display. (We just wouldn't recommend turning it into an alarm clock as Apple suggests. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the duo has a passport-style design like the samsung galaxy z fold 8, our favorite android foldable, just with rounder corners for a more polished look. It runs on the same powerful A20 chip as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, so it's zippy enough for all the multitasking your heart desires, and optimized apps work incredibly well. While the Duo doesn't last as long as those regular iPhones, its battery life is fine for a foldable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you'll have to temper your expectations with the duo's cameras — it lacks a telephoto lens, and the hidden facetime camera on its inner screen is straight-up "bad," schroeder said. That said, this is the case with most foldables.

Diungkapkan bahwa on a final note, some inaugural duo owners reported that their device's inner screen cracked shortly after they started using it (a problem that's since become known as "crackgate"). The good news is that the issue doesn't seem to be as serious as social media might have you believe. In a statement, Apple told us that it's isolated to "a small number" of Duos, and that impacted buyers should contact AppleCare for a replacement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if it helps, schroeder has been using the duo for nearly a month and hasn't noticed any hinge or display defects with his review unit. What's more, another Duo has withstood more than 200,000 folds (and counting) inside the "Fold-a-Phone" machine built by our sister site, CNET; they're folding it 900 times an hour until it breaks. You can catch the livestream daily on CNET's YouTube channel.

Commuters and frequent travelers: Like Apple's iPhone Duo, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a compact and versatile passport-style design that's tailor-made for multitasking on the go.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reluctant guinea pigs: unlike apple, samsung has been making foldable phones for many years now. Our reviewer noticed some "very minor bugs" with certain apps on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, but "most of the time, the phone just works," he said. (We think the iPhone Duo's "crackgate" issue is largely overblown, but it's still something to be aware of. And its construction is pretty much rock solid at this point. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, people who like a lightweight foldable: this is the lightest folding phone we've tested. It's 21 percent lighter than the iPhone Duo, 16 percent lighter than the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, and six percent lighter than Samsung's taller, book-style Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

Berdasarkan laporan, folks who want an "affordable" foldable: the galaxy z fold 8 is $100 cheaper than apple's iphone duo. If we're really splitting hairs, it's technically the thriftier choice.

Read Mashable's full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Diungkapkan bahwa google's pixel 11 pro fold is also a great android foldable, but ultimately, we prefer the wider, passport-style design of samsung's galaxy z fold 8 — it's sleeker and better for entertainment. Plus, its crease isn't as visible. (We also prefer it over the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra for similar reasons. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the galaxy z fold 8's spacious inner amoled screen is "far and away" its biggest asset, said mashable's timothy beck werth. It's smooth and so bright. "Likewise, while I've never been a huge fan of mobile gaming, the mobile version of Mario Kart looks and plays awesome here. "I generally avoid streaming TV shows and movies on my phone, but not with the Z Fold 8," he wrote. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the display has a glare-free finish that makes it easy to view in direct sunlight, as well as samsung's new "flex titanium" tech that keeps its crease subtle and hinge strong. Other highlights of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 include peppy multitasking performance and all-day battery life. While its cameras aren't spectacular — most foldables' shooters aren't — they're sufficient for most non-pro users.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the most advanced iphone ever built is here, and it doesn't disappoint. So, who should buy the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead of the smaller iPhone 18 Pro?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, battery life maximizers: the iphone 18 pro max is rated for up to 45 hours of video playback. It's the longest-lasting phone we've ever tested.

Mobile gamers who prefer regular (non-foldable) phones: This handset features a blazing-fast processor and a huge vapor chamber thermal system, plus a smooth, crisp, and massive display.

Berdasarkan laporan, people with big hands: at 8. 78 ounces, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the heaviest regular phone we recommend. It's the same size as the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, but weighs 16 percent more.

Read Mashable's full review of the Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

Sebagaimana diketahui, apple reorganized the components inside the iphone 18 pro max to squeeze in a giant new battery that can run for nearly two days between charges. It's so big that the company had to add a special setting that keeps it within shipping limits on battery sizes. It lasts up to nine hours longer than the smaller iPhone 18 Pro, no "Max. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the iphone 18 pro max's a20 pro chip ran laps around the competition in our benchmarking, and the new thermal management system that fills its chassis keeps it cool while you're running demanding apps. Mashable's Stan Schroeder "tested this out by playing a few games of PUBG: Battlegrounds on the highest settings for a full hour," and "The phone barely got warm," he wrote. Its battery life only fell by nine percent during that stress test, FWIW.

Diungkapkan bahwa the regular iphone 18 pro has the same hardware, but we think mobile gamers and movie-watchers will appreciate the bigger, more immersive screen on the "max" version. The two phones are basically identical otherwise, including their shooter setup. Opt for this model if you want the best iPhone for battery life and cameras.

Diungkapkan bahwa "if there's ever been a phone to make you ditch apple, this is it," said mashable tech editor timothy beck werth. The question is, who should make the splurge?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, advanced users: the samsung galaxy s26 ultra is a premium device with a zippy custom processor, a large, high-end display with stylus support, and elite cameras. It's "too much phone" for the average person, to quote our review; only professional creatives and developers will be able to use it to its full potential.

AI enthusiasts: This handheld comes crammed with powerful AI tools, including pre-loaded Gemini, Perplexity, and Bixby AI assistants.

Berdasarkan laporan, privacy sticklers: the galaxy s26 ultra has a unique built-in privacy display that blacks out your screen to those around you. It's not perfect, but it's still pretty sick — and you can't get it on any other phone, Android or otherwise.

Read Mashable's full review of the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Berdasarkan laporan, in october, samsung raised the prices of the galaxy s26 phones it released back in march — and they were already more expensive than last year's s25 models. A new S26 Ultra will now cost you $1,400, while the 1TB version is a whopping $2,000. But if you want the finest, most future-proofed Android smartphone available, this is it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the galaxy s26 ultra is faster than some mid-range laptops we've tried, so it can run just about any app, mobile game, or fancy ai feature you need it to. Its display would be elite even if its cutting-edge privacy screen feature weren't a thing — it's so crisp and bright. Plus, its upgraded vapor chamber makes sure it never breaks a sweat. Its battery lasts all day, and its cameras are almost unrivaled: Photos taken on the Galaxy S26 are vibrant and detailed, even at night or zoomed in quite a bit.

Diungkapkan bahwa teens with deep-pocketed parents: the trendy little galaxy z flip 8 makes a great starter phone for a younger person (though it doesn't have a "starter" price). It's cute, durable, and easy to hold in one hand.

Sebagaimana diketahui, people who don't obsess over photo quality: like foldables, flip phones aren't ideal for serious photographers. The Galaxy Z Flip 8's cameras underwhelm compared to those on regular phones that cost the same or slightly less.

Nostalgic Millennials: If you haven't used a flip phone since the early 2000s, this is a great entry point into the modern market.

Read Mashable's full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8.

Diungkapkan bahwa in addition to your usual next-gen upgrades — a faster processor, a slightly thinner, lighter design — the galaxy z flip 8 also features improved durability compared to last year's galaxy z flip 7. Mashable tech editor Timothy Beck Werth was particularly enamored by its small size and "charming good looks," calling it "a smartphone with good vibes. Like the Galaxy Z Fold 8, above, its new Flex Titanium display tech equates to a stronger hinge and a more subtle crease on its inner screen. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, its color options are few but cute; the pink one won over our newsroom full of apple users. While its cameras aren't much to write home about as a whole, it takes great selfies (as long as you don't use the selfie camera, ironically), and its AI image editing tools work really well. Regarding battery life, you should get over a day of use out of the Z Flip 8 before needing to charge it.

People who want a flip phone with great cameras: Flip phones aren't known for taking amazing pictures — Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip 8, above, is pretty representative of the market — but this model is an exception.

Folks who want a long-lasting flip phone: The latest Razr Ultra can last up to a day and a half away from an outlet, depending on your usage.

Fashionistas: This flip phone comes in two chic, Pantone-approved colorways featuring unique back covers.

Read Mashable's full review of the Motorola Razr Ultra.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you can spend a little more on your flip phone, we really like the 2026 motorola razr ultra, which mashable tech editor timothy beck werth deemed "a conversation-starting beauty. " Both of its pretty AMOLED displays (inner and outer) are bigger, smoother, and brighter than the ones on last year's model.

Sebagaimana diketahui, its external design is equally eye-catching: the pantone orient blue model's cover is finished in alcantara, a suede-like microfiber, while the pantone cocoa one has a wood veneer on the back. It takes "surprisingly good photos for a foldable," Werth said — better than the Galaxy Z Flip 8 for sure — capturing natural-looking colors and handling bright scenes well. Its 36-hour battery life is also an improvement over its Samsung counterpart, which taps out at 31 hours (same with the mid-tier Razr+, which also underwhelmed in the photography department).

Topics Android Apple Google iOS iPhone Samsung.

In early November 2026, I made some adjustments to this guide after our latest round of testing:.

The Apple iPhone Duo is our new favorite foldable iPhone.

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is now our top Android foldable.

Last month, I added the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max as picks for photography and battery life, respectively.

Berdasarkan laporan, released in fall 2025, the iphone air is apple's thinnest phone ever. Its ultra-sleek design is appealing, but it has worse battery life and inferior cameras compared to the standard iPhone 17 (which runs on the same processor. We think it's a very pretty and well-made phone, but not one of the best overall. and costs $200 less). For more info, check out our iPhone Air review and our dedicated guide to the best iPhones.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mashable has been covering phones for over a decade and a half, since the launch of the iphone 4s, samsung galaxy s ii, and motorola droid razr in 2011. As of 2026, our team uses the following metrics to test and evaluate the best smartphones:.

Berdasarkan laporan, we spend several days to weeks with every phone we review. We stress test them by playing games on them, opening multiple apps at once, and trying any unique software features they support. We quantify their performance using Primate Labs' Geekbench CPU benchmark.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, throughout our testing periods, we measure how much a phone's battery drains with heavy usage. We also see how fast it charges. In more recent phone reviews, we've started conducted an additional video rundown test using "Tears of Steel," an open-source Blender movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we assess the overall design, construction, and ergonomics of each phone as we use it. Is it comfortable to hold? Can it fit in a pocket? How sharp is its display? Is it waterproof? What colors does it come in?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we test each of the phone's cameras in a variety of lighting conditions and settings. We take photos indoors and outdoors, in low and bright light; we get macro, zoom, and night shots, and we snap a bunch of selfies. We include the photos in our reviews for reference.

Mashable tech editor Timothy Beck Werth and tech reporter Alex Perry also contributed to this guide.

#478. Voyager 1 is about to hit one light-day away. NASAs planning to party.

📅 12 Nov 2026

Voyager 1 is about to hit one light-day away. NASAs planning to party.

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/science/nasa-voyager-1-light-day-activities

If you step outside tonight and flick a flashlight toward deep space, that split-second pulse will race through the void at 186,000 miles per second.

Diungkapkan bahwa the light will continue its journey while you sleep, while you eat, while you go to work. Only when you reach the same time tomorrow could its photons potentially wash over a spacecraft more than 16 billion miles away.

Diungkapkan bahwa that robotic probe is nasa's voyager 1, the farthest human-made object in the universe. It will cross the one light-day-away milestone at 5:16 a. ET on Wednesday, Nov. 18. Radio signals move at the speed of light, so any message from Earth would need a full day to reach the spacecraft. m. One light-day is the distance light travels over 24 hours. Considering Voyager 1 never stops moving, that communication lag will only increase.

Berdasarkan laporan, to mark the occasion, the u. space agency has a couple of things planned, one of which involves pointing that flashlight toward the sky. S. The day after the milestone, you can watch the mission team talk about where the spacecraft has been and how it keeps going.

Sebagaimana diketahui, voyager 1 left earth in 1977 to explore the giant outer planets. The probe finished its tour decades ago but kept going at nearly 38,000 mph. NASA timed the launch to catch a lineup of those planets that comes around only once every 176 years. In 2012, it left the heliosphere, the protective bubble the sun blows around our solar system, and entered interstellar space.

Berdasarkan laporan, its twin, voyager 2, took a different path past uranus and neptune and left the solar system in 2018. But Voyager 2 won't reach a light-day until November 2035, most likely after it has depleted its fuel.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that's the bittersweet reality of voyager 1's historic achievement: both probes are dying, nearly tapped out of their nuclear power sources that turn heat from decaying plutonium into electricity. Since 2024, the team has shut off two science instruments on each spacecraft to stretch what's left. Sooner or later, the power will run out, and no one will be able to talk with the twins at all, regardless of time delays.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for now, though, the mission team is only thinking happy thoughts. NASA is asking people around the world to point a light at the sky to spell out VGR, Voyager's call sign, in Morse code. 17. The first way to get involved comes after sunset on Tuesday, Nov. Morse code is an old telegraph language that turns each letter into a pattern of short and long signals.

Diungkapkan bahwa the easiest way to do this is with a phone or tablet. NASA built an online flasher that blinks the code for you. (You can bookmark this story to keep the flasher link handy. After sunset, open the flasher in your device's web browser, point the device's screen at the sky, and let it send the signal. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, if you'd rather tap it out yourself, grab a flashlight, and switch it on and off or use your hand to block and unblock the beam. Short flashes, called dots, should last less than a second. Long flashes, called dashes, should last about one second.

You can repeat the pattern as many times as you like.

Sebagaimana diketahui, now, even if you were to point your flashlight in precisely the direction of voyager 1, the beam would fan out into a cone billions of miles wide, scattering its photons across the void. Because the light is diluted in space, virtually every photon would sail past the tiny 12-foot spacecraft without ever hitting it.

Berdasarkan laporan, but it's a symbolic gesture for wishing the old mission godspeed. You can tag @NASA on your photos and videos if you post them to X, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, or other social media.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the second way to join in the celebration comes at noon et / 9 a. Mission leaders and top NASA science officials will meet at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California to talk about the twins. PT on Thursday, Nov. They'll explain how the spacecraft are holding up, what they're still learning beyond the sun's bubble, and how engineers keep such old hardware running from far away. 19. m. The public can watch on NASA's streaming service, NASA+, or Youtube.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the team has plenty to talk about. This year, engineers tried a fix they nicknamed the "Big Bang. " They turned off three power-hungry devices on each probe that help keep it warm, and at the same time they switched on three lower-power replacements. The swap should keep them running for at least another year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but at this stage, the team has come to expect the unexpected. Last month, Voyager 1 had a mysterious issue with its thrusters that briefly caused a communication blackout. Engineers are still trying to figure out what caused the problem.

Berdasarkan laporan, if the distant spacecraft could send you a morse code message back, perhaps it would say the one recorded on its golden record: "ad astera per aspera. " In Latin, that means "to the stars through struggles. ".

#479. Rings of Power star Tyroe Muhafidin talks Theos dark side, Witch-king theories, and that heartbreaking death

📅 12 Nov 2026

Rings of Power star Tyroe Muhafidin talks Theos dark side, Witch-king theories, and that heartbreaking death

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/tyroe-muhafidin-interview-the-lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power-theo

Tyroe Muhafidin is ready to embrace his villainous side.

Diungkapkan bahwa the 20-year-old actor plays theo in the lord of the rings: the rings of power, his first professional role. A young Southlander, Theo has spent the first two seasons of the series caught up in a battle between good and evil that he can barely understand. But in Season 3, Theo hopes to take matters into his own hands, a choice that brings him face to face with Sauron (Charlie Vickers).

Sebagaimana diketahui, over the course of season 3's first four episodes, theo officially joins sauron's army as a nazgnagôl, or ring-servant. Later, in one of the show's heaviest scenes, he kills his former mentor, the elf Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova), at Sauron's command. Between accepting a ring of power and murdering Arondir, Theo's arc has bent entirely toward darkness, especially since the Nazgnagôl will soon become entirely corrupted, turning them into the Nazgûl of The Lord of the Rings.

In a conversation with Mashable, Muhafidin unpacked Theo's turn to the dark side, his final scene with Córdova, and whether Theo may become the Witch-king of Angmar, as the show so heavily implies.

Berdasarkan laporan, this season, theo gets up close and personal with sauron. In the first episode, he and the men of Pelargir head to Mordor for a ring of power. Tell me about how the five years under Númenórean rule have led to this decision from Theo.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the last five years, i think any of those dwindles of hope that theo had have now all dissipated. Then it just became pain upon pain upon pain, and loss upon loss for him. Basically, in the first two seasons, Theo was was very hopeful for a better life, and he really did believe that something good was going to come for his people. Five years, especially for a human, is enough time to set in stone for him the idea that those good days weren't ever coming, and if he was ever going to have any life that's different to the one that he's having now, it would be in Barad-dûr.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that fight between the southlanders for the ring is the most involved combat theo's been in so far. Walk me through training for that scene and embodying that fight-or-die feeling.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i feel like i've never really done anything where i was the attacker. A lot of the stunty stuff that Theo had done prior was always him running away from something. So I feel like this is the first time, and it's showing that he's grown now, and he can take on battles for himself, full-on, headfirst.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that fight was a bit hectic. It was really fun, but it was really grueling to shoot. The conditions in Barad-dûr aren't the most fun. There's fire everywhere and blood everywhere, and it's dark. He's on top of me, and you think that he would be heavy, but he did such a great job at keeping his weight just enough off me that it looked like I was holding all this weight. It took us a few weeks to choreograph and nail down. Adam [Basil], who's the loveliest guy ever — he's this 6-foot-8 guy, and his name on the call sheet was "Big Farmer" — was absolutely a dream to work with. But I guess that's the exact vibe that Sauron's lair would have!.

Speaking of Sauron, I'd love to hear more about working with Charlie Vickers this season and establishing that intriguing dynamic between Theo and Sauron.

Berdasarkan laporan, working with charlie was a dream. He'd always had a particular kind of arm around me since the first season. We were all out in New Zealand by ourselves, and he'd invite me around to play FIFA with him a bunch. It was kind of like an uncle relationship, Uncle Charlie. So we already had this dynamic, and now actually working with him, we could actually build upon that kind of big bro energy.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's been certain moments that they've shared prior, like the moment where theo held the sword up and said, "strength to the southlands. So, I think Sauron had an eye out for Theo. " Halbrand, at the time, recognized that. I think the moment that he stepped into Barad-dûr, her knew there was something about this kid.

Diungkapkan bahwa i love the whole scene where sauron uses dark magic to invite theo to commune with his late father. What's running through Theo's mind in that moment as he learns the truth about his father and his ties to Mordor?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at this point, his mind is racing. It's so filled with everything, it would be hard for him to think rationally at all. He just did a complete fight to the death with six other guys, and now he's having to talk to the Dark Lord and meeting his dad all of a sudden, whom he hasn't known for the last 20 years. It's literally the most insane sequence of events, so at this point he's genuinely the most vulnerable, mentally. His brain is at a point now where it will soak up anything that Sauron says to him, and it has left him easy to manipulate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finding out who his dad was is a question that he's asked his entire life, and when he learns, it's disbelief and shock. It's one of those things where you've been wondering for so long, so when you find out, you can't believe that it's true anyway. It's this weird, in-between world of knowing now, but still feeling like he doesn't know. I think Sauron can use that uncertainty in his brain, and with the presence of a ring, it was very easy to say what needed to be said.

Berdasarkan laporan, i have to talk about the witch-king in the room, because sauron tells theo he has it in him to be a sorcerer and a king. Obviously, a very famous sorcerer king with a ring of power in The Lord of the Rings is the Witch-king of Angmar. Are you able to confirm that Theo is going down that path?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, [laughs] you could theorize along those lines, maybe, but i guess you'd have to ask [co-creators] j. D. [Payne] and Patrick [McKay] about that one.

Diungkapkan bahwa theo puts on the ring and becomes one of the ring-servants. When did you learn that this darkness was really going to become a part of his arc?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there was always a presence of it from the first season. With the sword hilt, there was already a connection to the dark side, and there was the scene with Waldreg [Geoff Morrell] at the watchtower trying to get him to join him. There've been temptations throughout, and they were planted carefully, so that when it came to the point that he got offered the ultimate question, he'd already been broken down gradually, and let the darkness in so much that it was easy to say yes.

Diungkapkan bahwa i'd only found out just just before season 3 i actually get a ring. In the five years prior to that, I'd been poking at J. D. and Patrick saying, "Will I get a ring? Will I get a ring?".

Berdasarkan laporan, they always flipped it back on me, asking, "should theo get a ring?" and i was like, "i don't know. That's too much pressure!".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i did a little bit of sweet talking all the way through, saying it'd be cool to play a villain. Villain arcs are really cool, and there's some cool depth to them. Theo does have a real great sense of depth and reasoning behind his darkness.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, speaking of the rings, they all look different. Did you get a choice in which one you got to put on?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think i got the coolest. I remember seeing them all and being like, "I hope that one's mine. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, then when i got my costume for the first time, i got to see which ring was mine, and it was exactly the one i wanted. It was my favorite one out of all of them.

Berdasarkan laporan, we have to talk about the costume, because the image of the nazgnagôl armor and mask recalls the nazgûl in lord of the rings, and that has a lot of weight for the series. What was it like, stepping into that for the first time?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i'd done a lot of movement workshops and things like that to try and gauge a sense of the power that the nazgnagôl would have. I'd done it for a few weeks before any kind of costume fitting, but it wasn't until the day that I had my first costume fitting — there was no armor or crown or anything, it was literally just a bunch of black robes — that I immediately could feel the darkness attached to it. You could get a sense of power, even just in the robes. Then at each costume fitting, they introduced more and more to the costume, and then by the last costume fitting, I'd fully felt the power.

Berdasarkan laporan, i also requested if i could do some movement workshops in the costume, because it was actually really complicated to move in. The crown is essentially an extension of your head, so any movement of your head will be really exaggerated at the end of the crown. We had to figure out how to walk in a way so our heads weren't bobbing a bunch. There was a sense of trying to move like you're floating, because if we didn't do that, the crown would have just made us look goofy.

What's the secret to moving like the Nazgnagôl?.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's a sense of real strength and power, but also a sense of otherworldliness. The Nazgnagôl live in both the mortal life and the immortal life, so we wanted them to move as if they were in between worlds, and they're coming from one world to another. I think once the costume's on, though, it does 80 percent of the work for you. It was very much about moving with a slight bend at the knees, so every time you're moving, it's more of a glide than a walk. You just automatically feel it.

Berdasarkan laporan, it's very imposing. We've got to talk about the final scene of episode 4, with Arondir's death. Tell me about filming that final scene with Ismael and finding that last connection?.

Berdasarkan laporan, we shot that scene over two weeks, so we'd shot that specific sequence and the stabbing multiple times without getting any close up. It was so heavily emotional, like for both of us, it was a real bonding and brotherhood moment. It was daunting, but it was very fun. We were having fun on set, and then the day came where we were doing our close-ups, and the air just felt cold, and everyone could feel the sad energy. Feeling so deeply at that time in that moment, it really opened up a big space for us to connect. It was fun though. It was a big celebration of Ismael and all the hard work that he's put into this job and how awesome Arondir is. We had a really great time, and it was a really great group of us on set. We got a lot closer, because we could open up on our feelings. We'd done it wide a bunch of times, and every point up until then, we were really light-hearted. I'm so glad that he got to do all this really cool shit at the end.

What was your reaction to first reading that Theo stabs him?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i knew beforehand. I think initially J. D. I was like, "Oh, I guess that was the whole secret they were trying to keep from me. and Patrick's plan was to wait for me to just get the script and read it, but Charlotte Brandstrom, the first episode director, just blurted it out to me. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, so, i knew it was coming, but i didn't know how. Reading it, I just didn't imagine it to be as heartfelt as it was. I always thought that it was going to be a lot colder and a lot quicker. I knew at some point if I was going to go to the dark side, there would be a confrontation between them, because obviously they're fighting on opposing ends of the war, and they're both frontmen. So, reading it and seeing how close he was to really accepting Arondir was really heartbreaking. This is actually such a love-filled scene, and that's why it's so tragic and so heartbreaking, because there is so much love between them, and it just disappears in an instant, which leaves a real hollow feeling at the end of the episode.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there's that moment of compulsion from sauron that makes theo stab arondir. What's he thinking at that moment? Is he reevaluating his choice, or is his humanity too far gone?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, theo is definitely someone who's been a product of who his role models are and who is giving him guidance. This is the moment where his two biggest role models in his life at this point are meeting head to head. That moment when Sauron arrives is him thinking, "Oh yeah, I remember what I'm supposed to be doing now. For the last few weeks, Theo has been under the influence of Sauron. He has been fed however many ideas in his head about the elves. But then when he sees Arondir's face, all those ideas that Sauron had planted disappear, and he's almost ready to accept the hand that's put out in front of him because he can see the the love in Arondir's eyes. " It flips back into work mode, or servant mode.

Berdasarkan laporan, right now we know the nazgnagôl as ring-servants, but we know that the final iteration of them is the nazgûl, who are totally far gone. Assuming Theo stays on this path, what is an element of that transformation that you're most excited to play?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the cool thing about the nazgnagôl and the nazgûl is that they have a completely different living experience to anything else in middle-earth. They are living in between two worlds, and so you're trying to explore what it looks like to be detaching from the mortal world, becoming more spirit-like, and losing a sense of reality while being completely controlled and manipulated. It'll be really interesting because at this point in time, the Nazgnagôl are still men. They have autonomy over themselves and their decisions and what they can do, whereas it'd be great to see them slowly not be able to do that.

Berdasarkan laporan, the show has such a massive array of locations to visit. Going forward, what is one of the worlds within Middle-earth that you would like to work in?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i would love, love, love to do work in númenor. Any time I've been on the sets with the Númenóreans, they all seem to be getting along real well, whereas I've been hanging out with orcs who most of the time aren't that happy. Everything around it is so glorious and beautiful, and there's a real community vibe. The sets are just so magnificent. [laughs].

And who is someone from the ensemble you'd love to work with?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i'd love to do work with more or at least more stuff with leon [wadham], who plays kemen. I really wish we had more to do. When we were shooting Season 3, he was actually living above me, so we were constantly just borrowing stuff off each other all the time and just talking about work or whatever. We only ever had two days on set, and it was the last scene of Season 2 and the first scene of Season 3. I love Leon. But I also just think Kemen is not a nice guy.

Berdasarkan laporan, every time he's on screen, i'm angry. I don't even care if Theo's on the dark side. He deserves his vengeance a little.

Yeah, I'd love for Theo to face off against Kemen and give him what he deserves.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple's iphone duo has been my main phone for a month. I switched from the iPhone 17 Pro Max (I only tested the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max for a week), set up all my apps (including online banking and other finance apps, which typically require a more complicated setup) on the Duo, and put my other phones in a drawer.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is a different type of test than a typical phone review. When you're writing a review, you're looking for the new and exciting. Once you've switched to a new phone entirely, you're looking for apps that don't work and annoyances that can't be fixed. Had I found enough of these, I would've gone back to the Pro.

Diungkapkan bahwa but i feel zero desire to do so. The iPhone Duo has plenty of quirks, but none that would make me go back. In fact, I dread the moment when I'll have to go back to a regular-sized phone to do a review. The iPhone Duo is a game-changer for me. I am now a foldable phone guy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for my detailed review of the iphone duo, go here. In this article, I'll skip the details and highlight the interesting bits.

Diungkapkan bahwa my iphone duo works just as well as it did on the first day. The dreaded crease is still barely visible. I know that some unlucky folks have had screen trouble, but I haven't had anything of the sort so far. The hinge works smoothly. In fact, the only real trouble I've had with the Duo has been grease buildup on the inner display, which appears near-impossible to remove (but is, fortunately, invisible most of the time).

Berdasarkan laporan, not only did the hardware hold up, but i've gotten completely used to it. I perform the little tasks (check out a message, see the weather forecast) on the front display; I flip the phone open for anything taking longer than five seconds. It's become second nature, and I don't think about it anymore. I still awkwardly search for the volume buttons sometimes, but even that doesn't bother me much; I know they're there, somewhere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the camera is the duo's weak point, and i do miss the telephoto option. If there's one thing that would make me go back to a non-Duo phone, it would be the camera. The Duo's camera isn't bad, but it's roughly in line with what you'd get on an iPhone 16 or 17, and that can be hard if you've used a recent Pro model. For now, I'm sticking with it, but I really hope the next Duo gets a lot of improvements in this area.

Berdasarkan laporan, battery life isn't a problem. It's not as good as battery life on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but it the Duo lasts a full day for me. Still, I've never had to charge it more than once per day, which is good enough for me. It really depends on how you use it, and the Duo beckons you to use it more for gaming and videos, which drains the battery faster. Berdasarkan laporan, by far the most annoying bugs have to do with the fact that the iphone duo has four cameras and many apps still don't know when to invoke which one. Making a video call on Messenger, WhatsApp, or Apple's own FaceTime will yield different results depending on how the phone is turned; sometimes you'll be upside down for no good reason. Sometimes, the person you're on a call with will be in a narrow, vertical window awkwardly positioned in the middle of that large, horizontal inner display. I have no doubt this will all get fixed over time, but it is taking a bit too long.

Berdasarkan laporan, the other annoyance is that some apps still haven't been properly updated for the duo, and that could take months or perhaps years to fix. This includes some apps I use daily, such as Google Authenticator and TradingView. Others have been tweaked to fit the big display better, but those tweaks were just quick fixes. This isn't hard to get used to, but it just feels like the overall app experience on the Duo could and should be so much better.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the other day, i watched two entire episodes of slow horses on the iphone duo. I've never done something like that on any phone; the displays were always too small. Given the Duo's screen size, brightness, and quality, watching on the Duo would actually be an improvement over a crappy hotel TV (and TVs in hotels are still very often very crappy).

Sebagaimana diketahui, on my desk, i now have the iphone duo all the time as an additional display. I use it to control music, check my calendar and reminders, and manage my smart home devices. In fact, wherever I go, I prop the Duo up beside me; it's like a more portable HomeView.

Berdasarkan laporan, showing a bunch of photos to someone, playing a video for a group, and browsing through a shopping site together with my wife are all tasks that are borderline annoying on a regular phone, and almost invariably end with someone giving up very quickly. On the Duo, the experience is great, and is invariably greeted with the same comment: "That screen is nice. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, oh, and the fact that the stereo speakers are pretty great also helps a lot when you're playing music on the duo. Theoretically, you can prop up any phone on a table and play music, but you'll rarely do it because the sound is thin and tinny. On the Duo, it's good enough to be the background entertainer at a small gathering.

Sebagaimana diketahui, keeping it simple: how many times do i hold the duo in my hand and think, "damn, i wish i had a different phone now"? the answer is never. Or, perhaps, only when I need to take a photo, and even then the Duo is better for actually viewing the photos I've taken.

Berdasarkan laporan, the advantages of having an iphone with a massive, beautiful, ipad mini-like display in your pocket simply outweigh all of the compromises that you have to make with the duo. And I don't see myself going back anytime soon.

#482. Apple Watch Ultra 4 vs. Ultra 3: Why you might want to upgrade to Apples new rugged smartwatch

Apple Watch Ultra 4 vs. Ultra 3: Why you might want to upgrade to Apples new rugged smartwatch

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/tech/apple-watch-ultra-4-vs-ultra-3

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple dropped a new premium rugged smartwatch this fall, the apple watch ultra 4. While it looks the same as its predecessor on the outside, don't be fooled: Its has some updated internal hardware and fresh features that make it "an essential upgrade" for certain users, according to our reviewer.

Here's a closer look at the key differences between the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and last year's Apple Watch Ultra 3.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the apple watch ultra 4 and ultra 3 both start at $799 in one size with cellular connectivity. The latter is no longer available in new condition through the Apple Store, but third-party retailers were still selling it as of this writing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as mentioned up top, both apple watch ultras look virtually identical. The Ultra 4 is just slightly heavier by up to 1. They both have 49mm titanium cases that are water-resistant for up to 100 meters. 4 grams, depending on the case color, and the back of it is made from ceramic and zirconia instead of ceramic and sapphire crystal.

Berdasarkan laporan, apple didn't make any changes to the ultra's display between the two generations. The Ultra 3 and 4 both have a wide-angle, always-on OLED display with up to 3,000 nits of brightness. They're 50 percent brighter than the standard Apple Watch Series 12.

Berdasarkan laporan, the titanium cases on the ultra 3 and 4 both come in the same two colors: natural and black. You can pair them each with an Alpine Loop, Trail Loop, Ocean Band, Titanium Milanese Loop ($100 extra), or premium bands from the Apple Watch Hermès collection that Apple designed in partnership with the luxury French fashion brand. Those cost a pretty penny.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple rolled out several new band colors and one new hermès band style for the ultra 4. They also fit the Ultra 3, and you can buy them separately for $99 to $2,199:.

Alpine Loops: Desert, dark olive, and burgundy.

Trail Loops: Dark umber, sand, and burgundy.

Ocean Bands: Translucent gray, translucent kelp, and translucent black.

Apple Watch Hermès collection: Grand H Titane band.

Berdasarkan laporan, like the series 12, the ultra 4 runs on apple's brand-new s11 chip, which makes it capable of taking more accurate step counts and running some new audio intelligence tools (more on those shortly). The Ultra 3 has an older S10 chip.

Diungkapkan bahwa both apple watch ultras support wifi 4 and bluetooth 5. 3, and come equipped with 64GB of built-in storage.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ultra 3 is a very long-lasting smartwatch, but thanks to that s11 chip, the ultra 4 can stretch its battery life even further in a bunch of different scenarios. It taps out at 42 hours of normal usage and 72 hours in Low Power Mode. It's rated for up to 50 hours of normal usage and 84 hours in Low Power Mode, which is a boost of up to 19 percent compared to the Ultra 3. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Diungkapkan bahwa both ultras can charge to 80 percent battery in about 45 minutes, but the ultra 4 charges quicker on shorter cycles. Fifteen minutes on an outlet gives it up to 18 hours of normal use, while a five-minute charge delivers up to 10 hours of sleep tracking. Those numbers dip down to 12 hours and 8 hours, respectively, with the Ultra 3.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ultra 4 also has new extended workout and max extended workout modes. These get you up to 25 and 45 hours of usage during endurance activities while the watch is taking constant GPS and heart rate readings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chip and battery life aside, the ultra 4's biggest hardware upgrade comes in the form of its new optical and electrical heart sensors. The former glow green on the underside of the device.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thanks to these sensors, apple said the ultra 4 takes more frequent and accurate heart-rate readings and measures heart rate variability (hrv), a marker of stress and recovery, up to 24 times more often than the ultra 3. You can now compare your daytime and nighttime HRV measurements as well.

Berdasarkan laporan, both ultras run on watchos 27 and support apple intelligence tools like and siri ai. Key health and safety features like hypertension notifications, sleep apnea alerts, blood oxygen readings, cycle tracking, and Emergency SOS via Satellite are available on either model. But since the Ultra 4 has a more powerful chip and better sensors, it can do a couple things that the Ultra 3 can't.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one is calculate a readiness score, which tells the user how fit they are for future exercises on a scale of 0 to 10. This score is based on their recent activity, vitals, and quality of sleep.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ultra 4 also has a redesigned pedometer model that can track steps more accurately and a new steps complication on its watch face. On older Apple Watch models, a step count widget is something you have to DIY.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finally, the ultra 4 adds audio intelligence tools like sound recognition alerts, live rewind conversation transcriptions, siri recap conversation summaries, and automatic music recognition via shazam, which rely on its built-in microphone. Apple said they don't create or store any audio recordings, and that raw audio is processed separately from the rest of the system before being deleted. But if you're too sketched out by them, you can just turn them off.

All of these new features are also available on the Apple Watch Series 12, which has the same upgraded chip and sensors as the Ultra 4.

Berdasarkan laporan, after testing the apple watch ultra 4 for a few days prior to its release, mashable senior editor stan schroeder concluded that it's "an essential upgrade" for "an athlete, especially an endurance athlete, who needs the best battery life and the best heart rate measurement system available. " If your workouts aren't quite as intense, you'll probably be content with an Ultra 3.

Berdasarkan laporan, it should be noted that the ultra 3 is easier to find on sale these days since it's an older device. (It's been as cheap as $649 a couple times and regularly falls to $699, while the Ultra 4 has only hit $699. 99 once so far since launch. ) If you want a fancy and durable wearable at a great value, monitor retailers' listings for deals in the coming weeks, especially around Black Friday. That said, if both models are sitting at their usual price of $799 when you go to buy one, you might as well get the nicer Ultra 4.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, direct arylation of c–h bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. 1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge. 5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

Connections can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

Sebagaimana diketahui, each puzzle features 16 words and each grouping of words is split into four categories. These sets could comprise of anything from book titles, software, country names, etc. Even though multiple words will seem like they fit together, there's only one correct answer.

Berdasarkan laporan, if a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake—players get up to four mistakes until the game ends.

#496. Even giant anteaters in remote Brazil have microplastics in their blood

📅 13 Nov 2026

Even giant anteaters in remote Brazil have microplastics in their blood

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03660-5

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. Gemma Conroy is a freelance journalist in Mexico City and editor of Nature Briefing: Careers.

Diungkapkan bahwa giant anteaters traipsing across brazil’s pristine wetlands and savannahs have ingested traces of plastic pollutants. Credit: Sylvain Cordier/Gamma-Rapho via Getty.

Some of Brazil’s wildlife have traces of plastic circulating in their blood — even if they live far from land used by humans, according to an analysis published on 11 November in Nature1.

Berdasarkan laporan, researchers measured the concentration of microplastics in the blood of 47 animals: 26 lowland tapirs (tapirus terrestris) and 21 giant anteaters (myrmecophaga tridactyla). The scientists found that, on average, the creatures carry similar levels of plastic as many humans — roughly 74 particles per millilitre of blood. The animals that lived closest to human infrastructure and waste-management facilities had the highest levels of microplastics in their blood.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but even those living more than 100 kilometres from a waste sites and 65 kilometres from human infrastructure showed traces of the pollutants. This indicates that plastics can reach wildlife living far from where the pollution originates, says study co-author Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, a conservation scientist at the University of British Columbia’s Okanagan campus in Kelowna, Canada.

The findings are an important step to better understand how the particles impact wildlife, says Sofia Ya-Hsuan Liou, a geochemist at the National Taiwan University in Taipei.

Berdasarkan laporan, microplastics are tiny particles (smaller than five millimetres across) with many different chemical compositions. They can travel through the environment in rainwater, rivers and the atmosphere. Although several studies have measured microplastics levels in wildlife, few have explored how the surrounding environment influences what animals ingest, says study co-author Michael Noonan, a quantitative ecologist at the University of British Columbia’s Okanagan campus.

Diungkapkan bahwa to find out, noonan, ferraz and their colleagues collected and analysed blood samples from animals living across the amazon rainforest, the cerrado savannah and the huge and pristine pantanal wetland between february 2021 and november 2022. The researchers also used GPS data to track the animals’ movements and their exposure to a human footprint.

Daily briefing: Should old, bad science be culled from the literature?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03675-y

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. Hello Nature readers, would you like to get this Briefing in your inbox free every day? Sign up here.

Diungkapkan bahwa physicists used an algorithm to combine telescope measurements of a black hole in a different way from the original analysis. Thyagarajan, O. I. Lai, N. Wong and F. Credit: S. Diakogiannis/CSIRO.

Berdasarkan laporan, a re-evaluation of data from the event horizon telescope (eht) has corroborated the findings that yielded the first-ever photo of a black hole. After the blurry image was released in 2019, sceptics argued that the circular shape seen in the shot was an artefact of the team’s image-reconstruction techniques. Independent astrophysicist Samuel Lai and his team used different methods to reanalyse the original data and their results — including new images of the black hole — largely match those of the EHT team.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the funding that voters in california have approved to earmark for immunology research — the largest ever infusion of cash for science authorized by a public vote in us history. (Nature | 5 min read).

Diungkapkan bahwa researchers have catalogued almost 100 proteins that get a free pass through the blood–brain barrier to maintain the health of neurons. Most of these proteins were produced in distant organs, particularly the liver. The team found that the transport of some of these proteins is disrupted in mice with a brain disease that mimics early-stage Alzheimer’s disease. The work suggests that the brain actively imports the proteins it needs to stay healthy, and that the breakdown of that transport drives the dysfunction seen in neurodegenerative disease, says neuroscientist and study co-author Andrew Yang.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the launch of the artemis ii mission to orbit the moon produced unprecedented large-scale atmospheric disturbances, say researchers. Data from GPS receivers found that the Space Launch System — the most powerful rocket that NASA has ever built — disrupted the atmospheric layer known as the ionosphere. The GPS disruption was potentially large enough to “have a strong impact not only on self-driving cars but also on drone positioning,” says space physicist and study co-author Charles Lin.

Reference: Geophysical Research Letters preprint (not peer reviewed).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the scientific literature contains decades-old papers that detail fraudulent, unethical or merely incorrect results, but aren’t marked as such. Many of these papers are long neglected, but their digitization enables artificial-intelligence tools that summarize scientific literature on a topic to feed misinformation to a new generation. This leaves publishers to wrangle with the question of whether these historical papers should be retracted or flagged as suspect — a task that can be tricky if authors are dead, original records can’t be consulted or journals are no longer in print.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “you need a container before you can get the chemistry” that enables cellular life, says astrobiologist bruce damer. He’s among those researchers who favour a ‘lipid-first’ hypothesis for the origin of complex life: that the lipid membrane that corrals the cell is key to its success. Or even that bubbles of lipids, plus the chemistry they enclosed, could have propagated and evolved in a Darwinian-like way, before RNA (or DNA) arrived on the scene.

Enjoy more ideas about where we came from in Quanta Magazine’s Origins of Life Week.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, social scientists should be involved in the process of finding suitable locations for new observatories, argues anthropologist jaco de swart, co-principal investigator of a proposed neutrino detector to be built in the peruvian andes. Many suitable locations for such projects are sensitive ecological environments with cultural significance for Indigenous communities. Social scientists can help to integrate environmental care into these projects and build relationships with local and Indigenous stakeholders. “To build scientific infrastructure that is responsible, just and resilient, humanities scholars must have leadership roles from the start,” de Swart writes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, appearing in the jurassic park franchise is the strongest predictor of a dinosaur species’ popularity, according to new research — an example of the ‘blockbuster effect’. The media should leverage this effect to put a spotlight on endangered species, says zoologist Pâmela Lima. (Science | 7 min read).

Berdasarkan laporan, doi: https://doi. org/10. 1038/d41586-026-03675-y.

Diungkapkan bahwa the kangaroo is a multiple-choice mathematics challenge attempted by more than seven million children in around 120 countries, just for fun. The Guardian’s maths-puzzle-master Alex Bellos shared a Kangaroo question from the 2024 event that should be accessible to skilled secondary-school students — so Briefing readers will certainly be good to have a go. The answer is here.

Sebagaimana diketahui, did you manage to tame the kangaroo? let me know — along with any other feedback on this newsletter — at briefing@nature. com.

Marco Paggi is at the IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, 55100 Lucca, Italy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists’ knowledge of the connectivity, robustness and functionality of complex networks — such as those that describe interactions in chemical and biological systems, social relationships and the internet — has increased enormously over the past few decades1. The foundations of modern complex-network science were established by the pioneering contributions of Albert-László Barabási and Réka Albert2,3, who revealed universal mechanisms that explain the emergence of highly non-uniform network configurations. Writing in Nature, Both et al. 4 report that ideas from network science can be used to design materials that have remarkable mechanical properties, incorporating connection diversity and variable component sizes found in complex systems into materials engineering.

#502. DeepMind’s ultra-powerful AI for genome mapping wows scientists

📅 13 Nov 2026

DeepMind’s ultra-powerful AI for genome mapping wows scientists

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03673-0

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). com. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Berdasarkan laporan, in 2024, researchers found a new driver of inflammatory bowel disease (ibd): it was a gene called ets2 that is overactive in immune cells owing to a dna variant that predisposes people to the condition1. This variant had previously confounded researchers because it lies in a ‘gene desert’ nowhere near protein-coding sequences.

Diungkapkan bahwa that discovery had involved gene-editing and other sophisticated molecular-biology techniques, and it identified potential new ibd treatments. Now, researchers at Google DeepMind in London have replicated aspects of the finding using an artificial-intelligence model, and they have done this without lifting a pipette. Their model is called AlphaGenome 2.

Berdasarkan laporan, “they’ve managed to figure out the answer in 30 minutes, and it took us a year and a half of experiments,” says james lee, an immunologist and geneticist at the francis crick institute in london who led the 2024 study. “It’s reassuring from our perspective. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the alphagenome 2 model, which was announced today, is an update to an ai tool that predicts the molecular effects that ‘non-coding’ dna sequences have, such as on the expression of other genes. These sequences comprise 98% of the human genome, but they are among the hardest to decipher. The latest model makes these predictions in hundreds of mouse and human cell types.

Two months ago, Google DeepMind released the AlphaGenome Atlas: these were predictions for every possible single-letter DNA change to the human genome — a total of nine billion variants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these and other predictions were made with a tool called alphagenome 1 and came with a major caveat: they did not specify the precise kind of cell — be it antibody-making b cells or pancreatic β-cells — in which a variant was likely to act. “Having something that cannot predict cell-type specificity is a bit of a problem, which is why it hasn’t been hugely useful for us,” says Lee.

But researchers know that many non-coding DNA sequences — including the variant that Lee’s team mapped, which is part of a sequence called a gene enhancer — tend to be active in specific types of cell.

“If you want to understand variants associated with genetic diseases, then you have to ask yourself what are the cell types that are affected,” says Žiga Avsec, a DeepMind researcher who leads the AlphaGenome team.

Berdasarkan laporan, to develop an ai model that could decipher variant effects in diverse cells, avsec’s team trained alphagenome 2 on single-cell gene activity and other measurements made in more than 100 million cells, across 68 tissues. AlphaGenome 1, by contrast, was fed data collected in ‘bulk’ samples of heterogeneous cells.

The result is a richer, more fine-grained representation of the differences between cells, says Adam Gayoso, a Google DeepMind scientist and co-author of a preprint describing the model on the company’s website.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, alphagenome 2 also isn’t limited to making predictions in the 637 types of human cell and 311 kinds of mouse cell it was trained on. Researchers can provide the model with new single-cell gene-activity data — such as those from cells in a disease state — and generate gene-variant predictions. This could help researchers to identify variants underlying disease more quickly, says Gayoso.

#506. Biotech innovations are an opportunity to limit climate change

📅 13 Nov 2026

Biotech innovations are an opportunity to limit climate change

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03621-y

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Diungkapkan bahwa climate change is affecting many types of crop, including these unusually small potatoes. Credit: John Thys/AFP/Getty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, policymakers at the united nations cop31 climate conference that started this week in antalya, turkey, will know that the un environment programme has confirmed that global warming will exceed the limit of 1. 5 °C above pre-industrial temperatures agreed in 2015 in Paris. This meeting comes hot on the heels of the UN COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia, which affirmed yet again that the world is also in the middle of a biodiversity crisis. But researchers across scientific disciplines are now arguing that advances in biotechnology could provide solutions1. Progress in each case, whether preventing dangerous climate change or stemming biodiversity loss, is too slow. Methods such as gene editing and germplasm mining — the analysis of huge libraries of plant-genome sequences to find useful traits for crop improvement — can now be used to tackle global warming and protect nature, scientists write in a climate-themed issue of Nature Biotechnology.

Berdasarkan laporan, there was a time — not that long ago — when many considered biotechnologies a threat to the environment. But as the special issue shows, a shift is under way. Now, the field offers strategies for protecting both climate and biodiversity from the many damaging effects of industrial agriculture.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to feed a growing global population, between 2015 and 2024, the amount of cultivated land grew by roughly eight million hectares a year1. Land clearance and land-use change contributes up to five billion tonnes of carbon annually — and is a major cause of biodiversity loss. Yet, if the greenhouse-gas emissions, and thus global warming, this expansion causes is to be avoided, the world must work out how to produce enough food within its current agricultural footprint. Here, biotech solutions have some of the greatest potential, for example, by helping to increase crop yields and to protect plants from heat, drought and disease.

How biotechnology can mitigate climate change by curbing the global land squeeze.

How biotechnology can mitigate climate change by curbing the global land squeeze.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, of 77 such technologies with applications in agriculture, aquaculture and other sectors, many are ready for large-scale testing in the field, propose bioengineers shekhar mishra, lauren lui and adam arkin at the lawrence berkeley national laboratory in california in a perspective article2. Argentina, China and the United States have given the green light to engineered drought-tolerant crops.

Diungkapkan bahwa rice farming produces around 9% of human-caused emissions of the greenhouse gas methane. Now, researchers have found a way to slash these emissions, write agronomist Yunkai Jin at Hunan Agricultural University in Changsha, China, and his colleagues in a Comment article3.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but technological readiness isn’t enough: governments, regulators and the public need to be ready, too4. Readers might have a sense of déjà vu: in the 1990s, advances in biotechnology promised a revolution in food and agriculture — which subsequently stalled. The ambition was to genetically modify crops or engineer them in other ways so that they could tolerate herbicides, resist insects and fight viruses. But, at the time, many scientists, governments and corporations promoting the technology gave insufficient attention to several issues.

Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture.

Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture.

Berdasarkan laporan, one concern was public anxiety about the idea of eating food produced using transgenic technologies — crops modified by inserting a gene from another plant species or other organism. Another issue was that risks to the environment and to human health had not been studied sufficiently. A third problem was that multinational companies dominated both the research and the development of these technologies, creating fears that the rise of agricultural biotechnology would put many small family farms out of business.

Sebagaimana diketahui, environmental groups found common cause with consumer organizations. In the European Union, for example, risks to human health and the environment needed to be assessed before technologies producing genetically modified organisms could be commercialized. Together, they urged governments to enact strict regulations. Although this was necessary, it slowed down advances in low- and middle-income countries, because any nation intending to export produce to the EU would have to prove that it was not genetically modified.

Sebagaimana diketahui, since then, at least two things have changed, increasing optimism about the use of biotechnology to help the planet. The discovery of gene editing — in which an organism’s genes are modified precisely to produce specific traits — has proved transformational for agriculture. The method is being developed cautiously and is regulated in a more nuanced way than were conventional technologies that produce genetically modified crops. In June, the EU amended its regulations on genetic modification and now permits the cultivation of some gene-edited crops.

Low-methane rice is near — the world should deploy it.

Low-methane rice is near — the world should deploy it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a second development is that catastrophic events such as heatwaves and floods have meant that climate change and the planet’s protection have become mainstream concerns across science and society, not just for environmental research. In a way, we all need to be environmentalists now, and this provides a rationale for governments to reconsider adopting biotech solutions with appropriate safeguards in place.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, advances in biotechnology that limit land use should be deployed to slow down the rise in global temperatures and biodiversity loss. This will require a partnership between the private sector, scientists, conservationists and farmers. High-yielding crops produced using industrial agriculture have helped to feed the world but have also had a devastating effect on biodiversity. Organic agriculture is more sustainable but requires extra land, because its yields tend to be lower than those from industrial methods. Providing they are implemented wisely, safely and ethically, biotechnologies could contribute to innovative farming methods that offer the best of both worlds.

#507. How I balance my life as a professional surfer and a university researcher

📅 13 Nov 2026

How I balance my life as a professional surfer and a university researcher

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03183-z

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. com. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Cliff Kapono is a professional surfer and marine conservation scientist.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cliff kapono enjoys professional surfing as an adjunct to his academic career. Credit: Nani Welch Keliihoomalu for Nature.

Diungkapkan bahwa during my graduate studies at the university of california, san diego, long hours in the laboratory were often stressful, and not just because of the research. Most of my anxiety came from looking out the window at perfect surfing conditions and realizing I didn’t have much time to finish my experiments and leave while the ‘waves were firing’.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, several years on, i am now an assistant professor at the school of ocean futures at arizona state university (asu), working from hilo, hawaii, where i balance scientific research with my second job: travelling the world as a non-competitive professional surfer. Also known as a free surfer, I ride a variety of board designs — from conventional wooden surfboards to modern big-wave ‘guns’ — and produce social-media content, such as photos and videos, in exchange for endorsement opportunities.

Diungkapkan bahwa my research is also deeply connected to the ocean. I study coral microbiomes, sampling the community of microorganisms living on and in the coral before and after environmental stress to improve understanding of reef health and the sea-bed formations that create waves, referred to as surf breaks. In May, my colleagues and I reported on the importance of creating a framework to analyse systems with environmental, social and cultural components to protect surf ecosystems1.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in my faculty position, i work in nine-month appointments, and i am permitted to spend a number of work hours each calendar year on non-conflicting outside business. I spend roughly 85% of my work year on research and teaching and 15% on surfing assignments.

Berdasarkan laporan, many careers are no longer confined to a single discipline or identity, and some of the most meaningful work now happens at the intersection between different skills, communities and ways of thinking. When I was a student, I used to worry that I would have to choose between surfing and science. Surfing shapes the questions I want to ask as a scientist, while science provides me with ways to understand and protect ocean environments. Today, my career exists because I didn’t.

Berdasarkan laporan, when i graduated from high school in 2005, native hawaiians and pacific islanders made up less than 0. 2% of all science, technology, engineering and mathematics degree graduates in the United States. Today, that number remains at only 0. 3%2. As a Native Hawaiian kid, targeted fellowships and private programmes made university possible for me, covering my tuition and board.

Berdasarkan laporan, after i started a phd chemistry programme at the university of california, san diego, in 2012, my studies became much more demanding. Courses, a teaching-assistant role, fellowship requirements and lab training would keep me on land from sunrise until sundown. Despite being able to see the ocean from nearly every window on campus, it was the time in my life that I felt furthest from it.

Diungkapkan bahwa remarkably, it was during the third year of my phd programme that getting paid to surf actually became a reality. I stopped measuring success only by hours in the lab. After many nights spent in the lab, I decided to set academic boundaries and rededicate time to the waves, mostly as a way to protect my mental health. Instead, I treated time in the ocean as part of the scientific process.

Can a 'lullaby' save coral reefs from extinction?.

Can a 'lullaby' save coral reefs from extinction?.

Surfing-industry figures took notice, and not long after becoming more present on the beaches, I was offered modest ambassadorial contracts that developed into respectable budgets that let me travel to places with better waves and to collaborate with local board builders — when not in the lab, of course.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when i moved back to hawaii in 2018, i received a us national science foundation postdoctoral fellowship for broadening participation of under-represented groups in biology and i began to use surfing as a vehicle for communicating coral science. That eventually led to Arizona State University recruiting me to join its Hilo-based Center for Global Discovery and Conservation Science in 2021, a position that has since evolved into my current role.

Berdasarkan laporan, blending the two disciplines has made my research more creative and my surfing more meaningful. It also taught me the importance of protecting time for the parts of life that keep you grounded. Whether that be surfing, music, art or family, maintaining space for your passions is not a distraction from academic work; it is often the very thing that sustains it.

Here are some guiding principles that have helped me to navigate the worlds of surfing and academia.

Berdasarkan laporan, the best experiences come when you find a crew that wants to surf the same waves or explore the same questions as you. Some of the most important opportunities in my career came from relationships that started organically, often through time spent in the ocean and local communities, or through a shared curiosity, rather than formal networking.

Diungkapkan bahwa the researchers, surfers, photographers and conservationists i work with are people who genuinely care about the places we study and the communities connected to them. Over time, those shared values create trust that later opens doors to research projects, publications, funding opportunities and creative collaborations. I’ve found that the best way to find these people is not by chasing status or connections but by consistently showing up in the communities and places that you genuinely care about.

Hideki Shirakawa obituary: chemist who showed that plastics can conduct electricity
