Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kazuo akagi is a research professor at ritsumeikan university, kusatsu, japan, and professor emeritus at kyoto university and the university of tsukuba. He worked with Shirakawa on polyacetylene thin films starting in 1984, when he joined Shirakawa’s lab at the University of Tsukuba.

Diungkapkan bahwa hideki shirakawa pioneered the field of conductive polymers, overturning the common view that plastics do not conduct electricity. His demonstration that thin films of polyacetylene — an organic polymer — can become conductive when doped with small amounts of other chemicals earned him a share of the 2000 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (with Alan MacDiarmid and Alan Heeger). He was the second Japanese chemist to receive this award, after Kenichi Fukui in 1981. Shirakawa has died aged 90.

Diungkapkan bahwa shirakawa was born in tokyo. After graduating from secondary school in Takayama City, he studied chemical engineering at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (now the Institute of Science Tokyo). He went on to pursue master’s and doctoral studies there, under the supervision of polymer chemist Shu Kambara, earning a Doctor of Engineering degree for his research on how blocks of organic molecules combine to form polymer chains.

Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.

Chemistry education must change to help the planet: here’s how.

Diungkapkan bahwa after completing his doctorate in 1966, shirakawa was hired as a research associate in the laboratory of sakuji ikeda at tokyo tech. There, he began studying how acetylene molecules join together to form a polymer, using Ziegler–Natta catalysts (which are based on organic molecules containing transition metals).

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 1967, shirakawa was joined in his experiments by a visiting researcher from south korea, hyung chick pyun. The pair were polymerizing acetylene using a catalyst composed of tetrabutoxytitanium and triethylaluminium to produce powdered polyacetylene.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on one occasion, however, the protocol failed to produce the powder. Instead, a ragged film formed on the surface of the solution in the flask. On closer inspection, it became clear that the visiting researcher had mistakenly used a much higher concentration of the catalyst than was intended — 1,000 times higher. Shirakawa went on to synthesize a thin film of polyacetylene with a metallic lustre by introducing acetylene gas into a flask coated on the inside with the concentrated catalyst.

Chemists struggle to ditch hazardous solvents — even after decades of ‘green’ efforts.

Chemists struggle to ditch hazardous solvents — even after decades of ‘green’ efforts.

Diungkapkan bahwa subsequently, he travelled to the university of pennsylvania in philadelphia, where he worked with macdiarmid and heeger. The team discovered that adding small amounts of molecules that accept electrons (such as bromine) or that donate electrons (such as arsenic pentafluoride) increased the electrical conductivity of the thin film by a factor of ten million. This work led to the trio’s Nobel award.

#509. Give biologists the space to be curious, not just better tools

📅 13 Nov 2026

Give biologists the space to be curious, not just better tools

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03669-w

Berdasarkan laporan, thank you for visiting nature. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Edith Heard is the chief executive of the Francis Crick Institute, London.

As the Francis Crick Institute in London celebrates its tenth anniversary and I look back on my first year as chief executive, I find myself reflecting on both how much has been achieved and how profoundly life science is changing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as an epigeneticist, i can safely say that history and context matter. When I began my scientific career in the 1980s, experiments were painstaking, time-consuming, expensive and repetitive. Generating a knockout mouse or sequencing a gene could take weeks or months, and required resources that were available at few institutions.

The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update.

The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update.

Diungkapkan bahwa biology has since entered an extraordinary era. It is increasingly multidisciplinary, and researchers have an unprecedented range of technologies at their disposal, from single-cell and spatial biology techniques to advanced imaging, genome editing, tissue engineering and computational approaches.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, artificial intelligence is also transforming science. Its ability to bring together complex data sets offers fresh ways to connect the study of biology across scales, from molecules and cells to individual organisms and populations. It is also enabling the democratization of discovery and knowledge. Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold system, for example, has made predictions of millions of protein structures available to researchers worldwide.

Berdasarkan laporan, biologists are poised to at last understand the complexity of life: the influence of the environment, ageing and sex, alongside genetics, on the differences between us. Among the questions to which answers are within reach are how the genetic code gives rise to a living organism; how the control and expression of genes varies during development; how tissues communicate and bodily functions depend on one another; and why diseases develop differently in different people and treatments work for some but not others.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reductionism has served biology well, giving us a deep mechanistic understanding of life, health and disease. But many features of living systems cannot be predicted from their individual parts alone. They emerge from interactions between components and depend on the context in which those interactions occur.

Berdasarkan laporan, science needs both reductionist and holistic approaches: connecting molecular mechanisms and signalling pathways with inter-organ communication and physiology, while understanding how these systems respond and adapt to environmental challenges. And performing such studies requires research environments that allow scientists to think and work across conventional boundaries.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as director of the crick, i have seen the incredible value of an environment that is organized around people and scientific questions rather than institutional divisions. Shared infrastructure and specialist teams enable research to cross disciplines and deploy technologies in new ways. Connections between fundamental research, clinical science and industry also help discoveries to move towards real-world applications, swiftly and efficiently.

Berdasarkan laporan, but even the most sophisticated technologies and research environments are only as powerful as the scientists using them. Creating an environment in which people from diverse backgrounds and with different life experiences are encouraged to perform bold, rigorous science and harness the power of AI will be key to future discoveries. Patterns identified by AI need to be scrutinized by people and validated through experiment.

Heidi Ledford reports for Nature from Seattle, Washington.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, minimalist biotechnology companies that have just a handful of employees — or even as few as one — are becoming more feasible with the rise of artificial-intelligence tools. Credit: Getty.

How many scientists does it take to discover a drug?.

The question came to the fore after news that a biotechnology company armed with an artificial-intelligence assistant, two promising drug leads and just one full-time human employee had been acquired by San Francisco-based Anthropic as part of the AI giant’s expansion into biomedical science.

AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more.

AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more.

Berdasarkan laporan, in truth, it took many human scientists to develop the molecules that are the mini-company’s star products: two antibodies that are still in the early stages of development and were designed to treat a rare form of muscular dystrophy. Many more researchers will be needed to carry the drug further, especially if it eventually enters clinical trials. The company, Mithril Medicine in Cambridge, Massachusetts, also hired part-time consultants to advise on the project, and paid at least five contract research organizations to conduct experiments. “It takes a village to develop a drug,” says Jeb Keiper, a partner at Third Rock Ventures, a venture-capital firm in Boston, Massachusetts.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the news sparked a wave of discussions about whether the one-person biotech is the drug-discovery business model of the future. “They will be very powerful for identifying good opportunities and moving quickly. “We will see more and more of these small teams that are enabled by AI,” says James Zou, a computer scientist who works on biomedical applications of AI at Stanford University in California. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, itsy-bitsy biotechs are not a new concept. The company never had a physical laboratory, Davidson says. Entrepreneur Matt Davidson started his first biotech company in 2013, nearly a decade before ChatGPT’s public debut. Davidson kept the roster trim for years, with only two full-time employees until the drug he was developing was ready to enter late-stage clinical testing. All the lab work was contracted out.

Diungkapkan bahwa his current company, azora therapeutics in los angeles, california, has a whopping five employees. He uses AI more for summarizing reports than for scientific discovery and says that AI tools have made tiny biotechs more efficient. “We use consultants a little bit less than we used to,” he says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, anthropic’s ai biolab finds ‘crispr-like’ dna in viruses. What’s next?.

Berdasarkan laporan, anthropic’s ai biolab finds ‘crispr-like’ dna in viruses. What’s next?.

Berdasarkan laporan, mithril medicine leaned more heavily on ai than azora does, and tasked anthropic’s ai assistant claude with helping to analyse data and suggesting next steps, as well as taming the piles of e-mails and paperwork that come from working with multiple contract research organizations. (Tranbarger, who has worked for Anthropic since Mithril was absorbed into it, declined to speak to Nature, as did Anthropic. “What began as an exercise in staying lean evolved into the thesis for an entirely new operating model, which we now call Pipeline-in-a-Person,” wrote Cody Tranbarger, Mithril’s former chief executive and lone employee, on LinkedIn. ).

#511. Move over BMI: new obesity definition is better for predicting your health

📅 13 Nov 2026

Move over BMI: new obesity definition is better for predicting your health

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03636-5

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. com. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Mariana Lenharo is a reporter for Nature in New York City.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a study suggests that people are being misdiagnosed as having obesity with a metric known as the body mass index (bmi). Credit: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP/Getty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, clinicians have debated for years whether body mass index (bmi) — a metric derived from a person’s height and weight — is the best way to define and diagnose obesity. Now, an approach that measures waist circumference and focuses more closely on excess body fat has proved to be better than BMI at predicting a person’s risk of death.

New obesity definition sidelines BMI to focus on health.

New obesity definition sidelines BMI to focus on health.

Diungkapkan bahwa an analysis of data collected from more than 800,000 individuals found that using bmi to diagnose obesity failed to identify a considerable proportion of people with elevated health risks caused by excess body fat. The study was published today in Nature1.

Diungkapkan bahwa physicians know that bmi — calculated by dividing a person’s weight by the square of their height — doesn’t accurately reflect body composition. For example, a muscular person might have an elevated BMI but have little body fat. The latest study “reinforces that BMI is not a good measure of obesity at the individual level and is not good in terms of predicting who is going to develop cardiometabolic disease in the long term”, says Cátia Martins, an obesity researcher at the University of Alabama at Birmingham.

But given how simple it is to calculate BMI, it remains the most widely used tool to classify obesity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a person is usually diagnosed with obesity if they have a bmi of 30 or higher. The approach presented in the study — called the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, or CAD-obesity — goes beyond BMI, combining it with measures, such as waist circumference, that are linked to excess body fat. Physicians know that when fat tissue is preferentially stored in the abdominal area, it is associated with more negative health consequences than when it’s stored elsewhere, Martins says.

Why BMI is flawed — and how to redefine obesity.

Why BMI is flawed — and how to redefine obesity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, under the cad-obesity system2, first proposed last year, people with obesity who also have at least one of 18 specific health problems — including heart failure and sleep apnoea — are classified as having ‘clinical obesity’. This indicates that excess fat is harming their organs and tissues. Those with obesity but none of these health problems are classified as having ‘preclinical obesity’, in which a person has excess fat but their organs are functioning normally.

“We did not know until now whether or not this new framework had implications in the real world and a prognostic value,” says Francesco Rubino, a weight-loss surgeon at King’s College London who led the effort to create the system and is a co-author of the Nature paper.

Diungkapkan bahwa but rubino and his colleagues proved the system’s worth by examining medical records from four large groups of people in china, spain, the united kingdom and the united states. They used data from three of those cohorts, in which more than 50,000 deaths occurred over up to 15 years, to determine whether BMI or the CAD-obesity system was a better indicator of elevated mortality risk.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for decades, scientists thought of the blood–brain barrier as an impenetrable layer. Over time that view has changed, as researchers realized the barrier was more permeable than first thought. Now, a team have catalogued almost 100 proteins that can pass through it to maintain brain health1.

The team also found that the transport of some of these crucial proteins breaks down in mice with brain diseases that mimic early-stage Alzheimer’s disease.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the paradigm in the field has been that the blood–brain barrier is normally impermeable and then becomes leaky as a result of alzheimer’s disease,” says study co-author andrew yang, a neuroscientist at gladstone institute of neurological disease in san francisco, california. Instead, his team’s work suggests that the blood–brain barrier actively imports proteins that the brain needs to function and the loss of these proteins drives the dysfunction seen early in the disease, he adds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yang and his colleagues developed a technique to label a large array of proteins in the blood and track those that can enter the brain. Of the 861 proteins they mapped, 92 crossed the blood–brain barrier into the brain. Most of these proteins were produced in distant organs, particularly the liver.

Berdasarkan laporan, the team focused on apolipoprotein a1 (apoa1), which has been linked to potential protective effects against alzheimer’s disease2. Once inside the brain, APOA1 stimulates brain cells called astrocytes to release cholesterol, which is important for maintaining the synapses through which neurons communicate. But how the protein crossed the blood–brain barrier has been unclear until now, says Yang.

Berdasarkan laporan, his team found that two receptors for apoa1 — sr-b1 and abca1 — are present on the blood–brain barrier as well as astrocytes. This suggests how the protein moves from the blood–brain barrier to the specific brain cells that need them, the authors say.

When Yang’s team blocked the ABCA1 receptor in laboratory-grown astrocytes, the protein no longer had the same cholesterol-regulating effects.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists have long known that the blood–brain barrier breaks down as alzheimer’s advances, letting harmful molecules leak into the brain. Yang’s team found that a different problem emerges first.

Diungkapkan bahwa using their labelling technique in a mouse model of alzheimer’s disease, the researchers found that the blood–brain barrier stopped importing protective proteins such as apoa1 into the brain before the barrier began to break down. This disruption to the protein transport was accompanied by a loss of neuronal connections, behavioural changes and other early hallmarks of the disease.

Diungkapkan bahwa yang and the team wondered whether increasing the supply of apoa1 in the blood might help to counter some of the damage caused by alzheimer’s disease. When more APOA1 crossed the blood–brain barrier and entered the brain, the mice showed fewer Alzheimer’s-disease-related markers. To find out, the team engineered mice with Alzheimer’s to produce extra APOA1 in the liver. For example, they had reduced fat build-up in astrocytes and lower levels of inflammatory molecules.

#513. AI’s energy paradox: will the AI boom strain energy systems or be the source of solutions?

AI’s energy paradox: will the AI boom strain energy systems or be the source of solutions?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03412-5

Berdasarkan laporan, thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Melissa Hobson is a freelance marine-science journalist based in Hastings, UK.

Ginelle Greene-Dewasmes is working to make AI energy use more sustainable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, artificial intelligence is exploding in popularity, and many people have concerns about the sustainability of its energy consumption. Energy use by US data-centre servers more than tripled between 2014 and 2023 — reaching 4. 4% of the nation’s total electricity consumption. AI models need vast amounts of electricity: according to the International Energy Agency, a typical AI data centre can consume as much energy as 100,000 households each year. This figure is expected to at least double by 20281.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, ai might also hold the key to improving energy efficiency: offsetting some of the demand it creates. An article published by the World Economic Forum suggests that the use of AI tools across industries — in automating tasks or monitoring real-time energy use, for example — can reduce energy consumption by up to 60%. Ginelle Greene-Dewasmes, a sustainable-development specialist and an author of the article, has been working to lower AI’s energy demands while finding ways to use the tools to reduce wider emissions.

Diungkapkan bahwa originally from trinidad, greene-dewasmes became interested in solving energy-security issues for island states with few resources. Now based in Geneva, Switzerland, Greene-Dewasmes has been the Forum’s AI and Energy Lead since 2024. In 2021, she completed a PhD on the green-energy transition across small island developing states at the University of York, UK, before joining the World Economic Forum in 2022. Her work involves bringing together AI and energy leaders from around the world to identify shared challenges, align priorities and develop practical actions that can improve AI’s energy impact.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as well as looking at improving ai’s energy efficiency, greene-dewasmes and partners are exploring how models can find innovations that improve existing energy infrastructure, such as that in buildings that are already in use. Nature spoke to her about navigating the increasing energy needs of the technology and whether its benefits could outweigh this demand.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ai needs cloud networks, chips, graphics-processing units and cooling systems, all of which consume large amounts of energy. 5 billion queries daily. ChatGPT, the chatbot from technology firm OpenAI in San Francisco, California, has more than 800 million users each month and receives more than 2. Developing and training models requires high levels of processing power to crunch the data, but AI use is much more energy intensive overall because of the scale. As AI becomes mainstream, we need to build more energy infrastructure to keep up with the surge in demand.

Diungkapkan bahwa but, when it comes to scaling up ai, i think the conversation is too skewed towards the energy needed to power centralized infrastructure, when there are lots of other things that will contribute to ai’s energy requirements. Large data centres will exist in only the few countries that have the money, space and resources to host them. For most of the world, AI infrastructure will be disaggregated and decentralized. For example, if one million people are using their phones more intensively because of AI, that affects the energy infrastructure.

Berdasarkan laporan, although more complex llm queries are currently directed to remote data centres, some smaller tasks can be completed directly on new devices that have ai chips. As this becomes more common, what will that mean for infrastructure planning for energy? It’s much harder to measure this than the outputs from one data centre.

Diungkapkan bahwa ai’s electricity impact is currently about 0. The World Economic Forum, in collaboration with other specialists, has created a Net-Positive AI Energy Framework. 49% of total global electricity use — so it’s still fairly small, although it’s growing. It looks at how we can design AI models and infrastructure for efficiency — by optimizing chips, data-centre locations and liquid cooling, in which fluids are used for cooling owing to their high heat capacity — while using AI to bring down energy usage in high-impact sectors, such as transportation and urbanization, both by improving the efficiency of systems and coming up with solutions to global challenges.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for example, in azerbaijan, operations that keep buildings running, including lighting, heating and cooling, account for a large proportion of the country’s carbon emissions. This includes AI solutions that adjust heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) on the basis of building occupancy and use trends, and that predict the need for maintenance before faults arise. The Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution Azerbaijan (a public legal entity) is using AI-powered solutions to improve efficiencies as part of its nationally determined contribution commitments — the country’s pledge to reduce emissions. In some cases, this use of AI to hone efficiency has brought down HVAC energy use by 25% and emissions by up to 40%.

Berdasarkan laporan, we’re also encouraging people to use ai wisely. We want AI to reduce energy consumption overall, rather than adding strain to systems.

Berdasarkan laporan, the aim is to gather insights from leading voices in the ai ecosystem to generate thought leadership and encourage cross-discipline learning so people aren’t working in silos. We convened a community of about 40 people, which has increased to around 70 in nine industries around the world and is still growing. We try to hear from lots of voices: university academics, public-sector entities and technology, AI and energy companies (including renewables and nuclear) are all involved. It started off as one-on-one conversations with professionals working with AI, centred on the technology’s biggest challenges and opportunities. Together with our partners, we turn these insights into guidance and frameworks that can support the wider industry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’ve published two reports based on the learnings gleaned from these thought leaders. The Net-Positive AI Energy Framework is our North Star for clean, efficient and equitable AI. Artificial Intelligence Energy Paradox explores how to balance the challenges and opportunities of AI and energy. We’re now working on an AI Energy Readiness Compass: a methodology to support responsible AI energy developments and identify the causes of upcoming bottlenecks in the power grid that could be problematic for AI energy use.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one particular success from these collaborations is the willingness of hyperscalers — large organizations that operate cloud computing services and data centres — to embrace grid flexibility. At first, they were reluctant to adjust when they draw power because they wanted continuous access to reliable electricity, but they have come to see the benefits of balancing demand on the grid. As a result, they have embraced power flexibility, and 18 partners supported the launch of the AI Energy Management Alliance: a coalition of companies that promotes dynamic load-shifting (changing when energy is used to align with grid loads, the availability of green energy and the best pricing).

#514. Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

📅 13 Nov 2026

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03624-9

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Dyani Lewis is a freelance journalist in Melbourne, Australia.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in august 1987, a scandal erupted over work on the world’s highest mountain range. John Talent, a palaeontologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, announced he had found numerous anomalies in research charting the geology of the Himalayas. All of the problems were in papers by Vishwa Jit Gupta, one of India’s most celebrated palaeontologists at the time.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

Berdasarkan laporan, gupta was outraged. But further investigations over the following seven years revealed the scale and brazenness of his fraud. Littered through more than 450 publications were maps of collection sites that didn’t exist, plagiarized images and specimens stolen from collections that Gupta had visited. More than 100 experts had been duped into co-authoring descriptions of fossils Gupta claimed he had collected from specific Himalayan geological formations, but instead hailed from North America and Morocco.

“It destroyed the image of Indian science,” says retired geologist Ghulam Bhat, who completed his PhD on Himalayan geology in the same year that the allegations of fraud emerged.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gupta died in 2022, and many geologists know to steer clear of his work. When Nature contacted Bhat, who is now editor-in-chief of the Journal of the Geological Society of India (JGSI), he was unaware that Gupta’s papers were not marked as retracted. That’s despite the JGSI’s 1991 evaluation of 19 of Gupta’s papers that it published1, which concluded that “the fossil finds of V. J. But awareness of the problem is fading, and none of Gupta’s papers have been retracted. Gupta are not reliable [. ] the data is incomplete bordering on disinformation”.

Diungkapkan bahwa much of gupta’s work is inaccessible, having been published in now-defunct periodicals or in volumes that, although digitized online, have not been indexed in reference bibliometric databases such as scopus, web of science and dimensions. Despite this, Gupta’s falsehoods are now being propagated outside specialist circles, as his old journal articles are being surfaced through artificial-intelligence tools that summarize search results. When someone searches for geological landmarks in the Himalayas, such as the Tandi Limestone, Google’s AI overview obliges with direct links to Gupta’s discredited papers.

Diungkapkan bahwa bhat now plans to rectify the digital record and says that all other journals that have published gupta’s work should do the same. But he added that in general, when investigations of old papers are hampered by limited available information, an editorial expression of concern “is likely to be our preferred mechanism for alerting readers to potential issues”. (Nature’s news team is editorially independent of its publisher, Springer Nature. “If this problem is left as it is, unattended, it will pollute all of the geological literature in future,” he says. Gupta also published papers in Nature in the 1960s; Chris Graf, director of research integrity at Springer Nature, didn’t confirm that the journal would re-examine them. ).

The Himalayas case raises a wider issue: how to deal with fraudulent, unethical or even merely incorrect research from decades ago, especially in an era in which much old work is digitized and AI systems can pick up studies that might previously have been neglected.

There are many skeletons in science’s closet, but publishers can be reluctant to judge science of the past by today’s standards, and can find it more difficult to issue retractions when authors are dead, original records cannot be consulted or journals are no longer in print.

And as publishers struggle to deal with the fallout from rising research fraud and AI slop, finite resources can also mean that many old papers with known flaws are left as they are.

Gráinne McNamara, a council member of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in Eastleigh, UK, which advises journals on best practice, says that journals are increasingly contacting COPE to ask for advice about dealing with concerns on very old papers.

“Everybody is looking for what’s the best, most responsible way to handle these,” she says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the widespread use of retractions as a mechanism for maintaining integrity in the scientific record is a relatively recent phenomenon. The JGSI evaluation report about Gupta served as a warning notice to the community at the time, but didn’t use the word retraction. Now, a journal should issue a retraction notice, and leave the original paper intact, but with a modified title and a stamp or watermark indicating that it has been retracted. It also pre-dates the modern standardization of retraction processes, which happened in the 2000s. The information should then feed through to bibliographic databases.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the early 2000s, only around 30 retraction notices were published each year, and cope first developed guidelines to standardize the retraction process in 2004. The number — and rate — of retractions has exploded since then, with more than 10,000 recorded in 2023 alone.

Berdasarkan laporan, digitization of old records, combined with a wider propensity to retract flawed work, has seen journals reaching farther back in time to retract studies — and this has led to some startlingly long gaps between when an article was published and when it was formally retracted. Retraction Watch, an initiative that curates a database of more than 70,000 retractions and expressions of concern (a notice that highlights potential issues with a publication), has reported that the longest gap is 80 years. That’s for a prank case report published in 1923 in the Dutch medical journal Nederlands Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde.

Diungkapkan bahwa it described a man who died from “piss cough”, an affliction that caused him to cough up liquid smelling of urine. Realizing it had never been retracted and that others did not know it was fake, he sought confirmation of the hoax, and found it in the autobiography of a retired University of Amsterdam physician, who had helped to cook up the nonsense case when he was a medical student. In 2003, an editor at the journal happened to look up the case, which he thought was widely known to be a hoax. Accompanying commentary on the journal’s website said that a retraction was appropriate now that the older literature had become accessible through digitization.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to nature’s analysis of retraction watch data — which capture a subset of total retractions — the number of old papers that are being retracted is rising. Overall, some 358 retraction notices and 120 expressions of concern have been issued for papers or book chapters that were more than 20 years old at the time of the editorial action (see ‘Retracting the past’). 2% before 2010. 7% of the total number, up from 0. This is still a rare phenomenon: since 2015, the oldest retractions represent some 0. But around 3% of expressions of concern have occurred for works older than 20 years. That illustrates how publishers might choose to issue expressions of concern for older papers, rather than retract, because it can be harder to investigate historical records.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2005, biochemist barry milborrow sought to retract five of his own papers, published between 1980 and 1982, on biochemical pathways that bacteria, algae and plants use to make pigments, because later work had disproved their findings. Another journal issued a correction, but no notice was issued by the publisher of the remaining two papers. The Biochemical Journal, which published Milborrow’s self-retraction listing the five articles2, retracted both articles it had published. Ian Swift, Milborrow’s co-author and PhD student at the University of New South Wales in Sydney, Australia, at the time, says he only found out about the retractions many years later, after Milborrow had passed away.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to cope guidance, journal editors can retract articles if they no longer have confidence in the results and conclusions reported in them. By that rubric, many older papers could, in theory, be retracted, but, being rarely cited, are usually left alone.

Diungkapkan bahwa even when invalid papers are still being cited, retraction might not follow. The seminal work marked the birth of palaeogenomics, a field that earned Pääbo a Nobel prize in 2022. But the mummy DNA was actually contamination from a modern handler, as Pääbo, now at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany, has openly acknowledged. “What is problematic is if false conclusions lead other scientists and the community as a whole astray,” he told Nature when asked for this article. In 1985, for instance, geneticist Svante Pääbo reported that he had cloned DNA from an Egyptian mummy3. “I don’t think anyone is currently misled by the mummy paper,” he says, which is why he argues that the work should stand, adding that to correct very old papers with errors “would create more confusion than clarity”.

Retractions can reshape scientists’ careers in unexpected ways.

Retractions can reshape scientists’ careers in unexpected ways.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in practice, old papers tend to be considered for retraction only if they have widespread integrity issues that journal editors feel shouldn’t be allowed to stand unmarked. A major trigger for mass retractions of older work is when investigations of an individual’s research cast doubt over their entire body of work. For instance, a 2019 investigation by King’s College London into the work of psychologist Hans Eysenck and his German collaborator Ronald Grossarth-Maticek has led to papers dating back to the 1940s being flagged — albeit many with expressions of concern rather than retractions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eysenck died in 1997 as one of the most celebrated psychologists of the twentieth century. An accompanying editorial called on King’s College London — where Eysenck worked from 1955 until 1983 — to conduct a formal investigation. But in 2019, psychiatrist Anthony Pelosi, who had critiqued Eysenck’s work to no effect in the 1990s, published a renewed analysis of the studies4. The investigation report, also published in 2019, concluded that 24 articles by Eysenck and Maticek published between 1988 and 2000 were ‘unsafe’ and recommended they be retracted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, those recommendations weren’t followed entirely. Only 16 of the 24 papers have been retracted, and another 4 have expressions of concern. Four remain unflagged. After sustained criticism over the narrow scope of the 2019 investigation, King’s College London published a statement in October 2025 saying that other publications based on the data set used in the 24 papers it examined are also likely to be ‘unsafe’ and should be flagged by journal editors — although it did not list affected publications.

So far, 94 of Eysenck’s hundreds of papers have been either retracted or tagged with an expression of concern, the oldest of which was published in 1943 (see ‘Longest gaps’).

Diungkapkan bahwa such inconsistencies in how publishers deal with research-integrity issues are common and don’t relate only to very old papers, says andrew grey, an endocrinologist and research-integrity specialist at the university of auckland in new zealand. He alerted publishers to concerns over large numbers of articles by Yoshihiro Sato, a Japanese bone-health researcher who fabricated data in dozens of clinical trials, and has reported seeing some journals respond with retractions or expressions of concern, whereas others take no action5.

Berdasarkan laporan, one famous scandal of the past — the 1980s discrediting of work by john darsee, a us biologist — has led to just 17 retractions. Although news reports at the time stated that more than 80 of Darsee’s papers had been retracted, this refers to editorial notes and warnings that, in parallel with the Gupta case, don’t appear in modern records as retractions.

Another trigger for retracting old work is when it attracts renewed attention, particularly in medical fields.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, each year, marcel van der heyden, a physiologist at the university medical center utrecht in the netherlands, asks his final-year students to write a review article about a poison or toxin. In 2025, he chose caesium salts, and his students uncovered 20 case reports of people ingesting the toxic chemical6. Often, the individuals deliberately consumed the compound as an alternative treatment for cancer. Although the US Food and Drug Administration cautioned against its use in 2018, the deadly ‘therapy’ is still promoted in books and online by some wellness centres.

Berdasarkan laporan, the treatment traces back to two papers published in 1984 in pharmacology biochemistry and behavior. And in 2010, an inquest into the deaths of five people in Australia found that he had been treating patients remotely from Thailand. Sartori subsequently had his medical licence revoked in several US states in the 1980s and was sentenced to prison in Virginia in 1999 for practising medicine without a licence. One of the papers was written by Austrian-born Hellfried Sartori, who had been prosecuted in Maryland in 1982 for fraud relating to using the unproven cancer treatment. That case ended in a mistrial. Many more of his patients had also died under his treatment, the court heard.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the other paper promoting caesium therapy was by wisconsin-based aubrey keith brewer. Brewer died in 1986, but his namesake Brewer International Science Library continues to distribute information on caesium and other alternative therapies with a disclaimer that the protocols are “for information purposes only”, and that people should consult their physician if unwell. Nature contacted the website but received no response.

Sebagaimana diketahui, van der heyden contacted pharmacology biochemistry and behavior in august 2025, suggesting an expression of concern could be warranted. But the research-integrity team at the journal’s publisher, Elsevier, decided in January this year to remove the two papers, soon after Van der Heyden informed them that his review had been accepted for publication and that his university was poised to issue a press release about it. “Without the original data, it’s hard to tell whether there is a mistake made, or whether it’s on purpose,” he says. The papers were deleted entirely this April, as Retraction Watch reported.

The move to scrub a paper, rather than merely retract and leave it in place, can be taken if the contents could present a serious health risk to the public, according to COPE guidelines.

#515. Author or just ‘acknowledged’? How women are not gaining full credit for research

📅 13 Nov 2026

Author or just ‘acknowledged’? How women are not gaining full credit for research

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03448-7

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Anna Napolitano is a freelance journalist in London.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the number of men with high citation counts exceeds that of women. Credit: FotografiaBasica/iStock via Getty.

Berdasarkan laporan, women are more frequently mentioned in the acknowledgements section of papers than credited as co-authors, especially for research and analytical work, a study has found. But status seems to trump gender.

An analysis of more than 20,000 authors and 60,000 acknowledged contributors on papers published in seven PLOS journals between 2016 and 2021 highlighted persistent disparities between women and men in who gets authorship over an acknowledgement.

Diungkapkan bahwa the study, published in scientometrics1, also found that highly cited researchers — used by the authors as a proxy for higher status — were more likely to receive authorship over acknowledgement than were their less-cited collaborators, irrespective of gender. When a highly cited woman collaborated with a less-cited man, for example, the woman was more likely to be credited as an author.

Berdasarkan laporan, authorship is one of the most important metrics in research evaluation, grant reviews and promotion decisions, whereas acknowledgements aren’t typically factored in. One famous example is chemist Rosalind Franklin, a key contributor to the discovery of the DNA double helix. The difference between getting authorship credit versus an acknowledgement can make or break a researcher’s career. Franklin was mentioned in the acknowledgements section of the 1953 paper describing the finding, which went on to win the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, rather than being named a co-author with James Watson and Francis Crick.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the scientometrics study highlights the importance of status in determining who gets credit, and the uphill battle that many women in research have to face — especially in their early and mid-careers. The number of highly cited men exceeded that of women, suggesting that even if women benefit from high status once they have attained it, fewer women attain higher status in the first place.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we realized that the issue is double. One linked with gender bias, but another surprisingly due to hierarchy bias,” says Yukie Sano, a computational scientist at the University of Tsukuba in Japan, who co-authored the paper.

The impact of a researcher’s status and gender on academic credit is well-documented, but Sano and her co-authors point to the Contributor Role Taxonomy (CRediT) — a standardized system describing specific roles that individual scientists often take on during research — as a game-changer by providing high-quality data to track this metric across journals and disciplines.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sano and her colleagues used credit data from open-access plos journals (which implemented the system in 2016) to track the contributions of authors and devised a separate system to track contributions in the acknowledgements section. Author gender was determined using Gender API, an artificial-intelligence-powered service that infers a person’s gender on the basis of their name.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the team found that men were generally more likely than women to receive authorship credit — particularly in investigation roles (performing the experiments) and analysis roles (analysing or synthesizing the study data). Around 70% of men were credited as authors, compared with about 65% of women.

The size of the gender gap varied between disciplines, but was particularly evident in medicine, biology and computer science, whereas environmental science showed little evidence of a gender difference in authorship versus acknowledgement rates.

#516. Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers

📅 13 Nov 2026

Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03641-8

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Mariana Lenharo is a reporter for Nature in New York City.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists are engineering bacteria that can provide nitrogen, an essential ingredient for plant growth, to wheat crops. Credit: Shakeel Ahmed/Anadolu Agency/Getty.

Berdasarkan laporan, the world’s farms depend on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers to increase crop yields, but the production and use of these chemicals generates billions of tonnes of greenhouse-gas emissions every year. Now, scientists are making progress on a greener alternative: bioengineered bacteria.

Berdasarkan laporan, this approach takes a cue from natural bacteria that ‘fix’ nitrogen into a useful form and provide it to certain plants. Scientists are engineering genetic features into bacteria with the aim of enabling them to fix nitrogen for important food crops, such as maize (corn) and wheat, that don’t have such natural microbial partners.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a comment published on 10 november in nature biotechnology1, researchers suggest that bioengineered bacteria could eventually replace up to half of synthetic fertilizers. The bacteria deliver nitrogen more efficiently to roots than synthetic fertilizers do, which could reduce greenhouse-gas emissions and nitrogen pollution of waterways. But this would require a slew of advances, from getting different microbial species to work together to more-rigorous field trials.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, how crispr could yield the next blockbuster cropsome of these ‘biofertilizers’ have been augmented with genes and genetic snippets from viruses or distantly related bacteria. The bacteria are now being trialled on small plots of maize on farms in the Midwestern United States. This means that the engineered microbes are classified as transgenic — altered to include DNA from other species. The bacteria, developed by Switch Bioworks in San Carlos, California, are the first example of a transgenic biofertilizer approved for testing on fields in the country.

How CRISPR could yield the next blockbuster crop.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in september, switch bioworks received approval from the brazilian regulatory agency, the national technical commission on biosafety (cntbio), to test its strains there. This is the first time that a transgenic bacterium of any kind has been approved for field tests in Brazil, says molecular biologist Mario Murakami, who is the president of CTNBio in Campinas.

Berdasarkan laporan, companies that have focused on editing bacterial genes rather than producing transgenic microbes are further along. Pivot Bio in Minneapolis, Minnesota, has applied its gene-edited biofertilizers to tens of millions of hectares of US farmland over the past decade, says the company’s chief technology officer Travis Frey. Some of Pivot Bio’s products have also been tested in Canada, Argentina, Kenya and Brazil.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, most plants can’t use the form of nitrogen that is present in the air. Some crops, including soya beans and peanuts, host colonies of bacteria that can convert atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form. The plant takes up that nitrogen and, in return, provides carbon that fuels bacterial growth. But most staple crops lack these microbial partners, leading farmers to rely on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers. These chemical fertilizers account for 5% of global greenhouse-gas emissions, and drive damaging nutrient pollution in waterways.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for decades, researchers have tried to get bacteria to fix nitrogen for staple crops. “It doesn’t work,” says Jean-Michel Ané, a bioengineer at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, who is working on microbial fertilizers. Until recently, the approach was to collect wild strains of nitrogen-fixing bacteria from soil and apply them to seeds or spray them onto plants. The wild microbes fail to thrive when applied to crops that don’t provide them with carbon.

#519. Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?

📅 13 Nov 2026

Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03409-0

Diungkapkan bahwa thank you for visiting nature. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nic Fleming is a science writer in Bristol, UK.

Berdasarkan laporan, container ships were forced to dock at ports in the united arab emirates and other middle eastern nations after the iranian government announced that it would close the strait of hormuz in july. Credit: AFP via Getty Images.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, protesters burnt tyres and blocked roads in syria over fuel prices. French fishers blockaded a fuel depot and clashed with police. Government and household budgets were squeezed around the world as interest rates rose and the sales of electric vehicles roughly doubled year-on-year in several countries, including Australia, Brazil and India.

Berdasarkan laporan, these were just some of the many knock-on effects of the us and israeli airstrikes on iran that began in february. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 25% of the world’s oil trade and 20% of exported liquefied natural gas previously passed, caused what the International Energy Agency (IEA) called “the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market”, as fuel prices spiked worldwide.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the resulting strain has exacerbated the economic pressures already felt from previous shocks, including the russia–ukraine war, the covid-19 pandemic and the 2008 global financial crash, as well as from the continuing effects of climate change. The current global energy-security picture is “really bad on all fronts”, says Dan Marks, an energy-security researcher at the Royal United Services Institute, a think tank based in London. “It’s something of a perfect storm. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, governments seeking to improve national energy security are taking a variety of approaches — from measures to reduce demand and increase electrification to infrastructure updates and incentive programmes to encourage renewable-energy investment. Researchers, meanwhile, are doing their bit, driving scientific and technological advances that have the potential to deliver a stable and sustainable future energy mix.

Diungkapkan bahwa human energy consumption is both growing and changing (see ‘powering the planet’). Over that period, consumption increased from around 85,000 terawatt hours (TWh) annually to 178,000 TWh. Use of global primary energy — naturally occurring energy sources that have not undergone any processing by humans — more than doubled between 1980 and 2025. That’s approximately 71 times the yearly primary-energy consumption of France.

Sebagaimana diketahui, electrification — the replacement of technologies that burn fossil fuels with alternatives powered by electricity — is advancing in many countries as various industries look into switching to renewables. Worldwide, electricity demand is predicted to increase by around 40% by 2035, compared with current levels (see ‘The road ahead’). One-quarter of extracted natural gas is used to heat industrial buildings, and around 21% is used for heating and cooking in homes worldwide. Close to 99% of aviation and more than 90% of shipping relies on fossil fuels, for example. Most of the rest (40%) is used to generate electricity. Despite this, many industries are still reliant on fossil fuels. Although the share of primary energy generated by renewables is growing, oil, coal and gas still account for about 80% of energy production.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the iea defines energy security as reliable, affordable access to all fuels and energy sources. The impacts of global shocks to fuel supplies and prices also vary according to how reliant countries are on imported fossil fuels. Marks and others highlight that priorities vary internationally, with reliability often seen as of primary importance in high-income countries and affordability taking precedence in low-income nations. “There isn’t one global energy-security picture, but many different context-dependent pictures,” says Severin Borenstein, an energy economist at the University of California, Berkeley.

Berdasarkan laporan, economies that rely on imported oil products are particularly vulnerable to the current shocks. The World Food Programme, part of the United Nations, estimated in March that the US–Iran war could push an extra 45 million people into acute hunger, taking this year’s total to 363 million, as increasing oil and gas costs push up the prices of fuel, food and other crucial products such as fertilizer. “If, like in a lot of African countries, people are dependent on travelling long distances in vehicles and on other imported oil products, large oil-price increases can be existentially problematic,” says Marks. Some high-income nations have also been hit hard. In Japan — which was importing more than 90% of its crude oil from the Middle East before the conflict — household electricity bills have risen to their highest levels in three years, and government borrowing costs have risen to a 30-year high.

Diungkapkan bahwa by contrast, nations with domestic fuel supplies have been partially insulated. “There are price and macro-economic issues. “In most developed free-market economies, there isn’t an energy-security issue in the sense of availability,” says Borenstein. Although car users in the United States have seen big fuel-price increases, the country’s ample supplies of natural gas have shielded the nation from severe economic hardships. Some countries, like the United States, are better protected than others. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, global oil prices have jumped since the us–iran war broke out. During the Yom Kippur War, coordinated action by oil-producing countries caused prices to more than triple between October 1973 and January 1974. Brent Crude futures contracts, a global oil-price benchmark, hit US$126 a barrel in April — up from around $70 before the conflict. This has affected consumers and businesses, but not as much as some previous energy crises. And oil prices more than doubled after the 1978–79 Iranian revolution.

Diungkapkan bahwa many economists think that the global economy is better placed to avoid the soaring inflation, unemployment and recessions seen in many industrialized nations after the 1973 and 1979 oil shocks. And the IEA, established after the 1973 oil crisis, also requires its 32 member countries to keep reserves of at least 90 days’ worth of crude oil to guard against supply shocks. The ‘oil intensity’ of the global economy, that is, how much oil is needed to generate a unit of gross domestic product (GDP) in the form of goods and services, has fallen by more than 50% since the 1970s. “For most of the developed world, it’s a big inconvenience, and, for some, a substantial budget squeeze, but it’s not the complete disruption of the economy seen in the 1970s,” says Borenstein.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but economic and energy-security challenges are also expected to grow owing to climate change. Droughts are becoming more frequent and severe, resulting in big reductions in hydropower generation in nations such as China, Brazil, the United States, Spain and Zambia. Low water levels in rivers, including the Rhine and Danube in Europe, the Amazon in South America and the Yangtze in China, have caused freight delivery problems. The other effects of climate change include reduced wind-energy generation and increased demand for power to run air-conditioning units.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, governments, policymakers and others who are working to tackle energy-security challenges have various options. Reducing energy demand, especially for oil and gas, by electrifying industrial processes and home heating, for example, helps with these issues, especially in nations that are heavily reliant on imported fossil fuels. Managing demand volatility through improved energy storage and ensuring that power grids can transition towards greater energy generation from renewables are also part of the picture, Marks says.

Berdasarkan laporan, although governments and business leaders have parts to play in energy-demand management, electrification and infrastructure investments, researchers are driving scientific and technical innovations that support energy security. Tapping underground heat to produce geothermal energy, for example, emits only small amounts of greenhouse gases and can be used to generate electricity or to heat buildings. However, at present, geothermal energy produces less than 1% of electricity globally because few locations have the right combination of accessible underground heat, water and permeable rock.

That could change thanks to advances in enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), in which underground fractures are expanded or created in hot areas, and then fluids are pumped down, heated up and transferred back to the surface, usually to drive turbines and generate electricity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, russia has been experiencing a fuel crisis since mid-june caused by increased ukrainian drone attacks on oil refineries. Credit: Contributor/Getty Images News.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there have been small-scale egs research operations since the 1970s, but drilling times and costs have fallen substantially in the decades since thanks to techniques adapted from the oil and gas industries. These include the fracturing of rock with pressurized fluids, known as fracking, horizontal drilling to increase the exposure of fluid to heat reservoirs and the use of tougher, faster polycrystalline diamond compact drill bits. “It’s hard to overestimate how much of a game changer the new techniques have been,” says Roland Horne, a geothermal-energy engineer at Stanford University in California.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these innovations are driving investments in large commercial plants. One of the biggest of these is the Cape Station project operated by Fervo Energy near Milford in Utah, which began delivering power in September and plans to build the capacity to generate 500 megawatts (MW) by 2028 — enough electricity to power around 500,000 US homes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, there are obstacles to overcome. A number of EGS projects have been halted owing to earthquakes that geologists linked to increased underground forces generated by the EGS process. Lessons have been learnt from this and other incidents. 5 earthquake that injured 90 people was probably triggered by hydraulic fracturing at an EGS plant in Pohang, South Korea, in 2017. A magnitude-5. For example, EGS developers are deploying networks of sensors to better predict seismic risks and using multistage stimulation. This involves the use of pressurised fluids or chemical agents to fracture rock sequentially and more gently at several points rather than at fewer locations.

Diungkapkan bahwa horne says that he expects the levelized cost of electricity — the average cost of generating a unit of electricity across a power plant’s lifetime — for egs to drop to a commercially competitive $80 per megawatt hour (mwh) by 2027. The IEA says that this could drop to $50 by 2035 and that geothermal energy could generate 8% of global electricity supplies by 2050.

Diungkapkan bahwa efforts to develop more efficient solar cells could also help countries to improve their energy security by increasing sustainable domestic electricity supplies. In 2025, 9% of the world’s electricity came from solar, up from 3% in 2020. Today’s solar cells are mostly silicon-based and can typically convert light into electricity with efficiencies of around 20–24%.

Diungkapkan bahwa a worker inspects newly installed solar panels at the fuendetodos ii solar park near zaragoza, spain. Credit: Angel Garcia/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when sunlight hits a solar, or photovoltaic, cell, electrons inside the semiconductor material that it is made from are knocked loose, creating an electrical imbalance that produces a voltage and generates electricity. Researchers are now developing next-generation solar cells that use metal halide perovskites, a family of crystalline compounds with high light absorption and charge-transport capabilities.

#520. Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart

Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11204-0

Diungkapkan bahwa disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because dna synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative cmg (cdc45–mcm–gins) helicase1,2. Ablating the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment4. In human cells, the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress7,8,9,10, but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability3,4,5,6. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

Berdasarkan laporan, dna lesion bypass by leading-strand repriming was demonstrated for the core escherichia coli replisome, in which primer synthesis is performed by the primase also responsible for lagging-strand replication12,13. By contrast, eukaryotic replisomes reconstituted from purified Saccharomyces cerevisiae proteins cannot efficiently resume synthesis downstream of leading-strand lesions1 because the Pol α–primase complex that is responsible for priming each Okazaki fragment is targeted to the lagging-strand template14. This targeting mechanism is conserved in the human replisome14, indicating that inefficient priming on the leading strand by Pol α–primase is a universal feature of eukaryotic replisomes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unlike s. PRIMPOL is a 560-amino-acid (aa) monomeric enzyme comprising a 21-aa amino-terminal helix of unknown function, an archaeo-eukaryotic primase (AEP) domain, a single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) binding zinc-finger (ZnF) and two C-terminal replication protein A (RPA) binding motifs (RBMs)6,15. cerevisiae, humans have an additional primase called PRIMPOL7,8,9. Extensive evidence from human, mouse and chicken cell lines shows that PRIMPOL promotes replication fork progression under conditions that stall replicative DNA polymerases8,9,10 and that this requires PRIMPOL primase activity10,16,17,18, leading to the formation of daughter-strand gaps5,19. Current models indicate that PRIMPOL is recruited to replication forks through a direct interaction with RPA9,11,16. However, because RPA is constitutively associated with the lagging-strand template, it is unclear whether this mode of recruitment is sufficient for efficient PRIMPOL priming on the leading strand, or whether an additional mechanism directs PRIMPOL specifically to the leading-strand template to rescue stalled replication forks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the basis of our results and previous work, we propose the following model for replication fork restart by primpol-dependent repriming (fig. Our biochemical reconstitution has demonstrated that the PRIMPOL RBMs are not essential for leading-strand repriming in vitro. To accommodate these observations, we propose that the interaction of PRIMPOL with RPA, which is low affinity11 and therefore likely to be transient, serves primarily to localize PRIMPOL to actively replicating genomic loci, which may be necessary because PRIMPOL is a relatively low abundance protein in human cells15,30 (Fig. 6a).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on encountering a dna lesion, leading-strand synthesis by pol ε is blocked, but cmg continues to translocate along the template at a greatly reduced rate1,2, exposing ssdna on the leading-strand template between the helicase and polymerase (fig. Alternatively, Pol δ might facilitate the recoupling of leading-strand synthesis by extending the primer made by PRIMPOL until it reaches CMG, at which point the 3′ end is transferred to Pol ε. The anchoring of PRIMPOL on CMG suggests a pathway in which the primer might be handed off directly to the leading-strand PCNA loader CTF18-RFC and then to Pol ε. Through its interactions with MCM4 and MCM7, PRIMPOL is positioned to capture the exposed ssDNA to initiate leading-strand repriming (Fig. 6a). 6a, pathway (i)). After primer synthesis, Pol ε must reengage the leading strand for optimal fork progression to resume. This pathway has been observed following leading-strand lesion bypass by TLS in the yeast replisome31.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the direct interaction of primpol with cmg raises the possibility that primpol could travel with cmg to facilitate its immediate deployment on helicase–polymerase uncoupling (fig. 6a, pathway (ii)). In this regard, it is noteworthy that PRIMPOL does not clash with any known core replisome protein, including Pol ε (Fig. 6b). However, because the MCM4 and MCM7 ATPase domains undergo conformational changes during CMG translocation that could affect PRIMPOL binding, single-molecule studies will be required to determine if PRIMPOL can stably associate with moving replisomes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the mechanism of primpol recruitment via mcm4 and mcm7 ensures that repriming is tightly coupled to cmg progression to limit the size of the ssdna gap that is left for post-replicative repair pathways. Based on prior studies, this sequence is short and somewhat degenerate25, which should enable efficient repriming at most genomic loci. Our work further establishes that PRIMPOL displays a sequence preference for primer synthesis. However, regions of the genome devoid of optimal priming sites are likely to exist, for example in repetitive DNA, which could limit repriming and bias fork restart and stabilisation towards alternative pathways.

Berdasarkan laporan, the two-stage model for primpol recruitment involving both rpa and cmg interactions is analogous to a mechanism proposed for the recruitment of tls polymerases to the replication fork32. This mechanism has been observed in the E. coli replisome for the TLS polymerase PolIV, where an interaction with the single-stranded DNA-binding protein SSB concentrates PolIV at the fork to promote its interaction with the sliding clamp β33. We also note that RPA will accumulate on the leading-strand template during prolonged uncoupling, which should enhance PRIMPOL recruitment to stressed replication forks.

Berdasarkan laporan, apart from its low abundance, primpol activity is regulated by checkpoint and cell cycle kinases6,34,35,36, suggesting that excessive repriming and daughter-strand gap formation is deleterious. Consistent with this idea, addition of PRIMPOL mildly slowed fork progression on an undamaged template, and this effect was exacerbated by omission of CTF18-RFC, which compromises PCNA loading on the leading strand (Extended Data Fig. We reasoned that this could be a consequence of PRIMPOL being directed to the leading strand by CMG, causing it to interfere with Pol ε by competing for the nascent leading strand. 7a). Tight regulation of PRIMPOL might also indicate a capacity of the enzyme to interfere with normal replisome function. Importantly, this inhibition was dependent on the interaction of PRIMPOL with CMG but not on primase activity (Extended Data Fig. 7b).

Diungkapkan bahwa the widespread phylogenetic distribution of primpol37, and the conservation of its cmg interaction motifs, indicates an evolutionary pressure to keep replication forks moving by repriming. This raises the possibility that leading-strand synthesis might be considerably more discontinuous in human cells than previously appreciated. It is also interesting to consider that PRIMPOL could access the leading strand for priming potentially in any instance where synthesis is paused, for example during PCNA loading on the leading strand by CTF18-RFC. It also indicates that in the absence of chronic replication stress, repriming might be the default response of the replisome to impediments to leading-strand synthesis. This is possibly a frequent occurrence because PCNA abundance is reported to be similar on leading and lagging strands in yeast38.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, multiple pathways collaborate to protect and restart stalled replication forks during replication stress. Ablating replication fork reversal factors has been found to promote fork progression in a PRIMPOL-dependent manner6,34,39,40,41, suggesting an interplay between repriming and replication fork remodelling. The factors that dictate the balance between repriming and other fork processing pathways (for example, fork reversal), and how this is influenced by the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction, is an important area for future study, especially given that PRIMPOL promotes chemoresistance in BRCA1 deficient cells34.

Diungkapkan bahwa for decades, prokaryotic and eukaryotic replisomes were thought to function with a single primase to initiate dna synthesis on both template strands. This changed with the discovery of PRIMPOL as a second primase in many eukaryotic species, including humans7,8,9. However, although it has been demonstrated that PRIMPOL facilitates replication fork progression during replication stress in a range of metazoan cell lines, evidence for PRIMPOL primase activity being directed specifically to the leading-strand template, and a plausible mechanism for this targeting, was lacking. The work presented here demonstrates that, through its interactions with CMG, PRIMPOL is a dedicated leading-strand primase, establishing a division of labour in the human replisome: Pol α–primase acts on the lagging strand14, while PRIMPOL operates on the leading strand. Our data, together with the strong conservation of CMG-binding motifs in the PRIMPOL N terminus, indicate that many eukaryotic replisomes rely on strand-specific primases to maintain efficient replisome progression, and that this specificity is governed by helicase-directed primase recruitment to the replication fork.
