Diungkapkan bahwa on the basis of the data presented, we propose that the in vitro to in vivo disconnects long associated with nlrp3 biology can be explained, at least in part, by differences in ecm stiffness. Indeed, our finding that NRF2 is required for alum-induced peritonitis and for hyperactivator-mediated antitumour immunity (both NLRP3-dependent processes) contrasts with the NRF2-independence of MSU-crystal-induced peritonitis. However, previous work using chemical activators of NRF2 reported that NRF2 has anti-inflammatory effects. Our finding that NRF2 supports NLRP3 activation is consistent with previous reports that used genetic deficiency to assess the effect of NRF2 on NLRP3 activity46,47,48. All of these factors promote one-signal activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. For example, although KEAP1 (and its oxidation state) is likely to be a general regulator of NRF2, other factors such as GSK3 may regulate NRF2 in specific contexts84. Although our transcriptional data suggest that some effects of NRF2 activators may be off target, both models can co-exist, and we propose that the relationship between NRF2 and inflammation depends on the context. Regardless of the mechanism of NRF2 regulation, our findings highlight ECM stiffness as a foundational regulator of NRF2 functions in macrophages. The contexts in which NRF2 are most important for regulation of NLRP3 require further investigation, and there may be scenarios in which different NRF2 regulators control pathway function. Underlying NLRP3 regulation is the mechanistic link between ECM stiffness, the actin cytoskeleton, and ROS generation, which regulates NRF2 activity and the induction of Panx1. NRF2 may therefore operate as a mechanosensitive checkpoint that controls one-signal NLRP3 activation. The evidence presented herein provides a mandate to consider ECM stiffness as a determinant of immune cell functions in diverse contexts of health and disease.

#525. Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion

📅 13 Nov 2026

Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11282-0

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal–iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we show a kosmotropic anion–polar anion–nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water–Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc–I+–Nuc halogen bonds. This electrolyte framework is validated across diverse Nuc and in both aqueous Zn–I2 and Al–I2 batteries. Moving beyond conventional interhalogen stabilization, these findings establish a distinct electrolyte chemistry framework and represent a mechanistic shift for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

Berdasarkan laporan, the increasing integration of renewable energy calls for sustainable electrochemical energy storage systems beyond lithium-ion batteries1. Unlike intercalation-type positive electrodes, iodine positive electrodes store charge by reversible valence-state changes, offering access to multi-electron redox chemistry with increased capacity and redox potential4. 07 V versus the standard hydrogen electrode11. Most studies have focused on the two-electron I−/I0 redox couple, with a theoretical capacity of 211 mAh g−1 at a redox potential of 0. Extending iodine conversion to the successive I−/I0/I+ redox couples doubles the theoretical capacity to 422 mAh g−1 while introducing the I0/I+ redox process at a higher redox potential of 1. 54 V versus the standard hydrogen electrode10. Aqueous metal–iodine batteries offer a promising platform for large-scale energy storage by combining earth-abundant electrode materials, aqueous electrolytes and conversion-type iodine chemistry2,3. However, despite this potential, achieving reversible four-electron iodine conversion in aqueous environments remains a fundamental challenge3,7.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the crux of iodine conversion chemistry lies in interfacial reactions, where electrolyte composition and interfacial microenvironment govern reaction pathways. Electron-deficient I+ is strongly electrophilic and susceptible to nucleophilic attack by water, resulting in hydrolysis and poor reversibility in aqueous environments9,12. 1a). Previous studies have achieved four-electron iodine conversion in aqueous Zn–I2 and Al–I2 batteries by stabilizing reactive I+ through interhalogen complexes (for example, ICl2 or IBr2) in highly concentrated chloride- or bromide-containing electrolytes5,6,13. However, at water-enriched interfaces, hydration of nucleophilic species (Nuc) competes with these interactions and destabilizes I+ complexes (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Fig. Highly concentrated, halogen-containing electrolytes mitigate this competition by reducing water activity and increasing halide availability, but their high salt contents and corrosivity constrain broader implementation (Fig. In these systems, electrophilic I+ coordinates with two nucleophilic halide ions (Cl− or Br−) through non-covalent interactions8,14. 1), necessitating new electrolyte chemistry and a mechanistic framework that move beyond reliance on halogen-containing electrolytes and conventional interhalogen stabilization5,8.

IHP, inner Helmholtz plane; OHP, outer Helmholtz plane.

Berdasarkan laporan, given the competition between i+ stabilization and hydration at water-enriched interfaces, overcoming this challenge requires simultaneous regulation of the interfacial environment and water–nuc interactions. 2 and Supplementary Tables 1 and 2). Anionic chemistry offers a powerful lever to coordinate these interfacial and molecular interactions15,16,17,18. The applicability of this electrolyte framework is demonstrated across four halogen-free Nuc (urea, acetamide, pyridine and nicotinamide) and in both aqueous Zn–I2 and Al–I2 batteries (Supplementary Fig. Systematic experiments and theoretical calculations reveal how the synergistic effects of PAs and KAs coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, thereby stabilizing interfacial electrochemical behaviour and promoting reversible four-electron iodine conversion. Herein we establish a kosmotropic anion (KA)–polar anion (PA)–Nuc electrolyte framework for reversible I−/I0/I+ conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes (Fig. 1c). Beyond establishing a halogen-free electrolyte chemistry, this work reveals how electrolyte chemistry governs iodine conversion across interfacial, molecular and electrochemical scales, providing a mechanistic basis for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

Sebagaimana diketahui, stabilizing i+ against hydrolysis is essential for reversible four-electron iodine conversion in aqueous electrolytes. 3 and 4) and exhibits sufficient electrochemical stability (Supplementary Fig. This work establishes a mechanistic framework that integrates anionic chemistry with halogen-bond stabilization in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. 2a, strong PAs establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interface, whereas KAs weaken Nuc–water hydrogen bonding to facilitate halogen-bond stabilization of I+. These complementary effects underpin the halogen-free KA–PA–Nuc electrolyte framework, whose composition was subsequently optimized (Supplementary Figs. As illustrated in Fig. These approaches primarily address I+ stabilization through specific molecular interactions, whereas how electrolyte chemistry collectively regulates the interfacial microenvironment, molecular stabilization and the resulting iodine conversion pathways remains less understood. Previous studies have relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes for interhalogen stabilization19,20, whereas more recent studies have explored specific additive-halogen nucleophilic substitution reactions21,22. 5) for four-electron iodine conversion.

Berdasarkan laporan, nmr spectroscopy and molecular-dynamics simulations reveal the molecular origin of these electrochemical differences. By weakening Nuc–water interactions, SO42− increases the availability of Nuc for halogen-bond stabilization of I+, thereby promoting reversible iodine conversion. 35c, 39 and 40). These differences in water–anion coordination translate into distinct water–Nuc interactions. The 2H chemical shift follows SO42− > CH3COO− > NO3− > CF3SO3− > ClO4− (Fig. 4d), indicating progressively stronger anion-induced water polarization and restructuring of the aqueous hydrogen-bond network36,37. 32 and 36–38). Nuc solubility measurements, two-dimensional 1H–15N heteronuclear multiple bond correlation (HMBC) NMR spectra, and calculated Nuc–water distances and hydrogen-bond populations further support this interpretation (Fig. The corresponding 15N chemical shifts, together with the inverse trends observed in 1H and 13C chemical shifts, indicate that KAs such as SO42− polarize hydration water and thereby weaken Nuc–water hydrogen bonding, whereas chaotropic anions such as ClO4− interact directly with the Nuc backbone and facilitate Nuc hydration32 (Fig. 4g–i, and Supplementary Figs. 4e,f, and Supplementary Figs. These results reveal how anionic chemistry regulates molecular water–Nuc interactions to govern the reversibility of four-electron iodine conversion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, having established the complementary roles of pa and ka in interfacial and molecular regulation, we next examined how these effects manifest in the electrochemical processes governing iodine conversion. 44–50). Rate-dependent analysis identifies charge transfer, rather than ion transport, as the dominant kinetic contribution to iodine conversion in the KA–PA–Nuc electrolyte (Supplementary Figs. In the absence of either KA or PA, the DRT responses evolve distinctly with additional competing interfacial processes, whereas their combined presence maintains stable interfacial electrochemical behaviour throughout iodine conversion41,42 (Extended Data Fig. In situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) combined with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis was used to decouple the complex impedance response and identify individual electrochemical processes38,39,40 (Supplementary Figs. In situ Raman spectroscopy further links these electrochemical processes to iodine chemistry, revealing the reversible evolution of the Nuc–I+–Nuc species during cycling (Supplementary Figs. 1). 41–43). 51 and 52).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ka–pa–nuc framework supports four-electron iodine conversion across different operating conditions and cell configurations. A techno-economic analysis under standardized modelling assumptions further illustrates its theoretical cost-reduction potential by avoiding highly concentrated, halogen-containing electrolytes and costly current collectors (Supplementary Fig. 2–4). 53–55, 58a and 59). Zn–I2 cells retain 96% of their capacity after 1,000 cycles at 1 A g−1 and 94% after 2,000 cycles at 2 A g−1, while sustaining four-electron conversion at iodine loadings up to 12. 56–58b,c, 60 and 61). 2 mg cm−2 (Supplementary Figs. 58d–f and Supplementary Tables 3 and 4). 62–67 and Extended Data Figs. This electrolyte framework is also compatible with different current collectors and pouch-cell configurations and extends to aqueous Al–I2 cells using Al–Zn alloy negative electrodes (Supplementary Figs. Mechanistic and post-mortem analyses further reveal that the apparent low Coulombic efficiency and capacity fading involve coupled reversible and irreversible iodine inventory loss, with the latter becoming more pronounced at increased iodine loading (Supplementary Figs. Together, these results clarify the iodine conversion pathways while defining the applicability and remaining limitations of the KA–PA–Nuc framework, showing that sustained reversible four-electron iodine conversion requires not only stabilization of hypervalent iodine species but also broader management of the entire iodine inventory.

Berdasarkan laporan, all molecular-dynamics simulations were performed using the lammps package45 to investigate the bulk solvation structure of various aqueous electrolytes. 8)49. Each system was first energy-minimized and equilibrated in the isothermal–isobaric ensemble (300 K, 1 atm) using a Nosé–Hoover thermostat until both the density and potential energy were stable. The initial configurations were constructed using Packmol46, which randomly packed electrolyte components into a periodic cubic box according to the target molar ratios, ensuring no initial atomic overlaps. Force-field parameters for organic molecules were taken from the OPLS-AA family47,48, whereas others were adopted from validated aqueous zinc salt parameter sets in the literature. The simulation cell was then relaxed by energy minimization before subsequent equilibration. Interaction of water was represented by TIP3P50, and all X–H bonds were constrained using the SHAKE algorithm51. To partially account for polarization effects in concentrated electrolytes, the atomic charges were uniformly scaled (scaling factor 0. Subsequently, production runs were performed in the canonical ensemble for 5 ns (5,000 ps) with a 1-fs integration step to ensure complete equilibration while avoiding structural drift.

Berdasarkan laporan, radial distribution functions gij(r) were computed to analyse ion pairing and solvation structure. Both radial distribution functions and hydrogen bonds were identified using the hydrogen-bond analysis tools implemented in VMD52. Coordination numbers were obtained by integrating gij(r) up to their first minimum. Average hydrogen-bond numbers and distributions were determined over the equilibrated trajectories to characterize the reorganization of the hydrogen-bond network by different anions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to probe field-induced ion and molecular redistribution, an additional set of simulations was conducted in the canonical ensemble with a uniform static electric field applied along the z axis. The field strength corresponded to the experimentally estimated potential gradient.

Sebagaimana diketahui, density-functional-theory calculations were performed using the gaussian16 program package, using the m06-2x exchange-correlation functional53. Iodine was described using an effective core potential from the Stuttgart/Dresden group55. Geometry optimizations were conducted using a mixed basis-set approach: the 6-311+G(d,p) basis set was applied to all elements excluding iodine54. Solvent effects were accounted for using the polarizable continuum model, with water selected as the solvent56.

#526. Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis

📅 13 Nov 2026

Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11308-7

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Berdasarkan laporan, brown adipocytes (bas) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1,2,3,4,5. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

Berdasarkan laporan, functional cellular heterogeneity is well documented in hepatocytes, driven by liver zonation7, and in muscle fibres, shaped by local environmental cues, particularly motor neuron activity8. Single-cell technologies have revealed extensive new patterns of heterogeneity of specific cell types within the same tissue9, yet their biological importance remains largely undetermined.

Sebagaimana diketahui, thermogenic adipose tissue undergoes adaptive thermogenesis and is crucial for energy expenditure and thermoregulation1,2. Its specialized metabolism and precise responses to environmental and physiological stimuli make it an ideal model for studying functional cellular heterogeneity. Thermogenic capacity declines substantially with age in rodents and humans, leading to age-related cold sensitivity and metabolic disorders3,4,5, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, bas and beige adipocytes mediate ucp1-dependent non-shivering thermogenesis10. Although substantial progress has been made in identifying the key pathways that activate thermogenesis, most studies have been conducted at the whole-tissue level, leaving the mechanisms governing its activation, maintenance and deactivation incompletely understood.

Diungkapkan bahwa the heterogeneity of bas within the same brown adipose tissue (bat) and beige adipocyte cluster within inguinal white adipose tissue (iwat) has been characterized by our group6 and others5,11,12,13,14. At room temperature, BA-H cells constitute 30–50% of all BAs; BA-H cells predominate after cold exposure, whereas BA-L cells predominate under thermoneutral conditions6. We found that BAs heterogeneously express UCP1 and classified those with low expression as BA-L cells and those with high expression as BA-H cells6. This raises questions of why BA heterogeneity exists, and whether it reflects random variation along a thermogenic continuum or spatially organized, tightly regulated states within the tissue.

Berdasarkan laporan, here we identify dynamic bistable regulation of ba heterogeneity controlled by the spatial proximity of bas to il-1β puncta through a neuronal–immune regulatory mechanism. This regulation becomes dysfunctional during ageing, leading to cold intolerance in older adults. These findings highlight how different cell types collectively control cellular heterogeneity in a spatiotemporal manner, integrating environmental and internal cues to regulate tissue metabolism and function.

Diungkapkan bahwa regarding the metabolic differences between ba-l cells and ba-h cells, ba-l cells have half the basal respiration, but similar maximal respiration compared to ba-h cells, indicating similarly high mitochondrial potential6. Using in vivo [U-13C]glucose tracing22, we recently showed that BAT has the most active glucose oxidation among metabolically active tissues, while in vitro tracing confirmed active glucose oxidation in differentiated BAs23. To characterize BA-L metabolism, we performed [U-13C] glucose and [U-13C] palmitate tracing in freshly isolated BA-H cells and BA-L cells, followed by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analysis (Extended Data Fig. 4d). BA-L cells also showed lower citrate enrichment from both tracers, indicating lower glucose and fatty acid oxidation (Extended Data Fig. Fully labelled (m+16) free palmitate (C16:0) was about twofold higher in BA-L cells, indicating greater fatty acid uptake (Extended Data Fig. 4b), while fully labelled total palmitate was sixfold higher, suggesting preferential fatty acids storage in BA-L cells (Extended Data Fig. 4a). 4c). Thus, BA-L cells exhibit greater fatty acid uptake and accumulation but lower fatty acid and glucose oxidation, consistent with their lower basal respiration6.

Berdasarkan laporan, the advantages of this spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of ba heterogeneity are multifaceted. Second, it facilitates communication between different cell types through spatial proximity, thereby integrating stimuli from multiple systems, combining environmental and internal cues, and enabling precise regulation of cell states. First, it enables a dual-layered response: an immediate, acute response through readily active BA-H cells, and a longer-term, chronic response that involves shifting cellular heterogeneity. Third, shifting between BA-H and BA-L states preserves BAs from oxidative damage associated with sustained high thermogenesis.

Diungkapkan bahwa although this study primarily focused on ucp1-dependent thermogenesis, ucp1-independent mechanisms are also critical for thermogenic adipose tissue function and whole-body metabolic homeostasis39,40,41. Importantly, cold-induced TNAP expression was compromised with age, while remaining enriched in BA-L cells. Cold exposure increased the proportion of BA-H cells while inducing CKB and TNAP expression in BAT42, reflecting enhanced futile creatine cycle activity either specifically in BA-L cells or across all BAs, with BA-L cells retaining higher activity. We observed that TNAP, a key component of the futile creatine cycle, is enriched in BA-L cells. These results suggest that both UCP1- and futile creatine cycle-dependent thermogenesis are impaired with age.

Diungkapkan bahwa bat has long been recognized as a target organ for glucocorticoids, but their precise role remains unclear. Importantly, inducible GR deletion in BAs during the transition from cold to room temperature sustained the high BA-H/BA-L ratio and thermogenesis. Glucocorticoids have also been implicated in warm-induced beige adipocyte whitening50. Thus, systemic glucocorticoid treatments may not alter active glucocorticoid levels in individual BAs, potentially explaining previous conflicting observations. Some studies indicate that glucocorticoids suppress UCP1 expression and/or BAT activity43,44,45,46, whereas others reach the opposite conclusions47,48,49. Active glucocorticoid levels are regulated locally, independent of systemic levels25. This study shows that GR signalling in BAT regulates BA heterogeneity by locking BAs in the BA-L state and reducing their responsiveness to NA. The stage- and cell-subtype-specific requirement of GR signalling explains why Nr3c1-knockout mice do not exhibit altered BAT development or thermogenesis51,52, and indicates that targeting GR at selective timing could profoundly manipulate thermogenic activity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our study showed that ba heterogeneity is determined by communication from sympathetic neurons to immune cells, rather than by direct communication from sympathetic neurons to bas. We found that NA directly suppresses Il1b production in immune cells through β-adrenergic signalling, thereby modulating BA heterogeneity. Notably, a recent study showed that cold-induced β3-adrenergic activation transiently recruits neutrophils predominantly to white adipose tissue (WAT), particularly the visceral depot55. NA, the primary neurotransmitter from sympathetic nerves, has been shown to modulate immune cell response by regulating cytokine production by immune cells in the liver and adipose tissue53,54. Based on our findings in BAT, IL-1β may similarly suppress lipolysis through the H6PD–GR–RGS2–AC axis in white adipocytes. Notably, Il1b expression in WAT exhibits transient kinetics, peaking at 12 h after stimulation and returning to basal levels at 24 h. These infiltrating neutrophils produce IL-1β, which suppresses local lipolysis by attenuating cAMP-dependent signalling, thereby limiting excessive lipid mobilization. Given that NA suppresses Il1b expression in BAT, it may similarly suppress Il1b expression in newly infiltrated neutrophils in WAT.

Diungkapkan bahwa it remains unclear why in vitro-differentiated bas exhibit heterogeneity. Indeed, depletion of CD45+ immune cells from SVFs before differentiation substantially increased the proportion of BA-H cells, suggesting that SVF immune cells reduce the BA-H/BA-L ratio. BAs may intrinsically differentiate into cells with varying UCP1 levels to preserve thermogenic flexibility or maintain metabolic balance. Cross-talk between BAs and IL-1β+ immune cells in vivo may further reinforce and spatially organize this heterogeneity. Alternatively, IL-1β+ immune cells in SVFs during differentiation may influence the local environment. Future efforts with cell type-specific receptor knockout mouse models will help to validate and further elucidate how sympathetic innervation regulates IL-1β secretion and how IL-1β regulates H6PD protein stability.

Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of GR signalling by a GR antagonist raised the BA-H/BA-L ratio and improved cold-induced thermogenesis in aged mice, indicating that BA-specific GR signalling could be targeted to correct age-related cold intolerance and significantly increase basal metabolism. 60), other tissues and cell types may also contribute. Our study showed that Il1b is increased in aged BAT, consistent with previous studies reporting increased immune cell infiltration and upregulated cytokines in aged BAT59. Increased IL-1β stabilized large amounts of BAs in the BA-L state and suppressed thermogenesis in aged mice. Future efforts will focus on the effects of targeted inhibition of GR signalling specifically in thermogenic cells.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fluorescence microscopy images were acquired for three experimental conditions: room temperature, cold exposure and cold exposure with denervation. The PCC was computed using scipy. stats, providing both the correlation coefficient and associated P value for each image pair. Co-localization between UCP1 and IL-1β was quantified using the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), calculated pixel-wise across filtered cellular regions66. Statistical comparisons between experimental conditions were performed using Welch’s t-tests for independent samples with unequal variances. To eliminate low-intensity noise and focus analysis on meaningful fluorescence signals, intensity-based thresholds were applied to both channels: UCP1 (green channel) at 70 arbitrary units and IL-1β (magenta channel) at 20 arbitrary units. For each condition, dual-channel fluorescence images were collected with UCP1 labelled in the green channel and IL-1β labelled in the magenta channel, along with corresponding autofluorescence reference images for cellular region identification. After masking and thresholding, images were vectorized by flattening two-dimensional pixel arrays into one-dimensional arrays. To restrict analysis to cellular regions and exclude background artifacts, autofluorescence images were Gaussian-smoothed and used to generate binary masks with a threshold of 50 arbitrary units applied to autofluorescence intensity values65, ensuring that correlation analysis was performed exclusively on biologically relevant areas. Pixels were retained for analysis if they exceeded the threshold in either channel, using a logical OR to preserve regions with specific labelling while maintaining sensitivity to differential expression patterns. This approach accounts for potential differences in variance between experimental groups while providing robust statistical inference. All image analysis was performed using custom Python scripts using the tifffile, numpy, scipy and pandas libraries. Results were compiled into structured data frames and visualized using bar plots with error bars.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a, molecular mechanism for the maintenance of the ba-l state. BA has two stable states, low and high thermogenesis, based on UCP1 expression. Green arrows illustrate how BA-L cells are stabilized in a low-thermogenic state: IL-1β enhances the protein stability of H6PD in thermogenic adipocytes, thereby boosting the production of active glucocorticoids. Specifically, H6PD is a functional marker of BA-L cells and boosts the production of active GC. b, Bistable regulation of BA heterogeneity in a spatiotemporal manner governs thermogenic activity. Increased IL-1β levels in the BAT of aged individuals lock BAs in a low-thermogenic state, thereby lowering thermogenic activity and leading to cold intolerance. Illustration created with BioRender; Wang, Q. Glucocorticoid activates the expression of its target RGS2, which inhibits adenylyl cyclase and reduces cAMP production, thereby reducing UCP1 expression. This bistable regulation dynamically and precisely controls cellular heterogeneity in response to signalling from sympathetic nerves and the immune system, managing thermogenesis at the tissue level. https://BioRender. BA states are governed by their spatial proximity to IL-1β+ immune cells (mainly neutrophils and macrophages), which integrate signals from sympathetic neurons and immune cells to determine whether H6PD protein levels should be stabilized or degraded. High IL-1β levels persistently prevent H6PD degradation, desensitizing BAs’ cold response by locking them in BA-L states. We report that IL-1β-secreting immune cells, mainly neutrophils and macrophages, stabilize the surrounding BAs in a low-thermogenic state by preventing H6PD degradation; BAs farther from IL-1β+ cells are stabilized in a high-thermogenic state. https://BioRender. com/basqx8x (2026). Illustration created with BioRender; Wang, Q. GC then activates the expression of its target, RGS2, which inhibits adenylyl cyclase, reducing cAMP production and, in turn, UCP1 expression. The purple arrow illustrates that in aged individuals, IL-1β is elevated in BAT. Red arrows illustrate how BA-L cells switch into BA-H cells upon cold exposure: cold stimulation activates sympathetic neurons, which decrease local BAT IL-1β levels; lower IL-1β levels lead to H6PD protein degradation, turning BA-L into BA-H. com/mj195m9 (2026).

#527. Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis

📅 13 Nov 2026

Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11230-y

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Diungkapkan bahwa breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1,2,3. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4,5,6,7. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse.

Diungkapkan bahwa gene expression profiles classify breast cancers into luminal a or luminal b (hormone-receptor-positive (hr+)), her2-positive and basal-like subtypes. Among these, basal-like subtypes largely overlap with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC)2,3. These classifications guide treatment management and prognosis. Luminal HR+ breast cancer generally responds to endocrine therapy with favourable outcomes, yet many patients relapse8. Single-cell and spatial studies have revealed substantial intratumoural heterogeneity among subtypes, which potentially drive treatment resistance and recurrence4,5,6,7,9.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chromatin organization, mediated by dna and histone post-translational modifications (ptms), facilitates the acquisition of epigenetically distinct cellular states in genetically identical cells10,11,12. Single-cell profiling of histone marks, such as trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 27 (H3K27me3), implicates chromatin states in breast tumour heterogeneity and treatment resistance18,19. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell chromatin-accessibility sequencing (scATAC–seq) delineate intratumour heterogeneity13,14,15,16, the contribution of chromatin patterns remains unclear17. However, these methods measure a limited number of chromatin marks, which hinders analyses of complex patterns and interactions. We developed a cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) method to systematically profile multiple histone PTMs and decode population-specific chromatin patterns to examine heterogeneity among cancer cells20,21,22,23.

Berdasarkan laporan, tumour epigenetic states are also reflected in blood. Cell-free, plasma-circulating nucleosomes, released mainly by dying normal and cancer cells, retain tissue-of-origin epigenetic patterns24,25,26,27. Our single-molecule imaging platform, epigenetics of plasma isolated nucleosomes (EPINUC), captures multiple epigenetic features on plasma nucleosomes28. This method detects colorectal cancer, including low-burden early-stage disease28, and enables minimally invasive molecular profiling and treatment monitoring of paediatric brain tumours29.

Berdasarkan laporan, here we present a holistic epigenetic analysis of primary treatment-naive breast tumours and blood cell-free nucleosomes. Linking recurrent intratumoural epigenetic patterns to circulating nucleosomes connects tumour epigenetic heterogeneity with its potential clinical implications. This work reveals epigenetic alterations as key mediators of intratumour heterogeneity and potential biomarkers for early diagnosis and prognosis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to assess heterogeneity in breast tumour histone modifications, we performed epigenetic focused cytof on fresh, surgically resected tumours from treatment-naive women and quantified histone modifications at single-cell resolution (fig. 2d). 2b,c). CyTOF analysis of MCF7 (luminal) and four basal-like TN cell lines validated that GATA3 and K5 expression patterns can differentiate luminal and basal-like identities. 1b,c and Supplementary Fig. 1a and Supplementary Table 1). Partial overlap among luminal tumour cells from different patients probably reflects shared lineage-specific epigenetic programs. Using multiple cell-identity markers, we derived a PermCell luminal signature (Methods) that accurately distinguished the identities of the cell lines (Fig. 2a). Following batch correction and normalization, uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) analysis of all 12 tumours revealed that tumour cells largely occupied patient-specific regions, whereas stromal cells clustered together across patients. 2e). As expected, stromal cells expressed vimentin and αSMA, whereas tumour cells expressed the epithelial keratins, EpCAM and E-cadherin (Fig. Notably, the basal TN tumour differed from HR+ tumours, showing low expression of the luminal marker GATA3 and high expression of the basal marker cytokeratin-5 (K5; also known as KRT5) and mesenchymal vimentin markers (Fig. Stromal and tumour chromatin patterns also differed, a result that underscores their role in dictating cellular identity (Fig. The cohort included mainly luminal HR+ tumours and only one basal triple-negative (TN, HR–) tumour (n = 12; Supplementary Table 2 and Supplementary Fig. 1e,f). This result aligns with previous studies that measured single-cell genomic differences13,14 (Fig. 1b,c and Supplementary Fig. 1d and Supplementary Fig. 1a,b), as standard neoadjuvant therapy excluded most TN cases from treatment-naive eligibility. 1b, Methods and Supplementary Fig. Moreover, SHAP analysis30,31 identified these two markers as the strongest discriminators of tumour type (Fig. 1g).

UMAP clustering and density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) across all features revealed three subpopulations in each tumour, which we termed cycling, luminal and basal-like (Fig. 1a,b). 1a–c and Supplementary Fig. 3). Accordingly, the epigenetically inferred cycling fraction strongly correlated with Ki-67 levels (Fig. 1d). In tumours, only a luminal subset cycled and expressed high levels of Ki-67, a result consistent with previous immunohistochemistry (IHC) and scRNA-seq studies14,32. 1i, Extended Data Fig. 1k). 3). MCF7 cells showed similar luminal and basal-like heterogeneity, although most cells were cycling, as expected for a cell line (Extended Data Fig. CyTOF Ki-67 levels correlated with pathology estimates (Fig. 1c). 1j and Extended Data Fig. This finding validates the observed heterogeneity as an inherent feature of luminal breast tumours and excludes contamination of normal cells (Fig. We validated this result by repeating CyTOF analyses of two tumours (14 and 18), adding the established cell cycle marker phospho-Rb (pRb). pRb-positive cells showed an increase in core histones, as expected from cycling cells, and a larger increase in histone PTMs (Supplementary Fig. 1l).

Sebagaimana diketahui, most cancer cells strongly expressed gata3 and scored highly for the luminal signature, consistent with clinical classification (fig. 2d). 1n and Extended Data Fig. Moreover, in each tumour, the PDX samples and the MCF7 cells, we identified a minor recurrent subpopulation that acquired basal-like identity, with high K5 expression and a reduced luminal signature (Fig. In MCF7 cells, epigenetic UMAP and clustering similarly identified several clusters, including a K5hi basal-like population (Fig. 4a). 1a,b and Supplementary Fig. 4b). Notably, luminal and basal-like cells also had distinct histone PTM signatures (Fig. Independent CyTOF experiments, additional MCF7 parental cell culture and populations derived from independent single-cell clones revealed similar subpopulation patterns, a result that argues against a genetic basis for these effects (Fig. 1m). 2a–c). 1 and Supplementary Fig. 1h, Extended Data Fig. Accordingly, UMAP plots based solely on histone modifications revealed separation of the subpopulations, which validated the epigenetic basis of this phenotypic diversity (Supplementary Fig. This phenotypic diversity is consistent with previous single-cell studies of human and mouse breast tumours14,21,33,34. 1h–j, Extended Data Fig. 1h–j and Extended Data Fig. These basal-like cells with reduced luminal signalling appeared closer in UMAP space to the TN cell lines, which provided further support for their basal-like identity (Supplementary Fig. 4c). Moreover, individual PDX tumours derived from the same donor and grown independently in different mice showed similar subpopulation proportions, which provides support for a dynamic and plastic relationship between cell states (Extended Data Fig. 1). 4a). Overall, our data revealed inherent intratumour heterogeneity in luminal tumours, with epigenetic variability between distinct subpopulations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we further explored the characteristics of the cycling, luminal and basal-like subpopulations. Unsupervised clustering grouped corresponding subpopulations across patients, which confirmed their robustness and similarity (Fig. In each tumour, a model trained on a random subset predicted the remaining cells with 94% accuracy, which confirmed the robust differences between subpopulations (Fig. Across tumours, luminal cells expressed oestrogen receptor (ER), GATA3 and cytokeratin-8 and cytokeratin-18 (K8/18; also known as KRT8 and KRT18, respectively), whereas basal-like cells downregulated these luminal markers and highly expressed K5 (Fig. In detail, histone PTMs, particularly the four acetylation marks, were leading predictors of cycling cells despite overlap of individual marks with basal-like cells (Extended Data Fig. 3a). It also assigned 78% of unclustered ‘noise’ cells with >95% confidence, generating classifications that aligned with the original clustering and UMAP positions (Extended Data Fig. 2a). 2b). SHAP analysis identified the features driving each subpopulation. Diungkapkan bahwa having identified distinct dna methylation programs associated with tumour cell states, we next assessed cell-to-cell variability by clustering read-level methylation patterns across 100-bp genomic bins and calculating empirical entropy as an estimation of cell-type heterogeneity55. As expected, most CGIs were unmethylated across all cells56, thus showing zero entropy. This result suggests that empirical entropy, by capturing diverse DNA methylation states, can be used as a proxy for cell-to-cell heterogeneity and reveal functional differences between subpopulations. The variable CGIs (entropy > 0) were functionally enriched for EMT and the related Hedgehog signalling pathways, which indicated that these are differentially regulated in tumours57 (Extended Data Fig. Genes near high-entropy bins were associated with functional terms related to poor differentiation, tumour aggressiveness and basal compared with luminal identity (Supplementary Fig. 7a). We next calculated the mean entropy for each CGI (Extended Data Fig. 6a). 7b). This analysis suggests that intratumour variability in methylation patterns may be associated with cell identity transitions.

Despite its smaller size, EPINUC predicted recurrence with an AUC of 0. Combining assays did not improve performance, which indicated limited added value from OncotypeDX in this setting. 11). 81, and outperformed predictions based on classical prognostic parameters such as stage, grade and subtype (Fig. 5i, Extended Data Fig. 5h). The best model achieved an AUC of 0. 5e–g and Extended Data Fig. Pending larger prospective validation, these findings provide support for the use of EPINUC for early diagnosis and recurrence-risk stratification.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, single-cell studies have revealed clinically relevant phenotypic diversity across cancers, yet the epigenetic mechanisms fuelling this heterogeneity remain poorly understood75,76. Here we performed single-cell profiling of histone PTMs in luminal breast tumours. Quantitative mass-spectrometry also showed differences in global histone modification levels between breast cancer subtypes, which provides support for the idea that chromatin regulates cell identity39,77,78. Altered H3K4 demethylation can drive loss of luminal identity40, which suggests that changes in ER signalling, even without ESR1 mutations, may promote luminal-to-basal plasticity. Our analysis of luminal breast tumours uncovered tumour cell diversity consistent with previous transcriptomic and proteomic approaches14,21,33,34,54. By measuring multiple global chromatin modifications at single-cell resolution, we identified a recurrent epigenetic signature of K5hi basal-like cells across tumours, supported across modalities by single-cell genomic profiling of H3K4 methylation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reconstitution of the full heterogeneity spectrum in single-cell-derived mcf7 clones and independently grown pdx tumours provides support for epigenetically driven, interconverting states rather than genetically distinct clones. Accordingly, proteomic intratumoural heterogeneity increases with tumour grade independently of genomic heterogeneity, thereby implicating epigenetic mechanisms7. Subpopulation frequencies varied among patients and may be influenced by mutations that bias state acquisition, as reported in glioblastoma46. This plasticity may enable adaptation to therapeutic pressures, which then promotes resistance and progression. Whether epigenetic therapies can limit plasticity and state transitions remains to be tested.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, breast cancer prognosis depends strongly on early detection, yet accurate screening while minimizing false positives remains challenging79,80,81,82. Detection of molecular changes before clinical progression could guide treatment adaptation and maximize first-line benefit83. Tumour-level histone PTM signatures distinguished luminal breast cancer cell states, whereas EPINUC analysis of pretreatment plasma samples provided proof-of-concept for outcome prediction. Notably, H3K4 methylation marks were elevated in both basal-like tumour cells and in plasma from patients with recurrent disease, which suggests that there is a link between this subpopulation and disease outcome.

Diungkapkan bahwa unlike cytof, which resolves tumour cell populations, plasma measurements integrate signals from damage of healthy tissue, the tumour microenvironment and local and systemic immune responses29,84. Nevertheless, patient-matched histone PTMs analyses in tumours and blood revealed a positive correlation for most marks, with the highest correlation observed for the recurrence-associated marks H3K4me1 and H3K9ac, which provides support for their prognostic value. Overall, our tissue and plasma chromatin dataset reveals epigenetically driven intratumoural heterogeneity in breast cancer and supports the use of EPINUC as a potential approach for breast cancer diagnosis and prognosis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as samples were measured in batches, anchor samples, identical tumour samples measured in different batches, were used to implement batch-effect correction. This method non-linearly maps quantile values from one anchor sample to corresponding quantiles in another, which effectively aligns their distributions. Batch effects were corrected using a Q-Q transformation based on the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF). This transformation was then applied to tumour samples in the first batch.

Notably, as Q-Q plot transformation is inherently restricted to the range of the anchor samples owing to its reliance on interpolation, for values outside this range, linear extrapolation—based on the mean and standard deviation of the samples—can approximate the transformation’s slope and intercept, which provides a reasonable estimate of the nonlinear mapping beyond the observed data range.

Berdasarkan laporan, pps analysis on the data was conducted using a previously published algorithm (https://github. com/8080labs/ppscore). In brief, by calculating a cross-validated decision tree (repeated (10,000) 4-fold cross-validation) for the target variable (for example, diagnosis) using only one of the markers, it is possible to determine which of the markers in the datasets contributes most to the target variable.

Berdasarkan laporan, xgboost classifier was applied to the data, using all features measured and their combinations. Feature contribution was assessed by SHAP.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for roc curves, for each classification task, the most important features were selected using the boruta algorithm (with a random forest classifier)121. An additional feature engineering step was used to generate combinatorial combinations (multiplication, division and SQRT) of the selected features, and another round of feature selection was performed using Boruta. The final features selected were used either in a random forest classifier or in a soft voting classifier consisting of RF, XGBoost and LDA classifiers. The final classifier was used to generate a ROC curve with the associated confidence intervals using 10-fold cross-validation and 1,000 bootstrap repeats.

Diungkapkan bahwa to enable comparison across independently processed epinuc cohorts, batch correction was applied to account for differences in antibody labelling degree. The independently processed cohort was first standardized and subsequently rescaled to match the mean and variance of the reference dataset. In brief, the reference dataset was subsampled to balance group sizes, and feature-wise means and standard deviations were calculated. This approach allowed alignment of feature distributions across cohorts while preserving relative differences between samples.

Sebagaimana diketahui, histones were enriched from ffpe tissues as previously described122. For each histone modified peptide, a percentage relative abundance (%RA) value for the sample (light channel) or the internal standard (heavy channel) was estimated. The samples were separated by reversed-phase chromatography, acquired on a Q Exactive HF instrument (Thermo Fisher Scientific), and analysed using MaxQuant and QualBrowser, as previously described124. Approximately 4 µg of histone octamer was mixed with an equal amount of heavy-isotope labelled histones, which were used as an internal standard123, and separated on a 17% SDS–PAGE gel. Histone bands were excised, chemically acylated with deuterated acetic anhydride and in-gel digested with trypsin124. Light to heavy ratios (log2 transformed) of %RA were then calculated and are reported in Supplementary Table 8.

(c) The Basal-luminal index was used to score the transcriptional identity of tumor cells13, and cells from each tumor were divided into quartiles; a low index score corresponds to expression of luminal identity genes (Q1) and a high index score corresponds to expression of basal-like identity genes (Q4). #528. A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors

📅 13 Nov 2026

A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11259-z

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Diungkapkan bahwa rna-derived 2′,3′-cyclophosphate-terminated nucleotides act as immune signalling molecules in prokaryotes and eukaryotes1,2,3, but how plants perceive them remains unknown. Here we demonstrate that NIB1, a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein in rice, senses 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2′,3′-cNMPs; 2′,3′-cAMP and 2′,3′-cGMP) and adenylyl-(3′→5′)-guanosine 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate (ApG>p) produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of green stink bug during feeding. Exogenous application of 2′,3′-cAMP, 2′,3′-cGMP or ApG>p elicits NIB1 and EDS1-mediated immune responses. Binding of the RNase products promotes formation of nuclear condensates containing NIB1, which recruit the core immune regulator Enhanced Disease Susceptibility 1 (EDS1) and activate defence, potentially contributing to the immune signalling of Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) proteins that also produce the nuclease products. Sucking insects inject digestive enzymes including RNases into the host plant to acquire nutrients. Our findings unveil a conserved pathway in plants, in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins perceive the nuclease-generated second messengers to launch defence and point to a potential link between plant TIR nuclease activity and EDS1 signalling.

Sebagaimana diketahui, insect pests cause losses to crop production and damage vegetation4,5. During feeding, insects release oral secretions containing proteins and other molecules that can activate or suppress host plant defence6,7,8. Digestive enzymes hydrolyse cellular components to generate nutrients for herbivores. These breakdown products also act as host-derived damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that activate plant pattern-recognition receptors9,10. Identifying host-derived signalling molecules and their defence activation mechanisms is essential for developing new plant-protection strategies.

Berdasarkan laporan, t2-family ribonuclease (rnaset2) proteins, which preferentially cleave single-strand rnas between purine and uridine residues, are ancient enzymes that are widely distributed across organisms and functional in diverse biological processes2,11. Plant TIR domains generate second messengers such as 2′-ADPR and pRib-AMP, which promote the formation of EDS1–Phytoalexin Deficient 4 (PAD4)–Activated Disease Resistance 1 (ADR1) complex and trigger disease resistance15,20,21. Activated plant TIR also catalyses the production of ADPr-ATP and di-ADPR, leading to the complex formation of EDS1-Senescence-Associated Gene 101 (SAG101)–N Required Gene 1 (NRG1), inducing plant cell death16,22,23. Phytopathogens also secrete nucleases into host tissues13,14. Arabidopsis nudix hydrolase 7 (AtNUDT7) hydrolyses 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP and attenuates TIR-mediated cell death when overexpressed in Nicotiana benthamiana3. Human lysosomal RNaseT2 generates purine-2′,3′-cyclophosphate-terminated oligoribonucleotides that are sensed by Toll-like receptor 8 to activate innate immunity2. Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domains of plant intracellular nucleotide-binding and leucine-rich repeat (NLR) immune receptors possess enzymatic activities towards oxidized nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) and nucleic acids15,16,17,18,19. Plant TIR domains also synthesize 2′,3′-cAMP and 2′,3′-cGMP (2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP) through nuclease activity. Plant S-RNases, which mediate self-incompatibility, belong to this protein family12. However, the contribution of 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP to EDS1-dependent immunity remains elusive.

Diungkapkan bahwa plant glycine-rich rna-binding proteins (grps) encompassing one rna recognition motif (rrm) at the n terminus and a glycine-rich region (grr) at the c terminus regulate plant responses to abiotic and biotic stresses24,25. These data indicate that the RRM of GRPs is central to immune function, although the underlying molecular mechanism remains unidentified. Here we report that the rice GRP NIB1 interacts with invading insect T2 RNases (such as NVR1) to promote ribonuclease activity and the production of 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP and ApG>p. Arabidopsis GRP7 (AtGRP7) has a positive role in immunity, whereas the Pseudomonas syringae effector HopU1 suppresses AtGRP7-mediaed immunity by catalysing ADP-ribosylation of an arginine residue (R49) in the RRM of AtGRP726,27,28. Binding to the cyclic nucleotides via RMM stimulates NIB1 phase separation to assemble the plant defence machinery in the nucleus.

Sebagaimana diketahui, plants express many cell-surface and intracellular immune receptors to perceive alien molecules and activate defence38,39. The presence of NVR1 orthologues in oral secretions of the piercing-sucking pest Apolygus lucorum (ALR1; data not shown) and chewing insect C. medinalis suggests that T2-family ribonuclease effectors are conserved across divergent feeding types and may be a broadly deployed strategy in plant–insect interactions. Here we found that the rice GRP NIB1 interacts with invading RNaseT2 and senses 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP and ApG>p to induce plant defence. Given the involvement of 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP in abiotic stresses40,41,42,43, it is worth further investigating the role of GRPs in leveraging biotic and abiotic stresses. Whether and how plants discriminate between different sources of second messengers are also important questions to address.

Sebagaimana diketahui, condensates or membraneless compartments are engaged in a variety of plant developmental and stress response processes44,45,46,47. Exogenous spraying of these RNA degradation-derived signalling molecules triggered plant defence responses, highlighting their application potential as immune activators. Our study focuses on the immune function of nuclear NIB1, whereas the biological roles of its cytoplasmic condensates deserve future investigation. NIB1, as a sensor, perceives 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP and ApG>p and forms nuclear condensates that recruit the core immune regulator EDS135,36,37 and activate downstream signalling pathways, highlighting protein phase separation as a mechanism in response to second messengers. Our study opens a door for exploring the engagement of RNase products in plant defence, adaptation and development.

Sebagaimana diketahui, plant tir-catalysed and nad+-derived products induces formation of eds1–sag101–nrg1 and eds1–pad4–adr1 heterotrimers, as well as oligomerization of adr1 and nrg1 as calcium channels at the plasma membrane, to confer immunity. The link between TIR nuclease-derived 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP and EDS1 remains unclear, and the nuclear function of EDS1 in TIR-mediated immunity is unknown. benthamiana. The T2 RNase NVR1 produces ApG>p, and the nuclease product spectrum of plant TIR-only proteins awaits further studies. In bacteria, 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP have been shown to modulate activities of transcription factors48. 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP-induced NIB1 condensate in the nucleus recruits EDS1 to trigger defence, potentially via transcriptional modulation, providing a possible explanation for the biological relevance of plant TIR nuclease activity. Future studies could investigate whether other GRPs are also involved in perceiving such nuclease products and their interactions. Plant TIR-only proteins but not TIR–NLR receptors possess nuclease activity—thus, TIR nuclease activity and 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP are likely to be involved in TIR-only-mediated basal immunity but not TIR–NLR-mediated effector-triggered immunity3,49, consistent with the weak contribution of GRPs towards TIR-induced cell death phenotypes in N. Our unpublished data show that 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP does not contribute to the EDS1–SAG101–NRG1 or EDS1–PAD4–ADR1 heterotrimer formation, consistent with the proposed role of 2′,3′-cAMP/cGMP in amplifying rather than initiating TIR signalling3. Detailed analyses of NIB1 condensate components will add valuable knowledge to understanding this nuclease-based defence pathway.

Diungkapkan bahwa phytophagous insects, especially mesophyll feeders, generate various small molecules from biopolymers by injecting digestive enzymes into plant tissues, in addition to mechanical injury. lucorum (Miridae) and the green stink bug N. Although the wide-scale cultivation of transgenic crops expressing Bacillus thuringiensis insecticidal proteins has effectively controlled the lepidopteran chewing insects in the field, heteropteran mesophyll feeders such as the mirid bug A. viridula (Pentatomidae), are less sensitive to these proteins and are emerging as a threat to agriculture50. Detection of DAMPs is essential for plants to activate defence programmes. Our findings show that plant GRP is a sensor of the invading RNase products and orchestrates immune responses to activate an EDS1-dependent signalling pathway, providing a potential target for advanced plant protection technologies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the third-instar c. Three one-month-old, uniform rice plants per genotype were grouped and arranged triangularly to prevent positional bias. After 24 h of oviposition at 26 °C (12 h:12 h light:dark photoperiod), the total number of eggs laid on the three plants of each genotype was summed. medinalis larvae were placed on leaves of the 12-day-old rice seedlings of the indicated lines. The assay was repeated with three independent cages. 15 pairs of newly emerged moths were mated for 48 h. Subsequently, males were removed, and the 15 mated females were released into the cage centre with a 15% honey solution. Oviposition selection assay was conducted in nylon mesh cages (90 × 70 × 90 cm). Oviposition preference was quantified by the oviposition index: OI = (T − C)/(T + C), where T and C are the number of eggs in the mutants and wild type, respectively. Larval weight was recorded after the feeding for three days. The deviation of the oviposition index against 0 was tested using a one-sample Student’s t-test.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for larval feeding preference, leaf segments (3 cm) from 3 plant lines were arranged equidistantly in a circle within a petri dish. After 1 h of selection in darkness, the number of larvae settled on each plant was recorded. Ten third-instar larvae (pre-starved for 2 h) were introduced to the centre. The selection rate was calculated as Ntarget/Ntotal selection × 100%, where Ntarget and Ntotal selection represent the number of larvae on a specific plant and the total number of larvae making a definitive choice, respectively.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for field test, wild-type zh11 seeds were sown in soil, and 35-day-old plants were transplanted into six 1 m × 1 m field plots. Following treatment, 20 mated female C. medinalis moths were released at the centre of the enclosure. Each plot was surrounded by two rows of rice plants serving as buffer rows, and all six plots were maintained within mesh enclosure. Once rolled-leaf shelters became visible, the number of shelters was counted. Four weeks after transplantation, the plots were arranged in an alternating pattern and sprayed with either water or 50 μM 8-Br-2′,3′-cAMP. Insects and plant positions were randomized in laboratory assays, field treatments followed an alternating design, and outcomes were assessed blind to genotype or treatment.

#529. Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines

📅 13 Nov 2026

Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11278-w

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Berdasarkan laporan, the global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource1. However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs2,3. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the global imperative to transition towards sustainable energy systems has intensified research and development in renewable energy technologies. Near-term deployment targets are 1 GW by 2035 in the UK3, with international roadmaps project deployments eventually exceeding 300 GW worldwide by 20508. Unlike other renewables such as wind and solar, tidal currents are governed by an astronomical cycle, which offers a consistent and forecastable power source4,5. Among these, tidal energy presents a uniquely predictable and substantial resource. Tidal power is estimated at 50 TW h yr−1 in Europe6 and as much as 220 TW h yr−1 in the USA alone7. The scale of this resource is significant. These highlight the potential of tidal energy in contributing to energy security and renewable energy portfolios.

Diungkapkan bahwa despite their promise, the harsh hydrodynamic environment presents an important barrier to the economic viability of this renewable energy source. A primary challenge is the hydrodynamic load fluctuations that arise from large variations in flow velocity, turbulence, turbine yaw with respect to the incoming stream, velocity shear along the water depth2, wave-induced oscillating currents9, and wake interaction within turbine arrays10. These fluctuating loads are a primary design consideration and are associated with accelerated fatigue, reduced operational lifespans and unplanned downtime. These reliability concerns result in blade and turbine designs with high capital costs, which directly increase the levelized cost of energy (LCOE)3.

Diungkapkan bahwa to address the challenge of the dynamic loads, various mitigation strategies have been developed. Although the active control systems are effective in certain operational envelopes, the reliability of sophisticated sensors and actuators in the harsh undersea environment remains a concern. Active control typically deploys systems to actively regulate the pitch11 or camber12 of the blades, therefore, to regulate power output, control mean loads and improve start-up performance. Furthermore, the response times of the activator limit effectiveness against rapid, high-frequency load fluctuations13,14.

Diungkapkan bahwa to address these concerns, there has been an increased focus on developing passive control mechanisms. Passive pitch control involves designing blades that can rotate around their spanwise axis in response to changing hydrodynamic loads, thereby altering their angle of attack. Reference 18 has contributed a general framework for the design of passive pitching systems, identifying the locations of the pivot point for maximizing load mitigation. Experimental validations in ref. This is typically achieved by incorporating a pre-loaded torsional spring mechanism at the blade root. Theoretical work in refs. Passive control is mainly realized in two ways: introducing changes in the blade pitch or modifying the blade camber. 15,16 are among the first to introduce the concept. 17, which confirmed more than 80% load fluctuations can be reduced in sheared flow conditions, with additional benefits such as faster wake recovery, which improves turbine array performance. Both demonstrated that complete cancellation of the load fluctuation is possible without compromising the mean power. This is followed by a numerical study in ref. 19 have confirmed the ability of passive pitching systems in the reduction of time-averaged loadings.

Berdasarkan laporan, passive pitching systems are effective for low-frequency, large-scale adjustments and power regulation by adjusting the global angle of attack of the blades. However, the added inertia due to the displacement of the pitching axis required by effective pitching systems, as well as the bearing friction, limits the response of the system to high-frequency disturbances, such as turbulent eddies or rapid shear variations. Moreover, despite being simpler than active control systems, passive pitch blades still introduce extra moving parts and potential failure points in harsh undersea environments. Research has identified that for wind turbine applications, most of the failures originate from the pitch system20, highlighting the significant operational advantage of a robust, passive design.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an alternative design philosophy can be found in nature, where organisms from fish to trees passively reconfigure their shape through distributed material compliance to manage fluid dynamic forces21,22. Passive morphing blades are common in wind energy applications23,24, in which the blade twists to feather in response to a wind gust. In fact, for similar power-rated turbines, the bending moment experienced by tidal turbines is higher than that of wind turbines. Therefore, a faster response time can be achieved with a fixed-pitch blade that does not require hinges and bearings. Drawing from these biological principles, passive morphing flexible blades offer an alternative strategy, where flexibility is distributed along the blade, allowing each blade section to adapt automatically through fluid–structure interaction. This technique, known as aeroelastic tailoring, requires ad hoc structural design, whose scalability and reliability for large tidal turbines is yet to be demonstrated. Therefore, the need for a scalable, reliable, passive system that can mitigate both rapid, localized turbulent fluctuations and slower, large-scale changes in inflow velocity on large-scale tidal turbines remains unmet.

Diungkapkan bahwa this study directly addresses this challenge by proposing a blade with chordwise flexibility, rather than spanwise flexibility, as in aeroelastic tailoring. The frontal and thickest part of the blade, which provides structural integrity, is rigid. 0 m s−1, and tip-speed ratios (λ) from 3 to 9, with the flexible blades designed for optimal performance at u∞ ≈ 0. 5–1. The turbine was tested across a range of nominal inflow velocities u∞ = 0. Instead, the trailing edge is flexible from root to tip. 85 m s−1. Our analysis first addresses the low-frequency load mitigation over a tidal cycle before examining the high-frequency load fluctuations and the underlying physical mechanisms of the deformation of the blade. To demonstrate this potential, we experimentally evaluated the performance of these chordwise-flexible blades against a rigid baseline in the FloWave Ocean Energy Research Facility at the University of Edinburgh. Specifically, we provide the first comprehensive experimental demonstration that a carefully designed chordwise-flexible blade can achieve both control of the mean power and thrust with the quasi-steady variations of flow velocities over the tidal cycle (for example, the diurnal tidal cycle) and mitigation of the high-frequency (turbulence) hydrodynamic load fluctuations on tidal turbines, while enabling the same yield as a conventional rigid blade equipped with active pitch control. Overall, we demonstrated a new pathway to enhance turbine reliability and survivability, reducing capital costs associated with the active pitch system, and reducing maintenance costs by removing hinges, bearings and actuators, ultimately reducing the LCOE.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the key advantage of the flexible blade design is its ability to passively regulate peak loadings. However, at off-design conditions, the flexible blade exhibits higher CT and CM values than at its design speed. Under these conditions, the flexible blade thrust passively decreases, whereas the rigid one increases. While this results in higher thrust coefficients at lower velocities, the absolute forces, which scale with velocity squared (\(F\propto {u}_{\infty }^{2}\)), are much smaller during lower flow periods and are not as important for the structural design of the turbine as the peak loads experienced at or above rated velocity. However, the performance of the flexible blades diverges from rigid ones for λ values beyond this optimal range. Therefore, the ability of the flexible blade technology to match power performance while simultaneously offering a passive mechanism to reduce the most important structural loads represents a marked advancement for designing more durable and cost-effective tidal turbines.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the simulation first confirms that the passive design of the flexible blade does not compromise its primary function of energy capture. The normalized power profiles shown in Fig. 2c. 2b coincide for the rubber blade with speed control and the state-of-the-art active pitch control turbine, where the turbine speed is shown in Fig. As the total energy harvested is proportional to the integral of the power curves over the tidal cycle, the overlap of the curves confirms a negligible difference in overall energy yield. This demonstrates that the load-mitigation benefits of flexible blades can be achieved without a penalty to energy capture in a real-world setting.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the advantage of the flexible blade design is revealed by the differences in the quasi-steady thrust (fig. 2c). 2d) between the turbine configurations.
