Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to illustrate the physics of the passive load regulation mechanism demonstrated previously, the deformation of the flexible blade is visualized at the tip section. The successful application of this technique using fully submerged cameras represents a significant experimental achievement, as most underwater DIC studies to date have been performed through observation windows rather than submerging the camera in the fluid25. Figure 4 shows the phase-averaged digital image correlation (DIC) measurements of the tip of the same flexible blade at a constant azimuthal angle, in which the blade is horizontal with downward velocity. In this way, complex optical distortions and refractive index mismatches associated with viewing ports are avoided, thereby achieving a more accurate measurement. In this study, the DIC system measured the deformation of the suction side of the blade. The full blade profile was then reconstructed by adding the known thickness distribution of the undeformed blade to the measured deformed chord line.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, phase-averaged profiles of one blade tip measured with dic when the blade span is horizontal, and the tangential velocity is pointing downwards. Coordinates x, y are normalized by the chord length at the blade tip with origin at the quarter chord.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the measurements demonstrate the mechanism of the passive morphing concept. Under hydrodynamic loading, the flexible trailing edge deflects upwards, causing the entire profile to flatten into a shape with less camber. The high camber present in both the initial blade shape and the subsequent deformed shape before reaching the designed operating point is the primary reason for the higher thrust force generated by the flexible blade operating off-design. The undeformed flexible blade was designed with a significant initial camber, noticeably higher than that of the conventional rigid blade profile. This passive feathering becomes more pronounced with higher inflow velocities, which is the mechanism that reduces the thrust coefficient at high tip-speed ratios and velocities.

Diungkapkan bahwa dic measurements of different blades (extended data figs. 1 and 2) show that blades with lower flexural rigidity undergo greater camber reduction and exhibit stronger load shedding. Specifically, for blades with the same mould geometry, a too-stiff blade results in a too-low pitch and too-high camber, and thus high mean and unsteady thrust. Conversely, a too-soft blade results in an over-pitched blade and low power capture.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the observed mean load-shedding behaviour shown in fig. 1 arises primarily from quasi-steady passive morphing, and not from dynamic blade deformation resulting in hysteresis, vortex dynamics, and so on. DIC reconstructions of each individual blade at the same azimuthal position reveal only a narrow spread about the mean shape, corresponding to a standard deviation of the pitch variation of approximately ±0. 2° (Extended Data Fig. 3).

Sebagaimana diketahui, to further verify that the mean load-shedding behaviour is due to a quasi-steady morphing, we compare the measured blade deformations (fig. 4). 4) and the corresponding power and thrust (Fig. 1) with those computed with an in-house fluid–structure interaction solver based on a quasi-steady low-order model (Methods). The blade shapes computed with this program are in good agreement with those measured experimentally, and so are the predicted power and thrust for different tip-speed ratios (Extended Data Fig. Because the numerical solver assumes the blade is in static equilibrium under hydrodynamic loads, these results confirm that the governing physics is quasi-steady.

Diungkapkan bahwa the fluid–structure interaction of the flexible blades is governed by two non-dimensional groups such as the reynolds number (re) and cauchy number (ca) (defined in the methods). To ensure geometric similarity between the model and the full-scale strain of the flexible blades, the Young modulus E of rubber must be scaled up to maintain the same Ca across scales. The experiments are performed at sufficiently high Re that the hydrodynamic load coefficients are about the same as those at full scale, as shown by the almost identical values for the rigid blade tested at different velocities in Fig. As discussed in Supplementary Note 4, rubber features a sufficiently high range of E for full-scale applications. 1. Furthermore, rubber has the advantage of matching the mass density of water, enabling the design of buoyancy-neutral blades and preventing mass-related load fluctuations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to demonstrate the scalability of the present results, numerical simulations are performed using the in-house fluid–structure interaction solver to model a utility-scale turbine. 0 m s−1 and a 20-m diameter turbine is selected consistently with modern, state-of-the-art commercial turbines26 and typical energetic tidal sites27. 5), and therefore the present results are applicable to utility-scale turbines. Simulations performed at the respective Re and the same Ca confirm that power and thrust coefficient curves are similar at model and full scale (Extended Data Fig. Although E of the steel spar can be scaled up in numerical simulations, this is not possible in practice. A rated speed of u∞ = 3. Therefore, different full-scale spar design options are discussed in Supplementary Note 5.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, finally, rubber features high fatigue endurance. Preliminary calculations in Supplementary Note 6 show that the fatigue life of a full-scale rubber blade would substantially surpass the 20 years of service expected by state-of-the-art turbines.

Diungkapkan bahwa overall, by allowing similar control on power at thrust above rated speed than active pitch control systems, and mitigating load fluctuations, this technology offers a viable pathway to lower the lcoe. Furthermore, the reduction in load fluctuations enables deployment in energetic, highly turbulent sites previously deemed unviable due to the high fatigue loads. Further analysis of the potential industrial impact of this technology is presented in Supplementary Note 7.

Berdasarkan laporan, this experimental investigation has evaluated the performance of tidal turbine flexible rubber blades with passive chordwise flexibility, compared against conventional rigid blades. Our results confirmed that the power coefficient of the flexible blade at the design tip-speed ratio is comparable to that of its rigid counterpart, demonstrating that load mitigation benefits are achieved without penalty to the primary function of the turbine as an energy harvester.

Berdasarkan laporan, the main advantage of the flexible blades is their ability to deform, shedding the excess of load at off-design conditions. This reconfiguration allows control of power by manipulating the angular velocity of the turbine, while achieving passive mitigation of the high-frequency fluctuations that drive fatigue damage.

Berdasarkan laporan, therefore, the chordwise-flexible blades offer a compelling and robust alternative to state-of-the-art active pitch control. By mitigating loads with a much simpler setup, the flexible blade eliminates a significant source of potential failure and maintenance costs in offshore renewables.

Diungkapkan bahwa the mechanism for load mitigation is confirmed through dic measurement and a quasi-steady low-order code, which shows that the stiffness and initial geometry of the blade produce a controlled ‘feather’ as loads increase. The no-flow geometry and stiffness of the blade are designed so that, under flow conditions approaching the design point, it deforms toward the reference rigid-blade configuration.

Sebagaimana diketahui, looking ahead, this work opens up new pathways for tidal turbine design and cost reduction. The demonstrated reductions in peak and fatigue loading could allow a reduction in structural requirements for both the blades and their supporting structure, lowering capital costs and enabling higher generator ratings, which in turn improve rated capacity per unit mass. These factors contribute to a lower LCOE of tidal turbines, addressing the primary barrier to the large-scale deployment of tidal energy farms. Moreover, the increased robustness from the removal of the pitching system reduces operational and maintenance costs. By making the technology more financially viable, this technology offers a realistic and attractive option for renewable energy production.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all experiments were conducted in the flowave ocean energy research facility at the university of edinburgh, a circular combined wave–current basin designed for scaled testing of offshore renewable energy devices. The experiments were performed at six inflow velocities in the range u∞ = 0. 444–0. The tank has a diameter of 25 m and, for the present campaign, was operated in current-only mode with a working water depth of 1. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the results presented in the main text refer to four sets of blades: one set of rigid blades used as a baseline and three sets of rubber blades. The baseline rigid blades are CNC-machined (SS316) using a modified NACA 63-415 hydrofoil profile along the span. The profile was modified to ensure a blunt trailing edge, as specified in ref. These blades exhibited negligible flapwise and edgewise deformations. Notably, utility-scale tidal turbine blades exhibit some structural compliance. 31. However, here the model-scale rigid blade was deliberately made rigid to provide a defined geometry.

Diungkapkan bahwa the main text presents the results for the rigid blades and one set of rubber blades with the optimal stiffness. The flexible blades were manufactured by injecting a proprietary rubber mixture into a mould and around a steel spar. Conversely, the Extended Data figures also include results for the other two sets of rubber blades, with higher and lower stiffness than optimal. See Extended Data Fig. All rubber blades have the same mould geometry. 8 for schematics of the rubber blade. The aeroelastic properties of the blade are tailored along its span by varying the ratio of the rigid spar width to the local chord length, which increases from the tip towards the root with an average of 45%.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the thrust and torque are measured by a force transducer installed between the turbine rotor and the motor shaft (extended data fig. Calibration matrices for each sensor were obtained in situ before the test by applying known weights at four points along the cantilever beam attached to the sensor. The load cells were zeroed without flow before each set of measurements. The transducer is bespoke, manufactured by Applied Measurements, rated for an axial load of 1,300 N and a torque of 100 N m, and a resolution of 0. For each measurement, loads were recorded at a sampling frequency of 128 Hz for 300 s. 0004 N m, respectively. In this study, thrust is the net force measured by the hub transducer along the streamwise direction, and torque is the net edgewise moment about the hub axis. All force signals were transmitted to a National Instruments NI 9203 acquisition system through a slip ring. Moreover, each blade root was instrumented with a flapwise custom root-bending-moment sensor. 005 N and 0. 7). Rotor angular velocity was measured using an inductive proximity sensor that emitted one pulse per blade pass (three pulses per revolution), enabling determination of the revolution period and computation of the angular velocity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sensor accuracy and calibration uncertainties were propagated to the non-dimensional coefficients using standard bias-limit uncertainty analysis32, including thrust-torque transducer manufacturer specification (0. 1% of full-scale capacity) and primary uncertainties in u∞, ω and geometric parameters. For the present setup, the maximum total bias limits is of order 10−2 for CP and of order 10−2 for CT (representative values). Supplementary Note 1 provides the full derivations and tables.

Phase locking was achieved by using the proximity-sensor signal to trigger image acquisition as a blade passed a fixed azimuthal position, with a horizontal span and a downward tangential velocity. 56 m, sufficient to capture the full blade span (0. The camera system had a fixed focal length of 1. 1 m and a field of view of approximately 0. For each condition, between 89 and 447 instantaneous deformation fields were recorded over a 300 s period, depending on u∞ and λ.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, images were processed in lavision davis 11 using a subset size of 21 × 21 pixels and a grid step size of 2 × 2 pixels, resulting in a spatial resolution of approximately 0. A reference image in quiescent water was acquired before each set of measurements. 68 mm near the blade tip (approximately 2% of the tip chord). In the present configuration, DIC was used to measure the deformation of the suction-side surface of the blade. The full blade profile was reconstructed by combining the measured chord-line deformation with the known undeformed thickness distribution.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a bespoke fluid–structure interaction (fsi) solver was developed for the present study. This deformed blade geometry at equilibrium is then fed back into the outer BEMT loop to update the induction factors. Then, the pressure distributions from each blade section are combined to obtain a three-dimensional pressure distribution on the blade, which is used as input to Abaqus, in which a new deformed shape is computed. The process begins with an initial blade geometry. This iterative process continues until the blade shape converges. In the outer loop, the BEMT solver is used to calculate the axial and tangential induction factors on a finite number of blade sections at different radial coordinates. These values are used as initial conditions for the inner FSI loop. Then, the flow velocity and angle of attack experienced by each blade section are computed. This entire two-level process is repeated until convergence. The solver couples an in-house code based on blade element momentum theory (BEMT), with a panel method with an integral boundary-layer formulation (XFOIL), and a finite element analysis commercial software (Abaqus). This new shape is then discretized into sections and returned to XFOIL to recalculate the pressure field. The code uses a two-level iterative process, as schematically shown in Extended Data Fig. 9. First, the pressure distributions around each blade section are computed with XFOIL. The Abaqus model includes the steel spar. The power and thrust coefficients of the whole turbine are then computed by integrating the loads computed with XFOIL for each blade section and multiplying by three to account for the three-bladed turbine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this code was used to design the stress-free mould shape for each blade stiffness, ensuring that the equilibrium blade shape matches the reference rigid blade at the design flow speed and tip-speed ratio. In the full-scale simulations (Extended Data Fig. 5), the stiffness of both the spar and the rubber is 10. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the mould geometry xi,j is used as input, where i = 0 and j = 0 indicate the iteration number of the inner and outer loop, respectively. The inner loop is repeated till ∣∣Xi,j − Xi−1,j∣∣ is smaller than an acceptable threshold ϵi. The lift and drag coefficient curves (\({C}_{{{\rm{L}}}_{i,j}}(\alpha )\), \({C}_{{{\rm{D}}}_{i,j}}(\alpha )\)) are computed with XFOIL for various blade sections, and the induction factors (\({a}_{i,j},{a}_{i,j}^{{\prime} }\)) are computed with BEMT. If converged, the new geometry is Xi,j, where j is increased by one. Then the pressure distribution (pi,j(x)) around each blade section is computed with XFOIL and assembled into a three-dimensional load condition for Abaqus, where the new geometry is computed (Xi,j, with i increased by one). The outer loop is repeated from the computation of the lift and drag coefficient for the new geometry, till ∣∣Xi,j − Xi,j−1∣∣ is smaller than an acceptable threshold ϵj.

#531. Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife

📅 13 Nov 2026

Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11285-x

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Diungkapkan bahwa plastic pollution is a defining feature of the anthropocene1, and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats2,3,4,5,6,7, yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals’ proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.

Diungkapkan bahwa plastic pollution, once thought to be a predominantly aquatic issue, is increasingly being recognized as a threat to terrestrial ecosystems1. For wildlife exposed to microplastics, the small size and diverse chemistry of these particles facilitate ingestion11 and the penetration of biological membranes12,13. The high environmental mobility of microplastics has allowed them to infiltrate even the most pristine habitats8 where they can persist for centuries9,10. Microplastics (synthetic polymer particles with diameter less than 5 mm) are a particularly problematic form of plastic pollution, as these small particles are easily dispersed through pathways that include atmospheric deposition, precipitation, river transport and groundwater flow2,3,4,5,6,7. Once internalized, microplastics can bioaccumulate, biomagnify through food webs and pose severe health risks14,15,16,17,18.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although much work has been done on detecting microplastics in different biological compartments (reviewed in ref. Although such studies have proven informative for identifying the scope and scale of plastic pollution, this approach has left the bioaccumulation dynamics of microplastics in terrestrial environments poorly understood. Whether this is the case, however, is still largely unknown. As a result of this knowledge gap, even high-profile studies on plastic ingestion risk in wildlife have had to rely on assumptions about the relationship between individual habitat use and the uptake of microplastics rather than empirically grounded associations23. 19), studies in terrestrial ecosystems have largely been limited to descriptive surveys that document the presence of microplastics without investigating how these pollutants accumulate within wildlife20,21,22. Because both sources and dispersal pathways for microplastics are amplified by land-use change24,25,26, the intensity of human landscape modification should have a key role in shaping the internal microplastic burdens of terrestrial wildlife. With the continuing expansion of human-modified landscapes into wild spaces27 and the concomitant increase in global plastic production28, there is an urgent need to move beyond presence/absence studies and towards understanding the ecological and landscape-level factors that shape microplastic burdens in terrestrial species29.

Sebagaimana diketahui, here we integrate movement ecology, land-use data and in vivo contaminant measurements within the same individuals to investigate how the intensity and proximity of anthropogenic land-use change shape systemic microplastic burdens in terrestrial mammals. The role of anthropogenic disturbance in shaping internal plastic burdens is particularly pressing in regions facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil, where the extent of anthropogenic land-use change since the turn of the century has substantially outpaced the global average30,31 and deforestation, resource extraction, urbanization, agricultural intensification and an expanding road network are rapidly transforming the country’s landscapes30,32. By pairing in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution Global Positioning System (GPS) tracking data, we provide quantitative evidence that links individual-level habitat use and human landscape modification to systemic microplastic burdens in free-ranging terrestrial wildlife.

Diungkapkan bahwa between february 2021 and november 2022, we collected blood samples and high-resolution gps-based movement data from lowland tapirs (tapirus terrestris; n = 26) and giant anteaters (myrmecophaga tridactyla; n = 21) sampled at the arc of deforestation in the amazon, an agricultural mosaic in the cerrado, and a relatively undisturbed cattle ranch in the pantanal (fig. We then paired these data on in vivo microplastic burdens with the GPS tracking data to understand how inter-individual differences in habitat use and disturbance exposure shaped internal microplastic burdens. In particular, we quantified each individual’s exposure to human disturbance through the Human Footprint Index (HFI), a globally standardized measure of cumulative anthropogenic pressure ranging from 0 (undisturbed) to 50 (most heavily modified)33. For each individual, we quantified blood microplastic concentrations and polymer profiles using confocal Raman spectroscopy, detecting particles larger than 1 μm. 1a and Extended Data Table 1). We also examined local-scale effects through each animal’s proximity to the nearest human development (that is, the built environment including urban areas, mining infrastructure and power plants)34 and waste management facilities34.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although these results highlight how direct exposure to human-modified landscapes shapes internal microplastic burdens, plastic pollution is a transboundary issue with complex dispersal pathways36. The polymer profiles also varied across sampling sites in patterns that were broadly consistent with the dominant human activities at each site (Extended Data Figs. 94, P = 0. Focusing on direct HFI exposure alone can obscure such effects. Atmospheric deposition and waterborne transport are likely contributors, as airborne microplastics from urban, industrial and agricultural sources can travel long distances before settling in remote ecosystems, and rainfall runoff, river discharge and seasonal flooding redistribute particles across landscapes to habitats far from their original sources2,3,4,5,7,37. 3). Indeed, we found that the local-scale effects of human land use were particularly important in shaping the systemic microplastic concentrations of the monitored animals, with significant effects of distance to development (β = −0. 026, t = −2. 0057) and distance to the nearest waste management facility (β = −0. These relationships were all robust to sensitivity analyses (Extended Data Tables 2 and 3 and Supplementary Discussion) and highlight the role of anthropogenic land use in driving species’ exposure to plastic pollution. 032, t = −2. This finding is corroborated by several recent studies that reported substantial concentrations of microplastics in both aquatic environments and sediments throughout the Pantanal45,46,47, with the highest levels of microplastics (up to 1,174. Yet, we found microplastics in the blood of all of the individuals we sampled in the Pantanal, despite these animals living more than 65 km from the nearest development and more than 112 km from the nearest waste management facility. Unlike other biomes in Brazil, much of the Pantanal has remained ecologically intact owing to its remote location, limited infrastructure and seasonal flooding, which naturally regulate many human activities. Notably, even at an HFI of zero the model predicted blood microplastic concentrations of 10. 17 to 5. 2 particles per ml; intercept: β = 2. 2 items per m2) found near rivers flowing from urban areas46. 63 in 2020, representing a 26% increase. The Pantanal is the world’s largest and most pristine wetland, supporting an extraordinary diversity of wildlife within a relatively undisturbed landscape44. The relationship between human disturbance and blood microplastic concentrations identified here suggests that microplastic burdens in terrestrial wildlife will continue to rise as land-use change intensifies. 5 particles per ml (95% confidence interval 4. The plastic materials tied to the expanding human footprint thus have few barriers preventing them from becoming highly mobile environmental pollutants42. While we can not discount the potential that this non-zero intercept was the result of an unmodelled non-linear relationship at low HFI exposure, it does provide support that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. The seemingly pervasive reach of microplastic pollution is most strikingly illustrated by our findings from the animals in the Pantanal. Developing a mechanistic understanding of the pathways through which microplastics reach remote terrestrial ecosystems will be essential for protecting wildlife from this highly mobile pollutant. Although environmental sampling across these sites would strengthen the causal inference of these relationships by directly linking environmental polymer profiles to those detected in blood, isolation protocols for chemically diverse samples such as blood and soil complicate spectroscopy-based comparisons48,49. Across large parts of rural and interior Brazil, for example, solid waste collection remains inadequate and wastewater treatment is limited or absent altogether41,42,43. 92. This infrastructural gap leaves regions experiencing the most rapid change the least equipped to contain plastic waste. The presence of microplastics in the blood of animals living many tens of kilometres from the nearest development or waste facility highlights how microplastics are a threat not only to wildlife with direct exposure to human-modified landscapes, but also to species across even the most remote and ecologically intact environments8. This trend in land-use change was even more pronounced in Brazil, where the HFI rose by 42% over the same period, from 4. 58, P < 0. Problematically, anthropogenic land-use expansion often outpaces the development of waste management infrastructure39,40. 6–24. 36, t = 5. 001). 26 in 2001 to 6. Paired blood–environment sampling designs thus represent a productive, albeit challenging path forward.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by combining in vivo microplastic measurements with fine-scale movement data and high-resolution landscape disturbance indices, our study moves terrestrial microplastic research beyond detection surveys towards a spatially informed quantitative framework for predicting wildlife burdens from landscape context. This approach revealed how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics, and is readily transferable to other species and regions, offering a scalable tool for identifying vulnerable populations and informing targeted conservation responses. While no ecosystem is likely to be entirely free of microplastics50, we did find that animals in less disturbed habitats carried substantially lower burdens than those in close proximity to human infrastructure. These findings suggest that management efforts aimed at limiting animals’ exposure to human-modified environments and reducing their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure can serve to reduce the microplastic burdens carried by wildlife.

Berdasarkan laporan, the site in the amazon was located at tanguro farm, a privately owned 103,000 ha property in querência, mato grosso state, that sits at the transition between the cerrado savanna and the amazon rainforest along the southern arc of deforestation. Owned by AMAGGI, a major actor in Brazil’s soybean industry, the farm comprises 59,000 ha (57%) of croplands (soybean, corn, and cotton) and 44,000 ha (43%) of legally protected forest reserves. Forests in this region are shorter (~20 m) than the moist Amazon rainforest (~30 m). This region is the driest portion of the Amazon basin and experiences a prolonged dry season (May–September) with annual rainfall of 1,700–2,200 mm. About 40% of the farm was cleared for pasture (1976–1992) and later converted to soy cultivation (2003–2010), leaving riparian forests surrounded by croplands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, giant armadillos were captured between february 2021 and november 2022, using a method tailored to their natural behaviour56. Researchers tracked footprints and signs of recent predation, such as termite mounds, to locate burrows. When a burrow was identified and confirmed to contain an armadillo (indicated by the entrance being sealed with sand), an iron funnel trap (jequi-type) was placed at the entrance. Once captured, animals were transported in iron-reinforced wooden crates and held overnight for nocturnal species, with procedures beginning the following morning at the capture site.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, approximately 10 ml of blood was collected within 20 min of immobilization via venipuncture of the medial saphenous or cephalic veins using a sterile glass vacutainer system (bd vacutainer). Tapir captures were conducted in remote forest sites without access to field refrigeration. Blood samples were therefore stored in pre-cleaned glass collection tubes with no preservatives, sealed with clean aluminium foil and a metal cap to prevent contamination during storage, kept shaded at ambient temperature, and transferred to a −20 °C freezer on return to the base camp within 5–6 h.

Berdasarkan laporan, blood samples (~5 ml) were collected approximately 20 min after induction from the cephalic or saphenous veins using a sterile vacutainer system with 23g or 25g needles (bd vacutainer). Samples were transferred to pre-cleaned glass collection tubes with no preservatives, sealed with clean aluminium foil and a metal cap to prevent contamination during storage, kept refrigerated at 4 °C on site, and frozen at −20 °C within 12–24 h for subsequent processing. We note that blood samples were obtained from three individual giant armadillos, however we obtained repeat samples at two time points for two of these animals. Although these blood samples were processed individually, they were pooled (that is, averaged) in our statistical analyses.

Berdasarkan laporan, cold storage under the above-mentioned conditions is standard practice in microplastic analyses and does not affect particle abundance or polymer identity. Microplastics are chemically stable over these timescales, and method reviews emphasize that environmental samples containing microplastics are routinely stored at 4 °C for days to weeks prior to processing, or frozen at −20 °C for longer periods, without alteration of polymer composition (reviewed in ref. 57).

The mixture was incubated on a shaker at 60 °C and 250 rpm for 24 h. Depending on the sampling date, blood samples were stored at −20 °C for ~1–22 months between collection (Feb 2021–Nov 2022) and digestion (Dec 2022). The samples were then incubated under the same conditions (60 °C and 250 rpm) for an additional 24 h.

Sebagaimana diketahui, before analysis, we pre-processed the gps location data in order to calibrate the measurement error and filter outliers. We converted the HDOP values into calibrated errors by specifying 20-m error at an HDOP of 1 for 2D fixes, and 10-m error at an HDOP of 1 for the 3D fixes70. 1)69. 55% of the total 469,410 locations. 3. 2. Through this process we identified a total of 16,656 outliers, which represented ca. For each individual dataset, we then removed outliers based on error-informed distance from the median location, and the minimum speed required to explain each location’s displacement. Pre-processing was done via the methods implemented in the R package ctmm (v1. For each location estimate, the GPS trackers recorded a unitless Horizontal Dilution of Precision (HDOP), a value which is a measure of the accuracy of each positional fix. After filtering outliers, the final dataset consisted of 343,913 GPS locations across 20 individual giant anteaters, 6,072 GPS locations across 2 individual giant armadillos, and 102,769 GPS locations across 20 individual lowland tapirs.

Berdasarkan laporan, for each of the tracked animals, we used a continuous-time approach to estimate their movement rates and home ranges, enabling robust comparisons across individuals71. We first fitted a series of continuous-time stochastic process movement models to the location data. Parameters were estimated using perturbative-hybrid residual maximum likelihood (pHREML)72, and identified the best model via small-sample-sized-corrected Akaike’s information criterion (AICc). From both visual inspections of the semi-variograms, and the parameters of the fitted movement models, all animals occupied stable home ranges throughout the monitoring period with no indication of range shifts or large-scale dispersal events.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, from the selected models, we estimated each animal’s diffusion rate (in km2 day−1) as a measure of their movement rate. We next estimated each animal’s home range, using autocorrelated kernel density estimation (AKDE)73. AKDE home range estimates were conditioned on the autocorrelation structure of the fitted movement model, and we implemented the small-sample-size bias correction of Fleming & Calabrese (2017)74, as well as the optimal weighting of Fleming et al. (2018)75 to correct for uneven sampling. Home range areas (in km2) were estimated as the area contained within the polygon delimited by the 95% isopleth of the probability density.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we estimated the mean and maximum hfi within each individual’s home range. 38. A raster of HFI data with a spatial resolution of 100 m was obtained from Gassert et al. HFI is an aggregate measure of human disturbance that ranges from 0 in natural habitats to 50 in the most anthropogenically modified habitats33. We focused on habitats classified as water, development, agriculture, pasture, and native forest, which represented the majority of the land classes within the monitored animals’ home ranges. The proportions of each of these land classes within each animal’s home range were again estimated by calculating the weighted arithmetic mean. Development was a compound measure that captured the built environment, and was composed of the MapBiomas collection 10 classes: urban areas (24), mining (30), photovoltaic power plants (75), and other non-vegetated areas (25). We also estimated more nuanced patterns of habitat use via the MapBiomas database34, which details land use throughout Brazil at a spatial resolution of 10 m. Lastly, we used the MapBiomas land classification data, the Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI), and the Waste Methane Assessment Platform 1. From these spatial data, we estimated each animal’s mean distance to development and to the nearest waste management facility, estimated by calculating the weighted arithmetic mean.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to study how human land-use change shaped blood microplastic concentrations, we fit hierarchical generalized linear regression models using the methods implemented in the mgcv package (v1. 9-1)76. Because the microplastic concentrations scaled between [0,∞], we used a Tweedie distribution with a log link for the error distribution77, with parameters estimated via restricted maximum likelihood (REML). The regression models testing for correlations between individual habitat use and microplastic concentrations included a population-level effect, as well as random intercepts and slopes for each of the species, with the following general form.

Sebagaimana diketahui, where β0 represents the population-level intercept, β is the population-level slope, us[i] is the species-specific random intercept, vs[i] is the species-specific random slope, and s[i] indexes the species of individual i. This structure was used for all of the habitat covariates xi. From these models, inference was then made on the population-level trend.

Sebagaimana diketahui, no statistical method was used to predetermine sample size. Samples were processed in two batches, each with a procedural blank (Supplementary Methods); all lowland tapir samples were processed in the same batch. The polymer-integrity test shown in Extended Data Fig. Seven animals lacked sufficient GPS tracking data and were excluded from the habitat use models but retained in descriptive analyses. Each animal contributed one blood sample, with the exception of two giant armadillos sampled at two time points, whose values were averaged before analysis. This was an observational field study, so randomization was not applicable; animals were not allocated to experimental groups, and exposure to human land use was determined by each individual’s own space use. Sample sizes were determined by the number of animals that could be safely captured during the study period (February 2021 to November 2022) given the logistical constraints of live-capturing large, threatened, free-ranging mammals under national permits, and all animals captured during this period were sampled. The investigators were not blinded to species or sampling site during laboratory processing or analysis; however, particle detection and polymer identification were automated (Particle Scout and True Match software) and based on a fixed spectral-match threshold (HQI > 75%), which limits observer bias. 6 was repeated three times independently with similar results.

#532. Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice

📅 13 Nov 2026

Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11240-w

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nuclei in early mammalian embryos undergo epigenetic reprogramming that enables the zygote to develop into a complete organism. However, embryos that maintain nuclear deformability escape from this transcriptional interference. Nuclear stiffening by lamin B1 retention or its overloading results in incomplete activation of zygotic genes and impaired development. Whereas changes in chromatin state during this critical transition period have been extensively studied1,2,3, changes in the nucleus that houses chromatin remain poorly understood. An engineered molecular tether that stiffens the nuclei restricts these nuclear activities and suppresses expression of key zygotic gene activation genes. High-resolution microscopy and sequential three-dimensional fluorescence in situ hybridization analyses revealed an accumulation of active RNA polymerase II and coordinated positioning of key genomic loci near the deformable nuclear envelope. Here, using direct organelle capture and biophysical manipulation methods, we find that nuclei attain profound softness and plasticity during the two-cell embryonic stage in mice, facilitating major zygotic gene activation. The prominent nuclear deformability is attributable to the rapid clearance of lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope by the autophagy factor LC3. Together, our study identifies a distinct physical nuclear state that embryos acquire at the beginning of life that supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

Diungkapkan bahwa the physical characteristics of the cell nucleus are extraordinarily diverse, exhibiting distinct shape and mechanical phenotypes across tissue types, physiological states and disease conditions. Fragile or misshapen nuclei are hallmarks of cancer, cardiomyopathy and premature ageing4,5. Nuclei in stem cells gradually stiffen during differentiation4,5,6,7. While these changes are widely recognized as consequences of altered nuclear composition and chromatin dynamics, they also influence genome organization and transcription8,9,10. Despite the importance, the physical state of the nucleus at the earliest stages of mammalian development, when life begins, remains unclear.

Berdasarkan laporan, during the first few cleavages, nuclei undergo extensive epigenetic reprogramming, enabling the zygote to initiate a new developmental program. Lamins are long-lived, enriched in eggs and are crucial for mammalian development18,19,20. However, their dynamics and transiency, as well as the underlying core regulatory mechanism, during the earliest embryonic stages are poorly understood. In somatic cells, nuclear shape and mechanics depend on lamins, which line the inner nuclear membrane16,17. In mice, this transition occurs within the first approximately 48 h after fertilization and is associated with a surge in new transcript production, known as major zygotic gene activation (ZGA)11,12,13. Previous studies have documented that, of the two major types, A-type lamins exhibit cell-lineage-specific differential expression patterns, whereas B-type lamins are constitutively expressed throughout development16. Likewise, how the nuclear lamina, which forms a structural meshwork, controls nuclear mechanics and genome dynamics during this critical transition is unknown. Major ZGA occurs during the mid-to-late two-cell stage, and embryos that impair ZGA fail in subsequent development. By contrast, whether the nucleus organizing chromatin undergoes any crucial changes that drive ZGA is not known. Around the time of ZGA, chromatin exhibits distinct structural and biochemical changes accompanied by histone modifiers and transcription factors14,15. Investigating physical nuclear characteristics necessitates direct quantification and manipulation of their mechanical properties. However, achieving this without compromising cell viability poses a challenge.

Berdasarkan laporan, to investigate physical nuclear properties, we first performed high-resolution confocal scanning of fertilized mouse eggs during early cleavages (fig. and then gradually regressed by 32–36 h. Before the onset of deformation, two-cell nuclei had fully swollen and reached steady sizes; once deformed, the altered nuclear shapes persisted for hours (Extended Data Fig. i. (Fig. Our three-dimensional (3D) images of nuclei with H2B–mCherry, expressed without perturbing development (Extended Data Fig. p. 1e,f). 1e). p. i. ), peaked at 24–26 h. Two-cell nuclei underwent slow, incremental deformation, which started at around 21 h post-insemination (h. i. 1c,d and Supplementary Videos 1−3). 1b,c and Extended Data Fig. 1g) or mCherry–NLS for the nuclear interior (Extended Data Fig. 1a), revealed their distinct shape features, showing uneven local deformation at the two-cell stage in contrast to their predominantly spherical appearance at the one-cell and four-cell stages (Fig. 1a). 1d). Similar deformation was observed using emerin–eGFP for the nuclear envelope (Fig. Timelapse imaging revealed that one-cell nuclei remained spherical during the cell cycle (Fig. 1f) (Extended Data Fig. At the four-cell stage, nuclei were again spherical (Fig. 1b). p. 1g).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our study reveals physical characteristics of early embryonic nuclei and their distinct changes that facilitate zga. Our data show that the autophagy factor LC3 and lamin B1 clearance confer nuclear plasticity and softness, and that deformable nuclei are key to robust zygotic transcription. Extensive studies have profiled epigenetic states of chromatin and provided a genome-centred view of this critical developmental transition. Our study highlights the importance of physical nuclear state for this transition and underscores the need for integration of diverse embryonic parameters, including their subcellular material properties.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our work identifies a transient phase of nuclear deformability that manifests as cells transition through a totipotent state (fig. 5d–h). 4l,m). Notably, this nuclear change marks normal preimplantation development and contributes to transcription and gene locus movement (Figs. A flexible nuclear envelope may accommodate these internal and peripheral chromatin activities, mediating a mechanical conflict for the consolidation of functional genome architectures. 1). Our analysis also suggests that intense transcriptional activity near the deformable nuclear envelope enables the full activation of key ZGA genes that shape the two-cell epigenome14 (Fig. During ZGA, chromatin undergoes dynamic remodelling and compaction37,38,39, while maintaining contact with the nuclear lamina40. Notably, the sites of active DNA transactions appear a few μm beneath the nuclear envelope, often associated with local negative curvature, suggesting the generation of inward forces around these sites (Fig. 2, 4 and 5). Such mechanical control may also operate in naive embryonic stem cells, in which soft nuclei are linked to pluripotency and priming for differentiation41.

Berdasarkan laporan, we find that the embryonic mechanism governing lamin b1 clearance shares similarities with nuclear autophagy activated during oncogene-induced cell senescence23 (fig. As autophagy is accompanied by an increase in intracellular calcium levels and is independent of mTORC1 in early embryos21,42, the clearance is most likely developmentally programmed. 3). Our data suggest a role of nuclear translocation of LC3 and its distinct effect on nuclear shape and mechanics. Further analysis of its regulated nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling43 should reveal the mechanistic basis behind the physiological and pathological nuclear remodelling.

Third, soft and transcriptionally active nuclei, yet enriched with lamin B1 at the nuclear envelope, were prone to DNA damage (Extended Data Fig. Second, as lamins influence transcription44,45 and the chromatin–lamina contacts change during development40, understanding the interplay between mechanical cues and biochemical factors that ensures robust transcriptional control will be an essential next step. It remains to be explored whether the clearance of lamin B1 merely contributes to nuclear softening or controls DNA organization by sensing local nuclear curvature. First, our imaging assay detected diluted lamin B1 at convex regions of the nuclear envelope35 (Fig. As excess lamin B1 can cause persistent DNA damage46, autophagic clearance of lamin B1 may be necessary to protect against such damage. 5b,c). Berdasarkan laporan, physical nuclear stability is likely important for early embryos, given the potential mechanical challenges they face during passage through the uterine tube49. Early mammalian embryos are also prone to DNA lesions and chromosome missegregation50,51,52. Yet this period coincides with a transient state in which nuclei become less mechanically resilient. Understanding how embryos navigate the vulnerable state may reveal principles underlying developmental robustness.

Berdasarkan laporan, for image processing and quantitative analysis, raw nikon nd2 files from each hybridization round were opened in fiji with the bio-formats importer and automatically concatenated into a single five-dimensional (x, y, z, channel, time) hyper-stack. These bounding boxes were converted to regions of interest (ROIs); all voxels within each ROI were duplicated into individual multipage TIFF files, and integrated as well as mean fluorescence intensities were measured within a fixed 118 × 118 pixel window centred on the ROI. The DAPI channel was smoothed with a 3D mean filter (two-pixel kernel) and corrected for photobleaching using the bleach correction–simple ratio method. Sample drift within each stack was removed with the Correct 3D Drift plugin, using the DAPI signal as reference; the sequential imaging rounds were then co-registered by the Descriptor-based series registration plugin with an affine 3D +t model. Nuclear regions were identified in the corrected DAPI volume by Gaussian blurring (σ = 30 pixels), global thresholding, morphological closing and connected-component labelling with the 3D Objects Counter, generating bounding boxes for every nucleus. Out-of-focus slices were discarded. Each fluorescence channel was denoised with a three-dimensional median filter (1-pixel kernel). Finally, maximum-intensity projections, annotated overlays and the registered 3D image stacks were exported.

#533. Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA

📅 13 Nov 2026

Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11264-2

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Diungkapkan bahwa immunoglobulin a (iga) is the most abundant antibody isotype produced by mammals, and has a specialized role in mucosal homeostasis1. IgA is constantly secreted into the intestinal lumen and binds to commensal microorganisms to regulate their colonization and function2,3, with unclear implications for health. IgA deficiency is common in humans, but difficult to study, because of its complex aetiology and comorbidities4,5,6,7,8. In a reductionist culture system, IgA directly suppressed epithelial growth. In IgA-knockout mice, deleting the transmembrane and cytoplasmic signalling portions of DMBT1 was sufficient to reverse both the increased epithelial cell proliferation and the increased tumour susceptibility seen in these mice. Here we use genetically and environmentally controlled mice to show that various models of IgA deficiency result in increased susceptibility to several models of endogenous colorectal cancer. Cellular and molecular analyses revealed that, in the absence of IgA, colonic epithelial cells induce antibacterial factors and accelerate cell cycling in response to the microbiota. Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and targeted CRISPR screening identified DMBT1 as an IgA-binding epithelial surface protein that is required for IgA-mediated suppression of proliferation. Together, IgA and DMBT1 tune the normal cycling of absorptive colonocyte progenitors. Oral treatment with IgA was sufficient to reduce steady-state proliferation and protect mice from tumours; however, this function was due to the structure of the antibody rather than to binding specificity. These experiments establish a homeostatic function for IgA in tempering physiological epithelial responses to the microbiota to maintain mucosal health.

#534. Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia

📅 13 Nov 2026

Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11269-x

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Berdasarkan laporan, somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers1,2. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early drivers. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples3, collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. These faster-growing clones harbouring multiple driver mutations can cause complete somatic sweeps of the blood decades before diagnosis, a feature strongly associated with future acute myeloid leukaemia. Our data show that the clonal dynamics of blood are consistent with a set of remarkably simple evolutionary rules that strike a balance between chance and determinism.

Diungkapkan bahwa cancers develop through a process of darwinian evolution within tissues1,4,5,6. Although large-scale sequencing efforts over the last 20 years have provided comprehensive catalogues of the driver genes responsible for cancer development11,12,13, a complete quantitative understanding of the evolutionary dynamics governing how these drivers arise, expand and compete is lacking. Mutation, drift and selection in the large cell populations making up our tissues can result in the emergence of a clone that has acquired multiple genetic and epigenetic ‘driver’ alterations that disrupt tissue homeostasis and promote uncontrolled proliferation7,8,9,10. Why are cancer driver mutations widespread across many healthy human tissues2,14,15,16,17, yet cancers of many of these tissues are comparatively rare? Why in some people do initial clonal expansions progress to lethal cancers whereas in others they remain benign? What are the relative roles of chance and determinism in the evolution of cancer? Answers to these questions could guide more rational approaches to early cancer detection18, risk prediction19,20,21,22,23 and personalized intervention24,25.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, theories of oncogenesis on the basis of somatic evolution have existed since the 1950s and were used to explain the nonlinear increases in cancer incidence with age26. Applying similar approaches to cancer development, however, has proven challenging as serial samples of pre-cancerous tissue from asymptomatic individuals are difficult to obtain. These multi-stage models highlighted important roles for mutation26,27, selection28,29 and stem-cell population sizes30. However, these models have proven difficult to falsify with age-incidence data alone. Even when these tissues are available, they typically provide only a static snapshot of the somatic diversity present. The dynamics of molecular evolution, read-out using deep sequencing of serial samples, provide a more direct measure of the evolutionary dynamics and have transformed our understanding of microbial evolution31,32,33,34,35. To better understand the dynamics of pre-cancerous evolution requires serial samples collected with high temporal resolution.

Diungkapkan bahwa the haematopoietic system provides a unique opportunity to understand and quantify pre-cancerous evolution because serial blood samples in asymptomatic individuals can be collected antecedent to cancer development. We reasoned that serial blood samples collected regularly over decade-long timescales in people who subsequently develop AML could be used to better understand the evolutionary origins of AML. This phenomenon, termed clonal haematopoiesis, increases the risk of future blood malignancies such as AML19,20,21,22,23. Although some aspects of clonal haematopoiesis evolution have begun to be understood quantitatively38,39,40,41,42,43, our understanding of how these age-related changes evolve into AML is incomplete. Healthy blood displays ubiquitous and pronounced age-related changes driven by positive selection for genetic alterations that are recurrently mutated in acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) (for example, DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1)19,20,21,22,23,36,37. By leveraging developments in error-correctable sequencing44,45 and insights from evolutionary theory32,46,47, we sought to characterize when in life the key driving events of AML occur and to gain insights into the rules governing their establishment, growth and competition.

These 47 women were diagnosed with AML at a median age of 72 years (range 53–83 years) and had up to 10 serial blood samples (median 5) available before diagnosis (Fig. To precisely track the evolutionary dynamics in these longitudinal samples, we designed a highly sensitive sequencing strategy called TETRIS-seq. 1 and Supplementary Note 1). 1b, Methods and Supplementary Note 2). 1a, Extended Data Fig. One control was subsequently excluded owing to development of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). We obtained 249 pre-AML blood serum samples from these 47 women, as well as 249 timepoint-matched samples from 47 age-matched controls who remained cancer free. This approach incorporates duplex error-corrected sequencing44 of a panel that comprehensively covers clonal haematopoiesis- and AML-associated genomic alterations, including gene mutations, chromosomal rearrangements and mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs), in combination with a custom in silico de-noising algorithm (Fig. We identified all the women who subsequently developed AML during more than 12 years of follow-up, of whom 47 had sufficient blood sample available from at least two timepoints before AML diagnosis. Using TETRIS-seq we reliably achieved a duplex consensus depth of greater than 1,500×, enabling robust detection of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and indels at variant allele frequencies (VAFs) ≥0. Using the longitudinal nature of our samples, we phased single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) on sections of chromosomes affected by mCAs, enabling detection of chromosomal gains, losses and copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity (CN-LOH) events ≥5 Mb down to approximately 1% cell fraction (Supplementary Note 2k,l).

Diungkapkan bahwa we reasoned that the high sensitivity and temporal resolution of our data could be used to gain a quantitative understanding of how driver mutations expand and compete in the decades preceding aml diagnosis (fig. In this framework the dynamics of a given clone are determined by its occurrence time, fitness effect and the simplest interaction term: an increasing ‘mean fitness’ of all other clones in the population that ensures the population frequencies of all clones sum to 1. 3). We developed a mathematical framework for predicting how clones expand and compete through time inspired by models of microbial evolution32,46. The dynamics of a specific variant are determined by summing the frequency of the original parental clone (that is, the first clone to acquire the variant) and all daughter clones that inherited the variant (Fig. 3a–c).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, overall, these findings demonstrate that, once established in the hsc pool, the dynamics of pre-leukaemic clones are surprisingly predictable. Although we cannot exclude extrinsic effects altering some clones, one does not need to invoke more complex scenarios to explain the data: one can achieve remarkably close fits to variant trajectories by assuming clones have an intrinsic fitness and compete globally for one resource with minimal spatial structure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the quantitative picture of the evolutionary dynamics afforded by our data highlights several important features. Second, pre-leukaemic clones are subject to strong positive selection, with fitness advantages that vary by two orders of magnitude: ranging from 10% per year for the least fit single-mutant clones to 1,000% per year for the fittest quadruple-mutant clones. First, transformation usually involves the acquisition of multiple driver mutations in the same clone (range, 2–6), with considerable inter-patient variation in when these driver events are acquired. Third, the variant frequency trajectories exhibit diverse qualitative behaviours, suggesting strong clonal competition in some cases (for example, C92_012 and C92_022) but a complete absence of competition in other cases (for example, C92_005 and C92_007).

Berdasarkan laporan, despite its simplicity, this model reproduces many of the qualitative and quantitative features observed in our data. The variant frequency trajectories in the decades preceding virtual AMLs in this model also exhibit a similar spectrum of qualitative behaviours to the observed pre-AML cases, including examples of selective sweeps, reversals of growth, multiple reversals of fortunes and late rapid expansions (Fig. 5c). The model predicts a strongly increasing incidence of AML with age, in close quantitative agreement with the observed real-world incidence of AML (Fig. 5b). 5d). Both linear and branched patterns of evolution emerge under this model, with the linear pattern predicted to be more common (Fig. Despite the simulated controls being governed by an identical evolutionary process, these behaviours are almost entirely absent from controls (Extended Data Fig. 10a–d), demonstrating the profound effect that conditioning on a rare outcome can have on the observed dynamics.

Berdasarkan laporan, we next explored whether this model could provide insights into features of the evolutionary dynamics that identify future aml cases. 5e). In our evolutionary model, around 99% of virtual AML cases have had at least one full somatic sweep more than 5 years before diagnosis and about 98% have had at least one sweep more than 10 years before diagnosis. To check how predictive these somatic sweeps are of future AML, we considered all simulated individuals that acquired at least one driver variant that could have been filtered out as ‘germline’ in low-depth sequencing data (VAF > 30%), broken down by age (Fig. Simulated variant frequency trajectories plotted over a 50-year period revealed that most future AMLs in this model derive from instances in which a single-mutant or double-mutant variant has already completely swept the blood more than a decade before virtual AML (Extended Data Fig. 10e). The presence of a second somatic driver (VAF > 10%) in addition to the first sweep identifies a group at high risk of future AML, with a positive predictive value about 88% (44 of 50) at age 40, about 75% (214 of 292) at age 50, about 50% (564 of 1,152) at age 60 and about 22% (719 of 3,313) at age 70.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the presence of somatic sweeps could be used to identify groups at high risk of future aml that have previously been missed owing to the inability to distinguish somatic sweeps from germline variants21,22. 7 × 10–67, Fisher’s exact test). To demonstrate this, we considered individuals in the UK Biobank whose baseline blood sample contained somatic variants at VAFs high enough to be hard to distinguish from germline variants in low-depth whole-exome sequencing or whole-genome sequencing data (VAF > 30%, Fig. 5f). Considering variants at well-known somatic hotspot positions (Methods), in which the likelihood of germline variation is substantially lower, we find that individuals with at least one somatic sweep are at considerably increased risk of a future myeloid leukaemia relative to those without (odds ratio 107, 95% confidence interval 75–150, P = 2. This finding suggests filters imposed for removing germline variants from somatic variant calls may be removing complete somatic sweeps that are strongly associated with future AML risk.

Berdasarkan laporan, these data have produced a quantitative picture of how aml evolves from precursor clones in the decades preceding diagnosis. The fitnesses of these early pre-leukaemic clones are similar to those observed in clonal haematopoiesis39,42,43 and in our age-matched healthy controls. In these early stages the blood is usually polyclonal with multiple single-mutant clones expanding in parallel from low cell fraction, as observed in clonal haematopoiesis41. Estimates for the acquisition ages and fitness effects for the key driving events highlight that in most cases the first steps of the multi-step path to AML occur early in life. The dynamics of early driver variants are still dominated by positive selection rather than drift, but they expand slowly: taking years to double in size and decades to become detectable.

Diungkapkan bahwa the acquisition of further drivers on the background of these initial slow-growing clones seems to be a defining difference between controls and future aml cases. 5e). Given existing estimates for \(N\tau \) ≈ 105 years in humans38,39,41, our data indicate that, at every point in the multi-stage path to AML, the rate at which driver mutations are acquired is around 10−5 per cell per year, consistent with thousands of sites in the genome offering mutational paths to increasing fitness. In controls such multiple-mutant clones are rare: a double-mutant clone expanding to high VAF is expected to occur in fewer than 1 in 3,000 60-year-olds (Fig. In most pre-AML cases the initial slow-growing clone produces daughter clones carrying two, and later three or four, driver mutations that grow far more rapidly than the single-mutant clones. This conceptual framework may therefore partially reconcile the fact that cancer drivers are common in healthy tissues2,14,15,16,17, while still predicting that cancer itself would be relatively rare50. This evolutionary framework may also provide a natural way of incorporating recent findings on environmental risk factors51. Although fitness-increasing mutations are common at every stage, the probability that the full complement of drivers required for transformation are acquired in a given person is a small, albeit strongly increasing, function of age. These patterns emerge when the population size is large enough that fitness-increasing mutations are not rare, but not so large that they are very common (\(\theta =N\tau \mu \,\approx 1\)). At these later stages, the blood is often oligoclonal: multiple double- and triple-mutant clones arise on independent lineages and, because of their larger fitness effects, expand and compete with each other, producing classic patterns of clonal interference31,46,49. Exposures that increase the fitness of mutant clones would potentially promote oncogenesis, whereas exposures that suppress it would be protective.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, stochasticity plays a crucial role in these dynamics. The acquisition of highly fit double- and triple-mutant clones early in life seems to be a key determinant of future AML risk. Identifying early somatic sweeps in large-scale cohorts such as the UK Biobank is challenging owing to filtering of germline variants at high VAF. We observe this in at least a third of the 47 pre-AML cases—a conservative estimate as our panel misses some driver events. This is exemplified by early complete sweeps of the blood in which all blood cells derive from a single HSC ancestor. We speculate that risk prediction for future AML may be substantially improved by identifying somatic sweeps, for example, by removing germline contaminants using a second tissue sample such as buccal swabs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the fact that the second and third ‘hits’ typically occur more than a decade before diagnosis provides a long window of opportunity for intervention. The IDH2 R140Q double-mutant in C92_007 is a case in point. It expands exponentially for 14 years with a fitness effect of approximately 115% before diagnosis (Fig. Owing to the exponential nature of the clonal growth, even modest reductions in growth rate, compounded over decades, can have a profound effect on the size of pre-leukaemic clones and thus on the probability of them acquiring further transforming mutations. Were the growth of this clone to be reduced (for example, using an IDH inhibitor24 or a neoantigen vaccine25), it is tempting to speculate whether AML could have been prevented. 3e). We therefore speculate that low-toxicity interventions producing such reductions in high-risk clones may substantially reduce the risk of transformation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a limitation of our study is that we do not have direct access to diagnostic material, meaning we cannot be certain that the clones detectable in the pre-aml samples actually gave rise to the aml. Their absence in our samples strongly suggests they are late-occurring events. Indeed, there are interesting differences between the spectrum of mutations we find in pre-AML and those typically seen at AML diagnosis, for example, in patients aged 60 years or over, NPM1 and FLT3 mutations are found in 25–35% of cases52, and the chromosomal rearrangements targeted in our study are found in about 10% (ref. 53), yet both are rare in our cohort. These factors limit the completeness and certainty of ontogeny classification (for example, de novo versus secondary AML), although a subset of cases had clearly documented antecedent myeloid disease or previous cytotoxic therapy allowing confident classification (Supplementary Note 5). Approximately 20% of pre-AML cases in our cohort display either no clonal expansions or only rapid expansions limited to the 1–2 years before diagnosis. Two of these expansion-positive cases (C92_048 and C92_052) carried germline DDX41 variants. Importantly, incomplete ontogeny classification reflects not only limitations of clinical data capture but also the fact that early myeloid disease may remain clinically silent, particularly in older adults in whom age-related clonal haematopoiesis is common. Registry-based ascertainment may not capture all diagnoses or treatments. A clinical limitation of this study is that information on antecedent myeloid disease and previous chemotherapy was derived from registry linkage rather than direct clinical record review. Evidence from deep targeted methylation sequencing54 strongly suggests 50% (5 of 10) of these cases do contain a pre-existing clonal expansion (for example, C92_048, C92_052, C92_072), whereas others do not (for example, C92_055, C92_063). Furthermore, in some cases it is likely that the final transforming event occurs after our last blood sample. Accordingly, our cohort reflects the spectrum of biological and clinical backgrounds typical of AML arising in older adults, and the evolutionary dynamics identified represent processes operating across this real-world population rather than a single ontogeny-defined subgroup.

Sebagaimana diketahui, our model assumes a constant effective hsc population size, and biological factors such as pre-leukaemic stem-cell expansion or differentiation blocks could influence the relationship between vaf and true clonal burden. Consequently, our fitness estimates should be interpreted as the effective competitive advantage relative to the background population.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a surprising finding in our data was how predictable and deterministic the dynamics of established clones are. Variant trajectories are remarkably consistent with the simplest model of clonal competition: that is, that clones compete only via a global interaction term requiring that their frequencies sum to 1. This suggests that, by the time clones have grown to be greater than 0. 2% cell fraction in the blood, the effects of spatial structure in the bone marrow are averaged out owing to mixing and re-seeding of multiple niches55,56.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one aspect of the simple evolutionary model that does not agree with the observed data is the 20% of cases exhibiting late evolution. Our multi-stage model generally predicts such cases to be very rare. First, the model does not account for AML driven by a single ultra-rare event, for example, an AML-defining translocation such as t(15;17); PML::RARA. We believe there are two possible explanations. Second, it is possible that a pre-leukaemic clonal expansion has occurred outside of our sequencing panel. Although we do target the vast majority of known AML drivers, it is likely there remain rare AML drivers to be discovered, as suggested by clonal expansions of unknown genetic origin seen in clonal haematopoiesis41. This probably explains some of the cases, such as C92_052, for which our analysis of methylation54 strongly suggests the presence of a fully swept clone.

Berdasarkan laporan, our ability to measure how somatic evolution shapes, and is shaped by, disease risk is a new frontier of human genetics57. Our work is a step towards a complete quantitative understanding of AML development. The haematopoietic system is an ideal model for developing a quantitative understanding of somatic evolution owing to its ease of sampling, its relative lack of spatial structure and the existing quantity of large datasets. Further work is needed to understand whether and to what extent these principles translate to other cancers.
