Sebagaimana diketahui, our earlier attempts to label nup98 with various live-cell dyes were hindered by low signal-to-noise ratios, limiting measurement accuracy26. The recently developed silicon rhodamine derivative HDye653 (HD653) features a self-quenching tetrazine moiety that is activated on reaction with BCN28, reducing background fluorescence from unreacted or non-specifically bound dye. Its short linker also makes HD653 suitable for anisotropy measurements.

Berdasarkan laporan, to validate this approach, we expressed nup98 bearing bcn at residue 221 (nup98a221tag; methods) in cos-7 cells. On reaction with HD653, a distinct nuclear rim signal was observed (Fig. 1a,b), confirming efficient incorporation and labelling. 1b and Extended Data Fig. By contrast, substituting BCN with a non-clickable ncAA, t-butyloxycarbonyl-l-lysine (BOC) abolished the signal.

Berdasarkan laporan, the short linker of hd653 minimizes independent rotational motion of the dye29, increasing sensitivity to local segmental motion of the labelled fg-nup. TRFA measurements of purified enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) site-specifically labelled with HD653 or the established anisotropy dye Cy3B30,31 yielded hydrodynamic radii consistent with wild-type EGFP (Extended Data Fig. 1c and Methods), supporting HD653 as a reliable anisotropy probe for FG-NUP dynamics.

Berdasarkan laporan, trfa resolves a fast local dye-motion component and a slower anisotropy-decay component in an idp such as nup98 (fig. Accumulating photon counts from many cells at each labelling site, together with multi-exponential fitting, enabled reproducible estimation of this component for relative comparison. Because the fluorescence lifetime of HD653 is about 4 ns, the longer-timescale anisotropy component is estimated by model-based fitting rather than directly resolved in the fluorescence decay (Methods). 1c and Methods)32,33. We denote the fitted timescale of the latter as ρslow and use it as an apparent segmental-motion metric, rather than as a precise conventional rotational correlation time. Accordingly, lower ρslow values indicate faster apparent segmental motion, whereas higher values indicate progressively more restricted motion.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, using this framework, we systematically introduced bcn at 15 sites spanning the first and second fg domains of nup98 and labelled them in live cos-7 cells with hd653 (fig. Interestingly, a position-dependent trend emerged along the FG domains (Fig. 1g): sites closer to the N terminus, which extend towards the pore centre, exhibited faster apparent segmental motion, whereas those near the anchoring domain were more restricted. 1 and 2). 1e–g, Extended Data Fig. 1d). TRFA decays were collected using a custom-built single-photon-counting confocal microscope (Methods), yielding fitted slow-component timescales, ρslow, ranging from 57 ± 2 to 108 ± 5 ns (Fig. 1d and Supplementary Figs. This spatial gradient is consistent with previous findings that FG regions tethered near the NPC scaffold experience greater confinement3,34.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, together, these measurements capture the apparent segmental motion of nup98 fg domains on the tens-of-nanoseconds timescale. Probing slower motions, for example on microsecond timescales, would require complementary techniques such as polarized fluorescence correlation spectroscopy35. In spatial terms, structural correlations in IDPs typically extend over no more than about 50 residues31,33, indicating that this readout primarily reflects local segmental dynamics in this range.

This was accompanied by a progressive slowdown in apparent segmental motion, consistent with previous observations that FG condensates undergo molecular ageing, eventually forming a solid-like hydrogel4. 1h), reflecting their higher flexibility. By contrast, freshly formed FG condensates (in the first 5 min) initially exhibited apparent segmental motion similar to that observed in live cells but gradually transitioned to a more solid-like state over an hour (Fig. For the same labelling site tested in cells (residue 221), isolated FG chains exhibited considerably faster anisotropy decay (Fig. 1j and Supplementary Video 1; compare the stable live-cell measurements in Fig. 1h and 2a,b, Extended Data Fig. 1j), indicating the emergence of amyloid-like structures during maturation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, analysis of further labelling sites in nup98 confirmed that all tested residues exhibited slower apparent segmental motion as the condensates matured into a hydrogel state (fig. 2c). Notably, residue 100 showed the most pronounced reduction in apparent segmental motion. 1i). Thus, rather than being an outlier, this result aligns with the high propensity of this region to form amyloid-like assemblies. By contrast, no such transition was observed in live cells, even over extended measurement windows (for example, 2 h in Fig. This residue lies in a region recently identified by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy as a particularly aggregation-prone FG-rich segment (amino acids 85–124)11. These findings underscore a critical difference between the stable liquid-like dynamics of NUP98 observed in the cell and its time-dependent aggregation seen in vitro, raising the important question of what physiological factors prevent FG-NUPs from maturing into a gel-like state in their native environment.

Berdasarkan laporan, finally, we asked whether the simulation framework captures the relative segmental-dynamics trends measured by trfa. These relative trends parallel the experimental apparent segmental-motion trends (Fig. 1h). 9 and 10). The simulations showed that the bond-vector correlations decayed fastest in isolated chains and slower in bulk condensates and the NPC, reflecting the increased confinement imposed by neighbouring chains (Extended Data Fig. 7 and Supplementary Figs. We did not include molecular ageing in simulations of FG condensates, so we did not reproduce their long-time slowing; nevertheless, the relative hierarchy indicates that the model captures the principal effects of confinement, FG–FG interactions and FG–importin-β binding.

Berdasarkan laporan, the partial ability of importin-β to delay, but not completely prevent, the solidification of fg condensates in vitro (fig. 2d) indicated that further mechanisms must contribute to maintaining FG-domain dynamics in the NPC. O-GlcNAcylation has been implicated in modulating FG-hydrogel material properties48 and nuclear transport rates49, yet its effect on nanosecond-scale FG-domain dynamics has remained unknown. Among potential candidates, O-GlcNAcylation is particularly compelling because FG-NUPs are among the most heavily O-GlcNAc-modified proteins in metazoan cells, and NUP98 is itself heavily O-GlcNAcylated47,48. O-GlcNAcylation is a reversible PTM in which a single GlcNAc moiety is attached to serine or threonine residues by O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) and removed by O-GlcNAcase. To address this gap, we perturbed O-GlcNAc levels in live cells and in vitro.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, pharmacological inhibition of ogt with osmi-4 reduced global o-glcnac levels, as confirmed by rl2 immunoblotting, and slowed apparent segmental motion at several positions in the second fg domain of nup98 (fig. By contrast, O-GlcNAcase inhibition with Thiamet-G produced little further increase in apparent segmental motion (Fig. 8a). The spatial pattern broadly followed predicted O-GlcNAcylation propensities (Extended Data Fig. 4a,b). 4a), indicating that endogenous O-GlcNAcylation is already sufficient to support nanosecond-scale flexibility of FG domains under physiological conditions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the absence of o-glcnacylation (fgly = 0), fg-nups collapsed into a dense surface condensate surrounding the npc scaffold (fig. 5b–d and Supplementary Videos 7–9). 5e) and yielded 48 predicted O-GlcNAcylation sites, closely matching the 46 sites identified experimentally in Xenopus NUP9848. An O-GlcNAcylation level of fgly = 0. Increasing O-GlcNAcylation progressively expanded FG domains into the central channel (Fig. 3 reproduced the experimentally measured RE of NUP98 FG domains particularly well (Fig. 5a and Supplementary Video 6), leaving a large central void and producing NUP98 chain extensions inconsistent with previous in situ FLIM–FRET measurements26 (Fig. 5e). Higher O-GlcNAcylation levels yielded progressively more extended chains.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, o-glcnacylation also accelerated bond-vector relaxation, mirroring the experimental trend in which nup98 fg domains exhibit faster segmental dynamics inside the npc than in unglycosylated in vitro condensates, yet slower dynamics than isolated chains (figs. 9 and Supplementary Fig. 15). The effect of explicit O-GlcNAcylation on FG-NUPs can be reproduced by implicitly weakening FG-NUP attractive interactions through an interaction-rescaling parameter, α (Extended Data Fig. 1h and 5f and Supplementary Fig. 15). Remarkably, by then matching the RE of NUP98 to the FLIM–FRET measurements, we find the FG-NUPs to be near the critical point for phase separation in the Martini model, where relatively small changes in effective interactions can strongly alter FG-NUP organization, confirming our earlier observations from the residue-level coarse-grained FG-NUP models26.

Berdasarkan laporan, because o-glcnacylation weakens effective fg–fg interactions, we next asked whether differences in modification state could also influence mixing between fg assemblies. Simulations and selective-partitioning experiments showed that differences in O-GlcNAcylation promote demixing between otherwise similar FG assemblies (Supplementary Figs. 16–18 and Methods). Thus, differences in FG-NUP PTMs, including O-GlcNAcylation in metazoans and potentially O-mannosylation or phosphorylation in yeast, may tune FG–FG interaction strengths in ways that oppose mixing21.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, together, the combination of martini and residue-level coarse-grained simulations recapitulates key mesoscopic and microscopic features—from chain extension and apparent segmental motion to importin-β partitioning and transport behaviour—and bridges simplified in vitro studies with the crowded environment of the intact npc. These results highlight how O-GlcNAcylation and importin-β make complementary contributions to maintaining liquid-like FG-domain conformational dynamics and generating the spatial and dynamic heterogeneity characteristic of the permeability barrier.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by combining site-specific labelling with picosecond trfa, we directly monitored conformational dynamics of fg-nups in living cells. NUP98 retained rapid apparent segmental motion even in regions that aggregate readily in vitro, sharply contrasting with aged FG condensates that transition into solid-like hydrogels. Their progressive loss of apparent segmental motion is consistent with amyloid-like interactions observed by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and electron microscopy12,36.

Berdasarkan laporan, the discrepancy raises a key question: why do fg domains rapidly age into hydrogels in vitro4,5,13, yet remain dynamic in one of the cell’s longest-lived protein assemblies19,51? nucleocytoplasmic transport depends on ultrafast, reversible fg–fg and fg–ntr interactions, with thousands of transient sequential contacts supporting millisecond cargo passage24,25. We identify importin-β and O-GlcNAcylation as two factors that tune this behaviour. The apparent segmental motion detected by TRFA therefore provides a dynamic context for the rapid exchange of transient FG–NTR contacts during transport. Each partially suppresses molecular ageing in vitro, whereas together they reproduce the apparent segmental-motion trends measured in living cells (Extended Data Fig. 8f).

Diungkapkan bahwa molecular-dynamics simulations further showed how importin-β contributes to this stabilization. Importin-β dilutes aggregation-prone FG segments, swells condensates and enhances apparent segmental motion. Although chaperone-like properties of importin-β have been proposed previously36,37,38, our work demonstrates how it modulates FG-domain dynamics at the segmental level, particularly when FG–FG interactions are strengthened, consistent with the karyopherin-centric model of the NPC barrier10,52.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ptms provide another regulatory layer. However, selectively perturbing NUP98 phosphorylation in live cells remains challenging. By contrast, the extensive O-GlcNAcylation of NUP9847,48 allowed direct perturbation here. Altering O-GlcNAc levels changed both apparent segmental motion of FG domains and nuclear transport (Fig. Phosphorylation has been proposed to modulate FG-domain dynamics53, and NUP98 hyperphosphorylation promotes NPC disassembly54. 4e,f), linking O-GlcNAc–dependent tuning of FG-NUP dynamics to NPC function.

Berdasarkan laporan, serendipitously, our simulations also show the radial organization of the npc barrier. Our simulations further indicate that this organization emerges naturally from FG-NUP grafting geometry39 and locally elevated FG density near the pore wall. The peripheral distribution agrees with recent three-dimensional MINFLUX tracking of NTR-bound cargos14 and with our two-dimensional MINFLUX measurements. Under experimentally matched interaction strengths (\(\widetilde{{\epsilon }}\)FG–Imp-β = 0. 42), importin-β was enriched near the pore periphery, whereas extended FG domains occupied the centre; increasing FG–importin-β affinity instead drove importin-β to cluster in the pore centre (\(\widetilde{{\epsilon }}\)FG–Imp-β = 0. 3b,c and Supplementary Videos 3 and 4). 5; Fig. Consequently, importin-β exposure may vary along NUP98, potentially leading to position-dependent rescue of apparent segmental motion (Fig. 4c).

Sebagaimana diketahui, these findings provide a complementary perspective on central plug-like densities reported by electron microscopy55,56 and high-speed afm studies21. Our data do not exclude importin-β from central plug-like densities, but indicate that the central axis is not its predominant location. Differences in NPC conformation may partly underlie these observations, as in situ cryo-electron tomography shows a wider central channel in native cellular NPCs than in isolated preparations39. Because our MINFLUX measurements use NUP96 as a scaffold reference without directly resolving the inner-ring diameter, we cannot exclude effects of NPC dilation or constriction on the apparent importin-β distribution. One possible framework is a dual-route organization in which small and medium-sized cargos that interact efficiently with NTRs preferentially use the periphery, whereas larger or more slowly transported cargos occupy the central channel. Moreover, the central plug shown by AFM is highly mobile21, consistent with a dynamic transport-associated assembly rather than a rigid structure. In this view, some central densities could represent transient cargo or transport complexes rather than a permanent plug.

Diungkapkan bahwa more broadly, our study illustrates how cellular context can preserve functional dynamics of idps in crowded environments, with implications for diseases linked to fg-nup dysfunction, including cancer, viral infection and neurodegenerative disease57,58. Combining in-cell fluorescence measurements with multiscale computational modelling provides a general strategy for probing IDP conformational dynamics in their native cellular environment.

#539. Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti

📅 13 Nov 2026

Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11265-1

Berdasarkan laporan, thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Sebagaimana diketahui, extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change1. Their effects on species’ distributions and extinction risk remain poorly understood2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9. Most species distribution models rely on long-term mean climate, overlooking potentially important nonlinear effects of extremes. Across emissions scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) SSP1-2. 5) with 100-km dispersal, including severe drought increased the share of species losing suitable climatic area from 58–61% to 69–72%. Here we integrate new spatial data on severe drought10, including compounding effects of warmer temperatures, with a comprehensive curated dataset of cactus occurrences (648,316 records) and species distribution models to assess how severe drought alters projected suitable climatic area for 993 species of Cactaceae, a highly threatened family11 that is commonly considered drought tolerant. The proportion of species projected to lose over a quarter of suitable area increased from 26–43% to 55–58%, and the proportion projected to lose over four-fifths increased from 1–15% to 25–35%. In 91% of cases, models including severe drought were better supported than mean-climate models. These declines reduced regional richness, with five bioregions potentially losing over 25% of species. With severe drought, restricting dispersal from 100 to 0 km increased the share losing suitable area from 69–72% to 84–85% across SSPs. 6 to SSP5-8. These findings demonstrate that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability under climate change. Integrating climatic extremes into ecological forecasting will be critical for assessing biodiversity loss and designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems.

#540. Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics

📅 13 Nov 2026

Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11272-2

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Diungkapkan bahwa aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints1,2. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability3. Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

Berdasarkan laporan, modern silicon transistors continue to improve with technological advancement. To achieve substantial power reductions, device operation at reduced supply voltages has been explored extensively4,5. However, as scaling progresses, power efficiency has emerged as a critical constraint, especially for ultra-low-energy applications such as wearable electronics, implantable medical devices, Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, edge AI processors and distributed sensor networks. Nevertheless, silicon’s relatively small bandgap inherently increases leakage, while maintaining strong electrostatic control at scaled dimensions remains challenging6. A recent simulation study that compares silicon transistors with planar 2D field-effect transistors (FETs) from 16 nm to 1 nm technology nodes highlighted the low-power potential of 2D FET-based circuits7. These observations motivate the investigation of 2D semiconductors for low-power operation8,9,10,11,12.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the sizable bandgaps of 2d semiconductors suppress off-state current, while their atomically thin van der waals (vdw) structure enables excellent gate control, making them well suited for energy-efficient operation. Clean vdW integration of gate dielectrics with 2D semiconductors also minimizes interfacial traps caused by direct deposition processes21,22,23,24. 13,14,15), MoS2-MoTe2 (ref. High-permittivity, crystalline dielectric or buffer layers have been used to improve gate controllability by increasing gate capacitance and suppressing defect-induced degradation18,19,20. Most critically, WSe2-based p-FETs often have pronounced bipolar transfer characteristics, which are incompatible with robust CMOS operation and integration. One major source of this asymmetry is the gate stack: an imperfect 2D/high-κ interface degrades subthreshold swing, whereas unintentional dielectric-induced doping shifts the threshold voltage (Vth), impairing inverter performance. However, these demonstrations rely on non-scalable approaches, such as mechanically exfoliated flakes or lateral assembly of dissimilar materials and devices. Proof-of-concept inverters assembled from n- and p-type 2D semiconductors—including MoS2-WSe2 (refs. Their voltage gains are also limited (Extended Data Table 1), primarily because of asymmetric n-channel FET (n-FET) and p-channel FET (p-FET) transfer characteristics. 16) and pseudo-complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) based on single transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD)17—have demonstrated low-voltage and subthreshold operation with reduced static power consumption (Extended Data Table 1). Despite these advances, a scalable method for achieving pristine 2D/high-κ interfaces in both n- and p-type transistors remains elusive.

Diungkapkan bahwa here we show that standard amorphous hfo2 grown by atomic layer deposition (ald) contains prevalent charge traps that degrade wse2 fets by inducing unwanted bipolar transport, pronounced hysteresis, and compromised n- and p-type performance. The resulting MoS2 n-FETs and WSe2 p-FETs have ideal unipolar behaviour, well-matched enhancement-mode thresholds, near-ideal subthreshold swing and record-low hysteresis. Complementary inverters deliver high voltage gain, wide noise margins and record-low static power (subpicowatt) at low voltage. Patterned membranes are van-der-Waals-integrated with 2D semiconductors as top- or bottom-gate dielectrics, preserving pristine 2D/high-κ interfaces. We fabricated a -3-inch free-standing single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide (A-TiO2) membrane, a high-κ dielectric with κ ≈ 44–50 at a thickness of 18. Furthermore, non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) simulations show that this architecture is scalable to a gate length (Lg) of 10 nm, comparable with the 1 nm technology-node specifications in the IRDS 2031 roadmap while maintaining stable operation at 0. Transitioning to a single-crystal dielectric mitigates these issues. 2 nm. Although crystalline dielectrics retain structural imperfections, their threading dislocations are spatially confined to one-dimensional defects with self-passivated cores, making them less detrimental to two-dimensional interfacial transport. 3 V.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we use a laser scanning-assisted pulsed-laser deposition technique to fabricate free-standing 3-inch a-tio2 dielectric layers (methods). The optical image of the as-grown 3-inch LaAlO3//SrTiO3//Sr3Al2O6//A-TiO2 heterostructure and its cross-sectional high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image profile with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings are shown in Fig. A photograph of the as-released 3-inch A-TiO2 layer on a Si//SiO2 substrate is shown in Fig. 1c. In brief, a SrTiO3 layer was first epitaxially grown on a 3-inch single-crystalline LaAlO3 (001) substrate, followed by a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer that served as a template for the subsequent epitaxial growth of single-crystal A-TiO2 dielectric layers. 1a,b. The grown heterostructure is patterned into 100 × 100 μm2 squares using inductively coupled plasma etching to expose the underlying Sr3Al2O6 layer surrounding the defined squares. Owing to the vdW interaction between A-TiO2 and the substrate, the 3-inchpatterned A-TiO2 can be lifted off using a polymer support layer and transferred onto target substrates. The sacrificial Sr3Al2O6 layer is then selectively removed by immersion in deionized water, leaving the A-TiO2 layer in direct contact with the LaAlO3//SrTiO3 substrate. Diungkapkan bahwa in summary, this work demonstrates a 3-inch freestanding a-tio2 membrane as a gate dielectric that delivers exceptional thickness uniformity and favourable dielectric metrics. Density functional theory (DFT) combined with NEGF (NEGF-DFT) simulations further project that the proposed 2D CFET architecture can be scaled to the 1-nm node while sustaining stable operation (Supplementary Note 7). Building on this gate-stack platform, vertically stacked CFET inverter arrays have high voltage gain, wide noise margins and ultralow static power consumption. The atomically clean interface formed between A-TiO2 and 2D materials enables low subthreshold swing, record-low hysteresis and well-balanced enhancement-mode operation for both n- and p-type transistors. Together, these results establish wafer-scale single-crystal high-κ dielectrics integrated with 2D semiconductors as viable and promising platforms for energy-efficient logic technologies, positioning them as compelling candidates for the post-silicon electronics roadmap.

#541. Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*

Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11241-9

Sebagaimana diketahui, a new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the event horizon telescope collaboration synthesized an earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image1,2,3,4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy messier 87 (m87). 2 ± 1. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. 5 ± 0. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features3,5,6,7, with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source8,9. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42. 5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6. 5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

Berdasarkan laporan, the m87* supermassive black hole, with a mass of mbh = (3–7) × 109 m⊙ (refs. Its appearance on event horizon scales is expected, on the basis of general relativistic predictions, to be dominated by a central shadow, which, for a non-rotating Schwarzschild black hole, is characterized by a critical impact parameter that is proportional to the black hole mass15 as \(3\sqrt{3}G{M}_{{\rm{BH}}}/({c}^{2}D)\), in which G is the gravitational constant and c is the speed of light. 8 Mpc (refs. 10,11,12) located at a distance of D = 16. To observe with a spatial resolution capable of detailing the M87* black hole shadow requires unprecedented μas-scale angular resolution, roughly equivalent to the angle subtended by the width of a strand of human hair more than 1,000 km away. 13,14), offers a unique window into horizon-scale general relativistic physics. Achieving this feat requires a combination of millimetre wavelengths (λ ≈ 1 mm) and an effective aperture size comparable with the diameter of the Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, such a synthesis of an earth-sized aperture was realized through very long baseline interferometry (vlbi) techniques by correlating the signals from a global network of independent radio observatories, collectively referred to as the event horizon telescope (eht)1,16. Although this technique yields the requisite angular resolution to image the M87* shadow, the resulting virtual aperture remains substantially unfilled and lacks the sensitivity and reconstruction fidelity of a filled aperture. As the Earth rotates, the separation vectors between pairs of geographical stations sweep out elliptical arcs that incrementally fill the Earth-sized synthetic aperture. The data sparsity problem is further compounded by the requirement of calibrating rapid, station-based atmospheric phase and amplitude fluctuations on continental-scale separations, which often occur on timescales shorter than the coherence time of the observations.

Diungkapkan bahwa these inherent challenges make image reconstruction from vlbi and eht datasets an ill-posed problem, highly sensitive to instrument calibration and post-processing heuristics. The consequences are divergent representations of the fine-scale features of M87*, such as the surface brightness distribution and hotspot localization3,5,6,7,17,18. Present algorithms regularly use manually tuned and independently weighted data terms and regularizations to bias the solution towards plausible morphologies, which can inadvertently steer the reconstruction towards preferred solutions. Using traditional approaches, including CLEAN-based algorithms or hybrid mapping with self-calibration19,20,21,22,23, independent analyses showed that the resulting reconstruction is sensitive to methodological and hyperparameter selections, such as image initialization6 or adopted field of view8, with some independent analyses demonstrating reconstructions without a clear ring-like structure8,9, suggesting that, if the field of view extends to circular diameters beyond 120 μas, a single elongated bright spot solution is favoured over a ring8.

Diungkapkan bahwa to resolve the tension around the m87* results and advance beyond methodological uncertainties, we transition from traditional approaches towards a more autonomous and objective framework. The independence of our method is primarily grounded on our use of robust interferometric observables, called closure invariants24,25,26,27, which capture information on source morphology that is unaffected by errors in wavefront and instrument calibration. In contrast to the disparate closure phases24 and closure amplitudes25 that have traditionally served as such robust observables, the closure invariants formalism26,27 that we use provides a unified framework that carries equivalent information while eliminating the requirement for heterogeneous treatment typically observed in the literature. Closure invariants are also insensitive to absolute position and absolute flux scale, but these are not inherent morphological parameters. Therefore, closure invariants constitute robust information-bearing observables in radio interferometry, underpinning high-fidelity morphology reconstructions28,29,30,31. By making use of the rich calibration-independent, pure morphological information carried by closure invariants, we can bypass conventional techniques that require sensitive calibration tuning and observer-driven priors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to take full advantage of the closure formalism, we develop and apply the generative deep learning image reconstruction with closure terms (gendirect)31 algorithm, trained on images unrelated to astronomy and designed to generatively produce data-driven image reconstructions using only closure invariants. Unlike other machine-learning-based radio interferometric imaging algorithms, our algorithm is unique in using closure invariants to condition a latent diffusion model. GenDIReCT has undergone extensive testing on both synthetic31 and real data32 and has been demonstrated to be capable of consistently recovering diverse morphological structures, without manual intervention, prescriptive priors or parameter tuning (further detail in Methods).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for the first time, to our knowledge, closure invariants are used to image m87* through our gendirect algorithm, using the publicly available 1. 33) and two epochs (13 April and 18 April) from 2021 (ref. 1), two epochs (21 April and 25 April) from 2018 (ref. com/eventhorizontelescope/2019-D01-02). 3-mm EHT measurements from four observation epochs (5 April, 6 April, 10 April and 11 April) from 2017 (ref. For each of these models, we aggregate a large population of generative reconstructions into a single representative median image, comparing them with the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (EHTC) fiducial reconstruction that is reproduced using the public eht-imaging pipeline (https://github. We set several fields of view for the reconstruction (128 × 128, 225 × 225 and 450 × 450 μas2), in which each combination of dataset and field of view is an independent model and acts as an indirect prior on the maximum source size. 34). We also derive a composite image from the pixelwise median of all reconstructions of each epoch across all fields of view aligned to the single reconstruction with the best data fidelity score.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all datasets from independent observation epochs convincingly produce a compact, ring-like structure on an approximately 40-μas scale. On the highest-quality dataset of each year (11 April 2017, 21 April 2018 and 18 April 2021), our median reconstruction is a compact circularized ring of consistent orientation and diameter, independent of the reconstruction field-of-view window and brightened in the south or southwest direction. The appearance of the ring is most consistent with an observed inclination angle of about 20° from the approaching jet. We present the composites for our best reconstructions from these three datasets in Fig. 1.

Berdasarkan laporan, the consistency of the source size (about 40 μas) across all fields of view is strong confirmation of a compact source. Consequently, the suggested sensitivity of image morphology to the assumed field of view reported in independent reanalyses and demonstrated for the 5 April 2017 dataset8 is possibly an artefact of insufficient aperture coverage or low-quality data. Under the most-constrained 128 × 128-μas2 field of view, the median reconstructed image exhibits the highest image-domain similarity score with fiducial EHTC reconstructions and the performance on data adherence metrics is competitive with those of larger fields of view, supporting the prior expectation that extended emission of the M87* jet is unconstrained by the EHT datasets3,33. In our work, when higher-quality datasets are considered, the sensitivity to field of view disappears, contrary to predictions based on the traditional hybrid mapping approach8. On some infrequent reconstructions of epochs with lower-quality datasets suffering from even sparser aperture coverage3, lower signal-to-noise ratio or various observation deficiencies33, the ring-like morphology can become less clear, as noted by independent studies8. Our work thus yields a robust, independent verification of the ring-like geometry characteristic of the M87* black hole shadow image.

Diungkapkan bahwa in contrast to regularized maximum likelihood methods in the publicly available imaging pipelines used by the ehtc on m87*, our method does not require manually prescribing an image initialization. These methods typically exhibit marked sensitivity to the starting model6. For instance, the eht-imaging pipeline applied on M87* is initialized with a 40-μas full width at half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian, which serves as a powerful prior on the characteristic source size. When the eht-imaging pipeline is initialized with Gaussian priors larger than 40 μas (that is, 80–120 μas), the resulting image reconstructions exhibit phantom repetition or aliasing artefacts, which is a common issue for VLBI imaging algorithms28,35.

Diungkapkan bahwa it is important, therefore, that we consistently recover a single, compact source morphology in the absence of manual prescriptions. When our model is trained on different fields of view, the model learns an implicit statistical prior from its diverse training library conditioned on the input interferometric observables, namely, closure invariants. The convergence towards a stable, singular ring structure across varying fields of view indicates that the our model is successfully inferring the intrinsic source geometry from the data itself, rather than operating within the constraints of a manually selected initialization. The autonomy and capacity for imaging directly from calibration-independent observables of GenDIReCT represents a notable step towards objective blind imaging in the challenging data-sparse VLBI regime. By unequivocally recovering the ring-like structure of M87* across several datasets through this approach, we provide a rigorous cross-validation of published EHTC results.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we quantitatively demonstrate consistency with the ehtc image reconstructions by measuring ring characteristics from our reconstructed images and comparing them with published parameters. We apply an independent implementation of the image-domain feature extraction method used by the EHTC3 to measure ring properties from reconstructed event-horizon-scale images, including ring diameter, width, orientation (measured anticlockwise from north), azimuthal asymmetry and central brightness fraction. The measured properties from our median reconstructions of all datasets are presented in Table 1. Each cell represents the mean parameter measured from independent reconstructions on all three fields of view.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the measured ring orientation and diameter remain relatively stable between the gendirect and ehtc imaging methods. There is a clear anticlockwise trend in the ring orientation angle as measured by all methods between the 5 and 6 April reconstructions with 10 and 11 April in 2017, as well as between the 2017 and 2018/2021 observations. However, the evolution in 2017 may be caused by uncertainty in the azimuthal structure brought about by the sparse aperture coverage of observations taken on 5 and 6 April. In Fig. 2, we compare our image-domain measurements derived from our reconstructions with the EHTC analogue. Nevertheless, the evolution in ring orientation between the 2017 and 2018 observations is noteworthy, attributable to the turbulent nature of black hole accretion36. In particular, the observed ring orientation in 2018 and 2021 are closer in alignment with the large-scale forward jet of M87* compared with that in 2017.

Berdasarkan laporan, conversely, the measured ring width and central brightness fraction are heavily influenced by methodological differences, as seen in the variation between imaging algorithms. Likewise, the azimuthal asymmetry parameter is unstable between different days and different methods, which is indicative of sensitivity to variation in the aperture coverage. For instance, reconstructions from the DIFMAP algorithm37 are convolved with a 20-μas circular beam, which inflates the ring width compared with regularized maximum likelihood methods and our algorithm. Therefore, the ring width and central brightness fraction probably do not reflect intrinsic source properties.

Sebagaimana diketahui, our independently measured ring diameters and inferred black hole mass from gendirect imaging and geometric modelling are therefore in excellent agreement with previous stellar dynamical mass measurements11 and with image-domain feature extraction on the imaging methods applied by the ehtc. By contrast, the smaller ring diameter predicted by the black hole mass estimate from gas dynamics would have been challenging to resolve given the EHT beam dimensions of approximately 20 μas. Berdasarkan laporan, the appearance of the black hole shadow is also sensitive to the black hole spin, a⁎, and observed inclination angle. Note that we do not explore inclination angles >90°, as the resulting synthetic images are comparable with an inversion of the spin direction. 2° ± 3. 4. 3° jet viewing angle inferred from 43-GHz VLBI observations46,47. Diungkapkan bahwa this work uses the publicly available network-calibrated datasets of m87* (https://eventhorizontelescope. 33) and 2021 (ref. 2), 2018 (ref. Furthermore, the Greenland Telescope (GLT)57,58 participated in the 2018 observations for the first time as part of the EHT array, which improved the aperture coverage, particularly along the north–south direction. In 2017, EHT observations of M87* were conducted with seven separate facilities1: the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)49,50, the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment telescope (APEX)51, the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT)52, the Pico Veleta IRAM 30-m telescope (PV)53, the Submillimeter Telescope Observatory (SMT)54, the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT)55 and the Submillimeter Array (SMA)56, which heterogeneously and sparsely sample the Fourier plane as the Earth rotates. org/for-astronomers/data), reduced through the EHT-HOPS pipeline, on the basis of observations obtained in 2017 (ref. 34). For 2021, the 12-m Kitt Peak (KP)59 telescope and the upgraded Northern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA)60 facility joined EHT observations for the first time.

Berdasarkan laporan, the 2017 observations of m87* are spread over four separate epochs (5, 6, 10 and 11 april), whereas observations in 2018 and 2021 are separated into two epochs each (21/25 april for 2018 and 13/18 april for 2021). 1 (low) and 229. The datasets with the best single-day aperture coverage each year are 11 April, 21 April and 18 April, which we use as our fiducial datasets, whereas datasets on other days are used as cross-validation. We consider the data taken over two approximately 2-GHz bands centred at 227. 1 GHz (high), which we merge into a single dataset.

Berdasarkan laporan, the interferometric data on m87* comprise complex visibilities, correlated from signals between pairs of stations, referred to as a baseline, which are, by the van cittert–zernike theorem61, related to the source brightness distribution by a two-dimensional fourier transform after certain approximations62. Following the procedure in the publicly available M87* imaging pipeline (https://github. With typical scan lengths on the order of five minutes, temporal averaging can potentially introduce residuals from time-dependent gain fluctuations to closure invariants. com/eventhorizontelescope/2019-D01-02), we rescale short baselines to the total flux density estimated from the ALMA and APEX baseline to excise the contribution from extended flux. We have also internally validated that the short baseline rescaling procedure does not affect the recovered morphology from our imaging algorithm. Visibilities can be sequenced into scans, on the basis of the time difference between observations, from which we obtain coherently averaged visibilities. We have internally validated the robustness of our imaging products by computing closure invariants at the smallest possible cadence of the science-ready dataset (typically 10 s) before scan-level averaging. In this work, closure invariants are generally computed from scan-averaged visibilities. For quantitative comparison, we generate fiducial images from the publicly available eht-imaging pipeline to represent EHTC reconstructions.

Berdasarkan laporan, closure invariants are calibration-independent interferometric measurables produced from a generalized formalism of traditional closure phase24,63 and amplitudes25, with both a co-polar version26 and a polarimetric version27. GenDIReCT uses co-polar closure invariants constructed from elementary triangular plaquette variables called ‘advariants’. The complete minimal set of independent closed triads can be constructed from an array of n stations by selecting all pairs of array elements (a, b) pinned on a fixed reference vertex indexed at 0,.

Diungkapkan bahwa in which \({{\mathcal{v}}}_{{ab}}^{{\prime} }\) are corrupted visibilities measured from the baseline between stations a and b and |g0|2 is the unknown scaling factor associated with the reference station, which is shared by all complex advariants constructed in this way. In the co-polar formalism of closure invariants, traditional closure phases can be identified trivially from the phases of the advariants, whereas closure amplitudes can be derived from specific pairs of advariants. A key advantage of this formalism over traditional closure amplitudes and phases is that it avoids the heterogeneous treatment that phases and amplitudes necessitate. By normalizing all advariants by the L2-norm, for example, we produce \({N}_{{\rm{s}}}^{2}-3{N}_{{\rm{s}}}+1\) real-valued independent closure invariants, whose form is different but carry information equivalent to that in traditional closure amplitudes and phases. In internal validation tests, closure invariants as the sole likelihood term was found to be preferable over the independently weighted (log-)closure amplitudes and closure phases in terms of convergence and data efficiency.

Sebagaimana diketahui, various selections of the reference station can affect covariances between closure terms, despite carrying equivalent information. A different selection of reference station can influence the signal-to-noise ratio in the derived closure invariants but does not greatly influence the resulting image reconstruction32. For this work, to avoid bias from a single reference station selection, we present the combined results from two GenDIReCT models for each dataset, trained consistently on the first and the second most sensitive stations as the reference stations in each scan. Selecting from among the most sensitive stations maximizes closure-invariant signal-to-noise ratio and minimizes covariances between closure terms64.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the gendirect31 algorithm is an imaging algorithm that uses co-polar closure invariants26 for calibration-independent imaging under the constraints of sparse aperture coverage characteristic of vlbi data. Other machine learning interferometric imaging techniques have been presented in the literature, on the basis of CNNs68,69,70,71,72, normalizing flow73,74, denoising diffusion74,75, classifiers29,76, adversarial networks76,77 and transformers30. The architecture comprises a latent diffusion model65 conditioned on closure invariants and a multilayer convolutional neural network (CNN) used to optimize the closure invariants likelihood. Traditional imaging algorithms, such as hybrid mapping and self-calibration followed by deconvolution, begin with a simple initial model and iteratively solve for antenna-based complex gains and the image model to converge on a final solution that matches the measured data. These methods can be sensitive to and biased by image initialization and calibration errors, particularly in sparse and low signal-to-noise measurements6,19,22. Our algorithm bypasses the limitations of conventional techniques by using closure invariants as the robust interferometric measurable and produces an image reconstruction directly in a single forward pass. Although there are some similarities with other diffusion-based imaging algorithms74,75, GenDIReCT is unique in its closure-conditioned latent diffusion model and, notably, in its use of homogeneous closure invariants rather than the traditional closure phases and closure amplitudes that require heterogeneous treatment. Furthermore, in contrast to the newer regularized maximum likelihood methods that can also image using closure invariants as the sole data term28,35,66,67, our algorithm provides a generative solution that does not require a user-specified, hand-tuned image initialization at inference time. In this section, we provide a brief overview of our algorithm and its past applications.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the neural network architecture is composed of two distinct components. By having no cross-attention layers in the upsampling path, the result is a robust conditional denoising network that performs well even with noise from real observations. The first component is a conditional U-Net78 based on textually conditioned image generation architectures65 with denoising diffusion probabilistic models79, which has emerged as a highly effective image generation technique, capable of modelling complex data distributions. The second component of the GenDIReCT architecture is a standard multilayer CNN composed of three sequential downsampling layers, designed to compress a large set of diffusion-sampled images (each considered a separate channel) into a representative data-consistent single-channel image reconstruction. On the upsampling path, we implement two upsampling layers with self-attention and one final upsampling layer without attention. Our implementation is a latent diffusion model consisting of three convolutional layers set in a symmetric contracting and expanding pathway with residual connections80 from the contracting path that map features to their mirrored expanding layers. In the contracting path, we use one downsampling layer, followed by two downsampling layers with cross-attention, in which the closure-invariant features adjust convolutional features through the cross-attention mechanism, which conditions the denoising process. The latent shape is 4 channels of 16 × 16 grids, which is downsampled from the original 64 × 64 total intensity image grid using a pretrained autoencoder30. We note that we have experimented with several design variations and found this version to be suitable in all tested cases, but better-performing alternatives for specific datasets may be possible.

Berdasarkan laporan, gendirect works by learning realistic image characteristics (such as positivity and smooth brightness distribution) from a non-astronomical image training dataset, primarily composed of augmented cifar-10 natural images81. As a generative imaging algorithm, our algorithm has the potential to handle degeneracies and visualize multimodalities in the solution space, although they should not be interpreted as image reconstruction uncertainty under a Bayesian framework. By training on unconvolved ground-truth models, GenDIReCT achieves super-resolved reconstructions and enables generative visualization of structural variations that remain strictly consistent with the observed data. However, methodological and hyperparameter sensitivity, or inability to satisfy the underlying measurements, constitute signs that a reconstruction is not robust. The conditional latent diffusion model generates sensible image priors, which the multilayer CNN uses as input to optimize the data likelihood and refine the final image reconstruction. Generally, appearance of minor artefacts in low-sensitivity regions, different levels of smoothness and sharpness or super-resolution variations are acceptable consequences of a diversity in potential solutions to the ill-posed image reconstruction problem. Accordingly, unless otherwise indicated, we present unconvolved GenDIReCT outputs optimized to be consistent with the measurements.

Diungkapkan bahwa we have extensively tested our algorithm on synthetic datasets with the eht or next-generation eht (ngeht) array31, as well as non-horizon-scale eht datasets on active galactic nuclei, 3c 279 and centaurus a (ref. 83, reproducing the core-jet morphology across several independent epochs and enabling direct measurement of the superluminal relative proper motion between components in the image domain. 32). 84 is reproduced with 91% similarity with statistically compatible brightness ratios and opening angle between the north and south edge-brightened jet ridges. For the EHT dataset on 3C 279, our reconstruction is 98% similar to the EHTC ref. On synthetic datasets, our algorithm generalizes well to untrained morphologies and maintains >90% image similarity with ground-truth images at signal-to-noise levels well below the datasets of M87*. Moreover, its performance on quantitative metrics is comparable with other state-of-the-art imaging algorithms on the ngEHT total intensity analysis challenge82. For the EHT dataset on Centaurus A, the EHTC ref. These extensive tests on real and synthetic data demonstrate that our algorithm is capable of consistently recovering diverse morphological structures, without manual intervention or prescriptive priors.

Diungkapkan bahwa before applying to the real data, each trained model is extensively tested on an array of internal validation tests, which include quantifying its performance degradation with out-of-distribution image morphologies and varying levels of data corruption, accounting for the heterogeneous sensitivity of the array32. Only after passing internal validation are the models unblinded on real data to minimize risk of confirmation bias. No alterations are made to the model between the validation procedure and the unblinding, or post-unblinding.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for this work, we train our machine learning architecture with synthetic data derived using the data coverage from all four 2017 and both 2018/2021 observing days independently, combining the two 2-ghz bands into a single scan-averaged dataset for each epoch. Generally, we represent the aggregate reconstruction for each dataset by the median of all aligned reconstructions. We find the median representation to be more robust against outliers or source alignment issues and a better representation of the bulk of individual image reconstructions. The aggregate reconstructions for all datasets and fields of view are shown in Extended Data Fig. We choose 128 × 128-μas2, 225 × 225-μas2 and 450 × 450-μas2 reconstruction fields, each on 64 × 64-pixel grids as predetermined by the architecture. 1 alongside EHTC comparison reconstructions, GenDIReCT composites and a median to median absolute deviation (MAD) ratio panel. The median-to-MAD ratio is presented as a visualization of GenDIReCT’s reconstruction confidence31, in which features of low variance relative to the median pixel intensity (that is, high reconstruction confidence) are highlighted with filled contours.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the advantages of the generative imaging process of our algorithm is the potential to explore different imaging solution modes. We consider all observation epochs and all fields of view, presenting the median reconstructions from the most populated solution clusters in Extended Data Fig. On all fields of view, there is no non-ring solution that is favoured over ring-like morphology in the share of the reconstructed image population or data fidelity score. For other datasets, solution clusters that are not as clearly ring-like are typically of sparse occurrence in comparison with the bulk of reconstructions and exhibit a lower data fidelity score. Each cluster is also presented with the best data fidelity score in parentheses. Often, more than 50% of all reconstructions reside within the top two most populous and perceptually similar clusters. The most ambiguous case is that of the 25 April 2018 dataset, which is missing data from the LMT, resulting in reduced image fidelity compared with the 21 April 2018 observations. The M87* clustering results clearly demonstrate that the differences between reconstruction clusters for the observation days with the highest-quality data are in the surface brightness and extent of extraneous amorphous emission surrounding the ring, rather than fundamental changes to the ring structure itself. Image reconstructions are clustered by Hamming distance in their perceptual hash representation32 to illustrate multimodal solutions. 2. This clustering behaviour justifies the pixelwise median as a statistically sound and accurate aggregate representation. The absence of LMT-related baselines created a substantial gap in uv coverage at spatial frequencies corresponding to about 1 Gλ, as the LMT–SMT baseline provided the unique long-baseline constraint for structure in this regime33.

Diungkapkan bahwa unless otherwise stated, all models described in this work are trained on augmented non-astronomical images from the cifar-10 dataset81, as well as simple geometric shapes, such as gaussians, disks, rings, ellipses and m-rings85 of the first and second orders31. 3. We present an example grid of augmented training images in Extended Data Fig. The exact number of final image reconstructions depends on data volume. Therefore, we also investigate the outcome of training our architecture without geometric shapes in the training dataset and find no notable difference in the image reconstruction (Extended Data Fig. Once trained, we run the imaging sequence for 96 total GPU hours on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU for each dataset, producing several hundred (about 300) individual image reconstructions, each drawing from 4,096 diffusion samples. Although our algorithm has been shown to be generalizable to arbitrary source morphologies31, there is a concern that the presence of crescents and rings in the training dataset may be a source of bias for the image reconstruction. 3).

Sebagaimana diketahui, we use the reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{ci}}}^{2}\) metric to evaluate the consistency between our image reconstructions with the measurements. The reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) metric is defined as the sum of error-normalized residuals divided by the number of independent data terms,.

Diungkapkan bahwa in which \({\mathcal{c}}\) is an operator that maps the reconstructed image to its closure invariants, indexed by i, for a fixed observation arrangement and ci is the corresponding closure invariant of the measurement. The total number of closure invariants is denoted by Nci and \({\sigma }_{i}^{2}\) is the estimated uncertainty on the ith closure invariant. We also define the normalized residual of any data point, i, as \(({\mathcal{C}}{(A)}_{i}-{C}_{i})/{\sigma }_{i}\).

Diungkapkan bahwa although propagating the estimated uncertainty from each radio station’s system equivalent flux density is straightforward, the total error on each closure invariant is affected by other sources of systematic errors, including time-dependent errors from long coherent visibility averaging and limitations of the linear error propagation model. Generally, the fractional systematic uncertainty budget of 3C 279 and M87 data is about 5%, which is similar in magnitude as measured inter-pipeline differences2. 4. However, in this work, we present our results without further systematic error tolerance and we consistently use as reference the highest-quality single-day EHT-HOPS-reduced pre-scan-averaged dataset of each observation year (11 April for 2017, 21 April for 2018, 18 April for 2021) when evaluating the reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) to ensure a consistent metric across reconstructions. For these datasets, we illustrate the data fidelity from the best GenDIReCT reconstruction and the xsringauss geometric model in Extended Data Fig. A near-unity reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) value confirms that a reconstruction is self-consistent with the measured closure invariants but does not guarantee that the recovered morphology is correct in an absolute sense, making the reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) a necessary but insufficient metric for an accurate reconstruction.

Diungkapkan bahwa in some cases, it is useful to measure the similarity between reconstructions in the image domain, especially when comparing the gendirect reconstructions with the results from the ehtc imaging pipelines. The metric has been widely used to quantitatively measure image similarity, particularly with image reconstructions produced using only closure data terms28,31,32,82. We measure the image-to-image correspondence with the maximum normalized cross-correlation metric, ρNX, which has the advantage of being independent of image translation and total flux scaling. The ρNX metric is defined as.

Diungkapkan bahwa in which i1 and i2 are two images being compared and the hat operator, \(\hat{i}=(i-\bar{i})/{\sigma }_{i}\), normalizes each image i by its respective flux mean and standard deviation. To minimize the negative influence of high-frequency artefacts on the maximum normalized cross-correlation, we convolve each image by the fitted clean beam before computing ρNX. The maximum operator ensures that the metric is independent of image translation and it is also useful for aligning separate image reconstructions. We denote the forward and inverse Fourier transform as \({\mathcal{F}}\) and \({{\mathcal{F}}}^{-1}\), respectively. Throughout this work, we use ρNX to evaluate the inter-method consistency in resulting image reconstructions, often between the GenDIReCT and EHTC fiducial imaging pipelines or simulated images. As there is no ground-truth reconstruction for M87*, the ρNX metric does not constitute an independent ground-truth validation metric but as an image-domain similarity metric between various imaging algorithms.

Diungkapkan bahwa the image-domain feature extraction method presented here follows the framework established by the ehtc in their initial analysis of m87* (ref. We outline the reproduction of this algorithm below. 3). Given any plausibly ring-like image, we first search for the ring centre, (x0, y0), by evaluating all candidate centroid positions for the one that minimizes the normalized radial peak dispersion.

in which \({\bar{r}}_{{\rm{pk}}}(x,y)\) is the radius of peak brightness averaged over all angles, as.

Diungkapkan bahwa in which i(r, θ; x, y) is the intensity distribution of the image in radial coordinates, centred on (x, y). The dispersion, σr(x, y), is the corresponding standard deviation of rpk(θ; x, y) across all angles, θ. The ring diameter and its uncertainty can then be identified from \({\bar{r}}_{{\rm{pk}}}(x,y)\) and σr(x, y), respectively, given the measured ring centre, (x0, y0).

Diungkapkan bahwa once the ring centre is determined, most other characteristic features can be extracted directly from the polar image, including: the ring width wr, orientation η, azimuthal asymmetry a and central brightness fraction fc. The ring width, wr, is determined by measuring the mean FWHM at each radial slice for the given ring centre,.

Berdasarkan laporan, in which the floor value ifloor = ⟨i(r = 2rpk, θ)⟩θ is used to correct for any non-zero residual flux outside the ring. The uncertainty on the ring width, σw, is measured by the standard deviation in FWHM across all θ.

The orientation angle, η, of the ring (measured east of north) is the circular mean of the first angular mode from rin = rpk − wr/2 to rout = rpk + wr/2, as.

and the corresponding uncertainty, θη, is the standard deviation of the measured angles for r ∈ [rin, rout].

The azimuthal asymmetry, A, is the mean of the normalized amplitude in the first angular mode from rin to rout, which is.

Berdasarkan laporan, in which σa is the standard deviation in the measured asymmetry over r ∈ [rin, rout]. Perfect azimuthal symmetry corresponds to a value of A = 0, whereas a delta function with all flux concentrated at a single orientation angle corresponds to a value of A = 1.

Finally, the central brightness fraction, fc, is the ratio between the mean interior depression brightness to the mean ring surface brightness, as.

Berdasarkan laporan, in which the interior brightness is measured from the average flux in a small disk around the ring centre. Figure 2 presents the measured ring diameter and orientation across all datasets considered in this work. We present the measurements for ring width, azimuthal asymmetry and central brightness fraction in Extended Data Fig. Although we do not define an uncertainty for a single measurement of fc, we derive its uncertainty from several measurements across the three different fields of view used in GenDIReCT reconstruction. 5.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ehtc derived ring parameters using the rex module implemented as part of eht-imaging. Ring properties from three different imaging algorithms (DIFMAP37, eht-imaging28 and SMILI66) were reported for the 2017 data3, two Bayesian imaging algorithms (THEMIS86 and Comrade87,88) were included for the 2018 datasets33 and for 2021 data, one further CLEAN-based algorithm (GPCAL89) and two further regularized maximum likelihood algorithms (DOG-HIT67 and MOEA/D (ref. However, for the 2021 datasets, the EHTC used an alternative template-matching image-domain feature extraction algorithm34. 35)) were added. As such, to maintain methodological consistency, we have reproduced a single eht-imaging reconstruction to use as the EHTC reference.

Diungkapkan bahwa when comparing ring diameter between datasets, image reconstruction algorithms and across multiyear epochs, there is potential for systematic bias arising from the finite-resolution effect, in which variations in ring width can shift the apparent diameter derived from a direct image-domain feature analysis. Therefore, the apparent variation observed between imaging algorithms and individual datasets may be influenced by the finite resolution of each imaging method. In this work, we choose to maintain methodological consistency across all reconstructions by deriving diameters directly from the image domain without further adjustment. Recent EHTC analyses use a forward-modelling procedure to mitigate diameter–width degeneracy34. Despite this, the apparent ring diameter derived from our reconstructions remains self-consistent across all independent datasets.

Diungkapkan bahwa our complementary bayesian analysis uses the geometric xsringauss model4,90, which was designed to simulate the appearance of quasi-kerr black hole accretion disk radio images91. We develop the BASIS92 software package for Bayesian analysis with the xsringauss model independent from existing software from the EHTC. Moreover, as long as the object is plausibly described by the model, Bayesian sampling methods applied with geometric models enable direct inference of key features of interest from the observed object with associated uncertainties. In this section, we provide a brief description of the xsringauss model, the extra components we included to form the model for fitting and the complete analytical visibility function. The advantage of geometric modelling is that visibilities can be derived analytically from simple algebraic expressions and fit to the observed measurements, which substantially reduces the computational requirement of modelling compared with complex and highly nonlinear physical models, particularly when applied with Bayesian sampling algorithms. For the following discussion, we use \({\mathcal{F}}\) to denote the forward Fourier transform operator.

Berdasarkan laporan, the xsringauss model is parameterized with the following variables4. When f = 0, the crescent surface brightness is uniform and when f = 1, the surface brightness fades to zero at x = −Rout. The outer disk radius, Rout, and inner disk radius, Rin, create the centralized ‘top-hat crescent’, in which the offset of the inner disk centroid is controlled by the eccentricity, ϵ ∈ [0, 1]. At ϵ = 0, the centres of both disks are co-located at the origin and at the maximum eccentricity, ϵ = 1, the edge of the inner disk meets the edge of the outer disk. The fading parameter, f ∈ [0, 1], controls the surface brightness gradient across the crescent, with the maximum brightness located at the tip of the crescent, at which the crescent width is maximum. Note that we have deliberately adjusted the definition of fading from its original conception90.

Berdasarkan laporan, the xsringauss model also includes an elliptical gaussian centred on the inner disk edge, at which the crescent is widest. Its flux is determined by a fraction, fg, of the total flux and its width is set by σe, with axial ratio, ag. The longest axis is always oriented perpendicular to the crescent’s axis of symmetry. A circular Gaussian with flux Vf and width σf centred at x0 represents the floor component internal to the crescent. To complete the base xsringauss model, we blur the image with a circular Gaussian kernel of width σb and rotate the entire image by angle ϕ.

Sebagaimana diketahui, further components include a larger-scale circular background gaussian of flux vbg and width σbg centred at the origin, which is added to include short-spacing flux that is not examined by most of the long-baseline array. Finally, two more nuisance elliptical Gaussians are included, each with independent parameters for flux, width, axial ratio, position angle, angular offsets and Gaussian blur, to capture extraneous amorphous emission that is not modelled by the ring alone and as further degrees of freedom to absorb the effects from measurement errors and systematic uncertainties.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the fourier domain, the composite model is a linear combination of elementary components with analytic fourier transforms. The general Fourier transform (represented by tilde) of a disk with radius R and amplitude V is given by.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in which ρ is the fourier-domain radial coordinate and j1 is a first-order bessel function of the first kind. The Fourier transform of a Gaussian with flux V and width σ is,.

Berdasarkan laporan, in which the fourier transform of asymmetric gaussians are determined by exploiting the similarity property of the fourier transform, that is, \({\mathcal{f}}(g({ax},{by}))=\frac{1}{|{ab}|}\tilde{g}\left(\frac{u}{a},\frac{v}{b}\right)\). Multiplication in the image domain of the crescent by the sloped plane is represented in the Fourier domain by taking a derivative.

in which, for our specific linear slash function, l(x), the corresponding operation in the Fourier domain is.

in which the derivatives of Bessel functions of the first kind, Jn, can be expressed in terms of other Bessel functions, Jn±1, as.

Berdasarkan laporan, and h is responsible for normalizing the source to the desired total flux, v, which is dependent on the source structure. For the xsringauss model, the normalization factor is.

Sebagaimana diketahui, each image component can be further independently augmented by translation, rotation and gaussian blur. The final image model and its corresponding analytic Fourier transform is described by 28 parameters. 3 and we present covariance plots for all other datasets in Extended Data Figs. In general, image translations are represented with an extra phase term in the Fourier domain, \({{\rm{e}}}^{{\rm{i}}2{\rm{\pi }}({l}_{0}u+{m}_{0}v)}\), in which (l0, m0) denotes the translation in (l, m) coordinates. Image rotation is modelled by a rotation of the uv coordinates. Throughout this work, the xsringauss model is fit to observed data with DYNESTY, a Bayesian dynamic nested sampling algorithm, adopting uniform priors for all parameters. 6–8. The xsringauss model parameter covariance plot for the highest-quality datasets of 2017 and 2018 is shown in Fig. The final fitted image model is formed from the median value of the one-dimensional marginalized posteriors for each parameter. Then, by the convolution theorem, blurring in the image domain with a circular Gaussian kernel is a pointwise multiplication in the Fourier domain by \({{\rm{e}}}^{-{\rm{i}}2{{\rm{\pi }}}^{2}{\sigma }_{{\rm{b}}}^{2}{\rho }^{2}}\), in which σb is the width of the blurring kernel. We then apply the image-domain feature extraction analysis on samples from the posterior to measure all characteristic ring parameters (Extended Data Table 1).

Berdasarkan laporan, to compare the reconstructed composites to synthetic m87* images, we retrieve publicly available grmhd data (https://thz. 94, −0. edu/resources. 5, 0, +0. 94), evolving under the magnetically arrested disk or standard and normal evolution regimes. 5, +0. illinois. html) from the University of Illinois survey41, which includes fluid data for 1,000 time steps (in Rg/c) in the quasi-stationary equilibrium state and five black hole spin prescriptions (a⁎ = −0. astro. In this work, we consider only the magnetically arrested disk fluid models, which is the more likely evolutionary scenario for M87* based on jet power constraints94.

Sebagaimana diketahui, synthetic 230-ghz images of m87* are produced using the general relativistic radiative transfer ipole algorithm40 for all time steps, spins and inclination angles between 5° and 90° with a step size of 1°. Note that we use a coupled electron temperature model characterized by Rhigh = 40, which determines the relationship between the ion and electron temperature. Although Rhigh is a free parameter, the time-averaged magnetically arrested disk images are nearly independent of Rhigh and are sensitive primarily on black hole spin for a fixed inclination94. Simulations in ideal GRMHD models are scale-agnostic, enabling such adjustments to be made without affecting the underlying physics41,95. In this work, we compare all beam-convolved synthetic images with the reconstructed M87* composites in the image domain using the normalized cross-correlation metric after correcting for the observer position angle and making linear adjustments to spatial scale, for which both the rotation and scale adjustments of the synthetic images are chosen independently for each parameter combination of spin, inclination and time step, to maximize the resulting normalized cross-correlation comparison with the composite reconstructions. We also repeat our analysis for Rhigh = 80, presenting the figure in the GenDIReCT repository, and find a mild roughly 2° shift towards lower inclinations.

Berdasarkan laporan, left panels, fiducial reconstructions from eht-imaging for the single-epoch datasets. Data fidelity (\({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}},\text{min}}^{2}\)) on median reconstructions and image similarity (ρNX) scores are illustrated, for which ρNX is measured relative to the EHTC fiducial image reconstruction. Right panels, corresponding composite GenDIReCT reconstruction, median-to-MAD ratio and median representative reconstructions across several fields of view. The highest-quality dataset of each year is highlighted with a gold border. All panels are shown on a 225 × 225-μas2 window.

Berdasarkan laporan, the two most-populated clusters for each field of view are presented in descending order from left to right. Each row represents a separate single-epoch dataset and the highest-quality dataset of each year is highlighted with a gold border. The population of each cluster is represented by a percentage fraction alongside the minimum \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) in parentheses. Images containing the five most-populated clusters can be found in the GenDIReCT repository.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a, image grid showing an assortment of augmented non-astronomical cifar-10 images that constitute most of the training dataset. c, Alternative GenDIReCT composites for the highest-quality single-day datasets from observations in 2017, 2018 and 2021, without geometric shapes in the training data. Percentages indicate the fraction of the total training dataset composed by each class. b, Panels illustrate classes of simple geometric shapes used in training, which are not required to produce robust image reconstructions of M87*. The image similarity score is with reference to the EHTC fiducial reconstructions produced with eht-imaging.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, determined by the minimum \({\chi }_{{\rm{ci}}}^{2}\) of all gendirect (left) and xsringauss geometric modelling (right) reconstructions for each respective dataset, in which closure invariants are presented as real and imaginary values across the summed uv distance in gλ between all three participating stations. The residuals normalized by the expected uncertainty are presented on separate adjoining panels.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, similar to fig. 2, illustrating a comparison of the ring properties measured from image-domain feature extraction applied to our reconstructions with values from the EHTC, separated by observation epoch.

#542. Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity

📅 13 Nov 2026

Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11249-1

You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Diungkapkan bahwa tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by cd8+ t cells. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS–STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK–STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.
