#543. Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses

📅 13 Nov 2026

Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11277-x

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article.

Diungkapkan bahwa augmented reality (ar) displays, originating from early optical see-through head-mounted systems1, have evolved towards lightweight glasses that seamlessly integrate digital information with the physical world2,3. Here we show an all-day-wearable AR glass prototype based on spatially varying, interwoven metasurfaces that provide several grating vectors for multidirectional light control. The prototype produces bright and stable virtual images under outdoor ambient illumination, demonstrating the compatibility of meta-WGs with practical wearable display requirements. The resulting dual-layer metasurface-based waveguide (meta-WG) achieves a 30° FoV and an 8 × 8-mm2 two-dimensional (2D) eyebox while maintaining an average luminance efficiency of 1,938 nits lm−1 (up to 4,225 nits lm−1) within a 1. Diffractive waveguides (WGs) offer a promising approach towards lightweight AR displays yet face inherent trade-offs among field of view (FoV), optical efficiency and eyebox size owing to limited degrees of freedom in light control. However, their widespread adoption requires compact optical systems that enable bright, wide-field and comfortable viewing. 5-mm-thick form factor. By expanding the degrees of freedom for light routing beyond conventional diffractive WGs, our approach provides a scalable framework for balancing efficiency, viewing range and form factor, bringing high-performance AR glasses closer to practical consumer applications.

Why your physics project needs an anthropologist

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03623-w

Diungkapkan bahwa thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). Jaco de Swart is a historian and anthropologist of science at the University of Cambridge, UK.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the tambo team assesses suitable observatory sites in the andes mountains of peru. Credit: Jaco de Swart.

Diungkapkan bahwa it is uncommon for a social scientist to have a seat at a meeting about an astronomical observatory, let alone for them to jointly lead one. For one-quarter of attendees to be social-science scholars is almost unprecedented. But that’s exactly what happens at meetings about the Tau Air-shower Mountain-based Observatory (TAMBO), a proposed detector to be built in the Peruvian Andes to look for cosmic particles called tau neutrinos.

Space diplomacy: bridging the operating gaps between myriad missions.

Space diplomacy: bridging the operating gaps between myriad missions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tau neutrinos are elusive fundamental particles that are transmitted through space from black holes and other distant sources. 10, 947–951; 2026). When these particles interact with rocks on Earth, they can produce a shower of other, short-lived particles. The idea behind TAMBO is that if such a shower were emitted from one side of a deep canyon, it could be picked up by an array of 5,000 detectors on the other side (TAMBO collaboration. Nature Astron. The Andes Mountains of Peru contain many promising sites.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for those who live in the area, however, the case for tambo is less clear. The area is also affected by legal and illegal mining, large-scale infrastructure projects and legacies of colonialism. The Andes are a sensitive ecological environment and home to Indigenous farming communities that consider the mountains sentient beings that are integral to their society. This all leads to scepticism towards large projects that are developed by people from outside the area.

Diungkapkan bahwa i am the co-principal investigator of the tambo collaboration, alongside peruvian neutrino physicist carlos argüelles at harvard university in cambridge, massachusetts. I lead the social-science and ‘responsible siting’ side of the project. Having received funding to build a proof-of-principle experiment called TAMBITO, we are searching for a potential location for the observatory.

Developing astronomers in Africa: ‘We wanted to create a discipline’.

Developing astronomers in Africa: ‘We wanted to create a discipline’.

Berdasarkan laporan, since 2024, the tambo collaboration has built partnerships with 11 peruvian institutions, which are involved in the design and development of the telescope. No matter what their discovery potential is, big scientific experiments are not beneficial to everyone. Scientific links are an important starting point, but they are not enough. For example, construction of the Thirty Meter Telescope has been stalled since 2015 because of protests triggered by objections to its planned site on Maunakea in Hawaii — a mountain that is sacred in Native Hawaiian culture.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to integrate environmental care into the project and build good relationships with the communities that might host the telescope, tambo brought in experts on the andean region. In 2024, the collaboration held a workshop at Harvard’s Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study, at which scholars and policymakers discussed what equitable astrophysics in Peru would look like. This led to the formation of a responsible-siting team that includes geographers, sociologists and anthropologists who have worked in the Andes.

#549. California votes to give record $8.4 billion to medical research

📅 13 Nov 2026

California votes to give record $8.4 billion to medical research

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03635-6

Berdasarkan laporan, thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Sebagaimana diketahui, students, researchers and others at the university of california, los angeles, have protested over cuts to science funding made by the administration of us president donald trump during the past two years. Credit: Robyn Beck/AFP via Getty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, voters in california have approved us$8. 4 billion in funding for immunology research — the largest ever infusion of cash for science authorized by a public vote in US history.

Berdasarkan laporan, the funding proposal, known as proposition 38, appeared on the ballot for voters in california in last week’s us mid-term elections, but it has taken nearly a week for officials to count enough ballots to declare it a success. (This is unusual for science funding. The state government will pay for the research — which aims to find treatments that harness or re-engineer the body’s immune system to fight illnesses such as cancer and Alzheimer’s disease — by selling state government bonds. Bonds are typically reserved to pay for infrastructure projects such as road construction and require the state to pay back its debt with interest. ).

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science.

‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, supporters of the proposal say that the funding will provide stability for researchers in california, who have been affected by political turmoil. The administration of US President Donald Trump has pushed for massive cuts to science funding; put political appointees in charge of grant decisions at federal science agencies such as the US National Institutes of Health; and forced policy change at US universities that receive federal funding, including those in California.

Berdasarkan laporan, the $8. 4 billion “is an advantage to California that is unprecedented”, says Antoni Ribas, a cancer researcher and physician at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), who supported Proposition 38. It will make the state “even more of a global hub for immunology research”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the proposal has sparked debate. That’s because it calls for about half of the funding to be given directly to research institutes — and the only institute that matches the criteria called for in the proposal is one co-founded by Gary Michelson, a billionaire medical-device inventor. He wrote the proposition and donated about $45 million of his own funds to get it placed on the ballot and to campaign for its passage.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i feel like the voters have been taken advantage of,” says sarah hill, a political scientist at california state university in fullerton, who tracks the state’s ballot measures. Michelson did not respond to Nature’s request for comment before this story was published, but has said elsewhere that he will not personally profit from the bond revenue.

In California, citizens can place proposed laws directly on the election ballot by collecting hundreds of thousands of voter signatures.

Diungkapkan bahwa the state has funded scientific research through this process before. In 2004, after then president George W. Bush restricted federal funding for human embryonic stem-cell research, voters in California approved a $3-billion bond to establish the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine, which they then voted to replenish with another $5. 5 billion in 2020.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a campaign mailer encouraging california voters to support proposition 38. Credit: Smith Collection/Gado/Getty.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the model works,” ribas says. There has also been a flurry of research into developing vaccines, including the mRNA shots that have been the target of funding cuts by the Trump administration. Immunologists have been making great strides with medicines such as personalized treatments called CAR-T therapies, which are revolutionizing care, he says. Proposition 38 will ensure that such research can continue regardless of the political headwinds, Ribas adds.

Diungkapkan bahwa around $4 billion from proposition 38 will fund grants for researchers at select public universities and non-profit institutes in california through a competitive review process. According to the proposal, any commercialized therapies developed through funded research must be sold at a 20% discount to people in California, with 10% of drug royalties returning to the state’s general fund.

Sebagaimana diketahui, matthew montgomery, the science officer of a simulated mars mission organized by nasa, takes part in a ‘martian’ geology project. Credit: NASA.

Berdasarkan laporan, engineer matthew montgomery was one of a four-person crew who spent more than a year in a 158-square-metre, 3d-printed habitat for a simulated mission on the red planet. The hardware-engineering design consultant (and co-owner of a film production company) took charge of the hydroponic garden and participated in simulated ‘Marswalks’ wearing a protective suit. As well as dealing with a realistic 13–22-minute delay in their connection with mission control, the crew experienced a total communication blackout for two weeks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a new artificial-intelligence tool can identify an individual bird by its song, and can be used to track that bird’s movements over time. Researchers tested the model on recordings of male ovenbirds (Seiurus aurocapilla) — a species that sings individually unique songs — from more than 100 locations, and found that it could match songs to specific birds with up to 96% accuracy. The system provides a less invasive way to monitor birds than using physical tags. “This is almost a holy grail,” says biologist Scott Sillett.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the amount that preprint platform xsci pays referees for a quick-turnaround peer review. Authors pay up to $399 for a round of review. (Nature | 10 min read).

Diungkapkan bahwa protecting key underground fungal networks in mongolia could help to preserve biodiversity, boost climate resilience and revive iconic grasslands across the country, say researchers. In September, evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers and her team announced that they had found more than 500 types of fungus in networks across Mongolia, 90% of which were new to science. Mycologist Burenjargal Otgonsuren hopes that leveraging these networks could help to restore the swathes of degraded land in Mongolia — and preserve the 3,000-year-old way of life practiced by Mongolia’s 230,000 nomadic herding families.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sources: free to think 2026; v-dem dataset (https://go. nature. com/47UZF3P).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, academic freedom is deteriorating globally, according to the scholars at risk (sar) network, a human-rights organization based at new york university. Data show a steep decline in academic freedom in the United States, some of which preceded the 2024 election of President Donald Trump. But there is cautious optimism about the trend in Hungary following the end of Viktor Orbán’s 16-year premiership.

Diungkapkan bahwa by studying people who show no signs of neurodegeneration well into older age, scientists have identified several gene variants that could help to protect against dementia. These protective variants seem to defend the brain against the toxic clusters of proteins that cause Alzheimer’s — mechanisms that scientists now hope to exploit. “Nature has already done the experiment for us: certain gene variants protect us from Alzheimer’s,” says neuroscientist Guojun Bu. “Learning how they do this could guide us to new therapies. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the mathematics community’s reaction to openai’s huge drop of ai-generated proofs last month “ranged from exhilaration to despair”, writes mathematician ursula martin, one of the authors of the leiden declaration on artificial intelligence and mathematics, which put forward several safeguards on the technology. “The challenge … is to sustain the community of mathematicians on whom the discipline depends. “This is a moment to be clear-eyed about AI’s potential to make discoveries,” she writes. ”.

Reference: Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics.

Diungkapkan bahwa biomining strategies — those that use microorganisms to extract metals — could provide a more sustainable alternative to conventional technologies, which are struggling to keep up with soaring demand for critical minerals, argue a group of biotechnology and mining researchers. These methods can also extract metals from discarded electronics, reducing the need for virgin ores. For biomining methods to reach their potential, researchers must work with governments and industry to establish a pathway through which these technologies can be deployed at scale, the authors write.

Berdasarkan laporan, the nasa space probe voyager 1 is now almost one light-day away from earth. Nearly 50 years after its launch, finding ways to conserve power on the spacecraft requires innovative thinking, says heliophysicist Jamie Rankin, deputy project scientist of the Voyager mission. (Popular Science | 6 min read).

Berdasarkan laporan, doi: https://doi. org/10. 1038/d41586-026-03664-1.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, today i’m trying to be grateful for my typos after learning ‘how to make failure your friend and teacher’ in the latest nature careers podcast. Practice makes perfect, apparently — and that means doing the same task (such as trying to master Nature’s unusual Oxford spelling) again and again and again. Lucky for me, this newsletter offers me a fresh opportunity every day.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, let me know what you’ve taken a lifetime to master — plus any feedback on this newsletter — at briefing@nature. com.

#551. How microbes can secure the critical minerals the world needs

📅 13 Nov 2026

How microbes can secure the critical minerals the world needs

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03629-4

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. com. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Gerhard Schenk is a professor and senior research leader at the School of Chemistry and Molecular Biosciences and the Biosustainability Hub, University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia.

Paul Evans is a research fellow at the School of Chemistry and Molecular Biosciences and the Australian Centre for Ecogenomics, University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, torben v. Borchert is the scientific director of biomanufacturing at the Novo Nordisk Foundation, Copenhagen, Denmark.

Alan Tordoir is the director of new mining technology at Mining3, Basel, Switzerland.

Diungkapkan bahwa susan t. L. Harrison is a professor in bioprocess engineering and deputy vice-chancellor of research and innovation at the University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia.

Diungkapkan bahwa copper compounds (blue) can be extracted from solution using microorganisms — a process known as bioleaching. Credit: Dirk Wiersma/Science Photo Library.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the clean-energy transition is creating a paradox. To expand renewable-energy technologies, electrify transport and build infrastructure for artificial intelligence, society must extract unprecedented quantities of minerals. Demand for many of these ‘critical minerals’ is projected to increase several-fold over the coming decades1. Yet, the technologies used to obtain them remain rooted in an old model through which single metals are extracted from virgin ore2.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the consequences are increasingly apparent (see ‘critical-mineral supply under pressure’). 7% of global energy consumption and this number is projected to rise by up to eight-fold by 20604. That requires more energy and water. Mining accounts for around 1. As deposits of high-grade ores decline, larger quantities of rock must be mined and processed to produce the same amount of metal3. Many critical-mineral projects operate in regions facing high water stress, such as arid parts of Africa and Latin America1.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sources: top to bottom: ref. nature. 3; ref. 6 and go. 3; ref. com/4nzbbnx.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mining waste is growing, too. Already, hundreds of billions of tonnes of mine tailings are stored globally. Projections suggest that by 2050, up to two trillion tonnes of extra waste rock and tailings will have accumulated3,5.

Diungkapkan bahwa meanwhile, society is producing vast quantities of metal-rich waste that remain a mostly untapped secondary source of metals. In 2022, 62 million tonnes of electronic waste (e-waste) was produced globally — almost 8 kilograms for every person on the planet — and only around 22% of that was formally collected and recycled6.

How to widen access to the critical minerals that the world needs.

How to widen access to the critical minerals that the world needs.

Diungkapkan bahwa many discarded electronics contain valuable metals, including gold, palladium and rare-earth elements — in concentrations that can exceed those found in primary ores. However, recovering these metals remains technically challenging and is often economically unattractive using conventional approaches.

Sebagaimana diketahui, retrieval of metals and increasing metal circularity should be seen as a strategic capability to offset the growth of metal extraction from virgin ores. Nations that can efficiently recover critical minerals from waste streams, mine residues and low-grade resources will be less exposed to geopolitical disruptions and supply-chain shocks7.

Diungkapkan bahwa biology offers a powerful route forwards. Although biomining — which uses microorganisms to extract metals — was once considered a niche approach, it has evolved. Driven by advances in microbial ecology, synthetic biology, structural biology, protein engineering and machine learning, the scientific foundations for a new generation of mineral biotechnologies are emerging at speed8,9. These methods offer potential levels of selectivity for extracting and recovering certain metals that are often difficult to achieve through conventional hydrometallurgical processes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but, scientific progress alone will not transform mineral supply chains. The main obstacle is no longer a shortage of ideas. It is a lack of pathways from scientific discovery to industrial deployment. Here we outline how to develop those pathways, drawing on discussions at the International Workshop on Biomining of Critical Minerals and Elements, which was sponsored by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and held in Sitges, Spain, in September last year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, biotechnologies have demonstrated their industrial potential for decades. Bioleaching and biooxidation processes are already established for recovering copper, nickel, gold and cobalt from ores10. They involve irrigating heaps of crushed ore or treating ground mineral powders with specialist microbes that generate chemicals, such as acids or modifiers of reduction–oxidation reactions, that selectively dissolve either target metals or other minerals found with them.

Berdasarkan laporan, advances in synthetic biology have expanded the range of potential applications. 9% in one step under conditions that are simpler than conventional techniques, using aqueous solutions rather than organic solvents8,11. Biomolecules (such as the protein lanmodulin) can separate rare-earth elements with yields of 99. For example, engineered microbial systems can be designed to dissolve metals more effectively. AI-assisted protein design is further accelerating the discovery of macromolecules designed to selectively recognize, bind to and separate target metals from complex solutions of several elements9.

How the rush for critical minerals is neglecting human needs.

How the rush for critical minerals is neglecting human needs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, collectively, these developments suggest that biotechnology could become an important component of future critical-mineral supply chains. They often stall between proof-of-concept studies and commercial demonstration, a challenge familiar throughout industrial biotechnology. However, many promising approaches never progress beyond being validated in the laboratory. Even promising technologies often struggle to attract the capital, infrastructure and industrial partnerships needed to scale them up12,13.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, barriers must be overcome. Although a few bioprocessing pilot projects exist, their capacity is insufficient to evaluate technologies across the diverse types of ore, feedstock and process conditions encountered in practice. Investors are reluctant to finance first-of-a-kind projects when it is uncertain how well they will perform in the real world.

Diungkapkan bahwa regulatory frameworks for emerging biomining technologies are also inadequate. They often vary across biotechnology, environmental and mining sectors and between jurisdictions. Developers might need to navigate several regulatory authorities and approval pathways, creating uncertainty and delays as technologies advance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, electronic waste can contain higher concentrations of key metals than are found in natural ores. Credit: Martin Bernetti/AFP via Getty.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the european union, for example, the use of genetically modified microorganisms and their environmental applications are subject to distinct regulatory frameworks. Genetically modified microorganisms are allowed to be used in contained systems, whereas those used for field applications generally rely on naturally occurring or adapted microbial strains. The United States uses a coordinated multi-agency approach, involving the Environmental Protection Agency, the Food and Drug Administration and the US Department of Agriculture.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, valuable technical knowledge (on protein engineering, mineral characterization, hydrometallurgy and economic modelling, for instance) remains dispersed across disciplines, institutions and jurisdictions. This makes it difficult to generate the necessary evidence base — including long-term continuous operating data, metrics for tracking chemical cycles and validated economic assessments — to support large-scale adoption of such technologies.

Berdasarkan laporan, the result is a growing mismatch. Scientific advances in mineral biotechnology are accelerating, yet the mechanisms needed to deploy them are not keeping pace. Although billions of dollars are being invested to secure future supply chains for critical minerals, comparatively little attention has been devoted to building the innovation systems required to commercialize biological solutions.

Berdasarkan laporan, if biotechnology is to contribute meaningfully to critical-mineral security, environmental sustainability and circularity of resource use, then governments, industry, development banks and philanthropic funders must move beyond supporting research alone. They must invest in the institutions that enable translation of these new technologies as well.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, countries should establish shared pilot and demonstration facilities dedicated to mineral biotechnology. These facilities can support both pre-commercial and competitive studies. Shared facilities can help to overcome this barrier by allowing several organizations to evaluate biological processes using realistic feedstocks under industrially relevant conditions. Individual companies often cannot justify the risks associated with developing specialized infrastructure for technologies that remain commercially unproven. Similar approaches have been implemented successfully in synthetic biology and bio-refining, advanced manufacturing and in the clean-energy and semiconductor sectors.

The dark side of green technology: what do electric vehicles really cost?.

The dark side of green technology: what do electric vehicles really cost?.

Diungkapkan bahwa for the mineral sector, such facilities should be located near relevant resource and waste streams, including mining districts, e-waste recycling hubs and sites affected by acid mine drainage or metal-laden urban waste waters. They should have connections to universities, research labs and a skilled workforce.

Berdasarkan laporan, access to research and engineering expertise would enable rapid iteration, troubleshooting and integration of mineral biotechnologies with established processes. Such sites would extend beyond technology testing to generate the operational, environmental and economic data needed to inform investment decisions, regulatory approvals and commercial deployment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, initiatives in other sectors illustrates the value of such infrastructure. In Sweden, for instance, publicly funded pilot and demonstration facilities have been set up to test processes for biochemically converting biomass under realistic conditions14.

#552. Mongolia’s iconic grasslands are in crisis — invisible fungi could help save them

📅 13 Nov 2026

Mongolia’s iconic grasslands are in crisis — invisible fungi could help save them

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03589-9

Berdasarkan laporan, thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

April Reese is a journalist in Aveiro, Portugal.

Berdasarkan laporan, more than 70% of mongolia’s land is degraded, which has implications for the country’s nomadic herders. Credit: Timothy Allen/Getty.

Berdasarkan laporan, rising temperatures, desertification and overgrazing are taking a heavy toll on mongolia’s iconic desert grasslands, as well as its nomadic herding culture. But a team of researchers might have hit on an underground solution. They’ve found clues that protecting key fungal networks that support life above the surface could help to preserve biodiversity, boost climate resilience and revive degraded lands.

Diungkapkan bahwa in most ecosystems, invisible networks of fungi trade resources with plants by interlocking with their roots. These arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi provide the plants with nitrogen and phosphorus gathered from the soil; in return, the plants send excess carbon through their roots to the fungi, helping to sequester it from the atmosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “mongolia has very unique fungal networks that power these arid grasslands,” says evolutionary biologist toby kiers at the free university of amsterdam. Kiers is leading a project to map and identify mycorrhizal-fungus hotspots in Mongolia. “As we fight desertification, we want to be able to protect the fungi that are going to be so important for these plants and ecosystems to be restored. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, working out ways to maintain healthy fungal networks cannot come quickly enough. Around 77% of Mongolia’s land is degraded, and the country is warming three times faster than the global average. Kiers says that paying more attention to fungal networks could help to address the interconnected global challenges of desertification, biodiversity loss and climate change.

Diungkapkan bahwa it seems that fungi might be starting to get the attention they deserve: last month, at the latest meeting of the conference of the parties to the united nations convention on biological diversity, held in yerevan, armenia, 3 more countries signed a pledge to conserve fungi, bringing the total number of signatories to 17. And a road map to help countries make good on that pledge, the Global Strategy for Fungal Conservation, was launched.

Sebagaimana diketahui, kiers’s team is part of the society for the protection of underground networks (spun), a non-profit organization that maps fungal systems around the world and works to protect them. Kiers co-founded the organization in 2021. In September, its researchers announced that they had found more than 500 types of fungus in southwestern Mongolia, 90% of which were previously unknown.

Kiers’s team is in talks with several governments to present its maps of fungal hotspots and data in hopes of supporting the development of strategies to curb desertification and boost climate resilience.

Diungkapkan bahwa but at the same time as researchers such as kiers are documenting fungal hotspots, the hotspots might be disappearing. In Mongolia, the team found that degraded land had at least 44% fewer species of mycorrhizal fungi and 60% less plant cover than did non-degraded land.

Berdasarkan laporan, doi: https://doi. org/10. 1038/d41586-026-03589-9.

#553. PhDs worldwide are having a shake up — why now?

📅 13 Nov 2026

PhDs worldwide are having a shake up — why now?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03017-y

Sebagaimana diketahui, thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. com. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Jenna Ahart is a science journalist based in Washington DC.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, industrial phd programmes are increasingly being utilized in fields such as public engineering. Credit: Emanuele Cremaschi/Getty.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yifan wang didn’t realize that his thesis would be the first of its kind when he started his phd, although he knew it was likely to be more applied than most. By the beginning of his project in electrical engineering and telecommunications at the University of New South Wales in Sydney, Australia, Wang had already established a connection with an industry partner to gather insights from network traffic patterns — such as how users stream videos.

Diungkapkan bahwa but after wang began his research, australia rolled out its national industry phd programme, in which students undertake research projects co-designed by universities and companies in return for a funding boost from the government and industry partners. The goal, according to the programme’s website, is to “create a flexible pipeline of researchers who can transition between academia and industry and have multiple career pathways open to them after completing their PhD”.

Berdasarkan laporan, wang joined the programme’s inaugural class in 2023 and spent the remaining three years of his degree not only with an eye towards practical applications, but also with a community of peers spread across australia. And in May, he became the first student in the programme to submit his thesis.

Cake to the rescue: how these PhD students are cooking up a sense of community.

Cake to the rescue: how these PhD students are cooking up a sense of community.

Diungkapkan bahwa “at the beginning of my phd, i was a bit hesitant about whether i would want to do an engineering industry job or a research job,” wang says. I’m really determined to find a research position that solves real industry problems. “But now, I’ve found my interest. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as of june, the australian programme has funded 448 awards and has received more than 1,000 applications during seven funding rounds. And it’s just one of many innovative PhD models. Governments in many other countries have launched programmes supporting industry-oriented PhDs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “there’s certainly a lot of [experimental programmes] occurring around the world,” says anthony boccanfuso, chief executive of the university–industry demonstration partnership, a non-profit organization in columbia, south carolina. The partnership leads the Industry-Integrated PhD (I-PhD) programme in the United States, which was launched in July. Although Boccanfuso says that conversations about re-evaluating the PhD model have existed for the past 15–20 years, there’s now a “sense of urgency because of this need for talent” in high-demand fields.

Sebagaimana diketahui, intelligent manufacturing for rail transit systems is one of several areas to have benefited from china’s industrial phd scheme. Credit: Xiao Benxiang/VCG/Getty.

Berdasarkan laporan, at the same time, researchers worry that the programmes might take away from fundamental research. When the I-PhD programme launched, chemistry Nobel laureate Carolyn Bertozzi wrote on the social-media website Bluesky that “most PhD students pursue industry jobs anyways — that has always been true. Use NSF funds to support basic science that industry won’t support”.

Diungkapkan bahwa boccanfuso’s organization will oversee more than 250 students with funding from the us national science foundation — which will make a us$47-million investment over the next five years — along with industry and university partners. The programme aims to reduce the time taken to complete a PhD in the United States, from an average of 5. Students are jointly mentored by university and industry advisers and are expected to spend at least one year completing on-site industry research. Although the initiative is only just beginning, it’s already received “overwhelming interest” from students and universities, he adds. 6 years to just 4 years. It will also prepare STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) students for industry careers, which is where most of them are going, Boccanfuso says. Elsewhere in the world, including in China and the European Union, similar programmes have taken off.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as for why there’s been such a boom in these national-level initiatives, “it’s pretty straightforward”, says joão pereira, a civil engineer at the university of minho in guimarães, portugal, who manages one eu-funded initiative. “It’s much easier to justify applied research than fundamental research because of the proximity to yielding results. ” It can take decades for fundamental research to come to fruition, whereas applied research can deliver commercial applications — and therefore money and economic growth — “not immediately, but pretty close to it”, he adds.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, joshua twiggs, who works in the medical technology industry in sydney, australia, and has supervised industry phds, says that these initiatives aim to harness a country’s already sophisticated education system as a driver of innovation. “How do we leverage the incredibly smart work happening in universities through to actual industry implementations?” Twiggs says.

Diungkapkan bahwa such programmes reflect “the growing recognition that knowledge is a key driver of economic competitiveness and innovation”, says hans parmar, a spokesperson from innovation, science and economic development canada in ottawa, a government department focused on industry, commerce and scientific research. “Modern innovations are often too complex for a single individual, organization or even sector to develop alone,” Parmar adds. But these spanning initiatives mean that governments, universities and industries can all align their interests.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, julie dubuit is a civil engineer at the university of toulouse who took part in france’s industrial agreements for training through research phd programme. Credit: Julie Dubuit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the trend can also be assigned to “the fact that academic positions in universities can only absorb a small fraction of phd graduates”, says an official at the european commission, the eu’s executive branch. That makes “industrial PhDs very attractive with regards to future employment”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, china awarded its first batch of ‘practical phds’ in september last year. Rather than completing a conventional thesis, these students develop an innovative product, project or technique — such as intelligent manufacturing in rail transit systems. Since the law allowing these PhDs came into effect last year, more than 60 researchers have received practical PhDs.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we encourage students to implement ideas that can meet real demand in society, rather than just coming up with concepts,” says liu chun, executive dean of the national college of elite engineers at tongji university in shanghai. Candidates’ success could be measured by “how many patents a student has, how many international or domestic industry standards they have participated in setting and whether their product has successfully passed a pilot test”, Chun says.

NSF rolls out ‘industry PhD’ programme — joining a global trend.

NSF rolls out ‘industry PhD’ programme — joining a global trend.

Berdasarkan laporan, the european union’s marie skłodowska-curie actions (msca) programme offers applicants the opportunity to be part of industrial-doctorate networks of students, all of whom are focused on a single research topic. “All these interactions force students to create a set of skills they won’t get anywhere else. Each student has both an academic and a non-academic supervisor and must spend at least half of their fellowship on the premises of the non-academic partner. When all the cohort members and their supervisors come together, “it’s almost like a small conference”, says Pereira, who is part of a network that explores sustainable construction. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, one of the programme’s main goals, according to the european commission official, is to “nourish the talent pipeline for boosting employability in industry”. A 2025 study found that two years after completing their fellowships, 66% of industrial doctorate graduates were working outside academia, compared with just 43% of graduates from the MSCA’s standard doctoral networks1.

Berdasarkan laporan, i won three competitive grants in a row. Here’s how I learnt what to do.

PhD students in STEM: Nature wants to hear from you.

#554. The public trusts scientists with AI — more than it does anyone else

📅 13 Nov 2026

The public trusts scientists with AI — more than it does anyone else

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03578-y

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Elliot Yates is an intern on the Nature Careers and Supplements team.

Sebagaimana diketahui, almost half of survey respondents across nine countries thought that scientists’ use of generative artificial intelligence would make society better. Credit: gorodenkoff/iStock via Getty.

Scientists are perceived as the group of people most likely to have a positive impact on society through their use of generative artificial intelligence, finds a survey published by the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism in Oxford, UK, on 29 October1.

The survey, of nearly 19,000 people across nine countries, found that 46% of respondents think that AI use by scientists will make society better.

People who use AI tools on a daily or weekly basis were also overwhelmingly found to trust more strongly in the positive impact of the technology across all sectors than were those who seldom or never use it.

AI scientists are changing research — institutions, funders and publishers must respond.

AI scientists are changing research — institutions, funders and publishers must respond.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2024 and 2025, the team surveyed six countries, selected to provide cross-national variety among high- and upper-middle-income countries with broadly comparable levels of digital-media use. They were Japan, Argentina, France, Denmark, the United States and the United Kingdom. In 2026, Australia, Finland and Norway were added. Information was collected from about 2,000 people from each country.

Berdasarkan laporan, among the questions survey participants were asked was how much better or worse they thought each of ten groups’ use of generative ai would make their life or society. These groups included the government, politicians and political parties and ordinary people.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists ranked top in terms of public trust, closely followed by health-care professionals. By contrast, politicians and political parties were perceived as having the worst impact through their AI use (see ‘With great power’).

Diungkapkan bahwa the results did not surprise rasmus kleis nielsen, co-author of the report and a communication researcher at the university of copenhagen: scientists and health-care professionals performed well in the team’s 2025 survey, too2. As part of that investigation, respondents were asked whether generative AI would improve or worsen their experience of interacting with various sectors. Then, scientists ranked second of 12, behind only search-engine companies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this year, the team explored why certain groups were and were not trusted by assessing different sectors’ perceived ability, benevolence and integrity in their use of ai. “Much of the public believe that scientists are able to use generative AI well, are relatively benevolent in their use of it and have relatively high integrity,” says Nielsen.

Diungkapkan bahwa doi: https://doi. org/10. 1038/d41586-026-03578-y.

#555. Metascience should be a source of evidence, not a means of control

📅 13 Nov 2026

Metascience should be a source of evidence, not a means of control

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03620-z

Berdasarkan laporan, thank you for visiting nature. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). com. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Berdasarkan laporan, efforts to apply metascience to research funding must put evidence and scientists front and centre. Credit: Alamy.

Diungkapkan bahwa the european research council made headlines last month when the news broke that those applying for one of its core grants had only a 5% chance of success. Partly as a result of applicants using artificial intelligence, the ratio of submissions to grants at the European Union’s premier science funder is now so skewed as to be little more than a lottery. Some funders are already using lotteries to select grant recipients, viewing these as a fairer way to allocate funding.

More self-reflection in research can lead to better science.

More self-reflection in research can lead to better science.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is not a coincidence. The idea of distributing certain types of grant randomly has been tested experimentally over a number of years. It’s one example of how the field of metascience — the study of the practice of science itself — is having a real-world impact.

Diungkapkan bahwa metascience is not new. Nature frequently reports on metascience, invites researchers to share their opinions and publishes primary science in the field. A set of studies released in April, for example, investigated the reproducibility, replicability and robustness of research in the social and behavioural sciences1–4. The world’s oldest journal devoted to the study of science, Nauka Polska, based in Poland, was founded in 1918 and is still publishing. Developments in research funding, research organization, communication and evaluation are all aspects of metascience.

Diungkapkan bahwa metascience is also used by governments to support policy and funding decisions. In the past few years, a number of governments have established and funded metascience research units, as detailed in Seize the Meta Moment, a review by an international group of researchers and policymakers that was published last week by the Research on Research Institute in London (see go. nature. com/4z7pdt1). The author list includes members of some of these government-funded metascience units.

Huge meta-research project puts claims in social-science papers to the test.

Huge meta-research project puts claims in social-science papers to the test.

Berdasarkan laporan, in one sense, this is positive, an example of policymakers seeking solutions informed by research. They acknowledge that metascience will, to some extent, always be political, but that this should be acknowledged. But the review’s authors point out that political attention also introduces risks — namely that the discipline could be misused to serve government agendas or to justify decisions that are not supported by a consensus of the evidence. And they urge politicians to use metascience as a learning tool and a source of evidence, but not as a means of controlling researchers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the united states, the office of science and technology policy has tasked all federal science agencies with establishing metascience capabilities. nature. This was outlined in a July report, Science: A New Golden Age, which criticized excessive bureaucracy and slowness in US science, and embraced the idea of accelerating grant-awarding processes (see go. com/3uj6pf5). One concern is that the US administration could use metascience to push through major changes, such as funding cuts, support for higher-risk research or the adoption of AI, without engaging the broader scientific community.

I built the UK government’s metascience unit — here’s what countries need to know.

I built the UK government’s metascience unit — here’s what countries need to know.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the united states is not the only country where researchers are worried about potential metascience misuse; concerns have also been raised in the united kingdom, the first country to establish a government metascience unit. Last year, the nation’s main public funder of social science, the Economic and Social Research Council, announced a commitment to promoting economic growth. This is part of a broader economic push by the nation’s main public funder, UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), in response to a government priority.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the extent to which publicly funded science contributes to growth and the mechanisms underlying it are well-studied questions in the social sciences, and there are a range of views both supporting and critiquing the uk government’s objectives. It’s important that funders such as UKRI do not align themselves with just one view, and that the metascience unit does not reduce measurement of grant recipients’ performance to a metric that is itself still a matter of debate in the research community.

Why science has a credibility problem — and how to address it.

Why science has a credibility problem — and how to address it.

Berdasarkan laporan, most of the world’s science funding agencies were established when research careers were accessible to relatively few people. Funding agencies need to change how they work to adapt as the world changes. There is now a much larger and more mobile pool of researchers due, in part, to the expansion of universities and the globalization of science. That includes addressing the problem of falling success rates resulting from the greater demand for grants.

By far the best way for policymakers to use metascience to inform funding decisions is for them to work with researchers to create and implement tools designed to measure quality and competitiveness, and — as in science itself — to learn from experimentation and experience.

#556. Some people are resistant to dementia — here’s what their genes can teach us

📅 13 Nov 2026

Some people are resistant to dementia — here’s what their genes can teach us

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03625-8

Diungkapkan bahwa thank you for visiting nature. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Alison Abbott is a writer in Munich, Germany.

Diungkapkan bahwa specific gene variants seem to confer resistance to dementia, protecting individuals into old age. Credit: Hector Roqueta Rivero/Getty.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ravages of age touch us all — some more lightly than others. Geneticist Henne Holstege wanted to study people with a particular superpower: those resistant to neurodegeneration, despite their age or their genes putting them at high risk.

Brains of ‘super agers’ are strong producers of new neurons.

Brains of ‘super agers’ are strong producers of new neurons.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at first, she struggled to get funders interested. “For five years, all my grants were rejected,” she recalls. “Each time was a cup of poison. ”.

But she persevered, convinced that these super-agers could help scientists to understand why a privileged few people manage to avoid conditions such as neurodegeneration, which ail so many in older age.

She finally launched her project in 2013, and ever since, Holstege and others in her field have uncovered a rash of gene variants that seem to protect against dementias.

Researchers are increasingly convinced that understanding resilience to dementia is just as interesting as the more familiar genetics of high risk.

The brain, it seems, has its own defence mechanisms against the toxic proteins that cause Alzheimer’s — mechanisms that scientists now hope to exploit.

Berdasarkan laporan, they think that protective gene variants will help to illuminate how the disease emerges and worsens — and potentially how to treat it. Of particular interest is a group of variants that affect the workings of the ApoE protein (apolipoprotein E), which carries fat molecules essential for cellular function. Some forms of this protein are long-known contributors to the risk of Alzheimer’s. But some recently discovered and rare variants seem to confer resistance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “nature has already done the experiment for us: certain gene variants protect us from alzheimer’s and they do so safely,” says neuroscientist guojun bu from the hong kong university of science and technology. “Learning how they do this could guide us to new therapies. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the relentless course of alzheimer’s disease follows a decades-long progression that is kick-started when amyloid-β proteins in the brain clump into plaques. It concludes with loss of synapses and death of brain cells.

Berdasarkan laporan, except when it doesn’t. They stay free of dementia for most or all of their long lives. Just occasionally, people whose brains are full of plaques don’t follow the usual route. A few people don’t even build plaques, even though some might carry gene variants conferring a high Alzheimer’s risk.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the brain of a person with alzheimer’s disease (right), amyloid-β proteins clump into plaques, as shown in a magnetic-resonance-imaging scan. Credit: Mark & Mary Stevens Neuroimaging & Informatics Inst. /SPL.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the normal course of disease, the amyloid-β proteins in plaques activate immune cells in the brain known as microglia, which try to clear them. This, along with other cellular stresses, promotes the build-up and spread of a different, deadlier type of protein, called tau, which forms long, thin tangles. But if active for too long, the microglia become inflammatory and start to damage neurons. These tangles correlate with the development and severity of dementia symptoms.

Although lifestyle and environmental factors can affect the likelihood of developing the disease, the most powerful influence is genetics.

Diungkapkan bahwa the exact mechanistic details of how plaques lead to symptoms are still unclear. One such pathway might relate directly to clearance of toxic amyloids or spreading of tau, but could also be acting indirectly, by affecting energy systems in brain cells, for example. Gene variants that either accelerate or slow disease could affect many pathways. “That’s why it is important to identify these variants and discover their exact mechanisms,” says Holstege, who is at Amsterdam University Medical Centre.

Berdasarkan laporan, the search for gene mutations that contribute to the risk of alzheimer’s goes back decades. A small number of Alzheimer’s cases are strongly hereditary, involving mutations in genes that result in a higher proportion of stickier, toxic forms of amyloid-β proteins. Just one copy of any of these mutated genes almost inevitably leads to disease development early in adult life, most often when someone is in their 40s or 50s.

How to avoid dementia — what the science really says.

How to avoid dementia — what the science really says.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, familial early-onset alzheimer’s accounts for fewer than 1% of all cases; most cases affect people over 65. The protein it encodes, ApoE, is central to lipid transport between cells and around the body. The APOE gene is the most important genetic determinant of the late-onset form of disease. If it does its job properly, it can help to prevent amyloid build-up and clear it from the brain; it can also influence tau pathology, partly through effects on microglia.

Diungkapkan bahwa three main alleles of the gene exist, which generate a spectrum of risk. The alleles differ from each other in only one or two nucleotide positions. “The particular nucleotide substitution makes the protein it encodes more likely to aggregate and less likely to do its day job of transporting lipids,” says Bu. APOE2 dials the risk down: two copies can delay onset of Alzheimer’s by a decade. APOE3 is the most common variant. APOE4 dials the risk up and is the greatest genetic risk factor known. Only about 1% of the population has two copies of APOE2.

But however notable the effects of APOE alleles, the vast majority of late-onset Alzheimer cases result from the combined effects of many, often rare, gene variants — some increasing and others reducing disease risk — as well as short stretches of DNA that influence how much each gene is expressed.

Diungkapkan bahwa scientists have so far identified only part of the genetic contribution to alzheimer’s risk. They think that the missing genetics — including numerous but rare variants — might hold some of the most biologically informative clues about resilience.

A controversial Alzheimer’s surgery is said to reverse symptoms — here’s what scientists know.

A controversial Alzheimer’s surgery is said to reverse symptoms — here’s what scientists know.

Berdasarkan laporan, the usual way to search for variants is in genome-wide association studies (gwas), in which scientists analyse millions of spots on the genome for differences between groups — for example, those with disease or at high risk of disease, compared with those who are disease-free or cognitively resilient. These spots are called single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). A SNP can act as a flag for a stretch of DNA that looks different in high-risk individuals than in those who are cognitively resilient.

Berdasarkan laporan, to search for extremely rare resilience genes, you need sequences from huge numbers of people and sensitive identification techniques. Hundreds of thousands of genomes from people with and without Alzheimer’s are available from sources such as UK Biobank. Both have improved in the past decade or so. “The more people you look at, the more likely you are to spot very rare occurrences,” says Michael Greicius, a geneticist at Stanford University in California.

New cohorts are being put together all the time, and those that include people of Asian, African and other ancestry show significant differences in Alzheimer’s risk genetics compared with predominantly European-ancestry cohorts1.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, greicius’s team has found a rare protective variant known as w276c in a population of people with native american ancestry, which has not been seen in the other cohorts2. “There’s an incredible amount of power in ancestrally diverse data sets that we miss completely when we myopically focus on European ancestry,” he says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, once candidate resilience variants have been identified in human genetic studies, scientists begin the lengthy task of working out whether — and how — they might affect disease biology. They mutate these genes in mice or cell cultures and also look for cells or biological pathways that have been affected in donated brain tissue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a dozen or so rare gene variants have now been verified in this way as likely contributors to alzheimer’s resilience, although the strength of evidence varies greatly between them. All of them are gold dust for scientists. Three extremely rare variants of APOE3 have been found in people who seem to escape Alzheimer’s, and one variant of APOE4 seems to neutralize the risk usually carried by that form. APOE itself has produced some of the clearest examples. “These rare variants hold the key to understanding how the common risk variants do what they do,” says biochemist Rosie Jackson at the University of Dundee, UK.

Berdasarkan laporan, the changes to the protein might be tiny, but the consequences are huge. They all affect how the ApoE protein binds to molecules.

Diungkapkan bahwa apoe is shaped a bit like a hairpin (see ‘protective protein’). One arm has surfaces that attract and carry lipids. Once a lipid is bound, the protein opens up and reshapes itself around it. The other arm binds to receptors on cells, allowing those cells to ingest ApoE and use its lipid cargo. These receptors can also take up tau and contribute to its spread between cells.

Diungkapkan bahwa sources: t. Neurosci. Neuron 81, 740–754 (2014); H. Front. -J. Moon et al. Kanekiyo et al. Mol. 17, 1399965 (2024).

Berdasarkan laporan, there are three rare variants found in the apoe3 allele. One is known as the Christchurch variant (after the city in New Zealand in which it was discovered) and it affects the receptor-binding region of the ApoE protein. It is thought to bind ApoE less strongly to receptors, making tau less likely to spread.

The other two rare APOE3 variants influence the lipid-binding section, probably making the protein less sticky and less likely to clump and form plaques.
